Atomic Physics.title: Low Vibration Closed-Cycle Flow Cryostat for Ion-Cavity Experiments
Atomic Physics.summary: Cryogenic operation below 10 K suppresses trap-electrode and dielectric heating of trapped ions while cryopumping residual gases to ultra-high vacuum (UHV) without requiring a bakeout. These advantages are particularly important for cavity-integrated ion traps, where nearby dielectric surfaces can increase motional heating and rapid design-build-test iterations benefit from eliminating bakeout cycles. We have developed a custom 4 K cryostat cooled by a ColdEdge Technologies (CET) Stinger closed-cycle $^{4}\text{He}$ flow cryogenic system to study various ion trap optical cavity structures designed to serve as a photonic interconnect between remote, compute-capable trapped $^{171}\text{Yb}^{+}$ ion quantum processors, enabling long baseline entanglement distribution $(>10\text{ km})$. We integrate an Alpine Quantum Technologies (AQT) Paul trap and Fabry-Pérot optical cavity at the 4 K stage. The cooling capacities of the cryostat 40 K and 4 K stages were measured to be 5 W at 45 K and 0.5 W at 6.1 K. Vibrations of the 4 K stage relative to the optical table are less than $12\text{ nm}_{\text{RMS}}$ in three dimensions, as measured using a Michelson interferometer. An ultra-high vacuum (UHV) is inferred by studying the rate of hydrogen-$\mathrm{Yb}^{+}$ ion collisions. Ion storage times exceeding 5 days without laser cooling have been reported and the position of the trapped ions are reproducible within $\sim10\text{ }μ\text{m}$ following repeated thermal cycles to room temperature. The uptime of this system is 72 days and offers convenient access to the 4 K stage for in-vacuum maintenance and system modifications. Using this platform, we demonstrate spatial overlap and interaction between a trapped $^{174}\text{Yb}^{+}$ ion and the optical cavity mode on the 1345 nm transition, establishing preliminary experimental validation of the integrated cryogenic ion-cavity structure.

Atomic Physics.title: High-Harmonicity Planar Penning Traps for Single-Electron Qubits
Atomic Physics.summary: We present a detailed account of the design choices required for planar Penning traps that feature a highly harmonic confining potential. High harmonicity is indispensable for a number of applications, particularly for confinement of single electrons as qubits in quantum-information processing. The present work extends previous studies [J. Goldman and G. Gabrielse, Phys. Rev. A 81, 052335 (2010)] by a fully analytic treatment of finite electrode gaps and their relevance for small traps on the millimeter size scale and below, when relative gap sizes are non-negligible. We derive the overall trap potential with a particular focus on different models of finite-gap potentials and show how to find the optimum trap geometry and electrode voltages to minimize anharmonicities. The analytic calculations are compared with detailed finite-element simulations.

Quantum Physics.title: The replication-energy limit of PQG reduced-density-matrix theory from a single-fragment semidefinite program
Quantum Physics.summary: Variational two-electron reduced-density-matrix calculations are not size extensive: the energy per fragment can decrease when identical, strictly noninteracting fragments are replicated [M. Nakata and K. Yasuda, Phys. Rev. A 80, 042109 (2009)]. For the $P$, $Q$, and $G$ conditions (PQG) we prove the following. (i) The energy per fragment converges to the minimum of a semidefinite program (SDP) on one fragment. The limit is reached through negative interfragment covariances of order $1/(k-1)$ for $k$ replicas, which cancel the local electron number and spin fluctuations consistently with a global singlet. (ii) The energy per fragment is nonincreasing in the replica count. (iii) It reaches the limit exactly at a finite replica count. (iv) The defect is tied to the local electron-number variance: a sharp local electron number restores additivity without a spin constraint. (v) In chains of identical units the energy per unit has a limit that tends to the same minimum as the coupling vanishes. The key tool is that the $G$ condition [C. Garrod and J. K. Percus, J. Math. Phys. 5, 1756 (1964)] keeps the variances and covariances of one-body operators positive semidefinite without a representing state, so that the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality applies. PQG therefore admits explicitly constructed replicated points whose compensated local fluctuations lower the energy per fragment below the isolated value. Be, CH$_4$, N$_2$, and H$_2$O (STO-6G) and a four-site Hubbard fragment illustrate the results; in these examples the gap to the isolated value persists with three-index conditions $T_1$ and $T_2$.
Quantum Physics.comment: 26 pages, 15 tables, 1 figure; supplementary material (11 pages) as an ancillary file. Data and code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24293501

Quantum Physics.title: Tutorial: Understanding quantum Zeno and anti-Zeno regimes
Quantum Physics.summary: The quantum Zeno effect is a striking feature of quantum mechanics with foundational implications and practical applications in quantum control, error suppression, and error correction. In recent years, the effect has branched off into a variety of different interpretations, making it easy to miss its underlying unifying features. In particular, the quantum Zeno effect has been studied in the context of both selective and nonselective measurements; for both pulsed and continuous interactions; for suppression and enhancement of decay (Zeno / anti-Zeno effects); and even in the absence of measurement entirely. This tutorial presents a unified picture of these effects by examining how they all arise in the pedagogical example of a driven qubit subjected to measurements or dissipation. Zeno and anti-Zeno effects appear as regimes of a unified effect that appears when a measurement-like process competes with non-commuting evolution. The current landscape of Zeno and anti-Zeno effects is examined through this unifying lens, with a focus on experimental applications and implementations. Thus, this tutorial is ideal for new researchers interested in learning about cutting-edge tools in quantum control and measurement, while remaining highly relevant to quantum computing specialists aiming to understand the quantum Zeno effect's applications in adjacent subfields or apply it in a novel way in their own research. The quantum Zeno effect is found to be both ubiquitous and essential for the future of near-term quantum computing.
Quantum Physics.comment: 34 pages, 9 figures. Replaced for journal final version

Quantum Physics.title: Modulation equations and coherence dynamics in a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon
Quantum Physics.summary: We derive modulation equations for the joint quantum amplitudes of a circulating fluxon and an exchange-coupled qubit chain whose endpoint interacts with the field. A unitary passage operator combines the translational packet, vacuum dressing, and discrete oscillatory modes. A resonant normal form separates the slow amplitude evolution from nonresonant corrections. Ordered emission and return amplitudes generate a second-order correction that changes the population and coherence of an internal qubit. The next ground-band coefficient gives compensating diagonal and near-resonant off-diagonal contributions to the accumulated error. We bound the state error a posteriori. At a velocity-selected resonance, direct propagation over 81 passages gives a mode contribution of order $6\times10^{-8}$; the cubic ground-band approximation agrees with an expanded full calculation to $1.5\times10^{-9}$ in the tested observables. The equations describe how the source profile and field memory affect coherence inside the chain.

Quantum Physics.title: Correctable Enrollment and One-Transaction Seed Proofs for Ethereum's Post-Quantum Migration
Quantum Physics.summary: A quantum computer running Shor's algorithm can extract the private key of every Ethereum account whose public key is published, and accounts exposed by their own transactions hold 54.6% of execution-layer ETH. As the first such machine may stay secret, a migration cannot wait for visible thefts, and once keys are extractable, legacy signatures no longer tell owners from attackers. We design a migration in which owners enroll post-quantum keys cheaply with their existing signatures before ECDSA is retired at a scheduled time, while a zero-knowledge proof of the wallet's BIP-39 seed can correct any such enrollment until a common deadline afterward; an account nobody enrolled stays frozen and recoverable by seed proof without a deadline. Each proof binds the new key, a nonce and a fee cap, so neither a paying sponsor nor a reordering block builder can redirect or replay it. Validators switch to hash-based keys first, at a finalized checkpoint and under a stated bound on the attacker's voting power. We prove the account guarantees under explicit assumptions, model-check the rules, and implement the design in go-ethereum and a Lean consensus client. A three-layer recursive hash-based STARK yields a seed proof of about 190 KB that fits one transaction, verifies in 38 ms and takes a median of 111 s to generate on a laptop; four proofs aggregate into one. In a ten-node simulation with mainnet-derived accounts and fee demand, block space rather than proving sets the duration: the 4.45 million accounts with at least 0.1 ETH would migrate in 29.4 days if all enroll before ECDSA is retired and in 235 days if all recover after it in batches of four. In a mass enrollment, an enrollment waits a median of 19.1 minutes in the public mempool, longer than published estimates for a fast quantum computer to extract its key, so owners with a seed and an unexposed key should migrate by seed proof.
Quantum Physics.comment: 27 pages, 11 figures, 15 tables. v2: title changed ("Transition" to "Migration") and acknowledgments removed; no other changes. Code: https://github.com/DaseinDa/ethereum-pq-transition

Quantum Physics.title: Spin-1 quantum annealing with anisotropy-controlled intermediate-state pathways
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum annealing offers a promising strategy for solving complex optimization problems by encoding the solution into the ground state of a problem Hamiltonian. While most implementations rely on spin-$1/2$ systems, we explore the performance of quantum annealing on a spin-$1$ system where the problem Hamiltonian includes a single ion anisotropy term of the form $D\sum (S^z)^2$. Our results reveal that for a suitable range of the anisotropy strength $D$, the spin-$1$ annealer reaches the ground state with higher fidelity. We attribute this performance to the presence of the intermediate spin level and the tunable anisotropy, which together enable the algorithm to traverse the energy landscape through smaller, incremental steps instead of a single large spin flip. This mechanism effectively lowers barriers in the configuration space and stabilizes the evolution. These findings suggest that higher spin annealers offer intrinsic advantages for robust and flexible quantum optimization, especially for problems naturally formulated with ternary decision variables.

Quantum Physics.title: When Does Fine-Tuning Beat Prompting for Qiskit-to-CUDA-Q Translation? An Execution-Verified Study
Quantum Physics.summary: Moving quantum code from Qiskit to NVIDIA CUDA-Q is a practical adoption cost that language models are starting to automate. We ask whether a small open model can learn this translation, and how to measure it so that the result can be trusted. Both programs can be executed and their state vectors compared, so a kernel counts as correct only if it prepares the same state as the Qiskit reference (fidelity >= 0.999), with no text matching and no LLM judge. We build a 640-task benchmark with three test sets (larger circuits, an unseen circuit family, an unseen Qiskit coding style) and a QuantumKatas regression probe, and we test the evaluator before training. Measurement counts miss every phase-only error; a surface rule-based translator solves two of three original splits (text substitution); a converter that executes the Qiskit input and maps the circuit solves all 640 tasks -- so the benchmark measures source-level translation, not whether a circuit can be ported after running it. No base model emits a valid CUDA-Q kernel zero-shot. On Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, LoRA reaches 83.9%, tying a 4-shot prompt (83.1%), but generalizes worse to unseen style (48.5% vs. 65.5%) and cuts QuantumKatas from 23.8% to 8.9%; on Qwen2.5-Coder 7B, LoRA beats the prompt overall (92.0% vs. 82.8%) and on unseen style (78.5% vs. 65.0%), and on the 1.5B model as well, so whether fine-tuning pays off depends on the base model, while the Qiskit regression appears in all three. Mixing two replay formats is the best mitigation trade-off (84.4% translation, Katas 21.5%). On 48 parametric functions that must become kernels with arguments -- where executing the input cannot yield a parametric kernel -- models reach up to 83%; on 27 real QED-C kernels, every model scores 0%. Language models can do source-level translation of simple parametric code, but not yet of real programs.
Quantum Physics.comment: 18 pages, 1 figure, 11 tables. Code, data and results: https://github.com/anapaulaappel/qiskit-to-cudaq

Quantum Physics.title: Joint Dynamics of Spins and Frequency-Resolved Bosonic Occupations: A Projection-Operator Approach
Quantum Physics.summary: We derive weak-coupling kinetic equations for frequency-resolved bosonic mode occupations in the spin--boson model. Rather than integrating out the bath completely, we retain these mode occupations as independent dynamical variables whose equations are coupled to those for the spin observables. A projection-operator construction closes the dynamics on a product-spin ansatz and an undisplaced Gaussian environment with a diagonal covariance matrix. The equations are obtained to second order in the interaction parameter $λ$ for an arbitrary number of spins within this factorized closure, and are solved numerically for a single spin. A fixed-truncation calculation using the hierarchical equations of motion provides a benchmark for the spin dynamics with the Drude--Lorentz spectral density. The numerical results reveal a redistribution of bosonic mode occupations concentrated near the spin transition frequency $Ω=\sqrt{Δ^2+h^2}$. We also examine the response of the coupled spin--boson system to structured spectra, nonthermal initial occupations, and slow modulation of the coupling. The calculated mode occupations also allow changes in the bath-side occupation and energy densities $p(ω)δ\langle N_ω\rangle(t)$ and $ωp(ω)δ\langle N_ω\rangle(t)$ to be obtained without requiring an exponential decomposition of the bath correlation function. Its scope is restricted to weak coupling, diagonal Gaussian bath states, and, for time-dependent couplings, the adiabatic regime.

Quantum Physics.title: Estimating a Transition Point from Gibbs and Ground States
Quantum Physics.summary:
We study how observed many-body system size affects the number of state copies needed to estimate a zero-temperature first-order transition point. The unknown Hamiltonian has bounded, translation-invariant on-site and nearest-neighbour interactions on a 3D cubic lattice with local dimension three. The field coupling is known, and all models share a known boundary field penalizing one local level. The limiting order parameter is uniformly separated across the transition. Each query returns an independently prepared Gibbs or ground state at an adaptive field and system size.
  For error $ε$ and fixed confidence, we prove an exponential separation between two size caps at the same temperature. There are absolute constants $0<c_0<C$ and $c_1>0$ such that, at inverse temperature $β=c_1/ε$, restricting side lengths to $L\le c_0/ε$ requires $\exp(Ω(1/ε))$ copies in worst-case expectation, even with collective measurements. Allowing $L\le C/ε$ permits $O(\log^2(1/ε))$ copies and $O(ε^{-3})$ total spins, using local measurements and polynomial classical postprocessing. The minimax expected total spin count is $Θ(ε^{-3})$ uniformly for $β\ge c_1/ε$. At fixed positive temperature it is $Θ_β(ε^{-2})$, attained from one- and eight-site Gibbs states followed by exponential classical computation. For ground-state copies it is $Θ(ε^{-3})$.
  The lower bound uses a three-state ferromagnet whose boundary suppresses the sector carrying transition information. A spanning-forest argument and edge-boundary counting control its Gibbs weight uniformly over fields and allowed sizes, and a trace-distance hybrid argument handles adaptive learners with quantum memory. The upper bound combines finite-volume free-energy estimates, concavity and local order-parameter measurements.

Quantum Physics.title: Stopping-Time Leakage in Blind Quantum Delegation
Quantum Physics.summary: Blind quantum computation lets a client delegate a computation while hiding it from the server, up to a declared leakage. Its security definitions cover a single round. A variational quantum algorithm, however, delegates many rounds, and its classical optimizer decides from private data when to stop. We study what the resulting round count tells an honest-but-curious server. For protocols with one-time-padded transcripts and fresh randomness in every round, we prove that the server's best distinguishing advantage over the whole sequence equals the total-variation distance between the stopping-time distributions, so the round count is the only residual channel in this model. We also show that soundness composes as $δ\,\mathbb{E}[T]$ under adaptive stopping, given a conditional per-round soundness property that composably secure verifiable protocols provide. In simulated delegated eigensolvers for the transverse-field Ising chain, the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz ratio measured in iterations 5 to 15 predicts the noiseless stopping round with a leave-one-out error of 1.7 iterations, compared with 10.3 for a constant predictor. Across 14 configurations that differ in optimizer, stopping rule, initialization, system size, shot budget and problem family, the leakage is significant in 12 and ranges from 0.14 to 1.68 bits, and a maximum-entropy bound estimated on held-out sessions lies above it in all of them. For defense, we show that any mechanism acting after the stopping decision can only add rounds, and that differentially private padding costs the full adjacency radius. A fixed public iteration budget removes the channel completely; set at the median run length, it costs 10% of the remaining energy gap. A differentially private stopping rule based on AboveThreshold protects every pair of instances, but it must often stop too early, which makes it costly.

Quantum Physics.title: Exact many-body scars of generic spin models from singlet covers
Quantum Physics.summary: The square-lattice transverse-field Ising model has exact zero-energy eigenstates at any field: products of singlets on alternate plaquette diagonals. A longitudinal field isolates them from a symmetry-protected degeneracy. The mechanism is that a site coupled equally to both ends of a singlet annihilates it. The result thus holds for any spin $s$, anisotropic exchange, a large class of bond disorder and certain three-spin terms. This mechanism decides which lattices host such states: two of the 11 Archimedean lattices (four at $s=1/2$), bcc and quasicrystals with spins on the edges. Singlet pumping cools any state into them.
Quantum Physics.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures; Supplemental Material: 7 pages, 1 figure

Quantum Physics.title: An extensive theory of nonlinearly intercoupled pseudomodes for noise model reduction in circuit QED
Quantum Physics.summary: Superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamical (cQED) platforms present a persistent modeling challenge: the intrinsic nonlinearity of the Josephson potential couples to a dissipative electromagnetic environment in ways that resist both perturbative treatment and naive Markovian reduction. Standard approaches either scale poorly with system size or absorb undeclared approximations about the noise structure into their master equations. In this work, we generalize Garraway's pseudomode construction to accommodate nonlinearly intercoupled auxiliary modes, providing a nonperturbative and systematically reducible framework for open-system cQED dynamics. The key observation is that pseudomode elimination is not fundamentally tied to linearity but to representability: any eliminated sector whose influence on the retained subsystem admits a rational self-energy can be replaced by a finite set of damped auxiliary modes, independent of the internal nonlinear structure of the retained Hamiltonian. We develop the general theory in the Heisenberg picture via a Dyson equation for the retained-mode Green's function, then demonstrate closed-form elimination for two-, three-, and four-mode Kerr-coupled systems with bilinear exchange and three-wave mixing interactions. The resulting framework substantially reduces the computational overhead of open-system cQED modeling while remaining faithful to the underlying physics, provided the spectral description of the eliminated sector is chosen to match the experimentally measured response functions of the hardware.

Quantum Physics.title: What can a quantum network promise about the entangled pairs it delivers?
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum networks will give users entangled pairs of qubits, the resource behind teleportation and quantum-secure keys. But a user cannot check a pair without destroying it, so networks promise the quality of each pair, its fidelity, from a physical model rather than from a measurement. If the model is too optimistic, the delivery rule alone may miss the error. We ask: what can a network actually guarantee? Our main result has two sides. By testing some pairs at random, in secret, users can put a lower bound on the average fidelity of the pairs they keep, without any model and at every moment. But when they test only a small fraction and keep most pairs, the tests cannot reliably show that every kept pair meets a fidelity threshold: a rare bad pair can still slip through. A promise about every single pair therefore rests on a model, and we give a rule that bounds each user's risk of ever receiving a bad pair under any data-driven routing, as long as the model is not optimistic or a large enough margin is declared in advance. Real data show calibration noise beyond chance, and in simulated networks a model error of the size seen in one experiment breaks the per-pair promise unless the margin was declared. On real data from trapped-ion and diamond links, the number of pairs decided how strong the certificate was: with about 3,000 pairs of a kilohertz link and 20% tested, the median certificate was 0.818, against the 0.817 we predicted in advance. We then ran the protocol ourselves on a 36-qubit trapped-ion processor in 50 pre-registered jobs. The certificate came within 0.003 of the measured fidelity, dropped by the predicted amount when we secretly damaged a third of the pairs, and, without changes, certified three- and four-qubit entangled states. The same tests also catch an optimistic model, but slowly. We pre-registered every confirmatory analysis and report the failures too.
Quantum Physics.comment: 47 pages, 9 figures, 12 tables. Code, pre-registrations and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24447997

Quantum Physics.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched Rényi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers under conditions on local mixing and local energy estimates. We verify these conditions for one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature and for finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.

Quantum Physics.title: Magic Production and the Fundamental Forces of Nature
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum magic is a resource for universal quantum computation and may also provide a probe of fundamental interactions. We study its production in forward scattering of two distinct Standard Model fermions in the chirality basis. In the single-mediator-exchange approximation, magic production vanishes for gluon, photon, W-boson, Higgs-boson, and graviton exchange. For Z-boson exchange in purely leptonic scattering, it also vanishes at $\sin^2θ_W = 1/4$, close to the phenomenological value. By contrast, Z-boson exchange involving elementary quarks generally produces nonzero magic. These patterns raise the question of whether the construction of the fundamental forces encodes, at least in some channels, a tendency to suppress magic production.

Quantum Physics.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
Quantum Physics.summary: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.
Quantum Physics.comment: added a robust self-test of the ideal strategy in arbitrary dimension (Theorem 2); corrected errors in the proofs. 34 pages, 3 figures

Quantum Physics.title: Bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces
Quantum Physics.summary: How small can entanglement fluctuations be at fixed entropy? For a class of holographic conformal interfaces supported by a scalar with a potential, we prove $c_\text{eff}\leq c_\text{cap}\leq c_\text{eff}^2/c_{LR}$, relating entropy, capacity, and energy transmission. The coupled gravitational response is a transport term minus a positive scalar contribution; the background Einstein equation bounds that subtraction. A long Janus throat allows unbounded capacity at a finite entropy coefficient while the scalar response remains gapped.

Quantum Physics.title: Infrared finite scattering theory: Non-relativistic Coulomb scattering
Quantum Physics.summary: We revisit non-relativistic quantum-mechanical scattering in a Coulomb potential. The long-range nature of the interaction leads to divergent integrals in conventional S-matrix calculations using the Born series. Dollard showed that a well-defined scattering operator can be constructed by replacing the free Hamiltonian $ H_0 $ with an appropriate asymptotic Hamiltonian $ H_{\rm D} $. However, explicit perturbative calculations within Dollard's framework have remained scarce. We develop a perturbative formulation of the Dollard scattering operator in which the Coulomb divergences cancel to all orders. Perturbatively, we demonstrate this cancellation explicitly through second Born order and show that the resulting amplitude reproduces the known exact distributional Coulomb amplitude, including its forward-scattering contribution. With the aim of generalizing our analysis to quantum field theory, we reformulate the problem in the Heisenberg picture. We construct a new set of canonical variables through a time-dependent canonical transformation that removes the logarithmic Coulomb correction from the asymptotic phase-space coordinates. Using these variables, we construct the corresponding Heisenberg S-matrix through several complementary approaches. This leads to a formulation of the Lehmann--Symanzik--Zimmermann (LSZ) reduction formalism adapted to the modified asymptotic dynamics, which we relate to the Dollard scattering operator. This construction provides a framework for extending the LSZ formalism to infrared divergences in relativistic quantum field theories with long-range interactions and massless fields.

Quantum Physics.title: Local redundancies are necessary for long-lived memories in finite spatial dimensions
Quantum Physics.summary: We prove a no-go theorem for exponentially long-lived thermal memories, based on the structure of redundancies among Hamiltonian terms. For local stabilizer Hamiltonians in finite spatial dimensions, the absence of local redundancies---relations in which the product of a small number of Hamiltonian terms equals the identity---is known to preclude bulk thermodynamic phase transitions. Yet glassy dynamics can still sustain long-lived memories even without a thermodynamic transition, as demonstrated by LDPC codes on non-Euclidean graphs. A longstanding question, exemplified by Haah's cubic code, is whether such a mechanism can also support passive (quantum) memory in finite-dimensional Euclidean systems. We show that this route fails for local stabilizer Hamiltonians without local redundancies: at any constant nonzero temperature, local heat-bath dynamics is fast mixing, with $O(N)$ mixing time, where $N$ is the number of qubits. We establish this by proving a strong decay of correlations property of the thermal Gibbs state. We further prove rapid mixing with $O(\log N)$ mixing time under a stronger condition on induced redundancies in suitably chosen regions. This stronger result applies to several well-studied examples, including Haah's cubic code and its generalizations, as well as three-dimensional layer codes. Our work identifies redundancy structure as a key property for understanding thermal memories.

Quantum Physics.title: GeneCS: Synthesizing Resource-Efficient Code Surgery for Arbitrary Quantum Stabilizer Codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Efficiently realizing logical operations on general stabilizer codes remains a long-standing challenge in fault-tolerant quantum computing. While code surgery provides a general framework with provable guarantees through joint logical measurements, existing constructions are largely theoretical and incur substantial ancilla overhead in practice. We present GeneCS, a resource-efficient synthesizer of code surgery protocols for arbitrary stabilizer codes, designed for the backend of fault-tolerant quantum compilers. Our approach leverages structure-aware optimizations to eliminate redundancy in graph construction, dynamically balance expansion and congestion, and incorporate code degree constraints. Experimental results show that GeneCS reduces ancillary qubits and checks by over 85\% on average for both single-code and cross-code logical operations, while the optimized constructions exhibit logical-error-rate behavior comparable to the baseline under BP-OSD (belief propagation with ordered-statistics decoding). On surface-code stress tests with more than $10^4$ physical qubits, one independent synthesis run takes about one second on average. These results enable practical logical operations and efficient cross-code communication for modern QLDPC (quantum low-density parity-check) codes and heterogeneous code systems.

Quantum Physics.title: Towards the Geometry of Quantum Optical Measurements: Kraus Trajectories in the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg Group Manifold
Quantum Physics.summary: Since ancient Greek times, geometry has been a method by which humans can make inferences, by the use of similar triangles, about the world far beyond their immediate senses. Similarity plays an equally important role in quantum measurement, except that instead of between triangles on wax tablets and in the sky, the similarity is between the infinitesimal generators of transformation (i.e. rotation, affine canonical transformation) on the page and within the atom. For many quantum optical measurements of a single mode, these generators produce Kraus operators that are contained within a twelve-dimensional Lie group: the Instrumental Weyl-Heisenberg group manifold ($\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$). In particular, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is general enough to include all diffusively generated 'dyne measurements. In this paper, $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ will be used to develop two more general classes of 'dyne measurement: one that interpolates between diffusive homodyne and diffusive heterodyne (``slomodyne'') and one that adds to 'dyne measurements adaptive squeezing and displacement. Our analysis uses an approach known as the Instrument Manifold Program (IMP). In particular, a Harish-Chandra-like decomposition of $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ is used to calculate the vielbein transformation from a right-invariant basis to the corresponding coordinate basis, allowing us to universally and autonomously navigate $\mathrm{IWH}^{\textbf{12}}$ and locate the Kraus-operator of whatever selective process is being considered as it evolves in time according to the measurement record.

Quantum Physics.title: TopoLS: Lattice Surgery Compilation via Topological Program Transformations
Quantum Physics.summary: Lattice surgery is a leading approach for implementing fault-tolerant logical operations in surface code quantum computing. Current compilers largely treat lattice surgery as a layout problem downstream of a gate-level circuit; this circuit-centric view hinders a substantial optimization opportunity: lattice surgery computations are topological programs whose semantics are determined by connectivity, so different concrete space-time realizations may implement the same computation while offering different space-time volumes. Circuit-centric compilers, however, commit to fixed realizations throughout the program. We tackle this problem by presenting TopoLS, a topology-centric compiler that uses ZX diagrams as the intermediate representation (IR) for automated lattice surgery compilation. Compiler transformations on this graph preserve its semantics, and the backend must produce a valid pipe diagram, i.e., a 3D space-time layout of the lattice surgery program, with the same semantics. TopoLS first simplifies the graph and slices it into layers, and then uses Monte Carlo Tree Search to place the graph's nodes as cubes in a 3D grid and to route its edges as pipes. To scale to large circuits, TopoLS partitions the graph so that each search step routes a bounded number of connections. Across evaluated benchmarks, TopoLS reduces space-time volume by 46% on average over prior circuit-centric compilers, with improvements ranging from 25% to 90%, while exhibiting strong empirical scalability on large benchmark families.

Quantum Physics.title: Molecular Attoscope: Pulse Shape Spectroscopy of Electronic Coherence
Quantum Physics.summary: Tracking the coupled motion of electrons and nuclei on their intrinsic timescales is essential to understanding and controlling photochemical transformations. While attosecond techniques have provided unprecedented insight into electronic dynamics, they have largely been restricted to ionic systems, with nuclear motion often neglected or indirectly inferred. Here, we demonstrate a ``molecular attoscope", which uses shaped laser pulses in the deep ultraviolet to perform a coherent measurement of electronic and nuclear dynamics in an entangled wave packet in neutral benzene. This enables us to trace both the 856-attosecond-period electronic motion and the 36-femtosecond-period nuclear motion. We observe electronic coherence persisting over hundreds of optical cycles, modulated by nuclear dynamics. Our holographic approach is general, and lays the groundwork for coherent measurements capable of visualizing the evolution of the coupled electronic-nuclear wave function in real time.

Quantum Physics.title: Improved two-way capacity upper bounds for amplitude-damping channels
Quantum Physics.summary: We derive an improved upper bound on the two-way-assisted capacities of the qubit amplitude-damping channel with decay probability $γ$, given by $\log_2[1+(1-γ)γ^{γ/(1-γ)}]$. It applies to quantum communication, entanglement distribution, private communication, and secret-key agreement, and, for every $0<γ<1$, strictly improves the PLOB relative-entropy bound, the analytic max-relative-entropy bound, and the optimized balanced squashed-entanglement bound. At high damping, a known triple-rail protocol attains more than $99.54\%$ of its leading coefficient. Our method extends sector teleportation simulation to qubits: phase rotations and permutations give exact simulations within fixed-excitation subspaces while preserving the two-level input structure. We determine the exact, additive relative entropy of entanglement of the amplitude-damping resources and the exact regularized entanglement gain at fixed input population. We then derive explicit bounds for generalized amplitude damping, which includes thermal excitation. Combining the amplitude-damping gain with unital and entanglement-breaking channels gives a closed expression that recovers the zero-temperature result and vanishes throughout the entanglement-breaking region. It improves established benchmarks over broad parameter ranges, while the exact entanglement of the generalized resources remains open. Both results admit refinements under an average-excitation constraint. The bounds provide quantitative limits for adaptive communication through relaxing qubits and show how a sector simulation can remain useful beyond channels whose resource entanglement is known exactly.

Quantum Physics.title: Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks for Power Grid Analysis under N-x Contingencies
Quantum Physics.summary: The combinatorial growth of network configurations under N-x contingencies presents significant computational challenges for power system analysis. In this work, we introduce a quantum algorithm based on Controlled Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CCTQWs) that evolves a quantum walker conditioned on a contingency register held in a uniform superposition of all x-line outage configurations representing the contingency scenarios. The proposed framework encodes transmission line availability in a quantum register and employs controlled Hamiltonian evolution to account for topology changes induced by contingencies. We develop a gate-based implementation using Trotter-Suzuki product formulas and investigate the associated approximation errors and computational requirements. As a demonstration of the proposed methodology, we introduce a contingency-averaged occupation centrality measure derived from quantum-walk measurement statistics. Numerical experiments on an 8-bus power network under N-2 contingencies demonstrate the implementation of the algorithm and characterize the convergence of the resulting centrality estimates with respect to the observation window, sampling and Trotter steps. Comparison with established classical centrality measures shows a qualitatively consistent characterization of network structure, particularly in identifying the most central nodes. The proposed framework establishes a methodological foundation for quantum-walk-based analysis of power networks under contingencies, providing a starting point for future investigations of quantum algorithms for power system security assessment.

Quantum Physics.title: Soft information from neural-network logits and correlation-aware matching gaps
Quantum Physics.summary: To utilize quantum error-correcting codes, a decoder must infer the logical sector from the measured syndrome. Beyond producing a hard logical decision, some decoders provide soft information that estimates the reliability of that decision. For minimum-weight perfect matching (MWPM), a common confidence measure is the complementary gap. Neural-network decoders trained with binary cross entropy naturally output a different confidence score, the logit, whose usefulness for post-selection has already been demonstrated. Here, we compare the logit of a pretrained graph neural-network (GNN) decoder with the complementary gaps of uncorrelated and correlation-aware MWPM, evaluated on identical syndromes from rotated-surface-code memory experiments under circuit-level noise. Incorporating correlations substantially improves matching-based hard decisions, post-selection performance, and calibration, reversing the GNN's advantage at larger code distances while leaving it superior at smaller distance. Exchanging confidence scores shows that their ability to rank logical failures is decoder-relative. An exact-posterior comparison at small distance, together with larger-distance log-loss measurements, further shows that neither score universally provides the closer approximation to posterior soft information. These results reveal that much of the apparent advantage of learned confidence over the standard matching gap arises from correlations omitted by the matching model. Nevertheless, learned logits provide useful soft information without requiring an explicit detector error model or competing-sector matching calculations at inference, offering an alternative where matching-based confidence is costly or unavailable.
Quantum Physics.comment: 19 pages, 9 figures, 8 tables. Major revision: added correlation-aware MWPM, an exact-posterior benchmark, and expanded confidence discrimination and calibration analyses. Scientific conclusions revised

Quantum Physics.title: Extraction erases the gain: cavity loss bounds dynamical-Casimir metrology at ultrastrong coupling
Quantum Physics.summary: Ultrastrong light--matter coupling dresses the vacuum with virtual photons whose response to the coupling strength exceeds that of any coherent probe, yet these photons never leave the cavity and cannot be detected. A parametric drive at the dynamical-Casimir resonance converts them into real photons that a detector can collect. We show that this conversion is self-limiting: converting the virtual photons of an ultrastrongly coupled probe into real, extractable photons opens the cavity port that removes them, so the retained metrological gain is set by the accumulated cavity loss rather than by the pure-state ceiling. In the driven quantum Rabi model the pure-state quantum Fisher information on the coupling reaches $1.7\times10^{5}$ times the coherent baseline; at a cavity linewidth of $246$~MHz, typical of coplanar-waveguide flux-qubit circuits, master-equation dynamics retain $0.96\%$ of it. In a 32-qubit Dicke model the retained fraction is $2.6\%$ at the largest photon basis computed. Eighteen lossy configurations from both models fall on one curve of the accumulated loss, the product of linewidth and interrogation time, which halves the retained information at $0.13$. The extraction cost, not the lossless ceiling, is the figure of merit for any protocol that reads bound vacuum correlations through a lossy port.
Quantum Physics.comment: 26 pages, 10 figures, 9 tables; Supplemental Material included (25 pages)

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum tomography of ququart states of optical vector vortices based on measurements in mutually unbiased bases
Quantum Physics.summary: In this paper we present an original method for quantum state tomography of vector optical vortices with an axially symmetric transverse polarization profile. We present an interference technique which allows one to distinguish states of vector vortices with a fixed topological charge with high accuracy. We also demonstrate the feasibility of experimental quantum tomography of the density matrix in the logical ququart space built on vector vortices, with high fidelity for all 20 basis states. It is shown that the proposed tomography scheme provides a uniform characterization of states in all mutually unbiased bases of the ququart space.

Quantum Physics.title: Direct quantum simulation of compressible Navier-Stokes flow via finite homotopy linearisation
Quantum Physics.summary: We develop a direct quantum simulation algorithm for finite homotopy approximations to the non-isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations. A primitive-variable formulation gives polynomial residuals in the fields and their spatial and time derivatives, including density-weighted time derivatives. On a periodic grid, applying each spatial stencil uniformly to every factor in a shifted product preserves the dynamics of the finite homotopy hierarchy in an affine linearisation. Because each deformation equation depends only on lower homotopy orders, the lifted generator matrix is strictly block lower-triangular and hence nilpotent. The resulting finite-polynomial solution evaluates the final state directly without time-stepping error, while explicit short-time convergence conditions bound the homotopy truncation error on a fixed grid. In two-dimensional Taylor-Green flow, initial pressure balance removes the leading longitudinal acceleration and delays the onset of dilatational kinetic energy from quadratic to quartic in time. At Mach numbers 0.2 and 0.4, the fifth-order hierarchy reproduces viscous dissipation over a longer interval than pressure-dilatation at the same relative tolerance. We identify auxiliary variables representing the same evolving product, compile the finite-polynomial evolution into logical quantum circuits, and recover a signed velocity Fourier mode via Hadamard interference. Together, the Taylor-Green energy budgets quantify the accuracy windows of each homotopy order, while coarse-grid circuits verify the signed readout and measure gate counts. For higher-order evolution on finer grids, merging coincident stencil terms and combining block-encoded products along strictly increasing homotopy-order paths substantially reduce the predicted normalisation cost.

Quantum Physics.title: Network contextuality beyond binary outcomes
Quantum Physics.summary: Can a joint measurement reveal nonclassical behaviour in independently prepared systems that share no entanglement? We study network contextuality by extending the two-qubit test of bi-contextuality [G. Ruffolo et al., arXiv:2507.08461 (2025)] to projective measurements with more than two outcomes. In one laboratory, an observer measures the systems individually or jointly performs two compatible global measurements constructed from them. The individual probabilities constrain the possible classical correlations at each source. For our preparations, every noncontextual model with outcome-deterministic and source-independent assignments predicts a nonzero average product of the two global outcomes. The joint quantum measurement gives zero. We construct explicit product states realizing this contradiction for $N=d$ independent sources, each preparing one $d$-dimensional system, with $2\leq d\leq9$. We derive an inequality in observed probabilities, prove its single-source bounds are exact for these preparations, and give sufficient thresholds for violations under independent depolarizing noise. For this family of preparations the dimension range is sharp: for every $d\geq10$ the individual probabilities admit a zero assigned average, so the certificate fails. The same data admit a noncontextual explanation when source independence is relaxed.

Quantum Physics.title: Just another Markovian embedding for open quantum systems
Quantum Physics.summary: In this work, I present one more method for analysis of non-Markovian open quantum systems by embedding them into larger Markovian systems. As many other approaches, this method starts from finding a rational approximation for the bath correlation function in the frequency domain, the difference is that I retain $ω\to -\overline ω$ symmetry for the poles of the approximation. This allows to reduce the dimension of embedding from one- to half-degree-of-freedom per pole. In case of odd number of poles, the resulting equation describing dynamics of the system turns out to be not a Lindblad, but a hybrid quantum-classical master equation.

Quantum Physics.title: Gradually opening Schrödinger's box reveals a cascade of sharp dynamical transitions
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum mechanics predicts that unobserved systems may exist in a superposition of states, yet measurement produces definite outcomes, a tension at the heart of the quantum-to-classical boundary. How the transformation between these opposing regimes unfolds as observation strength increases has remained experimentally elusive. Here, by continuously tuning the measurement strength on a superconducting qubit, we reveal that measurement-dominated dynamics emerge not gradually but through multiple sharp transitions marked by the halting of coherent oscillations, state freezing near an attracting state, and the onset of quantum Zeno dynamics. Decoherence, rather than washing out this structure, reshapes it, reordering the transitions and decoupling signatures that coincide in idealised models. These results establish that the passage from quantum dynamics to measurement-dominated behaviour unfolds through a sequence of distinct transitions governed by the interplay between observation and environment.

Quantum Physics.title: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links
Quantum Physics.summary: High-dimensional quantum key distribution tolerates more noise than qubit-based protocols, but the dimension that maximizes the secret key depends on turbulence, background light, device imperfections, and block size, all of which change during an airborne or satellite pass. Finite-size security analyses of high-dimensional protocols fix the dimension in advance, and the dimension-adaptive schemes reported so far have been analyzed only asymptotically. Here, a controller sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block using only public data from earlier blocks. Each block is therefore a standard fixed-length protocol, and composable finite-key security against coherent attacks follows from sequential composition; an inaccurate channel model reduces the key rate but does not weaken security. The controller estimates turbulence from observed error rates, maximizes the expected key under forecast uncertainty, and recalibrates its model online. We evaluate it on a simulated entanglement-based orbital-angular-momentum link between an aircraft and a ground station, using Kolmogorov phase screens and the Hufnagel--Valley turbulence profile. Accounting for forecast uncertainty increases the key by 31\%--47\% relative to a naive planner. Over night, dawn, daytime, and model-mismatch scenarios, the recalibrated controller retains at least 98.8\% of the key obtained with the best fixed dimension for each scenario, while every fixed dimension drops to 73.5\% or less in at least one scenario. Running the link's measurement statistics on a superconducting quantum processor shows device errors close to a constant offset; with these errors included, the best daytime dimension changes from eight to four, and the controller adjusts accordingly.

Quantum Physics.title: Unbiased Estimation of Conditional Covariance for Quantum Optomechanics
Quantum Physics.summary: Continuous measurements can prepare macroscopic mechanical oscillators in conditional quantum states, but their covariance is difficult to verify. For each quadrature, the conventional retrodictive estimator is unbiased exactly when the conditional and future-likelihood variances are equal, and it needs a separate rule for the position-momentum cross covariance. Here, we derive an estimator that recovers all three independent covariance entries using one exact identity for linear-Gaussian models. It combines the forward trajectory, a future-likelihood center, and the smoothed trajectory. Using these three trajectories, we reconstruct the covariance of the center-of-mass motion of a 7.71-mg suspended mirror. This covariance describes a thermally squeezed conditional state with a principal-variance ratio of $4.7\pm0.7$. The reconstructed covariance and the measured bias difference between the conventional and three-trajectory estimators agree with the model predictions within propagated uncertainties. Varying the upper band edge resolves changes in all three covariance entries. For upper edges up to 1 kHz, the measured changes agree with the finite-band predictions. Every experimental record covers only a finite frequency band; these results show how such records can be used to characterize conditional mechanical states and provide a basis for future tests of macroscopic entanglement.
Quantum Physics.comment: Revisiting v1 and v2, we found normalized quadrature amplitudes 8.6% below the documented scale in all six archived records. V3 reanalyzes the raw voltage, uses six Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes instead of three for thermal force noise, and models laser frequency noise using the measured servo response. The covariance reconstructed over 130-2000 Hz is consistent with the full-band prediction

Quantum Physics.title: Nanohertz Loss in a Pendulum for Macroscopic Entanglement under Structural Damping
Quantum Physics.summary: Pendulums are attractive for macroscopic quantum control because gravitational dissipation dilution lowers the modal loss, while the $1/f$ force noise of structural damping allows nearly lossless trapping to suppress the noise at an upshifted resonance. The same $1/f$ spectrum, however, produces a low-frequency tail that penalizes entanglement. To overcome this penalty, we realize a 7-mg pendulum suspended by a stepped fused-silica fiber. Ring-down measurements give an energy-decay rate $Γ/2π=361(39)$ nHz at the bare resonance $ω_0/2π=2.63$ Hz. The reduction in $ω_0Γ$ relative to the previous uniform suspension more than offsets the penalty. Although both suspensions support entanglement in the error-free model, only the stepped one allows robust verification in the multimode model with experimental uncertainties.

Quantum Physics.title: Non unitary and nonlinear quantum generative large model design and fast large-scale training without back propagation
Quantum Physics.summary: Transformer-based large models require huge computational and storage costs. Quantum computation is expected to address that due to its potential to speed up classical algorithms exponentially. Key challenges of implementing quantum large models include the linear, unitary nature of qubit evolutions contrast with the non-unitary matrices and nonlinear functions in classical Transformers, as well as the difficulty of implementing gradient back-propagation on quantum hardware. Here we propose a fully quantum large model containing all the Transformer layers, implementing the non-unitary transformations through SVD-decomposition-based quantum circuits, and approximated nonlinear activation functions through pre-trained parameterized quantum circuits. We also propose a quantum circuit training algorithm based on multi-agent Reinforcement Learning, which can train large-scale parameterized quantum circuits without back-propagation. The dependency between the inference time complexity and the model's hidden dimension has been reduced from polynomial to logarithmic, showing an exponential advantage. The inference executions on the quantum hardware verify our model's 300-1000 times speed-up, and the measurements on the sequence-to-sequence tasks shows its learning ability. The training algorithm achieves only 25% complexity of the best SOTA quantum circuit training algorithms, especially this ratio decreases fast as the parameter scale increases. Our work not only proposes a quantum large model that can significantly reduce the computational cost, but also promotes the quantum computation towards general computing.

Quantum Physics.title: Differentiable collision-model control for multipartite state engineering: reachability, geometry, and preparation cost
Quantum Physics.summary: We study a differentiable control architecture for multipartite state engineering in which partial-SWAP collisions, a Heisenberg exchange, are interleaved with layers of local phase rotations. Singular collision angles confine the evolution to invariant supports, impose exact fidelity ceilings, and generate an inverse-distance lower bound on the preparation time nearby. Away from them, numerical certificates show that the sampled couplings reach the whole fixed-excitation sector for sector dimensions up to 21, and optimizations reach fidelities above 0.999 for dimensions up to 1716. At generic couplings the number of rounds needed for a given Dicke fidelity, measured by the ratio of independent phase controls to the projective dimension, is nearly independent of the system size, and the quantum Fisher information spectrum is close to that of a random Gaussian Jacobian. Near full SWAP, a slow-time theory, the sharp form of the inverse-distance bound there, predicts microscopic hitting times without fitted parameters: the distance from the singular point sets the clock and its direction selects the effective control geometry. A detuning sweep along two rays shows that the Dicke horizon follows this law up to a detuning of 0.1, where it is two to five times shorter than at a generic coupling in sectors of dimension 70 to 252, while phase-uniform, random-sign, and Haar-random targets are delayed; beyond a detuning of about 0.3 all targets return to the generic cost. The slow-time value for the Dicke target is nearly the same for sector dimensions from 35 to 252. The exchange graph of the effective theory offers an interpretation of this ordering. Counted in two-qubit gates, generic-coupling preparation is costlier than known Dicke circuits; the architecture offers fixed global couplings, local phase rotations as the only control, and no measurement.

Quantum Physics.title: On-demand frequency-entangled microwave biphotons from a transmon-resonator dimer
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose a superconducting circuit QED source of on-demand frequency-entangled microwave photon pairs, with one photon emitted into each of two separate waveguides, enabling individual manipulation. The design is based on a transmon-resonator dimer, which consists of two transmon-resonator subsystems coupled through a cross-Kerr interaction. We outline a viable circuit-QED realization in which the required cross-Kerr interaction is implemented using Josephson-junction couplers. To analyze the emission dynamics, we derive and numerically solve the set of evolution equations that enable tracking the evolution of the joint spectral intensity of photons. We characterize the resulting photon-number correlations, frequency anticorrelation, and spectral entanglement. By varying the coupling strengths, we obtain biphotons with distinct joint spectral intensities and Schmidt spectra, ranging from broadly distributed multimode entanglement to states dominated by two nearly equally weighted Schmidt contributions. In the latter regime, optimizing the transmon-resonator coupling and detuning yields an output biphoton state that has fidelity $F \approx 0.956$ with a two-dimensional maximally entangled state. Restricting the local target modes to separated frequency bins yields a fidelity $F_\mathrm{bin} \approx 0.949$, indicating that the output state closely approximates a frequency-bin Bell pair. Thus, the proposed microwave biphoton source provides a route toward distributing frequency-encoded quantum resources between remote superconducting nodes.

Quantum Physics.title: Interaction-Driven Photocurrent Enhancement in a Quantum Photocell with Opposite Transient and Steady-State Responses
Quantum Physics.summary: We study photocurrent control in a quantum photocell with interacting qubit-qutrit donors coupled to an acceptor. We show that stronger Heisenberg exchange coupling and anisotropy increase the transient photocurrent but reduce its steady-state value, whereas the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction favors steady-state output at the expense of transient enhancement. This reversal highlights the need to distinguish rapid current generation from sustained operation when tuning quantum photovoltaic devices. Analysis of donor purity further reveals that the qutrit's local purity tracks the photocurrent trends in both regimes. These results demonstrate that the effects of donor interactions depend crucially on the timescale of operation, suggesting a strategy for tailoring the response of hybrid quantum photocells to different operating regimes.

Quantum Physics.title: Symmetry-Protected Bipartite Entanglement in Hopf-Linked Quantum Rings
Quantum Physics.summary: We study two interacting electrons in Hopf-linked quantum rings, one electron on each ring. In the absence of the inter-ring interaction, the two lowest orbital states on each ring have the same energy. For the ideal geometry, the Fourier coefficients of the three-dimensional Coulomb kernel satisfy $V_{1,0}=-V_{0,1}$, making the positive-parity block of the four-state Hamiltonian diagonal in the Bell basis. Unitary symmetries of the full orbital Hamiltonian preserve the parity sectors under virtual transitions. For pure states odd under ring exchange followed by a half-turn on each ring ($\mathcal Y=-1$), the Schmidt weights occur in equal pairs, giving at least one bit of entanglement between the rings. An elliptic deformation changes the Coulomb selection rule to first order while preserving the link. Finite-basis diagonalization shows that higher orbitals can reduce the probability of obtaining the encoded Bell pair by projection onto the two lowest orbitals of each ring even when the entanglement between the rings remains close to one bit.

Quantum Physics.title: Ground-State Manifold Curvature and Phase Transitions in the Kitaev Honeycomb Model
Quantum Physics.summary: The Kitaev honeycomb model is an exactly solvable spin model whose ground state realizes a quantum spin liquid with gapped Abelian phases and a gapless phase that becomes a non-Abelian phase in a magnetic field. Here we study its phase transitions through the geometry of the ground-state manifold, using the Ricci scalar of the quantum metric. In the three gapped phases we obtain closed-form expressions for the curvature, which is negative and diverges at the critical lines; the three phases are related to one another by an exact change of coordinates. In the gapless phase, the curvature of the infrared-regularized metric is positive and decays inversely with the logarithm of the system size, with a size-independent amplitude that diverges at the phase boundaries, with an exponent different from that of the gapped side. The change of sign and the divergences together reproduce the complete phase diagram. A magnetic field gaps out the gapless phase and plays the role of the infrared cutoff, so that away from the critical lines the curvature of the non-Abelian phase becomes finite and positive, while around the critical lines it opens a crossover region whose width scales quadratically with the field. Since divergences of geometric quantities are often regarded as signatures of phase transitions, the divergence of the Ricci scalar at the critical lines provides a geometric signature of these transitions.

Quantum Physics.title: Unveiling the Action of Randomized Compiling on Quantum States: A Geometric Perspective
Quantum Physics.summary: Randomized compiling (RC) converts coherent errors into stochastic Pauli noise, but this conversion alone does not imply isotropic contraction of the output state. Here we use the generalized Bloch vector (GBV) representation to examine the cumulative effect of RC on state purity and orientation in multi-layer circuits. For the independent, isotropically distributed weak coherent errors considered here, the accumulated ensemble-averaged RC channel lies close to the depolarizing direction, producing a state-level near-isotropic contraction that sacrifices a small amount of purity to achieve a substantial suppression of orientational deviation. When dephasing coexists, RC suppresses the coherent-error contribution but leaves a residual deviation dominated by dephasing, setting a limit that we term the "dephasing wall". We experimentally validate these findings on a superconducting quantum processor through GHZ state preparation and phase estimation in a simulation of topological braiding. The results confirm that RC's effectiveness stems from its ability to suppress the orientational bias of coherent errors---a structural transformation not resolved by fidelity alone but directly visible through GBV diagnostics.

Quantum Physics.title: A single-photon quantum sensor via single-atom cavity-QED
Quantum Physics.summary: We describe a cavity-QED sensor using an optical probe with exactly one photon per pulse. This has a better sensitivity than a coherent pulse with the same average power when no global coherent phase reference is available. The sensor measurement is based on the estimation of the Raman-controlled absorption probability of a single-photon pulse. We use the Fock state master equation to determine the dynamics and performance of the Raman-controlled absorption of a single photon pulse and optimise the sensitivity using machine learning. Two examples are presented; (1) the target parameter is the detuning of the two-level system itself, and (2) the target parameters describe a remote reflecting cavity. In the second case, the scheme does not require a shared coherent phase reference.

Quantum Physics.title: Scaling of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence
Quantum Physics.summary: Phase rigidity vanishes as a power law near exceptional points, reflecting the coalescence of eigenstates at these points. In this Letter, we show that non-Hermitian skin effects induce distinct asymptotic behaviors of phase rigidity without eigenstate coalescence. To demonstrate this, we derive exact analytical results for three non-Hermitian chain models and verify them numerically. For the ordinary skin effect, phase rigidity decays exponentially with increasing system size $N$, as the right and left eigenstates are exponentially localized at opposite boundaries. For the scale-free skin effect, phase rigidity exhibits an $N^{-2}$ power-law approach to a nonzero constant as the right and left eigenstates have decay lengths proportional to $N$. For the algebraic skin effect studied here, phase rigidity can exhibit an $N^{-1/2}$ power-law decay to zero, with the right eigenstate algebraically localized near a boundary and the left eigenstate spread across the chain. These findings show that non-Hermitian skin effects govern phase-rigidity scaling by shaping the spatial profiles of the right and left eigenstates, enabling control of eigenstate nonorthogonality without exceptional points.

Quantum Physics.title: Multi-port few-photon diodes
Quantum Physics.summary: We investigate single- and two-photon scattering dynamics in a system comprising two one dimensional chiral waveguides coupled to a dissipative Rydberg atom pair. By employing the Laplace transform method, we analytically solve the scattering problem and characterize the transport properties. Our results demonstrate robust perfect single-photon diode effects in this system with or without dissipation, exhibiting unity transmittance in the forward direction and zero transmittance in the backward direction. Unlike previous studies where perfect nonreciprocity requires a specific dissipation rate, our scheme achieves this effect without fine-tuning such parameters. Furthermore, we extend the nonreciprocal transport to multi-port configurations at the one and two-photon levels. The system exhibits pronounced photon nonreciprocal behavior in lossy and lossless scenarios, without the need for precise parameter matching. This work provides a robust platform for on-chip nonreciprocal photonic devices.

Quantum Physics.title: Analytic continuation of the T- and S-matrices to unphysical sheets in a multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model
Quantum Physics.summary: We consider a matrix multichannel extension of the Friedrichs-Faddeev model. First, we formulate conditions on the kernels of the potential matrix that guarantee for the T-matrix (and then for the S-matrix) the existence of analytical continuation to unphysical energy sheets. We also obtain explicit representations for the analytically continued T- and S-matrices on unphysical sheets in terms of these matrices themselves, but only taken in the physical sheet. From the explicit representations obtained, it follows that the resonances on a certain unphysical sheet are nothing but the points at which the corresponding truncation of the scattering matrix in the physical sheet has an eigenvalue of 0.

Quantum Physics.title: No-Go Theorems for Transversal and Automorphism Clifford Gates on Prime-Dimensional Qudit Stabilizer Codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Logical Clifford gates are a basic primitive of fault-tolerant quantum computation. For stabilizer codes on qudits of prime dimension $p$ that encode $k\geq 2$ logical qudits, we prove that Clifford gadgets that are transversal with respect to a fixed partition of the physical qudits into blocks of fewer than $k$ qudits cannot realize the full logical Clifford group, and that this block size is tight. Code automorphisms, which combine single-qudit Clifford gates with qudit permutations, also fail for every $p$. Both obstructions come from prime-order logical Clifford elements that these gadgets cannot reach.

Quantum Physics.title: Bogoliubov-picture thermofield dynamics in anharmonic environments
Quantum Physics.summary: Thermofield dynamics (TFD) describes finite-temperature quantum relaxation through a purified wavefunction, without sampling thermally populated initial states. For harmonic environments, TFD is typically combined with a thermal Bogoliubov transformation to obtain a compact wavefunction representation. This transformation can also be useful for anharmonic baths, but preparing the corresponding thermal state in the transformed representation poses additional numerical challenges. Here, we explore TFD approaches tailored to anharmonic potentials and compatible with efficient tensor network methods for quantum propagation. We show that the conceptually appealing route of converting a harmonic-reference thermal state into the target anharmonic state by imaginary-time propagation can be numerically ill-conditioned. As a practical alternative, we formulate a multilayer multiconfiguration time-dependent Hartree (ML-MCTDH) protocol that separates thermal-state preparation from the harmonic-reference Bogoliubov transformation. We prepare the thermal purification in the bare representation and then apply finite-basis Bogoliubov unitaries to the physical--auxiliary mode pairs. For independent bath modes, direct construction of the thermal amplitude provides a complementary initialization procedure. We illustrate this protocol through vibrational relaxation and spatial-superposition decoherence of a harmonic subsystem coupled to a Morse-oscillator bath. We find non-monotonic energy relaxation, shifts in the dominant resonant response, and oscillatory energy exchange at zero and finite temperature. For decoherence, we recover the expected harmonic-bath scaling and find a pronounced non-monotonic dependence of the decay rate on anharmonicity at finite temperature in a low-frequency model, with a weaker dependence in a high-frequency model.

Quantum Physics.title: Reconstruction and geometry of $4\times4$ quantum Sudoku
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the reconstruction and geometry of $4 \times 4$ quantum Sudoku, viewed as arrays of rank-one projections whose rows, columns and blocks decompose the identity. We give necessary and sufficient conditions for two prescribed opposite blocks to admit a completion, prove its uniqueness, and obtain explicit reconstruction formulas, also expressed in the language of quantum logic. The sixteen overlaps between these blocks determine the unitary equivalence class of the grid, while the number of nonzero overlaps equals its cardinality. Using a matrix representation, we parametrise the equivalence classes by five closed squares, with the sides of one square identified with the diagonals of the other four. The quotient by classical cell symmetries is a closed disc containing exactly two classical classes. Finally, measurement in the basis of the first block gives a fractional Sudoku that retains the full unitary class and is a convex combination of at most four classical grids. This measurement map embeds the five-square model into a seven-dimensional polytope whose vertices are the twelve classical Sudoku.

Quantum Physics.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
Quantum Physics.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time surprisal FT treats the complete channel, identifies the nonunital correction, and yields a GSL bound for unital dressed evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that does not mix distinct dressed-charge sectors and preserves the full dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The entropy bounds establish the GSL in a controlled slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections.

Quantum Physics.title: Nonempirical Determination of the Optimal TAO-DFT Fictitious Temperature for Molecular Systems in the Lowest Singlet State
Quantum Physics.summary: Thermally-assisted-occupation density functional theory (TAO-DFT) [J.-D. Chai, J. Chem. Phys., 2012, ${\bf 136}$, 154104] has been developed to investigate the ground-state properties of large electronic systems exhibiting varying multi-reference (MR) character. As a central parameter in TAO-DFT, the fictitious temperature $θ$ is closely linked to the degree of static correlation in an electronic system. While the conventional system-independent $θ$-scheme is computationally efficient and broadly applicable, a fixed, preassigned $θ$ can be overly large for single-reference (SR) systems yet too small for strongly MR systems. To overcome this limitation, we propose a nonempirical scheme based on spin-symmetry restoration to determine the optimal system-dependent fictitious temperature $θ^{*}$ for molecular systems in their lowest singlet states. Across benchmark tests encompassing both MR systems (the bond dissociation of H$_{2}$, N$_{2}$, Li$_{2}$, and LiH, as well as the torsional rotation of twisted ethylene) and pure SR systems (the dissociation of He$_{2}$ and Ne$_{2}$), our nonempirical approach demonstrates superior overall accuracy compared with the conventional fixed-$θ$ scheme. Furthermore, relative to standard Kohn-Sham density functional theory (TAO-DFT with $θ= 0$), TAO-DFT employing $θ^{*}$ yields substantial improvements for MR systems while preserving comparable accuracy in SR systems.

Quantum Physics.title: High-Harmonicity Planar Penning Traps for Single-Electron Qubits
Quantum Physics.summary: We present a detailed account of the design choices required for planar Penning traps that feature a highly harmonic confining potential. High harmonicity is indispensable for a number of applications, particularly for confinement of single electrons as qubits in quantum-information processing. The present work extends previous studies [J. Goldman and G. Gabrielse, Phys. Rev. A 81, 052335 (2010)] by a fully analytic treatment of finite electrode gaps and their relevance for small traps on the millimeter size scale and below, when relative gap sizes are non-negligible. We derive the overall trap potential with a particular focus on different models of finite-gap potentials and show how to find the optimum trap geometry and electrode voltages to minimize anharmonicities. The analytic calculations are compared with detailed finite-element simulations.

Quantum Physics.title: Spin-coherent quantum designs
Quantum Physics.summary: Coherent states bridge the gap between quantum and classical physics, but their overcomplete and nonorthogonal nature makes it difficult to identify finite sets that represent spin observables exactly. Finite spin-coherent tomography and discrete coherent-state operator bases already exist. Here we address a more specific problem: preserving the canonical contravariant-symbol representation. For a spin-$J$ system, the canonical finite coherent-state formula reconstructs every operator in the rank-$S$ irreducible tensor sector exactly if and only if the sampling directions form a spherical $(2J+S)$-design and the corresponding coherent-state projectors then form a spin-coherent quantum design. We also give an explicit Gauss-Legendre construction which leads to weighted spherical designs. These results provide a systematic way to determine spin-operator moments from finite coherent-state POVMs without full state tomography, with practical protocols for polarimetry and magnetometry. Presented construction can be extended to other compact symmetry groups.

Quantum Physics.title: Frustration-free control for quantum-state preparation: an exact first-passage theory
