Quantum Physics.summary: Local measurements and feedback can autonomously prepare and stabilize entangled many-body states. In frustration-free control, the target manifold is fixed by local constraints, whose violations are detected by measurement and removed by feedback. We develop an exact theory of this mechanism for Dicke states of $N_q$ qubits, which span the permutation-symmetric subspace with one Dicke state per magnetization sector. Local singlet projectors define the constraints and detect departures from permutation symmetry. The dynamics closes exactly on the span of the $N_q(N_q-1)/2$ singlet-pair projectors and maps onto a classical first-passage process: measurements move the pair endpoints, while feedback absorbs pairs on measured bonds. The closure reduces the exponentially large many-body Liouvillian to a generator of polynomial size, fully quantifying the preparation process. In one dimension we solve it in closed form. Its slowest rate, $Λ_{\rm pair}=2[1-\cos(π/N_q)]$ in units of the measurement rate, is the full Liouvillian gap. For any such scheme, the relaxation time is bounded below by the inverse fraction of pair configurations on which feedback acts; local feedback reaches $O(N_q)$ of $O(N_q^2)$ configurations and thus needs a time at least linear in $N_q$. A second exact closure gives the final state for any initial condition. Extensions to modified transport, restricted feedback, and physical errors yield an exact transport-to-absorber crossover, geometric preparation laws, and a bound on the stationary leakage. An exact second-moment closure determines the ensemble fluctuations: measurement noise is conserving, while feedback generates the shot noise of removal and correlations between pairs. Preparation, acceleration, robustness, and fluctuations are thus all governed by one exactly solvable process: the transport and absorption of local constraint violations.

Quantum Physics.title: Optimizer or physics? Machine-learning surrogates for collision-based preparation of multipartite entangled quantum states
Quantum Physics.summary: Repeated partial-SWAP collisions can prepare symmetric Dicke states, including the $W$ state, without measurement or postselection. The collision sequence uses only two global collision angles, and its fidelity is evaluated after a final layer of local phase rotations is optimized numerically, so each candidate pair requires a many-qubit simulation and a phase fit. We study when learned surrogates reduce the number of such evaluations, and what limits the best-found fidelity, for 65 Dicke targets with 11--20 qubits in noiseless simulations. At 50 evaluations per target, Gaussian-process Bayesian optimization (GP-BO) exceeds fixed Sobol and grid designs by 0.088 and 0.063 in mean best-found fidelity. Bounded Nelder--Mead reaches 0.760 against 0.762 for GP-BO, and has the higher three-seed mean on 41 of the 61 targets with a reference value; in this two-parameter problem, adaptivity matters far more than the choice between the two methods. A neural-network ensemble pretrained on 750 observations from smaller systems needs 32\% fewer new evaluations per target than GP-BO at comparable fidelity, but the full neural search takes 1.6 times the wall time of GP-BO in our implementation. In a separate source-only test, the best of five neural proposals per target exceeds the best of five population-model proposals by 0.070 in mean fidelity. Exact symmetries and state diagnostics help explain why the leading adaptive methods reach similar family-mean fidelities. The collisions conserve the magnitude of the bare Dicke overlap and the total-spin weights, and for the best controls on a 12-target diagnostic panel, 79% of the infidelity is an amplitude deficit that a final phase layer cannot remove, which motivates interleaved phase control.

Quantum Physics.title: Chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing via flux-mediated transmon mechanical coupling: Theory and device requirements
Quantum Physics.summary: Measurements of local gravitational acceleration support geophysics and inertial navigation. We develop a circuit-level model of a chip-integrated superconducting gravimetric sensing head that longitudinally couples a nanomechanical beam in a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) loop to an independently flux-biased transmon. The interaction encodes changes in gravitational acceleration in the qubit Ramsey phase. We derive the phase response and evaluate the quantum Fisher information of the reduced qubit state and the classical Fisher information accessible through Ramsey readout. The model includes qubit relaxation and dephasing, mechanical damping, flux noise, readout infidelity, and cycle overhead. With other model inputs fixed, the competition between phase gain and responsivity-dependent decoherence yields a finite optimal transmon frequency responsivity to mechanical-loop flux. The decoherence model includes dephasing from low-frequency flux noise in the mechanical SQUID loop and coupling-dependent qubit dephasing from the mechanical bath. For the prospective integrated-device parameter set, Ramsey readout at the first mechanical revival gives a conditional projection of the sensing head's sensitivity of $1.1\times10^{-5}$ m s$^{-2}$ Hz$^{-1/2}$ at an interrogation time of 10.0 $μ$s. This estimate uses the single-cycle-equivalent Fisher-information rate for statistically independent cycles. A separate analysis identifies the joint mechanical, circuit, flux-noise, coherence, timing, and readout parameters needed within the model to reach $10^{-6}$-class internal sensitivity. These results specify the design tradeoffs and component requirements for Ramsey gravimetry in the proposed SQUID-transmon electromechanical sensing head.

Quantum Physics.title: Approximation of Semigroups of Random Processes on a Hilbert Space
Quantum Physics.summary: This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous semigroups of operators arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. The main focus is on applying Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The justification of the passage from discrete quantum measurements to continuous ones depends essentially on the choice of topology and function spaces. We propose conditions for convergence to bi-continuous semigroups on subspaces that weaken the classical requirements of the Chernoff theorem. The existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup is established in each of the three cases: commutation of the approximating operators, their asymptotic commutation, and uniform convergence of difference quotients over a family of approximating operators. For diffusive models with a generator having bounded coefficients, the derivative of the approximating function is computed explicitly on the subspace of test functions with rapidly decreasing second derivative; the limitations of applicability of this result are discussed. Applications to generalized models of continuous imprecise quantum measurement with unbounded observables, as well as to Poisson and diffusion processes, are outlined as directions for further research.

Quantum Physics.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. For reversible local binary-spin dynamics, we establish volume-uniform $O(\varepsilon)$-$L^2(π)$ approximation bounds for local observable dynamics using connected-cluster spaces with neighborhood radius $O(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ and cluster order $O(\log^2(1/\varepsilon))$. We further establish error bounds for repeated one-step propagation using exact moment matrices and their sparse-plus-rank-one compressions, uniformly in the time step and number of iterations.

Quantum Physics.title: Entropic Uncertainty Relations for Mutually Unbiased Operator Frames
Quantum Physics.summary: We develop an operator-frame formulation of entropic uncertainty relations in the Hilbert-Schmidt space of operators. For general continuous indexed operator frames, we derive an entropic uncertainty relation for the associated coefficient distributions by combining endpoint norm estimates with Riesz-Thorin interpolation. We then identify a distinguished class of mutually unbiased operator frames, defined through constant-modulus trace overlaps. Under suitable structural conditions, the corresponding coefficient amplitudes are related by a bilinear Fourier transform, leading to a stronger Hirschman-Beckner-type entropic uncertainty relation. As canonical realizations, we consider Weyl displacement operators and Wigner kernels, as well as Cartesian dyadic frames generated by position and momentum eigenstates. These examples recover familiar continuous-variable Fourier dualities while extending entropic uncertainty relations beyond measurement outcomes to operator representations themselves.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings
Quantum Physics.summary: States prepared in laboratory experiments are generally mixed because of imperfect preparation and residual coupling to the environment, whereas pure initial states represent an idealized limit. Motivated by this distinction, we investigate quantum entanglement and coherence in a pair of Unruh-DeWitt detectors initially prepared in a general two-qubit X state. One detector remains inertial and uncoupled, while the other undergoes uniform acceleration and interacts locally with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We obtain the reduced detector state within a perturbative treatment and evaluate its concurrence, $l_1$ norm of coherence, and relative entropy of coherence. For the initial-state families considered, the resulting expressions exhibit entanglement sudden death at finite acceleration, with larger initial entanglement associated with a higher threshold. Both coherence measures remain nonzero beyond this threshold and approach zero in the formal infinite-acceleration limit of these expressions. We also examine the dependence of these resources on the detector energy gap and interaction duration. The results distinguish the persistence of coherence from that of entanglement in the mixed-state detector model and identify initial mixedness as a relevant ingredient in relativistic quantum information.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Geometric Tensor in Parameter-Dependent Quasi-Hermitian Systems
Quantum Physics.summary: A parameter-dependent physical inner product makes the comparison of quantum states at different parameter points non-unique. We formulate two geometric prescriptions for this comparison in quasi-Hermitian systems. The Type I QGT is defined by an inner-product-compatible covariant derivative and horizontal projection. It is a Hermitian, positive-semidefinite Gram tensor, and, for any normalized solution of the inner-product-preserving dynamics, its tangential component equals the physical energy variance. The Type II QGT is constructed from the endpoint overlap of physical dual states and is invariant under local $GL(1,\mathbb{C})$ rescalings. We show that, on a normalized section, it coincides with the established left--right (LR) QGT, while providing an endpoint-overlap interpretation of that tensor. Our central result is an exact relation between the two constructions: in the positive Dyson frame, the Type I QGT is the positive Gram block of the dressed-derivative sector, while the real symmetric part of the Type II QGT is this metric minus a positive-semidefinite contribution from the metric connection; the full complex tensor also contains cross terms. This relation clarifies the origin of the possible indefiniteness of the Type II metric and separates it from the positivity of the physical Hilbert-space metric. We further distinguish instantaneous Dyson mappings from the fixed inner-product-preserving dynamics and characterize the conditions under which the corresponding QGTs agree. Three two-level models illustrate these results. The physical content of the two tensors is then identified through the energy uncertainty and evolution speed for Type I, and the symmetrized endpoint overlap, complex holonomy, and signed dynamical response for Type II.

Quantum Physics.title: Constraint-Preserving Quantum Circuit Compilation for Graph Independent Sets via Persistent Occupancy Encoding
Quantum Physics.summary: Constraint-preserving mixers for graph independent sets repeatedly evaluate overlapping neighborhood conditions, increasing CX costs across ordered quantum optimization circuits. We propose a structure-aware compiler that reuses these conditions through persistent occupancy encoding. Exploiting mutual exclusion within true-twin classes, our reversible encoding stores class occupancy on the original data register across mixer operations and cost layers. Local mixers are synthesized using target compensation, blockwise parity queries, and coherent restoration; nonuniform cost phases are preserved by an exact coefficient transformation. We prove that the compiled circuit reproduces the original program's unitary action on the feasible subspace for any prescribed operation order and independent layer parameters, and establish exact separability of source-level caching costs under a fixed synthesis recipe. Across 134 evaluation programs and 72 independent confirmation programs, total CX counts fall by 22.61% and 19.87%, respectively, relative to the best of six reference implementations selected per program. Against a matched no-cache implementation, persistent encoding yields additional reductions of 4.10% and 9.13%.

Quantum Physics.title: Electrical-Circuit Simulation of the Uhlmann Phase
Quantum Physics.summary: The Uhlmann phase extends the concept of geometric phases to mixed quantum states through a parallel-transport condition on purification amplitudes, but its experimental realization has so far required sophisticated quantum platforms with carefully engineered auxiliary degrees of freedom. In this work, we reformulate the Uhlmann parallel-transport condition as a linear matrix differential equation and vectorize it to obtain an effective dynamical generator. This generator can be directly mapped onto the admittance matrix of a classical RC circuit, thereby translating the Uhlmann dynamics into the evolution of circuit node voltages. We illustrate the mapping using the equatorial-loop model and, via a rotating-frame transformation followed by a real decomposition, derive a time-independent, real-valued dynamical system suitable for analog implementation. LTspice simulations of the resulting active RC network faithfully reproduce the Uhlmann geometric phase and its topological transition at the critical purity, demonstrating that classical electrical circuits offer a simple and accessible platform for probing mixed-state geometric phases.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum aspects of the classical Maxwell's equations in free space from the perspective of the generalised correspondence principle
Quantum Physics.summary: Due to the advent of Quantum Mechanics' 100th anniversary in 2025, we wrote this review paper in order to present a discussion that addresses the foundations of this theory. And since the creation of this Mechanics and other quantum theories was guided, for instance, by correspondence principles that needed to be identified between them and other well-established physical theories, this paper will be devoted to discussing the correspondence between Quantum Mechanics and Maxwell's theory of electromagnetism. More precisely, what we will do throughout this paper is discuss how the Maxwell's electromagnetic theory in free space and the generalised formulation of the correspondence principle already pointed, together, to the basis of a Quantum Mechanics that would only be formulated half a century later. And, in order to make this very clear, we will show that the quantum-mechanical description of a photon can already be identified, simply, by manipulating Maxwell's equations in free space with mathematical resources that, for instance, were already well known before the advent of Quantum Mechanics.

Quantum Physics.title: Where to Hide the Traps: Robust Placement in Verifiable Blind Quantum Computation
Quantum Physics.summary: Trap-based verification of blind quantum computation hides test qubits among the positions of a measurement pattern, and existing protocols choose the trap configuration without regard to the delegated computation. We model trap placement as a zero-sum game between a client, who chooses a trap distribution, and a server, who chooses where to apply a Pauli deviation, with a damage profile $w$ and a per-trap detection constant $c$. Since the client cannot know how damage from several positions combines, we solve the game for all monotone subadditive damage functions consistent with $w$ at once. In a single round, placing traps in proportion to $w$ guarantees soundness error $1-c/\|w\|_1$ and is optimal up to a factor $1+\max_iw_i$, while the optimistic solution can fail completely. Over $T$ test rounds, the error decays exponentially against a server that repeats the same deviation, but a general server can keep it at $Θ(\|w\|_1/(cT))$, and against such servers the damage-weighted placement is exactly optimal. Damage profiles follow from the flow of the pattern: for brickwork patterns with $m=4h+1$ columns, only $(2h+1)^2$ positions can affect a decision qubit, whatever the width. With $k$ traps per round, placing them on this set reduces the number of test rounds by the same factor as for a single trap; with unrestricted trap sets and flat damage we recover the known optimality of fractional coloring. Finally, trap statistics certify the aggregate damage with a number of rounds independent of the number of positions $N$, whereas locating the damage requires $Ω(Nε^{-2}\logδ^{-1})$ rounds.

Quantum Physics.title: Transverse momentum as the counter-diabatic generator in bent waveguide couplers
Quantum Physics.summary: Axis bending of a mode-evolution coupler realizes the counter-diabatic (CD) protocol [Opt. Express 34, 1214 (2026)]. We identify the operator responsible. Rigid lateral displacement is generated by the transverse momentum $\hat p_x$, which in a real two-mode supermode basis is purely $σ_y$: exactly the form of the CD term, and the one form that detuning and coupling cannot supply. Equating the two gives the axis slope in closed form, as a ratio of two matrix elements at a single cross section, or $\dot{x}_0=\dotθ/(γΔβ^{2})$ in coupled-mode variables. It agrees with a numerical offset search to 0.3% and is shown to be the earlier curvature condition viewed from the Kramers-Henneberger frame. Beam propagation simulations compare the bent coupler directly with the unitary-transformation realization built from the same reference structure: the two reach supermode fidelities of 0.994 and 1.000 against 0.886 for the untreated coupler, show comparable bandwidth and fabrication tolerance, and differ inside the device by the frame transformation that relates them.
Quantum Physics.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures. v2: revised version, with a comparison of the devices against device length (Fig. 7) and an expanded discussion

Quantum Physics.title: Undecidable quantum storage: no algorithm can tell from the noise rate whether a fixed circuit remembers
Quantum Physics.summary: Below a threshold noise rate, error correction lets larger quantum memories store a qubit for longer, without limit. Can the noise rate alone tell us whether a given noisy circuit does this? We construct fixed local circuits for which no algorithm can, already in one dimension under single-qubit noise. Each circuit is translation-invariant and time-periodic, with depolarizing noise on every wire after every layer, including all classical control. A computable list of disjoint rate intervals is indexed by the inputs $n$ of a universal Turing machine; local noise statistics select the input that the circuit simulates, and halting triggers erasure. If the machine runs forever on $n$, a qubit is stored throughout the $n$-th interval at entanglement fidelity at least $15/16$ for a time that grows without bound with size: linearly on rings, exponentially in six dimensions. The encoding and decoding maps are noiseless and global; they depend on $n$, the system size and, for decoding, the time, but not on the rate. If it halts, the fidelity of every encoding falls below $1/2+η$, for any fixed $η>0$, after a time independent of size and rate. The labels of the intervals with unbounded storage form a $Π^0_1$-complete set, and intervals of both kinds accumulate at zero, so these circuits have no noise threshold. Without rate selection, the ring construction is a translation-invariant, time-periodic memory: from an initialized classical hierarchy it stores a qubit for a time linear in the ring length at every sufficiently small rate, addressing the memory part of a one-dimensional question raised by Dünnweber, Styliaris and Trivedi. These are existence results: registers and interaction ranges are very large and the rates astronomically small.
Quantum Physics.comment: 177 pages, 4 figures, 13 tables. Archive and Lean sources: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24254845

Quantum Physics.title: Single-Phonon-Gated Pair Charging of Quantum Batteries
Quantum Physics.summary: Charging a quantum battery requires both an energy source and access to a channel through which that energy can be transferred. If that access depends on a quantum state, charging becomes conditional on the state while the external controls remain unchanged. We show that a single phonon in a common mechanical mode enables a second-order resonant pair transition in a two-cell battery formed by the electronic spins of two nitrogen-vacancy centers, whereas the mechanical vacuum supports no corresponding resonance. At fixed controls and mean phonon number, the final stored energy and ergotropy reached with a one-phonon Fock state are unattainable with any classical mixture of coherent states. An energy balance shows that the microwave drives supply nearly all of the stored energy, while the phonon contributes only a small fraction. Our results open a route to quantum-state-conditioned charging in quantum batteries under experimentally feasible parameters.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A Majorana Relativistic Quantum Spectral Approach to the Riemann Hypothesis in (1+1)-Dimensional Rindler Spacetimes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a Hilbert--Pólya approach to the Riemann zeta function via a Mellin--Barnes integral for massive Majorana modes in $(1+1)$-dimensional Rindler spacetime. The boost spectrum is continuous on the full wedge and discrete with a reflecting wall. Summing positive momentum modes on a transverse circle yields $ζ(2s)$ in the radial Mellin transform. Building on our one-sided Cesàro criterion for additive correlations of $Λ(n)-1$, we assign each prime $p$ a chiral channel of optical length $\tfrac12\log p$. Its $k$th return at $u=k\log p$ carries weight $\log p$. The centered correlation obeys $C(u)\le C(0)$ for all real $u$ exactly when the Riemann hypothesis (RH) holds. For a Majorana oscillator with linear mass profile, a bounded self-adjoint function of its Hamiltonian assigns period $kT_1$ to mode pair $k$. The first $n$ pairs have least common period $T_n=T_1\operatorname{lcm}(1,\ldots,n)$, so $\log(T_n/T_{n-1})=Λ(n)$ for $n\ge2$. Set $m=\lceil\sqrt{x}\rceil$, $N=\lfloor mx\rfloor$, and $ψ(y)=\sum_{n\le y}Λ(n)$. The signed revival mean $A(x)=m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{m-1}(N/j-ψ(N/j))$ satisfies $A(x)=R(x)+o(\sqrt{x})$, where $R(x)=\sum_{n\le x}Λ(n)(x/n-1)-x\log x+(1+γ_{\mathrm E})x$. At each zeta zero $ρ$ of multiplicity $d$ with $\Re(ρ)>1/2$, the meromorphic continuation of $\int_2^\infty A(x)x^{-s-1}\,dx$ has a simple pole of residue $d/[ρ(1-ρ)]$. For fixed $λ>1$, $1/2<θ<\Re(ρ)$ and $K>0$, the Kaczorowski--Pintz theorem gives $A(x)>Kx^θ$ at some $x\in[Y,Y^λ]$ for all large $Y$. Thus RH follows if for each $\varepsilon>0$ there is a $C_\varepsilon$ with $A(x)\le C_\varepsilon x^{1/2+\varepsilon}$ throughout $[Y,Y^λ]$ for arbitrarily large $Y$. For $λ=3/2$, the independent theta-lift estimate reported by Alpöge and Claude for $G=R$ gives this bound for $A$.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Compactification and non-zero density in (2+1)-dimensional four-fermion model
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The phase diagram of (2+1)-dimensional NJL type model has been studied with one compact dimension. The effect of compactification and fermion density on the chiral symmetry breaking is considered for periodic boundary conditions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: short letter to be published in Physics of Atomic Nuclei

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We establish a geometric framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms that are beyond standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. We also propose a generalized class Chern character and three conjectures: (i) the finite dimensionality of independent couplings at fixed derivative order, (ii) the representation of all-order mixed RR-gauge-scalar interactions through finitely many effective even forms, and (iii) the generation of higher-derivative contact terms from finitely many primitive tensor structures. Our framework provides a systematic mathematical foundation for reconstructing D-brane effective actions and exploring their underlying geometric and cohomological structures. We also introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity and their constraints.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: V2: Various references added, explanations and clarifications on several sections are carried out, 22 pages, no figure, Latex File

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A single field inflationary model consistent with recent observations: reheating and radiative stability
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study single field inflation with the inverse exponential potential, which has one free parameter besides the energy scale. For a wide range of parameter space, its predictions for the scalar spectral index and the tensor to scalar ratio lie within the $1σ$ region of the combined SPA$+$BK$+$DESI data, and the wider family of inverse power law exponential potentials behaves similarly. We compare these predictions with those of the $R^2$ model, monomial potentials, $α$-attractors, non-minimally coupled Higgs like inflation and a radiatively corrected plateau potential. The $R^2$ and monomial predictions lie near or outside the $2σ$ boundary of the same data, whereas the non-minimally coupled Higgs like and radiatively corrected plateau families overlap the favoured contours over part of their parameter space. To describe reheating, we add a steep exponential term that is negligible during inflation and, together with the inverse exponential term, creates a minimum about which the inflaton oscillates. The maximum reheating temperatures are $T_{\rm rh}\sim10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,{\rm GeV}$, consistent with the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis bound. Coupling the inflaton to a Dirac fermion through a Yukawa interaction, these temperatures require couplings comparable to the standard model charged lepton Yukawa couplings. Nonperturbative fermion production transfers negligible energy, and perturbative decay completes reheating. The same coupling induces a one loop correction to the inflationary potential, which limits the radiatively safe reheating temperature to $T_{\rm rh}\lesssim10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 16 pages, 1 table, 14 figures, enhanced analysis and title updated accordingly

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction ξof the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming ξ\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 37 pages, 10 figures, some changes to the text, added references

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Algebraic versus physical uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We give explicit determinant counterexamples to the uniqueness of MHV gravity numerators from their degrees and simultaneous pair zeros. At seven points the solution space has dimension seven; Bose symmetry removes six directions and leaves the Hodges line. At eight points a two-dimensional Bose-symmetric space remains. Regular integer-spinor configurations distinguish these deformations from the Hodges numerator. On the eight-point plane, collinear factorization, the leading positive-helicity soft coefficient and ordinary BCFW decay each select the Hodges line. For $n\ge5$, we prove two results on the full fixed-degree, common-denominator ansatz, without pair-zero conditions. Complete collinear residue functions on all pairs determine at most one numerator; Bose symmetry makes one channel sufficient. The splitting law and a normalized lower-point amplitude supply the boundary function, starting from an explicit five-point seed. With Bose symmetry, $O(Z^{-1})$ decay under one fixed same-helicity shift at generic conserving kinematics also selects the Hodges line. Normalized collinear and soft data fix the eight-point scale; the homogeneous shift condition leaves one constant per multiplicity.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 44 pages, Reproducibility materials and a Lean 4 companion are available at https://github.com/ybzhang-nxu/autoNMHV

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $ξ$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $ξ$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 24 pages, one figure, Submission to SciPost

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Lie Algebra Cohomology and Seiberg-Witten Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the algebra of perturbative holomorphic-topological local operators of pure $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theory with gauge group $SU(2)$, proving a conjecture of the author: it is the Poisson vertex algebra generated by a Virasoro element $X$ of central charge zero and an odd primary $Y$ of weight three, subject only to $X^2=0$. Equivalently, we compute the relative Lie algebra cohomology $H^*(\mathfrak{sl}_2[z,w]/(w^2),\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and the self-Ext groups of the unit in the coherent Satake category for $SL_2$ and $PGL_2$. The proof uses factorization on configuration spaces of points on the affine line, a depth argument, and two deformations of the coefficient algebra $\mathbb C[z,w]/(w^2)$.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Bounds on entanglement fluctuations at holographic interfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: How small can entanglement fluctuations be at fixed entropy? For a class of holographic conformal interfaces supported by a scalar with a potential, we prove $c_\text{eff}\leq c_\text{cap}\leq c_\text{eff}^2/c_{LR}$, relating entropy, capacity, and energy transmission. The coupled gravitational response is a transport term minus a positive scalar contribution; the background Einstein equation bounds that subtraction. A long Janus throat allows unbounded capacity at a finite entropy coefficient while the scalar response remains gapped.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Infrared finite scattering theory: Non-relativistic Coulomb scattering
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We revisit non-relativistic quantum-mechanical scattering in a Coulomb potential. The long-range nature of the interaction leads to divergent integrals in conventional S-matrix calculations using the Born series. Dollard showed that a well-defined scattering operator can be constructed by replacing the free Hamiltonian $ H_0 $ with an appropriate asymptotic Hamiltonian $ H_{\rm D} $. However, explicit perturbative calculations within Dollard's framework have remained scarce. We develop a perturbative formulation of the Dollard scattering operator in which the Coulomb divergences cancel to all orders. Perturbatively, we demonstrate this cancellation explicitly through second Born order and show that the resulting amplitude reproduces the known exact distributional Coulomb amplitude, including its forward-scattering contribution. With the aim of generalizing our analysis to quantum field theory, we reformulate the problem in the Heisenberg picture. We construct a new set of canonical variables through a time-dependent canonical transformation that removes the logarithmic Coulomb correction from the asymptotic phase-space coordinates. Using these variables, we construct the corresponding Heisenberg S-matrix through several complementary approaches. This leads to a formulation of the Lehmann--Symanzik--Zimmermann (LSZ) reduction formalism adapted to the modified asymptotic dynamics, which we relate to the Dollard scattering operator. This construction provides a framework for extending the LSZ formalism to infrared divergences in relativistic quantum field theories with long-range interactions and massless fields.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A note on Holographic Renormalization for Polarized IKKT
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a boundary counterterm for the on-shell action of type IIB supergravity solutions dual to vacua of the polarized IKKT matrix model. The construction is based on the variational principle, with off-shell fluctuations whose fall-off conditions are based on the asymptotic equations of motion. The renormalized on-shell action of the supersymmetric saddles reproduces the matrix- model result once we pass to the ensemble of fixed D1-brane charges, which we implement off-shell by dualizing the RR two-form potential.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Scattering amplitudes in AdS$_5\times$ S$^5$ from the pure spinor superstring
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We formulate a BRST-invariant prescription for the integration of zero modes in the pure spinor superstring on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The measure includes contributions absent in flat space and admits a description in terms of picture changing operators or a non-minimal regulator. The prescription is valid for genus-zero amplitudes with arbitrary multiplicity and external states and removes a central obstacle to amplitude computations in this background. We use it to perform the first direct worldsheet computation of two and three-point amplitudes of half-BPS supergravity states. The properly normalised three-point amplitudes exactly reproduce the results of planar ${\mathcal N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The AdS/$\mathsf{C}$-$\mathsf{P}$-${\mathsf T}$ Correspondence
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the realization of $\mathsf{C}$, $\mathsf{P}$, $\mathsf{T}$ in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM -- corresponding to charge conjugation, parity, and time-reversal -- and identify the $\mathsf{C}$, $\mathsf{P}$, $\mathsf{T}$ global symmetries of ${\cal N}=4$ SYM with bulk (gauge) symmetries of string theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$. The dual bulk transformations are symmetries of Type IIB string theory on $AdS_5\times S^5$ that combine string worldsheet symmetries, with geometric transformations acting on $AdS_5\times S^5$. We show that $\mathsf P$ and $\mathsf T$ map to $\mathsf{CP}$ and $\mathsf{CT}$ under $S$-duality (combined with an $SU(4)$ R-symmetry outer automorphism),while $\mathsf C$ and $ \mathsf{CPT}$ are invariant. We define codimension-two charge conjugation monodromy defects in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM, which have an unusual large $N$ expansion, and discuss their bulk dual description. We elucidate the relation between symmetries on the string worldsheet and symmetries of target space string field theory, global vs gauge symmetries in quantum gravity, among related topics. Defects in ${\cal N}=4$ SYM and in quantum gravity play a central role in this work.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: latex, 54 pages; v2 Added more details and revised the discussion of charge-conjugation monodromy defects; v3 published

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 23 pages; minor corrections; additional details on the Pfaffian factorization of \(g_n\) and on GCD have been added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $γ$, scaling as $(2γ_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $γ_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2γ_{\mathrm{PPN}} - β_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $β$-$γ$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $σ_{2γ-β}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $σ_β\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $γ$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $σ_β\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $γ$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $σ_γ\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 15 pages (two columns), 4 tables, 2 figures.v2: title partially changed, discussion improved, references added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive the primordial $\langleζζh\rangle$, $\langleζhh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of photon statistics in strong gravitational fields and for non-comoving observers, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the relativistic Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order in the relaxation time. The results reveal novel phenomena absent in flat space. At second order, the gravitational field renders the transport coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse particle and energy fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect in electromagnetism. Using the first-order results, we derive the relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks around Schwarzschild black holes. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Matches the version published in PRD

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: BPS invariants from resurgent topological string
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We review recent progress on the conjectural relation between the resurgent structure of topological string free energies and BPS invariants of type II string theory compactified on the same Calabi-Yau threefold. In this picture, Borel singularities are located at integral periods associated with central charges of stable D-brane bound states, while Stokes constants encode their BPS indices, or generalized DT invariants. After introducing resurgence and perturbative topological strings, we explain how trans-series solutions of the holomorphic anomaly equations determine non-perturbative amplitudes and illustrate the proposed correspondence in local and compact geometries. We discuss the behavior under changes of polarization and moduli, and review supporting arguments based on exact WKB analysis, blowup equations, the Stokes automorphisms of flat coordinates and dual partition functions, and Kontsevich-Soibelman wall-crossing. We conclude with open questions concerning a general proof, the interpretation of non-perturbative amplitudes, and the construction of non-perturbative completions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 32 pages, 9 figures, proceedings to CY 50 conference, some typos corrected, funding information added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Symmetry resolved spread complexity for BMN matrix model
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the symmetry-resolved spread complexity of the Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase (BMN) matrix model under a global $U(1)$ symmetry acting within the transverse $SO(6)$ scalar sector. Decomposing the time-evolved charged thermofield double (cTFD) state into orthogonal fixed-charge sectors, we examine the return amplitude, spectral moments, tridiagonal Lanczos coefficients, and early-time spread complexity across the low-temperature confined ($βμ\gg 1$) and finite-temperature deconfined ($T \gg μ$) phases. In the low-temperature gapped regime, effective sector dynamics map onto decoupled, displaced harmonic oscillators with a Casimir-like zero-point offset, yielding factorized moments, linear drift in diagonal Lanczos coefficients $a_n^{(q)}$, and sub-linear $\sqrt{n}$ off-diagonal growth with thermally suppressed initial hopping. Charge-dependent Boltzmann weights, vacuum shifts, and degeneracies break complexity equipartition, while inter-sector coherence and charge dispersion enforce an early-time positivity bound $ΔC(t) = C_{\text{total}}(t) - \bar{C}(t) \ge 0$. In the \emph{finite}-temperature continuum phase, modeling the planar large-$N$ spectral density as a thermal Gaussian gives constant diagonal coefficients $a_n^{(q)} = \bar{E}_q$, universal square-root scaling $b_n^{(q)} = σ_E \sqrt{n}$, and a quadratic spread launch $\mathcal{C}^{(q)}(t) = σ_E^2(q,T)\,t^2 + \mathcal{O}(t^4)$ governed by the backreacted sector energy variance. Holographically, these regimes distinguish coherent string fluctuations in horizonless Lin-Maldacena (LM) droplet geometries from dissipative scrambling near charged ten-dimensional black D0-brane horizons.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Thermodynamics of QCD+QED from the lattice
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: QED corrections to observables in QCD are by now well-understood at zero temperature, where QED effects are perturbative and required for precision physics observables, such as the neutron-proton mass difference or the muon anomalous magnetic moment, among many others. However, there are indications in the literature that at finite temperature the introduction of QED can lead to non-perturbative effects, affecting the structure of the phase diagram, since the combined theory is exactly center-symmetric. In this proceedings article, we analyze the structure of the combined theory and the different strategies to simulate it on the lattice, as well as presenting novel results of lattice QCD+QED simulations at finite temperature, focusing on understanding the role of the electromagnetic coupling in the thermodynamics of this system. We also discuss new features that arise in the combined theory and the challenges that these simulations entail, which require the development of new algorithms in order to understand the phase diagram of QCD+QED from first principles.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, contribution to the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2026), July 26 - August 1 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time surprisal FT treats the complete channel, identifies the nonunital correction, and yields a GSL bound for unital dressed evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that does not mix distinct dressed-charge sectors and preserves the full dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The entropy bounds establish the GSL in a controlled slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Solving the Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields as a Dynamical Solution
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay-a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its efficacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Poisson-Lie T-duality and D-brane Configurations of $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ Backgrounds
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a non-Abelian dual pair for the $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ background via Poisson-Lie T-duality on a semi-Abelian double. Using a specific parameterization of the six-dimensional Lie group ${A}_2 \times {A}_2 \times A_2$, we formulate the original $σ$-model incorporating the $AdS_2 \times H^2 \times H^2$ metric with a vanishing Kalb-Ramond field ($B$-field), and derive its dual background, which features a non-vanishing $B$-field and a physical singularity. We investigate the conformal properties and test the generalized supergravity equations for the complete geometry; although a generalized Killing vector exists, the full background fails to satisfy these equations. We then analyze the asymptotic structure and coordinate domains, revealing distinct exterior and interior sectors separated by curvature-singular boundaries, alongside an asymptotic approach to the original background. Finally, we investigate the transformation of $D$-brane boundary conditions under Poisson-Lie T-duality for the semi-Abelian Drinfeld double $({\A}_2 \oplus {\A}_2 \oplus {\A}_2 , 6{\A}_1)$. By analyzing seven classes of gluing matrices, we examine the eigenvalue spectra, identify candidate dual D-brane configurations, and construct the corresponding Dirichlet and Neumann projectors. We also investigate the integrability of the Neumann distributions and determine the associated gauge-invariant two-forms and world-volume field strengths, providing a systematic framework for studying the geometric and boundary condition properties of the dual branes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Teleparallel formulation of $E_{8(8)}$ Exceptional Field Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The potential of $E_{8(8)} \times \mathbb{R}^+$ exceptional field theory, suited for studying three-dimensional maximally supersymmetric compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, is derived in teleparallel formulation. This means that, starting from an ansatz of the most general combination of the quadratic scalar contractions of the intrinsic torsion, which is manifestly invariant under generalised diffeomorphisms, one selects the potential by imposing the invariance under infinitesimal rotation of the maximal compact subgroup of the duality group. The teleparallel formulation makes manifest at geometric level the preeminent role of the intrinsic torsion in studying compactifications of higher-dimensional supergravities, where the intrinsic torsion is identified with the embedding tensor of the resulting gauged supergravity.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v2: 30+1 pages, typos corrected, extension added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Möbius Fusion Algebra
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Given a pseudo-unitary modular tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ with an anti-monoidal involution $\mathsf{P}$, we define a generally non-commutative algebra from this data, which we call the Möbius fusion algebra $\mathfrak{M}$ of $(\mathcal{C},\mathsf{P})$, in terms of ribbon graphs drawn on the Möbius band, where the orientation-reversal of the Möbius band acts on the graphs by $\mathsf{P}$. We show that this algebra is semisimple, and give a formula for the dimensions of its simple modules, in terms of the modular $S$-matrix of $\mathcal{C}$ and a certain set of quantities extracted from the action of $\mathsf{P}$. This formula is expected to play the role of a non-orientable analogue of the Verlinde formula, in the context of Reshetikhin-Turaev-type topological quantum field theories on non-orientable manifolds.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 65 pages, many figures. Animated versions of the proofs of Propositions 4.23 and 5.6 are available at https://ippo0127.github.io/movies/mobius_prop4_23.html and https://ippo0127.github.io/movies/mobius_prop5_6.html

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Propagation and horizon formation in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet scalar collapse. I. Characteristic conditions, bounds and formation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study scalar collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling as an exact classical theory. On spherical scalar backgrounds, gravitational characteristic conditions reduce to inequalities in two local invariants. In five dimensions, they imply $R_h^2>\tildeα$ for regular marginal spheres on the GR branch and the sharp Kretschmann bound $\tildeα^2\mathcal R_{abcd}\mathcal R^{abcd}<28$ for nonnegative mass. Under the stated finite-domain hypotheses, spherical continuation places the first characteristic degeneration on a smooth background. Within this setting, a future marginal sphere formed while the characteristic conditions hold throughout the preceding evolution forces their later failure. For every allowed radius, separately chosen complete smooth data form marginal spheres with mass arbitrarily close to the sharp lower bound; in six dimensions both radius and mass can be arbitrarily small. At sufficiently large scale, complete nonspherical data with weak curvature contain marginal surfaces with prescribed $S^3$ metrics under a spectral condition. These surfaces are outermost and strictly stable. A separate Berger family has arbitrarily small area at one common ADM mass; formation from untrapped data remains open. Exact nonspherical developments have smoothly convergent initial data but tidal tensors that fail to converge to the reference values at a chosen time after the reference core loses hyperbolicity. Under local geometric uniqueness for developments of the same data on overlaps connecting the initial slice to the observers, classical existence on a common region and continuous dependence of the tidal tensor cannot both hold. The constructed solutions themselves extend smoothly. Fixed time averages converge on the controlled interval, but this does not establish a predictive effective-field-theory continuation.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analytical Solution of Spinning, Eccentric Binary Black Hole Dynamics at the Second Post-Newtonian Order
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Recent gravitational wave (GW) detections showing signatures of eccentricity and spin precession underscore the need to model binary black holes (BBHs) possessing these features simultaneously. Most efforts over the past fifteen years to model spinning BBHs and their corresponding GWs have relied on heuristically twisting waveforms from nonprecessing systems. This approach is based on empirical observations rather than first principles. This article aims to model the dynamics of spinning and eccentric BBHs from a first-principles approach using the post-Newtonian (PN) approximation within general relativity. Building on the already-existing 1.5PN solution, we construct an analytical solution for the time evolution of the relative separation vector, the individual black hole spin vectors, and the orbital angular momentum vector at 2PN order for BBHs with arbitrary spins and eccentricity. Such a solution is not fully 2PN accurate in that the tiny orbital timescale fluctuations in the solutions for the spins are only leading 1.5PN order accurate, instead of 2PN. However, it is shown that our new 2PN solution is still an order of magnitude improvement over the earlier 1.5PN solution, underlining the subdominant nature of the neglected next-to-leading-order oscillations in the spin solutions.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 41 pages, 5 figures; v4: Mathematica notebook (.nb) and package (.m) provided as ancillary files

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Classification of Chern-Simons Couplings and Deformed Pull-Backs on D-Branes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We establish a geometric framework for classifying higher-derivative Ramond-Ramond (RR) couplings on Dp-branes, focusing on the complete scattering amplitude of a closed-string RR state, a gauge field, and two transverse scalars. The low-energy expansion reveals infinite massless poles and local interaction terms that are beyond standard Myers and Taylor expansions. We propose a higher-class deformation of the pullback using mixed Chern-Simons transgression operators to address these complexities. We also propose a generalized class Chern character and three conjectures: (i) the finite dimensionality of independent couplings at fixed derivative order, (ii) the representation of all-order mixed RR-gauge-scalar interactions through finitely many effective even forms, and (iii) the generation of higher-derivative contact terms from finitely many primitive tensor structures. Our framework provides a systematic mathematical foundation for reconstructing D-brane effective actions and exploring their underlying geometric and cohomological structures. We also introduce a higher-class pullback operator \( P_{\infty} \) and mixed transgression operators \( \mathcal{T}_{\infty} \), emphasizing amplitude-derived pole residues and local contact terms as key physical data. This formalism distinguishes admissible tensor structures, presenting characteristic-form aspects as conjectures alongside their validity and their constraints.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: V2: Various references added, explanations and clarifications on several sections are carried out, 22 pages, no figure, Latex File

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A single field inflationary model consistent with recent observations: reheating and radiative stability
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study single field inflation with the inverse exponential potential, which has one free parameter besides the energy scale. For a wide range of parameter space, its predictions for the scalar spectral index and the tensor to scalar ratio lie within the $1σ$ region of the combined SPA$+$BK$+$DESI data, and the wider family of inverse power law exponential potentials behaves similarly. We compare these predictions with those of the $R^2$ model, monomial potentials, $α$-attractors, non-minimally coupled Higgs like inflation and a radiatively corrected plateau potential. The $R^2$ and monomial predictions lie near or outside the $2σ$ boundary of the same data, whereas the non-minimally coupled Higgs like and radiatively corrected plateau families overlap the favoured contours over part of their parameter space. To describe reheating, we add a steep exponential term that is negligible during inflation and, together with the inverse exponential term, creates a minimum about which the inflaton oscillates. The maximum reheating temperatures are $T_{\rm rh}\sim10^{12}$--$10^{13}\,{\rm GeV}$, consistent with the Big Bang Nucleosynthesis bound. Coupling the inflaton to a Dirac fermion through a Yukawa interaction, these temperatures require couplings comparable to the standard model charged lepton Yukawa couplings. Nonperturbative fermion production transfers negligible energy, and perturbative decay completes reheating. The same coupling induces a one loop correction to the inflationary potential, which limits the radiatively safe reheating temperature to $T_{\rm rh}\lesssim10^{12}\,{\rm GeV}$.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 16 pages, 1 table, 14 figures, enhanced analysis and title updated accordingly

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction ξof the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming ξ\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 37 pages, 10 figures, some changes to the text, added references

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Observational constraints on early time non-phantom behaviour of dynamical dark energy
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate dynamical dark energy models in which the scalar field component is non-phantom at early times. The models include a single-exponential thawing field, a double-exponential scaling--thawing field, and extensions in which a steep exponential scaling field is combined with a cosmological constant, a constant-$w$ fluid, or a CPL fluid. We confront them with Planck PR4 CMB temperature, polarisation and lensing data, DESI DR2 BAO measurements and the Pantheon$+$ supernova sample. The background parameters are stable across all models, with $H_0 \simeq 67.7$--$68.3\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, so none of the models relieves the Hubble tension. The CPL parametrization prefers $w_0>-1$ and $w_a<0$ at $\sim\!2.7σ$ relative to $Λ$CDM, corresponding to phantom behaviour at low redshift. The constant-$w$ and thawing models remain consistent with a cosmological constant. When an early scaling phase is added, the data limit the peak early dark energy fraction to $f_{\mathrm{EDE}}<0.0075$ ($f_{\mathrm{EDE}}<0.015$ for SC$+$CPL). This requires a steep potential, $λ_2 \gtrsim 30$, and keeps the scalar-field density below the half-percent level at matter--radiation equality. Early scaling dynamics therefore cannot alter the sound horizon enough to address the Hubble tension. The scaling models fit the data as well as $Λ$CDM ($Δχ^2_{\mathrm{min}}\lesssim 1.4$), but they are disfavoured by AIC and BIC because of their additional, weakly constrained parameters. Adding a scaling field to CPL does not improve the fit. Late-time evolving dark energy is mildly preferred by the data, while a simple early scaling phase offers no benefit.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 13 pages, 2 tables, 7 figures, accepted in EPJC

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Deglobalising the fit: how to search for physics beyond vacuum General Relativity in LISA catalogues
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna will observe up to $\sim 10^{7}$ overlapping signals, which have to be characterised simultaneously with a \emph{global} fit. This is a challenge for model comparison since rerunning the global fit for every model of interest, including deviations from vacuum General Relativity, is computationally demanding. An alternative is a two-step post-processing strategy: a first global fit with vacuum models only, after which selected target sources are reanalysed under a different model with all other sources subtracted. We show that in this strategy a beyond-vacuum effect in a target source can be partly absorbed by the overlapping \textit{nuisance} sources in the first fit, subtracted with them, and never reach the reanalysis. In the linear-signal approximation, the loss in reported detection significance is captured by a single number, the \emph{masking ratio} $\mathcal{R}\in[0,1]$: a deviation the global fit would detect at $n_σ$ is reported by post-processing at $\mathcal{R}\,n_σ$, and, for a single beyond-vacuum parameter, bounds in null tests are reported too tight by the same factor. We show how to compute $\mathcal{R}$ from the posterior samples of the vacuum global fit, and give an algorithm that ranks the nuisance sources by how much of the effect each can absorb, so that only the most correlated ones need to be refitted with the target. We validate our method with full Markov-chain Monte Carlo inference on a toy model of 21 overlapping chirping sinusoids, one of which carries a small non-linear chirp that represents the missed physics. Using our post-processing recipe, we are able to recover the global-fit result on the beyond-vacuum parameter to within $0.15σ$ by refitting only 4 of the 20 nuisance sources. This method can serve as a basis for tests of General Relativity in realistic LISA mock datasets.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quadratic-in-spin scattering of compact bodies at fourth post-Minkowskian order
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present the fourth-post-Minkowskian scattering angle of aligned spinning compact bodies through quadratic spin at arbitrary velocity and mass ratio. We include spin-induced quadrupoles and radiation reaction, supplemented by curvature-squared spin-tidal terms. Three-loop worldline integrals yield closed forms in polylogarithms and elliptic integrals. Infrared poles cancel exactly, fixing the tail logarithm. We obtain a new post-Newtonian coefficient and third-order angular-momentum loss for general quadrupoles. The new input shifts resummed predictions for black-hole scattering.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: $p$-Harmonic gauge and the regularity of spacetime isometries
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show every Lorentzian metric of class $C^{k,α}$, where $k\in\mathbf{N}_0$ and $α\in(0,1)$, admits local coordinates of class $C^{k+1,α}$ all of whose coordinate functions are temporal functions that are harmonic with respect to a nonlinear $p$-wave operator, where $p\in(-\infty,1)$. Unlike the classical wave operator, this operator is elliptic on temporal functions. As an application, we show that an isometry between Lorentzian metrics of class $C^{k,α}$ is of class $C^{k+1,α}$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Viscous damping of axisymmetric oscillation modes of uniformly rotating relativistic stars
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the effects of bulk and shear viscosity on the damping of axisymmetric oscillations of uniformly rotating relativistic stars, using the first-order viscous hydrodynamics formulation of Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha and Kovtun (BDNK). The equations of motion are implemented in a two-dimensional numerical code under the Cowling approximation, assuming the fluid evolves on the fixed spacetime of a rotating star. We build two sequences of polytropic stellar models and investigate how damping depends on rotation rate (from the non-rotating case to the mass-shedding limit) and compactness. Our study focuses on the quasi-radial $l=0$ $F$ mode and the $l=1,2,3$ fundamental modes, covering a dataset of 288 perturbed stellar models. For all modes and chosen viscosities, the BDNK runs show that oscillations decay within a few milliseconds, much faster than in the perfect fluid case. The $F$ mode damping is dominated by bulk viscosity, consistent with its global compression of the star, while the $l=2$ and $l=3$ modes are mainly damped by shear viscosity. The $l=1$ mode is largely insensitive to both viscosity coefficients, and its decay rate is dominated by numerical dissipation. Rotation renders the $F$ mode sensitive to shear viscosity. Since the inherent numerical damping does not affect the slopes of the decay rates, our viscous sensitivity estimates faithfully identify the dominant damping mechanism for each mode, shear or bulk viscosity, and reveal robust trends with rotation rate and compactness.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Equivalence of mapping gravitational wave background anisotropy across bases at equal information content
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Mapping anisotropies in the gravitational-wave background (GWB) requires choosing a basis to represent the sky intensity, such as pixel and spherical harmonic bases. Each introduces a truncation---e.g., a number of pixels or a maximum multipole l_max---often set by a naive counting argument that relate the number of measurable modes to the number of independent cross-correlations, N_pair, in a pulsar timing array (PTA). However, such truncations can lead to reconstruction artifacts, as they do not reflect the true information content of the PTA response. Increasing the value of truncation parameters spans the observable space better but reveals poorly constrained modes, making the inverse problem ill conditioned and requiring regularization. A natural approach is to restrict the reconstruction to a well-measured subspace via principal maps, defined by the dominant eigenmodes of the detector response (or Fisher) matrix. However, these maps are not a fundamental parametrization of the sky but, rather, are derived from an underlying representation---such as a pixelization or a spherical harmonic expansion. While their explicit form depends on basis choice, they can span the \textit{same subspace} when the underlying representation is sufficiently complete. Here, we show that reconstructed anisotropy maps via different bases are equivalent, provided they retain the same information content, i.e., span the same principal subspace. As illustrative cases, we consider a toy model for PTA configuration and several GWB anisotropy shapes: point source, an extended source with deterministic anisotropy, and a statistical isotropic background, along with its summary statistic---the angular power spectrum. Although the reconstructions are equivalent, their computational costs can differ. We conclude with brief comments on the construction of principal maps for ground-based interferometers.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Scalar field perturbations in Non-commutative Schwarzschild spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: This work presents a comparative analysis of quasi-normal modes and ringdown profiles of scalar field perturbations in the non-commutative Schwarzschild black hole spacetime, focusing on two non-minimal curvature couplings: in the first, the scalar field is coupled to the Ricci scalar of the background geometry, while in the second, its derivatives are coupled to the Einstein tensor. Using the sixth-order WKB approximation and the time-domain integration method, the dynamical stability is investigated across the parameter space. It is shown that while the tensor model loses its hyperbolic evolution for large couplings, no physical instability is found within its well-posed regime. Moreover, an opposite \(\ell\)-dependence of the threshold couplings is identified between the two models. Finally, using the result of the scalar sector, a model-dependent length scale for the non-commutative parameter is estimated in the case of light primordial black holes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analytical Criteria for Potential-Well Formation in Non-Minimally Coupled Scalar-Tensor Theories: A Necessary Condition for Instability
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Although the existence of a potential-well does not necessarily imply instability, its formation is a necessary prerequisite for the existence of unstable bound states. We investigate the formation of an effective potential-well for scalar-field perturbations in two non-minimally coupled scalar-tensor theories, involving couplings to the Ricci scalar and the Einstein tensor. In the context of the near-horizon approximation, we derive an analytical expression for the threshold coupling in each model at which the extremum of the effective potential reaches the event horizon. We use this criterion for the stationary, spherically symmetric black holes in this paper, in particular for a number of regular black holes spacetimes. We examine the dependence of the threshold couplings on the scalar field mass, angular multipole number, and the background parameters. At this distinguished coupling, the real part of the near-horizon quasi-normal mode frequencies vanishes, yielding purely imaginary frequencies. We further demonstrate that the universal area spectrum of spherically symmetric black holes can be recovered from the near-horizon frequency spectrum without invoking the highly damped-mode approximation. Remarkably, this spectrum is independent of the specific non-minimal coupling scheme.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $γ$, scaling as $(2γ_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR).
