For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $γ_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2γ_{\mathrm{PPN}} - β_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $β$-$γ$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $σ_{2γ-β}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $σ_β\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $γ$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $σ_β\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $γ$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $σ_γ\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages (two columns), 4 tables, 2 figures.v2: title partially changed, discussion improved, references added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A tale of three points: mixed and tensor bispectra beyond leading order in Horndeski gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We derive the primordial $\langleζζh\rangle$, $\langleζhh\rangle$, and $\langle hhh\rangle$ bispectra in general Horndeski theory through first order in slow variation, retaining their complete momentum and helicity dependence. The calculation includes the time evolution of the cubic coefficients, the correction to the scale factor, the first-order scalar and tensor mode functions, and the corrected power-spectrum normalization. We verify the tensor-soft and scalar-soft Maldacena consistency relations at the same order. We also study finite squeezing and show that, when $c_S\neq c_T$, the relevant soft variable is the ratio $c_Tq/(c_Sk)$, leading to an acoustic crossover not captured by geometric squeezing alone. We construct the corresponding nonlinearity parameters and apply the general results to a nonsingular contracting model, in which the mixed bispectra retain sensitivity to the contraction parameter through the scalar propagation speed.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Covariant linear response theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: To overcome the failure of the conventional non-relativistic description of photon statistics in strong gravitational fields and for non-comoving observers, we develop a covariant theory for a photon gas in curved spacetime, starting from the relativistic Boltzmann equation and employing the relaxation time approximation. The transport coefficients are computed up to second order in the relaxation time. The results reveal novel phenomena absent in flat space. At second order, the gravitational field renders the transport coefficients tensor-valued and induces transverse particle and energy fluxes, analogous to the Hall effect in electromagnetism. Using the first-order results, we derive the relativistic generalizations of Fick's and Fourier's laws and obtain the radiation diffusion equation for spherically symmetric accretion disks around Schwarzschild black holes. This provides a covariant description of radiative transport in strong gravitational fields for high-energy astrophysical applications.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Matches the version published in PRD

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: How graviton mass shapes angular correlations in a relic gravitational-wave background
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A nonzero graviton mass makes waves emitted at the same epoch travel different distances at different momenta. A finite band therefore samples a shell that is both closer to the observer and thicker. We derive the distribution of source radii and use it to calculate the band angular-power ratio $C_\ell^{BB}(m_{\rm g})/C_\ell^{BB}(0)$ for a relic stochastic gravitational-wave background. For a common source field with a scale-invariant spatial spectrum, a thin shell has the same angular power at every radius. Radial averaging cannot exceed this power, so any suppression relative to the massless single-epoch spectrum is due to shell broadening. We also ask whether source mixing can mimic massive propagation across two frequency bands. For two independent emission episodes whose mixing fractions are fixed across multipoles, massless propagation requires the low-band auto-power and the cross-power, each normalized by the high-band auto-power, to lie on a straight line when plotted against one another. This holds for arbitrary angular spectra of the two sources. A massive benchmark near the low-band propagation threshold violates this relation. A joint massless fit with power-law sources nevertheless gives an rms logarithmic residual of $0.013$ over $2\leq\ell\leq10$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Birefringent Imaging and Interferometry with Periodic Orbits and Accretion in Einstein-nonlinear-electrodynamics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate birefringent imaging, interferometric visibility, neutral periodic geodesics, and thin-disk radiation around a magnetically charged black hole in Einstein-nonlinearelectrodynamics, using the Euler-Heisenberg-type model of de Paula et al. [14]. The nonlinear coupling is treated as a free model parameter. Two effective photon metrics give rise to distinct unstable light rings, capture thresholds, and images. Transforming their image-order intensities into signed Fourier visibilities reveals separate critical-curve oscillations and a narrow-ring modulation scale in the unresolved sum. This two-mode correspondence does not require photon motion between two potential barriers. Rational orbital frequencies are then used to classify neutral bound trajectories and provide conservative gravitationalwave snapshots relevant to extreme-mass-ratio inspirals. A stationary thin-disk calculation supplies flux, temperature, emitted efficiency, and polarization-resolved thermal spectra. Across the sampled parameters, magnetic charge dominates the changes, while matched Maxwell comparisons resolve smaller nonlinear corrections. The static, optically thin emitters and the orbiting, optically thick thermal disk are distinct source configurations. Polarization comparisons use the same material source within each configuration; their brightness and spectral results are conditional on that configuration.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Regge calculus for $f(R)$ gravity with torsion
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We formulate $f(R)$ gravity with spacetime torsion in Regge calculus, but without an \emph{ad hoc} geometric definition of torsion. Working in D'Adda's formulation of simplicial gravity with coordinates, we show that the axial sector of the torsion is carried by a massless Kalb--Ramond two-form, which in four dimensions is dual to a single scalar on the dual vertices. The discretized theory is therefore pure Regge gravity coupled to two scalar fields, the scalaron and the axion, without a geometric definition of torsion on the Regge lattice. We derive the lattice action and the complete set of discrete equations of motion, and we verify the continuum limit. For a homogeneous and isotropic lattice we obtain the discrete Friedmann--Raychaudhuri system, compute the exact kinetic and curvature coefficients for a regular triangulation of $\mathbb S^3$, and show that the discrete equations reproduce the continuum closed solution at first order in the evolution time step. The results therefore present a very special case in which the torsional effects are completely described by scalar fields on the Regge lattice and there is no need of a full discrete differential calculus.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state--operator duality. Using a gravitational charge as a quantum clock, we construct a modular crossed product with density operators whose trace entropy reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time surprisal FT treats the complete channel, identifies the nonunital correction, and yields a GSL bound for unital dressed evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that does not mix distinct dressed-charge sectors and preserves the full dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The entropy bounds establish the GSL in a controlled slow-clock limit and quantify finite-width clock corrections.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quantum coherence and entanglement of mixed states in relativistic settings
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: States prepared in laboratory experiments are generally mixed because of imperfect preparation and residual coupling to the environment, whereas pure initial states represent an idealized limit. Motivated by this distinction, we investigate quantum entanglement and coherence in a pair of Unruh-DeWitt detectors initially prepared in a general two-qubit X state. One detector remains inertial and uncoupled, while the other undergoes uniform acceleration and interacts locally with a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We obtain the reduced detector state within a perturbative treatment and evaluate its concurrence, $l_1$ norm of coherence, and relative entropy of coherence. For the initial-state families considered, the resulting expressions exhibit entanglement sudden death at finite acceleration, with larger initial entanglement associated with a higher threshold. Both coherence measures remain nonzero beyond this threshold and approach zero in the formal infinite-acceleration limit of these expressions. We also examine the dependence of these resources on the detector energy gap and interaction duration. The results distinguish the persistence of coherence from that of entanglement in the mixed-state detector model and identify initial mixedness as a relevant ingredient in relativistic quantum information.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraining Dehnen-inspired dark matter halo with S2 star's orbit
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We use the orbit of S2 star around Sagittarius A* to constrain three black hole backgrounds motivated by Dehnen profiles with inner slopes $γ=0$, $1$, and $5/2$, which are characterized by the scale radius $r_s$ and density $ρ_s$ of the dark matter halo. An exact turning-point integral gives the pericenter advance at finite eccentricity, and an exterior expansion identifies the leading halo contributions. A fifteen-parameter Bayesian analysis combines astrometric and spectroscopic observations with the measured precession parameter, from which we obtain the marginalized $1σ$ upper limits $r_s/M<0.236$, $0.168$, and $0.030$, and $ρ_sM^2<0.536$, $0.578$, and $0.004$, respectively. The leading halo monopole in the first two metrics is degenerate with the central mass. At fixed dynamical mass, their leading radial profile correction produces retrograde precession. The $γ=5/2$ metric introduces an additional angular deficit contribution, which enhances the precession response and accounts for its smaller parameter limits.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Weak-field charged-scalar dynamics in Melvin--Kerr spacetime: an effective Kerr spectral problem
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the local weak-field reduction of the charged Klein--Gordon equation in the neutral-seed Melvin--Kerr geometry and the auxiliary Kerr spectral problem defined by that reduction. At fixed radius and fixed scalar charge, the metric has no term linear in the magnetic parameter $b$. In the chosen gauge the first-order Maxwell potential is $A_μ=b\,g_{μφ}$, so its interaction with an azimuthal mode $m$ is absorbed into $μ_{\rm eff}^{2}=μ^{2}+2qbm$. This identity applies to both separated equations and leaves the gauge-invariant horizon phase in the Kerr form. Extending the truncated equation to all exterior radii and imposing Kerr outgoing boundary conditions defines an auxiliary spectrum, evaluated with Dolan's continued-fraction method. Its linear magnetic response is the complex mass derivative of the Kerr spectrum. Numerical examples for the fundamental $\ell=1,2$ branches illustrate this relation, including the continuation through negative effective mass squared. The tabulated modes remain damped, and their real-frequency shifts have opposite signs for the two positive-frequency azimuthal sectors in the surveyed range. We separate numerical accuracy within the auxiliary problem from local weak-field power counting and the unresolved exterior boundary problem. No matching to the exact magnetized exterior is performed; consequently these frequencies are not established approximations to global Melvin--Kerr resonances.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Sound of Keplerian binaries in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We formulate the dissipation due to sound-wave emission from a Keplerian binary embedded in a homogeneous Newtonian fluid background at rest in the binary center-of-mass frame within linear perturbation theory. Rather than starting from the local wake force, we treat the binary as a localized periodic mass source and compute the sound-wave fluxes carried away by the medium. The time-averaged energy, linear-momentum, and angular-momentum fluxes are obtained from Noether currents of the fluid perturbations. For a classical inviscid barotropic Newtonian fluid, retaining the self-gravity of density perturbations while adopting the Jeans prescription, we derive explicit flux formulas for circular and eccentric binaries with arbitrary mass ratio. This formulation also clarifies the ultraviolet behavior of point sources: in a nondispersive fluid, the harmonic sum becomes cutoff-sensitive precisely when at least one component becomes supersonic. We examine explicitly how finite source size removes this divergence using a uniform-sphere model and relate the resulting regularization to a corresponding effective harmonic cutoff. The associated secular eccentricity evolution exhibits circularization in the subsonic regime when the fluid self-gravity is sufficiently weak but can change sign outside this regime, with eccentricity growth in the strictly supersonic UV limit. For a Schrödinger-Poisson quantum fluid, quantum pressure instead softens the high-frequency contribution and renders the point-source fluxes UV finite within the nonrelativistic regime; our numerical results further indicate eccentricity growth due to sound radiation over the parameter space explored. Finally, we translate orbital-decay measurements of two binary pulsars into order-of-magnitude bounds on the homogeneous quantum-fluid density surrounding each system.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Propagation and horizon formation in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet scalar collapse. I. Characteristic conditions, bounds and formation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study scalar collapse in five- and six-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity with positive coupling as an exact classical theory. On spherical scalar backgrounds, gravitational characteristic conditions reduce to inequalities in two local invariants. In five dimensions, they imply $R_h^2>\tildeα$ for regular marginal spheres on the GR branch and the sharp Kretschmann bound $\tildeα^2\mathcal R_{abcd}\mathcal R^{abcd}<28$ for nonnegative mass. Under the stated finite-domain hypotheses, spherical continuation places the first characteristic degeneration on a smooth background. Within this setting, a future marginal sphere formed while the characteristic conditions hold throughout the preceding evolution forces their later failure. For every allowed radius, separately chosen complete smooth data form marginal spheres with mass arbitrarily close to the sharp lower bound; in six dimensions both radius and mass can be arbitrarily small. At sufficiently large scale, complete nonspherical data with weak curvature contain marginal surfaces with prescribed $S^3$ metrics under a spectral condition. These surfaces are outermost and strictly stable. A separate Berger family has arbitrarily small area at one common ADM mass; formation from untrapped data remains open. Exact nonspherical developments have smoothly convergent initial data but tidal tensors that fail to converge to the reference values at a chosen time after the reference core loses hyperbolicity. Under local geometric uniqueness for developments of the same data on overlaps connecting the initial slice to the observers, classical existence on a common region and continuous dependence of the tidal tensor cannot both hold. The constructed solutions themselves extend smoothly. Fixed time averages converge on the controlled interval, but this does not establish a predictive effective-field-theory continuation.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: QTG minimons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study static, spherically symmetric, regular horizonless solutions of quasitopological gravity (QTG), which we call QTG minimons. These configurations form the small-mass branch below the threshold for regular black holes. We include vacuum polarization by coupling the spherically reduced QTG action to the Polyakov action for two-dimensional conformal matter. For an arbitrary characteristic function $h(p)$, we derive a constrained first-order system in the static, asymptotically empty state. We obtain central expansions in $D\ge4$ and analyze four-dimensional solutions in the Hayward-type and Born--Infeld-type models. Both models retain a de Sitter-like core. Along the near-critical branch, the asymptotic mass decreases with the quantum coupling, while the central blueshift can become large even for a small coupling. The numerical results indicate that vacuum polarization is a nonuniform perturbation near the critical limit. Assuming a smooth constant-radius limit in proper distance, we derive a candidate $\mathrm{AdS}_2\times S^{D-2}$ throat geometry for the limiting configurations, which we call QTG extremons.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Probing Dirac Dark Matter in Composite Higgs Models with Xenon and Argon targets
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Recent advancements in direct detection (DD) experiments stimulate the investigation of the interactions of dark matter (DM) with nucleons and nuclei. In the framework of Composite Higgs Models (CHMs) the lightest Dirac composite particle (LDCP) can be stable composing a significant fraction ξof the observed DM relic abundance. We consider the elastic scattering of the LDCP on nucleons as well as on xenon (Xe) and argon (Ar) nuclei within the CHMs in which the LDCP magnetic moment, its mass and its coupling to the Higgs doublet are suppressed by an approximate U(1) symmetry. The LDCP with non-zero magnetic dipole moment can result in a substantial enhancement of the differential event rate in the DD experiments at low recoil energies of nuclei. Assuming ξ\ge 0.1, we identify the region of the parameter space where such enhancement may be potentially observable. In addition we specify some observables that can be useful in discriminating between the DM fermions with non-zero magnetic moment and other types of dark matter particles which don't have similar electromagnetic properties.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 37 pages, 10 figures, some changes to the text, added references

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Thermodynamics of QCD+QED from the lattice
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: QED corrections to observables in QCD are by now well-understood at zero temperature, where QED effects are perturbative and required for precision physics observables, such as the neutron-proton mass difference or the muon anomalous magnetic moment, among many others. However, there are indications in the literature that at finite temperature the introduction of QED can lead to non-perturbative effects, affecting the structure of the phase diagram, since the combined theory is exactly center-symmetric. In this proceedings article, we analyze the structure of the combined theory and the different strategies to simulate it on the lattice, as well as presenting novel results of lattice QCD+QED simulations at finite temperature, focusing on understanding the role of the electromagnetic coupling in the thermodynamics of this system. We also discuss new features that arise in the combined theory and the challenges that these simulations entail, which require the development of new algorithms in order to understand the phase diagram of QCD+QED from first principles.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, contribution to the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (LATTICE2026), July 26 - August 1 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Solving the Domain Wall Problem: Primordial Magnetic Fields as a Dynamical Solution
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay-a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous Chern-Simons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its efficacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Perspective on Proton Transversity Distribution Functions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Using available information on proton tensor charges and constraints from perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD), Ansaetze are introduced for hadron-scale in-proton valence-quark transversity distributions functions (DFs). The concept of a QCD effective charge, which defines an evolution scheme for collinear parton distribution and fragmentation functions that is all-orders exact, is then used to deliver predictions for the $x$-dependence of these DFs at the scale $ζ_{2} = 2\,$GeV. Although the approach is largely algebraic, its predictions remain viable after comparisons with results obtained using computationally intensive methods. Thus, given the scarcity of data that can today be used for inference of proton transversity DFs, it may be worth using the results herein to inform and constrain related experiments and phenomenological fits.

Atomic Physics.title: On-site interaction energies for Hubbard models with shielded polar molecules
Atomic Physics.summary: We show how to control on-site interaction energies $U$ for pairs of shielded ultracold molecules on the same lattice site. We use 2-dimensional effective potentials appropriate for microwave shielding, which have dipole-dipole character at long range but feature a very large repulsive core when the two molecules come close together. This causes very strong correlation between the motions of two molecules on the same site and produces field-linked states. We identify field-linked states for which $U$ can be tuned over a wide range, including across zero, as a function of lattice strength or shielding conditions. This will give access to previously unexplored regimes of strongly dipolar Hubbard physics with multiple site occupancy.
Atomic Physics.comment: Accepted for publication in Physical Review Letters. Supplemental Material included

Atomic Physics.title: Breit interaction in elastic scattering of vortex electron on Hydrogen atomic target
Atomic Physics.summary: The interaction of electron vortex beams with atoms is fundamental to their applications, yet existing studies of elastic scattering have considered only the Coulomb interaction. The role of the Breit interaction, which represents the leading relativistic correction to the Coulomb potential between two electrons, has not been systematically examined. In this paper, we study the elastic scattering of a vortex electron by a hydrogen atomic target, with emphasis on the role of the Breit interaction. Comparisons are made between two situations: the pure Coulomb contribution and the pure Breit contribution. Our results show that the Breit interaction dominates the scattering process when the total angular momentum of the vortex electron is larger than a certain threshold, which challenges the conventional notion that the Breit interaction makes little contribution to electron scattering for low-$Z$ atoms. This phenomenon arises primarily because a vortex electron with large angular momentum possesses a substantial magnetic moment, and the Breit interaction precisely describes the interaction between magnetic moments. The threshold can be adjusted by changing the parameters of the initial vortex electron. Moreover, we further compare the single-atom, mesoscopic, and macroscopic target cases, and show that the target size significantly influences the observability of the Breit-induced effects, with a smaller target size being favorable for observing this phenomenon. Vortex electrons add a new tool to the well-established electron-atom scattering tool box. Our results are important for applications of vortex electrons: they show that, when large total angular momentum is involved, the Breit interaction must be taken into account in calculations.

Quantum Physics.title: What Can Postselection on Halting Decide?
Quantum Physics.summary: A probabilistic program can produce an answer on some runs and continue forever on others. Suppose it halts with positive probability on every input and we count only the runs that halt. Aaronson et al. showed that if the correct answer must be more than twice as likely as the wrong one, such programs decide exactly the problems solvable with a finite list of halting questions chosen in advance. They asked what happens when the correct answer need only be more likely than the wrong one. We prove that the resulting class is exactly $\boldsymbol{Δ^0_2}$: the halting questions can now be asked one at a time, with each answer helping to determine the next question. This remains true if the program must halt with probability at least 99%, or with any other prescribed rational lower bound below one. Our main technical result is the exact query bound when the program gives two guarantees. Suppose it halts with probability at least $ρ$ and, among the runs that halt, the correct answer has probability at least $a$. For rational $0 < ρ< 1$ and $1/2 < a < 1$, these programs decide exactly the problems solvable with at most $n$ halting questions chosen in advance, where $n$ is the largest integer satisfying $ρ(a/(1-a))^n \le 1$. Every value of $n$ occurs, and different values give different classes. The proof measures how much additional halting probability a change of answer requires, and counts these changes as in Ershov's hierarchy. The results extend to quantum machines with computable gates.

Quantum Physics.title: Local failure of disjoint additivity
Quantum Physics.summary: Local Gauss constraints can prevent commuting regional algebras from generating the full algebra assigned to their union. We investigate disjoint additivity on the full magnetic physical subspace of finite-group quantum-double models while keeping the original lattice edge supports fixed. Every finite non-Abelian group exhibits a counterexample on vertex-disjoint regions contained within a contractible disk on a regular square torus. For a fixed eight-edge loop and a specified peripheral contact family, additivity fails if and only if the group is non-Abelian and the selected contacts cover all four interior faces of the loop. Leaving an inner face uncovered restores additivity; for the same loop, so does any second region avoiding the specified testing neighborhood. A peripheral projector restricts the exterior tests on a loop transition, allowing their product to preserve the constraints even when the loop factor does not. We construct union observables that deterministically separate orthogonal relative-sign superpositions that yield identical outcome statistics under every measurement whose effects lie in the generated regional algebra. For a separate wrapping pair, we also determine the complete matrix-block inclusion, identifying missing center-orbit coherences, and construct an independent regular-torus counterexample for the eight-dimensional Kac-Paljutkin Hopf algebra.

Quantum Physics.title: Compact and Long-Term Stable Polarization Entangled Photon-Pair Source
Quantum Physics.summary: We present a robust, compact polarization-entangled photon-pair source based on bulk optics that achieves long-term stability, a spectral pair generation rate of $4.24 \times 10^6$ pairs s$^{-1}$ mW$^{-1}$ nm$^{-1}$ constant for pump powers up to 700 mW, an intrinsic heralding efficiency of 59.8% , and a polarization contrast visibility of 99.6%. The source is mechanically designed for vibrational robustness, employing an engineered base plate and a reduced optical layout for less alignment sensitivity and complexity. It operates at telecom wavelengths in C-band with a typical type-0 SPDC spectral output of 70 nm width. We demonstrate its integration into a deployed entanglement-based QKD system that bridges the gap between laboratory prototypes and practical quantum communication hardware.

Quantum Physics.title: Path Integrals on Functional Lattices
Quantum Physics.summary: Path integrals in quantum field theory are commonly approached through finite-dimensional approximations, but existence and regulator independence of the infinite-dimensional limit require separate analysis. We introduce a scheme in which spacetime remains continuous and the field is expanded in a discrete complete family of localized functions, called a functional lattice. Truncation to finite-dimensional functional subspaces yields ordinary finite-dimensional integrals while leaving the continuum differential operator unchanged. For the massive free Euclidean scalar field, we prove convergence of the finite-dimensional covariance operators and normalized generating functionals by a Galerkin argument. The limit is independent of the compatible functional lattice: any sequence of finite-dimensional subspaces dense in the quadratic-form domain converges to the same continuum covariance and generating functional. A direct Minkowski construction is obtained at fixed Feynman regulator $iε$, followed by the distributional limit $ε\downarrow0$. For interacting theories, each truncation gives an ordinary non-Gaussian integral. At fixed perturbative order, convergence follows when the finite-resolution graph integrands converge pointwise and admit an integrable majorant independent of the functional resolution. Numerical results for one-dimensional $φ^4$ theory approach the known first- and second-order mass-gap coefficients, while four-dimensional calculations exhibit the expected mass divergence and logarithmic wave-function renormalization. Thus functional lattices provide a continuum-space approach to path integrals with mathematically controlled limits in the cases considered here.

Quantum Physics.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
Quantum Physics.summary: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.

Quantum Physics.title: A Frequency-Learning Interpolation-Based Coordinate Descent Method to Optimize Parameterized Quantum Circuits on Quantum Hardware
Quantum Physics.summary: Structure-aware optimizers have been the focus of recent study for the optimization of parameters in variational quantum circuits. Many of these optimizers follow a coordinate-based paradigm, making single parameter updates by using classical approximations to the cost function generated from quantum sampling. However, the performance of structure-aware optimizers on real quantum hardware at large system size has yet to be demonstrated. Recently, Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (ICD) has been proposed to unify many of these optimizers into one framework. ICD requires a preset frequency set for interpolation, which can be theoretically derived, but for which the cost function is generally sparse over and may require manual tuning. To address these issues, we propose Frequency-learning Interpolation-based Coordinate Descent (FLICD) to adaptively learn frequencies online, allowing easier scaling up to larger systems. We demonstrate that our algorithm is more accurate than an existing zeroth-order method COBYLA and requires fewer quantum resources than ICD on simulator. Using IBM quantum hardware, we execute FLICD on systems up to 100 qubits and observe robust performance with an increasing number of layers.
Quantum Physics.comment: Main article: 28 pages and 11 figures. Appendix: 12 pages and 7 figures

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum sine imaginary-time evolution: sequential and QSVT implementations of a probabilistic ground-state filter
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose quantum sine imaginary-time evolution (QSITE), a quantum algorithm for preparing ground states of a Hamiltonian. QSITE approximates imaginary-time evolution through an exact sine filter. We give two circuit implementations of this operator: a sequential one that applies it as a concatenation of linear combinations of unitaries (LCU), reusing two ancilla qubits across steps via mid-circuit measurement, and a coherent one based on the quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). A telescoping identity shows the two prepare the same state and succeed with identical probability, differing only in how that probability can be boosted. QSITE belongs to the family of ancilla-based probabilistic imaginary-time filters and we state rigorous convergence guarantees: we prove that the QSITE operator converges uniformly to the exact ITE operator, that the prepared state converges to the ideal ITE state, and that the filter probability increases monotonically with each concatenation step. Although the construction applies to an arbitrary Hamiltonian, we specialize it to optimization Hamiltonians, and this specialization is what exposes its structure more easily. Since MaxCut eigenvalues are integers, the probability of failure is periodic in the evolution time, yielding safe zones, the first located analytically and the second numerically. For MaxCut we further show that, when the tolerated energy error is a fixed fraction of the ground-state energy, the probability of failure can be bounded below 1/2 with concatenation steps growing linearly with the number of qubits in the first safe zone. We present numerical results for random Erdös-Rényi instances with up to 24 qubits and benchmark QSITE against QAOA.

Quantum Physics.title: Perfect state transfer on trees in the normalized Laplacian quantum walk
Quantum Physics.summary: We prove that, in the normalized-Laplacian model, perfect state transfer between two vertices of a tree can only happen if they are at distance at most $2$. We show that a conjecture of Coutinho and Baptista, stating that the only trees admitting perfect state transfer are $K_2$ and $P_3$, is true when the two vertices are at odd distance. We then construct infinite families of trees admitting perfect state transfer, disproving their conjecture in the general case.

Quantum Physics.title: Handed Ultrafast Dynamics in Chiral Cyanine Nanotubes
Quantum Physics.summary: We detect helicity-dependent excited state relaxation in a chiral exciton system. Using L-histidine as a chiral inducer, we prepared unbundled, double-walled J-aggregrate nanotubes of an amphiphilic cyanine dye with a net handedness, which gives a large circular dichroism dissymmetry factor ($g_{abs} = 3.6 \times 10^{-2}$). With two-dimensional electronic spectroscopy and circularly polarized pump pulses, we find that the relaxation rates of longitudinal excitons depend on pump helicity (4.5 $ps^{-1}$ for $\langle \textit{RRXX} \rangle$ vs 6 $ps^{-1}$ for $\langle \textit{LLXX} \rangle$, a difference of about 30%) and is the same in the inner and outer tubes. Transverse excitons show no significant dependence. Chirality and pump helicity therefore bias exciton relaxation on the femtosecond timescale for excitons delocalized along the helical structure.

Quantum Physics.title: Entanglement Geometry Beyond Polygons: Graph-Theoretic Entanglement Inequalities
Quantum Physics.summary: Entanglement entropies of pure multipartite states can be constrained by organizing subsystem cuts as edges (hyperedges) of graphs (hypergraphs). Starting from the one-party entanglement polygon inequality, we derive these constraints from strong subadditivity and pure-state complementarity, with optimal coefficients and explicit equality conditions. Our central result determines, for a distinguished two-party cut and an arbitrary weighted family of cuts, the optimal polygon coefficient: the smallest total weight of the cuts separating a member of the distinguished pair from a remaining party. A refinement involving three mutual information terms gives the exact minimum of the weighted sum at fixed entropies of the two parties and of their union, attained by at most three independent bipartite pure states. The analogous coefficient is also optimal for a distinguished one-party cut and for any distinguished cut that the family does not split. This criterion recovers the cycle and complete-graph inequalities and shows that uniform incidence parity, which we prove sufficient for polygon inequalities on hypergraphs, is not necessary. Averaging strong subadditivity over both sides of a bipartition gives a sharp $k$-marginal inequality with coefficient $2\binom{n-2}{k-1}$, and we determine uniformly optimal coefficients for collective hyperstar inequalities. For paths and overlapping hyperchains, the deficits are exact sums of conditional mutual information terms; genuinely multipartite entangled cluster states saturate the hyperchain inequality while the chain inequality remains strict. We characterize pure chain equality states, bound the trace distance to cycle equality states independently of the number of parties and local dimensions, and obtain bond-dimension bounds for matrix product states and sequential-recovery error estimates.
Quantum Physics.comment: 29 pages, 3 figures, comments are welcome; v2: added the weighted one-party cut inequality (Corollary 39), its refinement (Remark 40), and an extension to distinguished cuts not split by the family (Proposition 41); abstract, introduction, and conclusion updated

Quantum Physics.title: Construction of Kochen-Specker Sets from Mutually Unbiased Bases
Quantum Physics.summary: We give a constructive analysis of Kochen-Specker (KS) contextuality at the level of complete orthogonal bases (contexts). In dimension three, three noncomputational mutually unbiased bases generate a union of 165 rays and 130 contexts. Exact provenance accounting gives a symmetric decomposition: the three 69-ray lineages share 21 rays and 10 contexts, while each contributes 48 exclusive rays and 40 lineage-specific contexts. Each 69-ray, 50-context lineage is a KS configuration; as a hypergraph it is the 69-50 KS set reported earlier by Pavicic and Megill. This framework clarifies the relation among the Yu-Oh, Harding-Salinas Schmeis, Pavicic-Megill, and Cabello constructions. In dimensions four and five, we give parametrized orthogonality gadgets whose connector contexts force a central ray to be maximally unbiased relative to the computational basis. For the concrete four-dimensional example, the 20-ray gadget and the Cabello 18-ray set are informationally equivalent subsets of the 24-ray Peres-Mermin eigensystem, although their context hypergraphs have different two-valued-state behavior. The results show why both the rays and the complete incidence structure of their contexts are needed in assessments of KS contextuality.
Quantum Physics.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables, revised, one reference added

Quantum Physics.title: On locked states for damped driven Jaynes--Cummings equations
Quantum Physics.summary: We consider damped driven version of the Jaynes-Cummings equation which describes quantised one-mode Maxwell field coupled to a two-level molecule. The pumping and dissipation operator are polynomial in the creation and annihilation operators. The structure of the dissipation operator corresponds to the theory of completely positive trace preserving operators due to Lindblad, Kossakowski and others. We construct examples of {\it locked states} which are stationary states of the corresponding averaged dynamics in the interaction picture. The states are nonnegative Hermitian density operators with finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm. The calculations rely on the recurrence equation for diagonal entries.

Quantum Physics.title: Systematically improvable semiclassical clustering for accurate and efficient quantum dynamics in large spin ensembles
Quantum Physics.summary: Predicting the decoherence of spin qubits in realistic environments is key to identifying the interactions that limit their coherence---a prerequisite for designing better quantum technologies. While accurate methods for spin dynamics are limited to relatively small systems, the dissipative spin environments in real experiments typically involve orders of magnitude more spins. Semiclassical methods can reach these sizes, but their classical treatment of the bath cannot capture the sensor-bath entanglement that generates coherence revivals, especially under the application of refocusing pulses. Here, we resolve this tension. We introduce cluster spin-LSC, a method that clusters the sensor together with a few strongly coupled bath spins, treating them quantum mechanically in an otherwise classical spin bath. We show that our method is applicable to systems containing arbitrary spin species under dynamical decoupling pulse sequences. Our method converges systematically to the exact dynamics with cluster size, providing an internal consistency check when no exact benchmarks exist. We demonstrate that cluster spin-LSC recovers numerically exact coherence and population dynamics for a nitrogen-vacancy center and a molecular qubit, reducing day-long multi-GPU simulations to only minutes on a CPU. We further extend our method to systems with large spin baths that lie beyond the reach of exact methods. Our approach thus offers a scalable and systematically improvable route to accurately simulate the decoherence dynamics of sensors in realistic spin environments.

Quantum Physics.title: Q-TRACE: Physics-based zero-day attack detection for decoy-state quantum key distribution
Quantum Physics.summary: Practical quantum key distribution (QKD) is secure only while its devices match the assumptions of the security proof, and implementation attacks exploit mismatches while keeping the quantum bit error rate (QBER) low. We formulate attack detection in decoy-state BB84 as a sequential test against the honest-device manifold, the set of receiver statistics an attack-free link can produce under arbitrary channel loss. The resulting monitor, Q-TRACE (Quantum Telemetry Residuals Against Calibrated Expectations), calibrates a physical model of each link on commissioning data, profiles out the transmittance, and combines omnibus residual, physics score and setting-allocation tests with drift-robust references; no attack data are used. The formulation also yields a detectability exponent D* that lower-bounds the delay of any telemetry monitor and vanishes for a Trojan-horse probe with filtered back-reflection. On a count-level twin with model mismatch, over five held-out seeds and at a per-window false-alarm rate of 10^-3, Q-TRACE detects 63.6% of links under known attacks, 28.0% under unseen attack families and 65.3% under composite attacks, versus at most 51.2%, 6.7% and 42.3% for industry monitors, unsupervised and quantum-kernel detectors and a supervised classifier. Its delay attains the bound for strongly detectable attacks. On 33 parallel BB84 links of the IBM Heron processor ibm_marrakesh with physically executed entangling and amplitude-damping eavesdroppers, the measured information-disturbance relations agree with theory; a commissioning reference acquired under different operating conditions triggers alarms in every monitor tested, while a condition-matched reference detects a probe with 0.3% ideal QBER increase on 14 of 14 link-epochs with no false alarm on 66 honest ones.
Quantum Physics.comment: 33 pages, 11 figures, 14 tables. Code, raw hardware data and all results are available at https://github.com/Sumitchongder/Q-TRACE

Quantum Physics.title: Non-Abelian Twist Defects in Bivariate Bicycle Codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity-check codes combine efficient quantum storage with a rich Abelian anyon structure, providing a compelling platform for exploring the interplay between quantum error correction and topological order. A central challenge is how to realize domain walls that host non-Abelian twist defects at their endpoints. Here we explicitly construct electric-magnetic duality walls for arbitrary bivariate bicycle codes with finite anyon content using composite, interblock, and patch checks. These checks remove the unwanted local modes while preserving charge conversion, ensuring that topologically contractible closed ribbons act trivially on encoded states. For each fixed code, check weights and interaction ranges remain bounded independently of wall length. The wall endpoints have quantum dimension $2^{Q/2}$, where $Q$ counts the independent generators in each electric or magnetic charge space. As an application, we illustrate measurement-only braiding for $Q=3$ under the correspondence between measurements and defect transport. Our construction provides a valuable basis for exploring non-Abelian defect physics and developing logical operations in quantum low-density parity-check codes with Abelian topological order in future.

Quantum Physics.title: Coherent Floquet quantum reservoirs for molecular property prediction
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) uses observables of a driven quantum system to make predictions from a sequence of inputs. The robust subharmonic response of discrete time crystals (DTCs) has motivated their use as quantum reservoirs. Here we develop a DTC-QRC architecture for molecular property prediction in which successive graph events or surface-hopping frames drive a fixed Floquet reservoir. An adjustable reset probability controls how long earlier inputs influence the state, and measurements of the final polarizations and pair correlations yield a feature vector of fixed dimension. Weak reset favors classification of inhibitor activity and blood-brain barrier penetration from long graph prefixes, whereas forecasting electronic gaps in ethene favors greater weight on recent nuclear motion. With nonlinear decoding, DTC-QRC outperforms an echo-state network on these tasks at matched input lengths and readout widths. For gap forecasting with this decoder and final-state readout, the dissipative reservoirs share a low-error drive window near the DTC transition reported for related spin chains. Dephasing lowers prediction performance in both molecular applications. In six-qubit classification without programmed reset on the Quafu superconducting quantum cloud platform, pair correlations retain more of their noise-free predictive power toward the DTC side, and the full readout performs best near the transition among the drives tested. The architecture provides a common framework for molecular screening and time-resolved property prediction using quantum reservoir computing.
Quantum Physics.comment: 15 pages, 10 figures. Updated the data availability statement. Code is available at https://github.com/eternal-fly/article-git#qrc-quantum-reservoir-computing

Quantum Physics.title: Long-time dynamics of open quantum systems: mathematical and physical aspects
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum channels provide the mathematical framework for describing the evolution of open quantum systems, i.e., quantum systems interacting with an environment. This review focuses on the long-time or asymptotic dynamics of open quantum systems, a topic of growing interest due to its relevance for quantum information theory and noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. We present a comprehensive analysis of homogeneous evolutions in both discrete and continuous time, treating the dynamics in full generality within the Schrödinger and Heisenberg pictures. By systematically studying the spectral properties of quantum channels, we present general structure theorems that characterize asymptotic behaviour, illustrated through several paradigmatic examples. We further discuss how the asymptotic dynamics can be exploited for dissipative state engineering, the identification of decoherence-free subspaces, the design of quantum error-correction schemes, and the evaluation of the asymptotic capacities of quantum channels.

Quantum Physics.title: The resource--invariant gap: a protected Floquet invariant need not protect Wigner negativity
Quantum Physics.summary: Topological invariants constrain a driven Floquet generator, yet whether they protect a transient nonlinear bosonic resource remains open. We track boundary Wigner negativity of an even cat state in a chiral Floquet Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with boundary Kerr nonlinearity and structured loss. The quasienergy windings remain quantized at every chain length, yet the matched sector contrast flips sign when the chain grows under index-end shielding and is null within $3\times 10^{-5}$ under uniform loss at $t=T$ for $d\le 0.5$. Prepared and shielded on the physical dangling end, the contrast remains positive, modulated by local dimer return rather than set by the invariant. A three-site causal light cone and a boundary-Laplacian erosion law trace the flip to strong-bond bulk exposure: the sign is set by where the bulk-rate loss sits relative to the prepared site, not by chain length. We call this decoupling the resource--invariant gap.
Quantum Physics.comment: 32 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Supplemental Material: 49 pages, 5 figures, 28 tables

Quantum Physics.title: Modeling the Disjunction Effect within Classical Probability: A New Decision Process Model and Comparison with Quantum-like Models
Quantum Physics.summary: In a Prisoner's Dilemma experiment, participants defected less often when the opponent's move was unknown than when they were told that the opponent had defected or that the opponent had cooperated. This disjunction effect has often been interpreted as a violation of the classical law of total probability and has motivated quantum-like models of decision making. We re-examine this interpretation and identify a strong assumption implicit in the conventional classical model. The conventional model uses the two informed conditions to represent the full range of participants' expectations and thus treats every participant as certain of the opponent's move even when that move is unknown. We relax this premise by introducing a continuous parameter for each participant's degree of expectation that the opponent will defect. Participants are grouped by expectation level, with the intermediate groups representing ambiguous expectations. A standard quantum-like model offers a different account of this same uncertainty about the opponent's move. In that model, ambiguity arises through superposition, and ambiguous pure states are generic (dense and of full unitarily invariant measure on the unit sphere), so certainty states are mathematically exceptional. Despite this difference in how ambiguity is represented, the proposed classical model can reproduce the observed strong disjunction effect while satisfying the classical law of total probability. More generally, we prove that it can exactly reproduce any triple of defection rates strictly between zero and one, including every such triple generated by the quantum-like model. The proposed model is therefore no less expressive than the quantum-like model for these three observable rates while remaining entirely within classical probability, and the substantive difference between the two lies in how they represent ambiguity and interpret events.
Quantum Physics.comment: 30 pages, 2 figures. Revised for clarity, especially in the abstract and introduction

Quantum Physics.title: Increasing Quantum LDPC Code Distance through Explicit Extensions
Quantum Physics.summary: We give an explicit construction of quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes without searching for candidates at each size. A fixed pair partition (PP) and fixed integer parameters determine the parity-check matrices at a specified size. Using affine permutation matrices (APMs), we construct a $[[3072,772,32]]$ code with column weight 3 and check weight 8 in each of the X and Z parity-check matrices. A construction based on circulant permutation matrices (CPMs) gives $[[1270,260,\ge34]]$, with column weight 4 and check weight 10. We prove that the construction yields commuting checks and verify the resulting distances using exhaustive search and logical operators. For the main construction, we conjecture the existence of a finite structural distance upper bound and distance improvement toward that bound as the size increases.

Quantum Physics.title: Holevo-Bounded Total Information from Pair Distributions of Alternative Quantum Measurements
Quantum Physics.summary: The accessible information of a quantum ensemble can be strictly smaller than its Holevo information because a single-copy measurement may discard part of the label--system correlation. We ask whether information represented across two alternative measurement contexts can bridge this gap without assigning a joint distribution to their outcomes. Building on the relative-entropy-based projection method introduced by Harder et al., we define the directed posterior novelty of each record relative to the other, and an associated total-information quantity. For posterior-orthogonal records, this quantity equals the sum of the two record mutual informations. For finite-dimensional classical--quantum ensembles, we prove that optimizing this quantity over pairs of POVMs yields a value between the accessible and Holevo information. The upper bound follows by showing that the directed posterior novelty provides a lower bound on the infimum of the measured-relative-entropy recovery error. The uniform BB84 ensemble provides an example in which the quantity saturates the Holevo information while strictly exceeding the accessible information. Finally, we analytically establish the quantum validity of a redundancy-based information causality condition, resolving a question that has remained open since the condition was introduced.

Quantum Physics.title: A resource theory of asynchronous quantum information processing
Quantum Physics.summary: In standard quantum teleportation, the receiver must wait for a classical message from the sender before subsequently processing the transmitted quantum information. However, in port-based teleportation (PBT), this local processing can begin before the classical message is received, thereby allowing for asynchronous quantum information processing. Motivated by resource-theoretic considerations and practical applications, we propose different communication models that progressively allow for more powerful decoding strategies while still permitting asynchronous distributed quantum computation, a salient feature of standard PBT. Specifically, we consider PBT protocols augmented by free classical processing and/or different forms of quantum pre-processing, and we investigate the maximum achievable teleportation fidelities under such operations. Our analysis focuses specifically on the PBT power of isotropic states, bipartite graph states, and symmetrized EPR states, and we compute tight bounds on the optimal teleportation fidelities for such states. We finally show that, among this hierarchy of communication models consistent with asynchronous quantum information processing, the strongest resource theory is equally as powerful as any one-way teleportation protocol for surpassing the classical teleportation threshold. Thus, a bipartite state can break the one-way classical teleportation threshold if and only if it can be done using the trivial decoding map of discarding subsystems.

Quantum Physics.title: Optimal work extraction in measurement-based quantum Otto engines: Non-adiabaticity and generalized measurements can be beneficial
Quantum Physics.summary: Measurement-based quantum heat engines have attracted significant interest as alternatives to conventional thermal engines, as they replace the hot thermal reservoir with quantum measurements, thereby offering greater controllability and simpler implementation. Motivated by these advantages, we investigate a measurement-driven quantum Otto engine with a qubit working substance and study the optimal work extractable from such engines along with the corresponding efficiency, including whether their performance can surpass that of conventional quantum Otto cycles. We analyze the engine in both the infinite-time (adiabatic) and finite-time (non-adiabatic) regimes, considering two distinct implementations obtained through optimization over all projection-valued measurements (PVMs) and over all two-outcome positive operator-valued measurements (POVMs). We show that measurement-based engines can outperform conventional quantum Otto engines within specific parameter regimes and that POVM-based engines can yield higher optimal work extraction than PVM-based ones. Furthermore, by incorporating the thermodynamic cost associated with resetting the auxiliary system required for POVM implementation, we demonstrate that the resulting net work output can still exceed that of PVM-based engines under suitable conditions on the spectral gaps and cold bath temperature. We also identify regimes in which non-adiabatic implementations can yield higher work output and efficiency than their adiabatic counterparts. Our study provides operational guidelines for designing improved measurement-driven quantum Otto engines.
Quantum Physics.comment: 26 pages, 6 figures. Typos corrected, references updated, framework generalized to encompass arbitrary relative orientations of the qubit Hamiltonians of the qubit working substance, and analysis of the efficiency at the optimal work extraction expanded

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Metrology With Quantum Limit Cycles
Quantum Physics.summary: Beyond nonclassical states, emergent quantum phenomena offer new metrological resources. Quantum limit cycles, in particular, sustain long-lived oscillations that prolong coherent signal accumulation. However, quantum fluctuations may limit this advantage, leaving their metrological performance unclear. Here, we propose a quantum limit-cycle metrology protocol for collective spins by introducing nonlinear damping into the conventional collective-decay protocol. We develop a semiclassical phase-diffusion theory to characterize its metrological performance, in good agreement with numerical simulations. The limit-cycle protocol improves estimation precision and approaches Heisenberg scaling with system size. We further combine limit-cycle dynamics with spin squeezing, finding that squeezing improves short-time precision, but phase diffusion ultimately dominates, leaving the asymptotic scaling unchanged. Our results establish quantum limit cycles as a metrological resource and clarify the interplay between limit-cycle dynamics and squeezing in quantum sensing.

Quantum Physics.title: Approximate Virtual Quantum Recovery
Quantum Physics.summary: The recovery of quantum information after subsystem loss is a central challenge in quantum information processing. However, some quantum states remain beyond the reach of any recovery strategies. Here we identify the algebraic origin of virtual irrecoverability, the \emph{ghost information}---correlations present in the global state that leave no trace on any accessible subsystem. We introduce a scalar measure to quantify its magnitude and prove a universal error floor below which no virtual recovery map can operate, irrespective of resource investment. In such cases only \emph{approximate} virtual recovery is available. We derive upper and lower bounds on the sampling overhead for approximate virtual recovery. Moreover, we show that conditional mutual information, the standard entropic diagnostic, does not determine the sampling overhead. Our work thus establish an algebraic framework of information recovery beyond entropic criteria.

Quantum Physics.title: Resource-Efficient Quantum Reinforcement Learning on NISQ Devices with Dynamic-Circuit Qubit Reuse and Grover-Based Trajectory Search
Quantum Physics.summary: A resource-efficient quantum reinforcement learning framework for finite-horizon quantum Markov decision processes is presented, employing dynamic-circuit qubit reuse to reduce the interaction-workspace requirements of multi-step execution. The framework integrates quantum state-transition and reward encoding, dynamic-circuit execution, quantum return evaluation, and Grover-based trajectory search. Its central contribution is a dynamic execution model in which a fixed interaction workspace is reused across sequential agent-environment interactions through mid-circuit measurement, qubit reset, and next-state propagation. For the considered benchmark, this approach reduces the interaction-workspace requirement from 7T qubits under a static circuit to a constant seven qubits, independent of the interaction horizon T. This corresponds to a 66% reduction for the three-step benchmark and transforms the interaction-workspace complexity from O(T) to O(1). Trajectory returns are evaluated using reversible quantum arithmetic, and Grover's algorithm identifies the optimal trajectories, so that return evaluation and trajectory search are performed within a unified quantum-native pipeline. Ideal simulations demonstrate that the dynamic implementation preserves the valid trajectory structure of the static formulation, with quantitative comparisons assessing the agreement between their trajectory distributions. Finally, execution on an IBM Heron-class processor demonstrates the feasibility of the proposed dynamic-circuit architecture on noisy intermediate-scale quantum hardware.

Quantum Physics.title: Sharp Purity Based Entropy Bounds and Machine Learning Assisted Entropy Estimation
Quantum Physics.summary: Purity quantifies quantum-state mixedness, motivating the study of its role in controlling entropy variations. A sharp purity-based continuity bound is established for the von Neumann entropy of qubit states. The bound is attainable for every admissible purity difference and strictly improves the existing purity bound. In higher dimensions, an explicit sharp bound is derived within the family of pure states mixed with the maximally mixed state. Further continuity estimates are obtained for conditional entropy, quantum mutual information, quantum conditional mutual information, and squashed entanglement within specified bipartite and tripartite families. An application to machine learning assisted qubit entropy estimation illustrates how the sharp bound converts purity estimation errors into rigorous entropy error bounds.

Quantum Physics.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
Quantum Physics.summary: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the Rényi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

Quantum Physics.title: Feshbach resonances of the second order in a Friedrichs model
Quantum Physics.summary: We consider an extended version of the matrix Friedrichs model that may produce Feshbach resonances of the second order. In this model, under enlarging of the coupling constant, a pair of eigenvalues of the unperturbed Hamiltonian embedded into the continuous spectrum first transforms in resonances of the first order. At some moment later on, these two resonances merge into a single resonance but of the second order, and we fix conditions for this event. Being based on the operator interpretation of resonances, we found that, in the case under consideration, the operator roots of the transfer function have a very particular structure.

Quantum Physics.title: Many-Body Flux Selection in Chiral Quantum Batteries
Quantum Physics.summary: We study an interacting quantum-battery chain in which a synthetic flux controls interference between hopping paths. Keeping the internal battery Hamiltonian fixed, we seek the flux that leaves the most extractable work. Even a Gaussian reconstruction supplied with exact one-body information can rank competing flux settings incorrectly. A reduced many-body model that retains correlations within a few battery-occupation sectors recovers the correct ranking and selects nearly optimal fluxes across the finite systems and parameter ranges studied. Strikingly, the model can make an accurate control choice even when it excludes configurations carrying substantial probability in the exact state. Thus, choosing a nearly optimal charging flux can require much less information than reconstructing the full many-body state.

Quantum Physics.title: Phase-dependent atomicity and PPT edge states for cyclic-sign covariant qutrit maps
Quantum Physics.summary: Decomposable positive maps cannot detect entangled states with positive partial transpose (PPT). We obtain a necessary and sufficient criterion for decomposability in the entire seven-real-parameter class of Hermiticity-preserving cyclic-sign covariant maps on $M_3$. The criterion reduces to a one-variable inequality and, for positive maps in this class, characterizes indecomposability exactly. We apply it to a phase-dependent family obtained by adding a completely positive map to the Choi map. Every map in this family is positive, and we find the exact phase-dependent threshold for indecomposability and atomicity. At three phase values, the maps remain indecomposable for every finite deformation strength. Each indecomposable map gives an indecomposable entanglement witness through its Choi matrix. We construct PPT edge states of birank $(5,5)$ detected by these witnesses throughout the indecomposable region.

Quantum Physics.title: Revealing the Hidden Symmetry of the Asymmetric Quantum Rabi Model
Quantum Physics.summary: A longitudinal bias breaks ordinary parity in the asymmetric quantum Rabi model, yet exact crossings reappear when the bias equals an integer multiple $m$ of the oscillator energy spacing. We trace the hidden symmetry to exchange between equal-energy partners $m$ rungs apart on two displaced oscillator ladders. Tunneling to other rungs makes this exchange vary in time. We construct the exact symmetry operator by adding spin and oscillator coherences that cancel this variation. At nonzero coupling and tunneling, the resulting charge has no zero modes, and its sign divides the full Hilbert space into two generalized-parity sectors that cannot mix. Spin-resolved mirror interference probes coherence between the two opposite-parity states at a crossing. Its small-displacement exponent gives $m$, and its leading coefficient, together with the charge magnitude, predicts the mixing induced by a slight change in bias.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum nonclassicality as a marginal problem
Quantum Physics.summary: Classical explanations of quantum statistics---local, noncontextual, or causal---fail for one and the same reason: the probability distributions observed in different contexts are not the marginals of a single joint distribution. Every single context admits a classical model. This is Boole's problem of the "conditions of possible experience." Garg and Mermin treated it as a linear problem and showed, via Farkas's lemma, that its solvability is equivalent to a finite list of Bell-type inequalities, one for each extreme ray of a convex polyhedral cone; Pitowsky gave it the form of correlation polytopes. We sketch this common structure and discuss two examples: Aerts's elastic-band model, which reproduces the quantum cosine in one context but obeys the classical bound when contexts are combined; and nonclassicality in causal data fusion, where the contexts are supplied by interventions on a causal structure.

Quantum Physics.title: Banach-Cesaro positive operator-valued measure
Quantum Physics.summary: We construct a family of bounded, finitely additive, covariant positive operator-valued measures (POVMs) on the real line by applying generalised Banach-Cesaro asymptotic averaging to locally finite covariant POVMs. In contrast to the strictly shift-invariant case, where countably additive operator measures are restricted to scalar multiples of a single fixed operator, the introduced covariant setting allows for non-commuting averaged operator values while successfully normalising the total mass. We develop an integration theory for complex-valued functions by taking the completion of simple integrable functions with respect to the continuous operator norm induced by the positive integral of their absolute values. The integration spaces for the original and the averaged measures are shown to possess distinct null classes. Finally, we introduce the operator-valued Fourier transform on these integration spaces and analyze the core algebraic constraints imposed by the covariance property on the exponential multipliers.
Quantum Physics.comment: 11 pages; revision: introduction, proofs, conclusion and bibliography are extended

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum States over Spacetime Can Hide Setting-Dependent Dynamics
Quantum Physics.summary: Determining whether correlations across quantum events arise from one physical process is essential for interpreting quantum states over spacetime (QSOSTs). Yet separately realizable settings can share the same unconditional QSOST without admitting a common process, because compression hides distinctions between underlying dynamics. Using least positive lifts, we derive an exact joint-domination criterion for conditioned data to admit a common deterministic parent. A reset-dephasing example and a sparse interferometric witness make this obstruction testable under trusted readout assumptions. We further establish a minimum-five-reference theorem: for two laboratories with qubit inputs and outputs, any four fixed local product-unitary reference groups cannot universally identify deterministic processes from exact joint data, whereas a specified set of five suffices. These results establish when reconstructed temporal correlations support interpretation as alternative readouts of one stable quantum process, making preparation-readout separation a testable physical property.

Quantum Physics.title: A Few Reveal Many: Constraint-Enhanced Learning of Many-Body Quantum Systems
Quantum Physics.summary: Discovering properties of many-body quantum systems is challenging due to the large number of parameters involved. Here, we show that harnessing fundamental constraints among quantum observables improves quantum learning, enabling the inference of exponentially many quantities from a linear number of direct measurements. We leverage this result to design constraint-enhanced algorithms for evaluating key quantum features such as Entanglement and Magic in 100-qubit simulators. At a fixed number of measurement shots, they achieve up to an 83% reduction in relative error compared with protocols based on constructing "classical shadows" of quantum states. Quantum constraints themselves are therefore a resource for exploring large quantum systems, guiding the allocation of the measurement budget to highly informative observables.

Quantum Physics.title: A High-Frequency Flux-Driven DC-SQUID Threshold Detector at the Single-Microwave-Photon Energy Scale: A Numerical Feasibility Study
Quantum Physics.summary: In our recent work (Phys. Rev. B \textbf{113}, 224503 (2026)), we showed numerically that rapidly sweeping the bias current of a current-biased Josephson junction threshold detector (CBJJ-JTD) drives it out of equilibrium. This substantially reduces the effect of thermal noise on microwave detection and may enable threshold detection near the energy of a single microwave photon. The scheme requires very low damping ($β\leq 10^{-4}$) and a very fast bias-current sweep ($v/β\geq 1$), both of which are difficult to achieve with available junctions and low-pass-filtered cryogenic measurement lines. Here we propose a more experimentally accessible nonequilibrium threshold detector based on a high-frequency flux-driven direct-current superconducting quantum interference device (DC-SQUID) and investigate it by numerically solving the resistively and capacitively shunted junction (RCSJ) equations. The applied flux drives a circulating supercurrent and sustains nonequilibrium phase dynamics throughout the bias-current sweep, removing the need for a fast sweep or for transient oscillations set by the initial phase. Using typical experimental device parameters, we calculate switching-current distributions (SCDs) with and without a microwave input for both driven and undriven SQUIDs. We quantify detection performance using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves and their area under the curve (AUC). The simulations show that high-frequency flux drive reduces the impact of thermal noise and enables statistical discrimination of weak microwave pulses at the single-photon energy scale. We also numerically estimate detector characteristics such as phase selectivity and dynamic range.

Quantum Physics.title: Subquantum Pilot-Wave System Theory: Structural and Amplitude Nonequilibrium under Source Fields
Quantum Physics.summary: A source in the Schrodinger equation changes the norm of the guiding wave, apparently conflicting with the conservation of probability.
