In source-extended de Broglie-Bohm dynamics the conflict disappears: probability is carried by the particle ensemble, while the wavefunction guides its motion. The difficulty is then different. What does quantum equilibrium mean when the particle distribution remains normalized but the guiding density does not? We show that the departure has two independent components: a structural one, measured by the Kullback--Leibler divergence between the particle distribution and the normalized guiding density, and an amplitude one, measured by the Born weight. The Born rule holds precisely when both are equilibrated. Their evolution is governed by the complex source-to-wavefunction ratio; scale covariance further distinguishes an independently prescribed source, against which the amplitude of the wave matters, from state-dependent generators for which rescaling remains a symmetry. We develop a source-aware analytical--computational method, combining exact or semi-analytical guiding fields with Bohmian trajectory transport, ensemble quadrature and independent numerical checks. Free-space impulses expose the limits of global diagnostics and an exact jump rule; a driven ring has constant Born weight but either periodic or secular structural departure; oscillators show both source-generated structural change and amplitude-only evolution, including a finite-horizon weak-drive plateau far below its frozen-particle value; and a coupled two-body model exhibits nonlocal guidance and evolving particle entanglement. The source-free, initially equilibrated sector recovers standard quantum mechanics.

Quantum Physics.title: Two Operational Principles Single Out Quantum Theory
Quantum Physics.summary: Within a finite-dimensional causal operational-probabilistic theory (OPT), we show that adding just two postulates, local equivalence and purification, suffices to derive the mathematical structure of quantum theory as a whole, without separately assuming quantum rules for states, measurements, composites, or transformations. This resolves the question raised by Chiribella, D'Ariano, and Perinotti (CDP) [Phys. Rev. A 81, 062348 (2010)]. The key step is to establish homogeneity of state cones by combining infinitesimal cone-preserving deformations obtained from these postulates with geometric optimization. CDP purification requires every normalized state to be purifiable and purifications of the same state on any common ancilla to be related by a reversible channel on that ancilla. Our alternative assigns each system one operationally equivalent ancilla that purifies all its normalized states, requiring such reversible equivalence only there. Together with local equivalence, this condition also yields quantum theory.

Quantum Physics.title: photon number correlations in harmonics driven with classical and quantum light
Quantum Physics.summary: Recent reports of nonclassical intensity correlations in harmonic generation raised questions about whether strong harmonic correlations necessarily imply genuinely quantum behaviour. Here, we compare the low-photon-number perturbative harmonic generation driven by classical and bright squeezed vacuum sources. The latter generates strong auto- and cross-correlations in the harmonic spectrum. Cauchy-Schwarz inequality and heralding measurements show that the cross-correlations are fully classical and can be explained by the common fluctuations from the driving field. A visible scaling of the measured correlation function with mean harmonic flux is observed, which is well-explained by a click detector-response model.
Quantum Physics.comment: 13 pages (8 main, 5 supplemental), 8 figures (5 main, 3 supplemental), Submitted to Optics Express

Quantum Physics.title: Coherent Control of Single-Photon Emission in Broadband Plasmonic Resonators
Quantum Physics.summary: Encoding phase information with quantum emitters in metallic optical nanocavities is challenging due to ultrafast relaxation induced by the broadband nature of the plasmonic near field. Using macroscopic quantum electrodynamics theory, we demonstrate that an individual emitter strongly coupled to a plasmonic nanocavity field that is driven by a pulsed laser with frequency comb spectrum undergoes spontaneous emission of well-resolved one-photon pulses whose amplitude scales quadratically with the number of frequency comb components due to coherent accumulation, and ultrashort non-exponential temporal profiles with duration set by the light-matter coupling strength. Conditions are discussed for exponentially suppressing the probability of two or more emission events within the lifetime of the coupled emitter-nanocavity system. The spectral signatures of the optimal one-photon wavepackets are discussed. This work paves the way for the development of ultrafast laser-triggered single-photon emitters using atoms and molecules in optical nanocavities.

Quantum Physics.title: Secure PAC Learning: Sample-Budget Laws and Quantum Data-Path Admissibility
Quantum Physics.summary: Security in machine learning is fragile when data are exfiltrated or perturbed, yet existing frameworks rarely connect data-path security to learnability. In this work, we develop an operational theory of secure learning grounded in the probably-approximately-correct (PAC) viewpoint. An explicit stopping time combines the event that a trained hypothesis attains a target accuracy with the event that a run-based validation gate halts within a finite sample budget. We derive a closed-form sufficient budget requirement for this joint PAC-within-budget guarantee under an admissible random-classification-noise channel. We then specialize the construction to a BB84-like quantum label path. Under the stated ideal single-qubit, authenticated-classical-channel, memoryless, basis-symmetric, collective-attack, asymptotic, and one-way-reconciliation assumptions, the standard Holevo bound gives the protocol-specific information-advantage criterion $1-2h(η) > 0$, with the threshold $η_{\mathrm{BB84}} \simeq 0.11$. The quantum layer is not invoked to reduce distribution-free PAC sample complexity; rather, it turns a designer-chosen classical noise tolerance into a physically testable, protocol-dependent security condition by linking information acquisition to observable disturbance. Below the threshold, the PAC and information-advantage conditions provide complementary statistical and physical guarantees; at or above it, the present protocol and proof no longer certify the latter. Basis sifting is incorporated explicitly in the conversion from sifted-sample budgets to expected raw channel uses.

Quantum Physics.title: Coherence-generating power deviation: Fluctuations and input selectivity beyond average coherence generation
Quantum Physics.summary: Coherence-generating power (CGP) tells how much coherence a quantum process produces on average from incoherent inputs, but an average can hide where that coherence comes from. We introduce the coherence-generating power deviation (CGPD), the standard deviation of the generated Hilbert--Schmidt coherence over the uniform simplex of incoherent states. CGPD turns coherence generation into a landscape: a small value signals robust production across input populations, whereas a large value reveals selective conversion of particular population imbalances. By representing unitary coherence generation as a quadratic response on population space, we obtain exact first and second moments in arbitrary finite dimension. We prove that every nontrivial unitary generator must fluctuate, and we separate this unavoidable isotropic fluctuation from excess anisotropy. The resulting distinction between average strength and input selectivity has direct consequences for benchmarking, reliability guarantees, input-ensemble susceptibility, and four-copy measurement protocols; it also extends naturally to unital quantum channels. Matched quantum-walk and quasiperiodic-transport examples show that topology and localization can leave CGP unchanged while substantially changing CGPD, revealing structure invisible to the mean alone.

Quantum Physics.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
Quantum Physics.summary:
A streaming algorithm can keep classical or quantum memory, and its input arrives in adversarial or random order. Each resource alone is known to beat the basic model exponentially, but it was not known whether random order can help a quantum algorithm. We compare the four models by exponential space separations: every pair is separated on some problem and tied on another, and the two models with one resource each beat each other on different problems, one direction for random inputs, by concurrent work of Bouland, Ding, and Jain.
  The new phenomenon is that quantum memory and random order together can be exponentially stronger than each alone. We show this on a streaming version of Hidden Matching in which the bits of $x\in\{0,1\}^N$ arrive many times and $m\le\sqrt{N}$ matching requests must be answered on arrival. In random order a quantum algorithm uses $O(\log N\log m)$ space, while classical algorithms need $Ω(\sqrt{N})$, and quantum algorithms need $Ω(m)$ when all data comes before the requests. Two properties explain this. Consumability: answering a request destroys the quantum state. Replenishment: the state can be rebuilt from bits that keep arriving, which random order supplies and a data-first order does not. We prove that one quantum message answering $m$ Hidden Matching requests needs $Ω(m)$ qubits, a conjecture of Gilboa, Jain, and McClean, for $m\le N^{1/2-δ}$.
  The rest comes from Noisy Gap Cycle, a problem of Assadi and Sundaresan: tell whether a graph is a union of cycles of length $k$ or $2k$. With long cycles it needs linear space in all four models: we extend their random-order lower bound to quantum algorithms and obtain the first quantum random-order lower bounds for natural graph problems. With short cycles, $\mathrm{polylog}(n)$ classical bits suffice in random order, but adversarial order requires polynomial quantum space.
Quantum Physics.comment: v2: Significantly changed compared to v1

Quantum Physics.title: Causal Consistency and Cost of Quantum Control
Quantum Physics.summary: An unknown quantum state can supply the information needed to control a computation, but how much quantum data must be consumed to perform a prescribed action? We connect this resource question to causal consistency within the quantum state space. No-signaling requires identical observable predictions for remotely chosen ensemble preparations of the same complete input; quantum distinguishability then converts this requirement into finite-copy bounds. For amplitude amplification, we identify an exact low-copy obstruction and establish a dimension-independent, optimal quadratic dependence of the copy cost on angular gain at fixed accuracy, uniformly over arbitrary pure inputs. A coherent protocol attains this scaling without reconstructing a classical state description. Prior knowledge of a real two-level family additionally permits exponentially decreasing error with the copy budget at fixed gain. These results separate the resources needed to perform a specified quantum operation from those needed for universal state reconstruction. The central connection is operational: physical consistency restricts which distinctions a controller can expose, and the information carried by its complete input determines the cost of doing so. This links a causal requirement to quantitative limits on converting quantum data into computational control.

Quantum Physics.title: Machine Learning Electronic Hamiltonian with Long-Range Effects and External Fields
Quantum Physics.summary: Conventional machine-learning electronic Hamiltonian (MLEH) models rely on a local-environment approximation and can miss the effects of long-range (LR) interactions and external fields. Here, we introduce MLEH-LR, a framework that incorporates these effects into Hamiltonian prediction. Benchmarks across materials with different polarizations and dimensionalities demonstrate substantial improvements in the accuracy of the predicted Hamiltonians and resulting electronic structures. MLEH-LR enables accurate, large-scale, high-throughput electronic-structure calculations, as demonstrated for zigzag boron nitride ribbons under transverse electric fields. These calculations allow us to formulate a quantitative relation describing the joint width and field dependence of the band gap and to reveal the electronic mechanisms underlying its field response. Our work provides an efficient method and tool for studying electronic structure in materials where long-range electrostatics and external fields play an important role.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact stress-tensor fluctuations from conformal symmetry and black hole radiation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Semiclassical gravity is sourced by the expectation value of the stress tensor, and it is reliable only if the fluctuations around this value are small. In two dimensions, conformal symmetry captures the essential physics of Hawking radiation in its s-wave sector and determines the mean value exactly, for any background and any quantum state. We show that it also determines the local fluctuations of the null components $T_{\pm\pm}$. The square of the stress tensor is defined by the operator product expansion, up to a multiple $α$ of $\partial_\pm^2T_{\pm\pm}$ that labels point-splitting prescriptions. Its transformation law under the conformal map to locally inertial coordinates gives the variance in closed form. The relative fluctuation scales as $1/c$, with $c$ the central charge. For the Schwarzschild black hole it is $22/5c$ for the Hawking flux at infinity, that of flat-space thermal radiation. At the horizon it is $-44α/3c$ for the outgoing flux and $(238+720α)/5c$ for the ingoing flux that drives the backreaction. Both reduce to $22/5c$ for $α=-3/10$, which corresponds to the Möbius-covariant prescription. For large $c$ these results support the semiclassical approximation.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 13 pages, 1 table. 5 pages of main text and 8 pages of appendices

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ (leading) and $Δ=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $Δ=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$. This is achieved by taking advantage of the dS invariance of the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors of the photon field strength. In our outlook, we draw inspiration from a recent proposal for the microscopic description of $dS_4$ higher-spin gravity where conformal gauge fields in 3 dimensions play a central role, and we investigate a possible connection of the $Δ=1$ late-time operator with a conformal spin-1 gauge field in 3 dimensions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 43 pages = 39 pages + references. v2: Misprint in normalization of late time operators fixed. Missed terms in eqs. (2.7) and (7.9) inserted. Other minor misprints fixed. Matches published version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this work, we investigate how the one-loop running of local couplings in weakly nonlocal, super-renormalizable completions of $R+R^{2}$ gravity affects the predictions of the Starobinsky model. Our study is motivated by the larger scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by recent data. For a canonical inflaton at first order in slow roll, we derive the response of the observables to an arbitrary fractional deformation $Δ$ of the Einstein-frame potential $V$. We find that it is governed by $\mathcal{R}[Δ]=(V/V')Δ'$, and that the shift of the logarithm of the slow-roll parameter is twice the logarithmic derivative of the trajectory average of $\mathcal{R}$. This provides a test which requires one differentiation only. Deformations with constant $\mathcal{R}$, which we call removable, change the E-model exponent and shift $n_s$ at $O(\ln N/N^{2})$ only, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds, while $\mathcal{R}\propto N^{k}$ gives $Δn_s=[2k^{2}/(k+1)]\mathcal{R}/N$. When the running is improved at the Einstein-frame Hubble rate, the renormalization-group time is half the logarithm of the tree-level potential and the gravitational flow is removable. Under a naturalness condition, a matching to the nonlocality scale yields $|Δn_s|\lesssim3\times10^{-4}$, a factor of about $30$ below the shift preferred by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). However, for a scale tied to the Jordan-frame curvature, the same flow is not removable and $Δn_s\simeq K/3$, where $K$ is a linear combination of the running parameters. Removability is a property of the flow together with the scale prescription. None of the deformations proposed since ACT DR6 that raise $n_s$ to the preferred value is removable. These results hold within a projected truncation of the local couplings and a first-order improvement of the potential.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 42 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables, substantially revised, and references added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: History-Dependent Mode Selection in a Driven Holographic Superfluid
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study finite-rate mode selection among competing Landau-unstable modes in a holographic superfluid. The first mode to reach a prescribed amplitude need not be the instantaneously fastest-growing one. Time-dependent linear evolution on the driven homogeneous background closely reproduces the modal amplitudes obtained from full bulk evolution. Protocols with identical present driving conditions can reverse the relative ordering of two modes. For the controlled histories studied here, the change in their logarithmic amplitude ratio is well approximated by the excess accumulated differential QNM gain.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Thermodynamics of hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite chemical potential with Gauss-Bonnet corrections
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the confinement/deconfinement transition of the hard wall model of AdS/QCD at finite quark density in five-dimensional Einstein--Maxwell--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, with the back-reaction of the quark matter on the geometry included. The deconfined phase is a charged Gauss--Bonnet black hole, and the confined phase is thermally charged AdS cut off in the infrared. The infrared value of the gauge field, which Lee, Park and Sin fixed by requiring a consistent quark number, becomes a function of the Gauss--Bonnet coupling. We obtain the transition line in closed form at fixed quark chemical potential and at fixed quark number density. At fixed density the transition passes through a region where the two phases coexist. A negative Gauss--Bonnet coupling raises the transition temperature and extends the confined phase to higher density. A value inside the causality bound gives a transition temperature at zero density close to the lattice value. In the dense confined phase we compute the masses and decay constants of the $ρ$ meson and its radial excitations. All masses increase with density. A WKB analysis relates the increase to a shorter effective size of the confining region, and at nuclear density the $ρ$ mass rises by about one percent.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Generalized eigenstate thermalization beyond leading order in 2D large $c$ CFTs
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a Fock-space formulation that reduces expectation values of vacuum-family quasi-primaries in quantum Korteweg--de Vries (qKdV) eigenstates to a free-bosonic problem, and employ it to test the generalized eigenstate thermalization hypothesis (GETH) in 2D conformal field theories with a large central charge. We prove that the first two qKdV charges $Q_1$ and $Q_3$ lift all degeneracies except along at most countably many curves in the $(c,\,Δ)$ plane, where $c$ is the central charge and $Δ$ denotes the highest weight of the conformal family, so that the full-qKdV simultaneous eigenstates are unambiguously determined by $Q_1$ and $Q_3$. Based on this, a comprehensive toolkit for testing GETH within the scope of vacuum-family observables, i.e. equating qKdV eigenstates and thermal states of the generalized Gibbs ensemble in the sense of expectation values of vacuum-family local observables, is provided in this paper. We argue that GETH is satisfied when the infinite tower of qKdV charges is considered. A more restrictive form of the GETH, namely that all expectations of local observables of a definite level should be expressible in terms of the first few qKdV charges, is directly falsified at subleading order in the large-$c$ expansion. Specifically, at levels 6 and 8 in the vacuum family, expectation values of quasi-primaries in simultaneous eigenstates of the qKdV charges are not determined by any finite number of the lowest-index qKdV charges. The question of whether additional microscopic information about the eigenstate is required is left for future work.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: A new author is added to the list

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Classifying double copies and multicopies in AdS
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, we draw a parallel between solutions of pure three-dimensional gravity with a negative cosmological constant and classical double copies in four dimensions. In the former case, topological solutions, such as the BTZ black hole, deficit angles, and naked singularities, emerge from identifying points in AdS using elements from its isometry algebra $so(2,2)$. The type of solution corresponds one-to-one with the orbits of $so(2,2)$. We demonstrate how various double copies of four-dimensional AdS gravity similarly arise from the $so(2,3)$ isometry elements, which also correspond one-to-one with their orbits through a Penrose-type transform. We classify all such elements and generate the corresponding double copies, which include AdS black holes, black branes, and many others. The double-copy isometries originate from the centralizer of a given AdS isometry, allowing us to define canonical coordinates associated with its Abelian part. Additionally, the two Casimir invariants of $so(2,3)$ feature in the metrics via the characteristic polynomial of the AdS symmetry parameter. Our classification naturally extends to higher spins, providing nonequivalent multicopies at the linearized level.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 101 pages; v2: major revision of types II and III; all types are now identified with known solutions; added the relation between the metric structure functions and the characteristic polynomial of the background symmetry parameter; refs added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: False-vacuum bubbles in sphaleron scattering
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the collision dynamics of two bright sphalerons in a (1+1)-dimensional deformed $φ^6$ scalar field theory with a symmetric potential possessing false vacua. Two one-parameter realizations of the model, referred to as the barrier and well models, are considered and their static and linear instability properties are first reviewed. We then study head-on collisions of boosted sphalerons over a broad range of initial velocities and deformation parameters. The scattering dynamics exhibit a rich variety of final states, including the production of kink-antikink pairs, long-lived oscillons in true and false vacuum, multiple oscillons propagating in false-vacuum regions, and radiative decay. A particularly remarkable outcome is the emergence of a long-lived bubble of the false broken vacuum bounded by a kink-antikink pair, which repeatedly collapses and re-expands before eventually decaying into an oscillon. These results demonstrate that deformed $φ^6$ theories with false vacua exhibit considerably richer sphaleron dynamics than previously known and provide new insight into the role of unstable localized configurations in nonlinear field theories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Massive Particles in Carrollian Holography
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Understanding how massive particles are encoded in boundary operators is a central problem in Carrollian holography. We construct a three-dimensional Carrollian description of a massive scalar in four-dimensional flat spacetime, together with an explicit bulk-to-boundary integral transform. In this construction, nonzero mass requires infinitely many linearly independent primary states, while the absence of bulk spin imposes relations among their descendants. We show that these relations are equivalent to null-state decoupling and give a local constraint on the boundary fields. The integral transform preserves the full Poincaré symmetry and maps bulk scalar data to fields satisfying this constraint. We also obtain two- and three-point functions and the associated formal operator product expansion coefficients. The integral transform evaluates bulk data at complex momenta, making analytic continuation essential in Lorentzian signature. This construction provides a concrete starting point for relating massive scattering amplitudes to Carrollian correlators and for reconstructing bulk fields from boundary data.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Rotating End of the World
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the thermodynamics and interior structures of dynamical end of the world (EoW) branes in the rotating BTZ black hole. By mapping the induced metric of the branes to an effective Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) system, we derive the first law of thermodynamics for the boundary conformal field theory (BCFT), incorporating boundary degrees of freedom. To construct this thermodynamics, we adopt two frameworks of black hole chemistry and the duality between the JT black hole and the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model. In addition, we verify that the shadow entropy is equivalent to the boundary entropy via Hubeny-Ryu-Takayanagi (HRT) surfaces. Furthermore, we explore the possible interior configurations of the EoW brane inside the horizon. Two representative configurations, namely single and double-joint EoW branes, are considered. These disparate configurations share the same exterior brane configuration outside the horizon. By comparing their energies, we show that a transition could occur within the horizon.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entanglement, equivalence principle, and HBAR entropy, in a new bumblebee black hole
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate quantum correlations, atomic excitation, and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) entropy near a recently proposed bumblebee black hole with spacelike or lightlike Lorentz violating vacuum configurations. Using localized scalar field packets and the near horizon Rindler correspondence, we evaluate the logarithmic negativity and mutual information as functions of observer position, packet frequency, and geometric deformation. Configurations with the same geometry yield identical correlation measures. Positive geometric deformations partially counteract entanglement degradation, with the largest differences occurring at low frequencies. We also compute the excitation probability of a freely falling two level atom using the time coordinate normalized at spatial infinity. At leading near horizon order and within the frequency hierarchy adopted, its thermal factor agrees with the local flat spacetime acceleration radiation result. Finally, we derive the HBAR entropy flux and its relation to the radiative horizon area loss using the canonical conserved energy. The area coefficient depends on the causal character of the vacuum even for configurations with identical geometries: the spacelike case acquires a factor set by the bumblebee coupling, while the lightlike case gives the usual one quarter coefficient. These coefficients reproduce the corresponding thermodynamic entropy factors.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 19 pages and 5 figures -- version accepted for publication in Physics Letters B

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Pauli Spectra as a Boundary Spectroscope in Quantum Spin Chains
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show that Pauli spectra provide a boundary spectroscope in critical quantum spin chains, resolving microscopic boundary fingerprints and finite responses to physical boundary changes. Universal logarithmic corrections to stabilizer Renyi entropy can remain identical across distinct boundary configurations, while their finite contributions retain information about how the physical boundaries are related. Using critical Ising chains, we demonstrate that suitable combinations of Pauli moments isolate normalization-independent responses to boundary reversal and reveal nonadditive contributions associated with the joint boundary configuration. These responses become analytically accessible through an exact term-by-term correspondence that organizes individual Pauli magnitudes into classical-group statistical structures, with their moments represented by discrete Selberg sums associated with unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic ensembles. In particular, fixed-boundary reversal admits an exact symplectic-character representation, while the same framework provides access to boundary-sensitive behavior at the Rényi transition. Our results establish a new connection between nonstabilizerness and boundary criticality through the exact statistical structures of classical-group ensembles.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: BPS Chaos and Fortuity in Higgs Branches I: The Gepner Point
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The BPS states in Calabi-Yau compactifications of type II string theory can sometimes be described using quiver quantum mechanics whose Higgs branch is a complete intersection manifold. Their degeneracy resembles that of BPS black holes. A small fraction of these states corresponds to multi-center supergravity brane configurations and can be continued to the (near-Higgs) Coulomb branch. We identify them as monotone states. The overwhelming majority of states, known as pure-Higgs states, are fortuitous states, which concentrate at a particular $R$-charge. This division has a precise mathematical meaning as two different types of cohomologies of the Higgs branch target space. We argue that a natural probe of BPS chaos in these models is the Berry/Chern curvature. In the case of the Gepner model, we use localization techniques in an auxiliary two-dimensional CFT to compute the curvature, its RMT properties, and deviations from it.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory: partition functions beyond large-$N$ and quantum holography
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We identify families of Bethe vacua in the chiral $M^{3,2}$ theory whose individual free energies grow as $N^{3/2}$. High-precision data support closed forms for their all-order perturbative $1/N$ expansions. At a distinguished mixed Chern--Simons coupling, the baryonic magnetic flux distinguishes members of this family of vacua. We also study the three-sphere partition function numerically in the 't Hooft limit and Cardy limit, and propose an all-order Airy formula. The four-derivative and one-loop corrections are precision tests of holography.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Tachyon and massless sectors of the bosonic string effective action
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Recently, it has been observed that in certain schemes of the bosonic string effective action, the non-derivative tachyon appears only in the tachyon potential, while all other couplings involve covariant derivatives of the tachyon and massless fields. Within these schemes, a minimal basis can be found whose coupling constants are constrained by T-duality upon circle reduction. Using this constraint, one obtains sets of couplings at each order of \(α'\) that are invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the tachyon. In this paper, we observe that consistency of these T-dual sets with S-matrix elements requires an appropriate field redefinition, such that each set becomes invariant under Buscher rules supplemented by higher-derivative corrections for all base-space fields except the metric, dilaton, and tachyon. This separates the couplings into a massless sector and a tachyon sector. We determine the six-derivative couplings in the massless sector, with all coupling constants fixed, and find two T-dual couplings in the tachyon sector with arbitrary coupling constants. We show that the leading-order action and the massless-sector couplings exactly reproduce the expansion of the sphere-level S-matrix element of two tachyons and two massless vertex operators at six-momentum order, and that the coupling constant of the four-tachyon coupling in the tachyon sector is fixed by the expansion of the four-tachyon S-matrix element at six-momentum order.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 26 pages, no figure, latex file; it appears in JHEP

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In vacuum anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, the geometry admits a perfect tessellation by a geodesic network. This tessellation characterizes the background exactly, and a partial entanglement entropy (PEE) tensor-network toy model of AdS/CFT can be defined on it. It has so far been unclear whether this construction can be extended beyond vacuum AdS. In this paper we take the first step in this direction. We show that the exterior region of the Schwarzschild black hole and its Einstein--Rosen bridge are perfectly tessellated by a specific geodesic gas emitted from the boundary, so that Crofton reconstruction holds in these regions. We then prove that such a geodesic tessellation and the Crofton reconstruction it defines extend to more generic Riemannian manifolds. This allows us to construct a PEE tensor-network model of holographic duality on more generic geometric backgrounds. In the case of the PEE tensor-network model for the Schwarzschild background, we can concretely realize the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Ryu--Takayanagi formula and the ER=EPR proposal. Our approach opens a new route towards holographic toy models beyond AdS/CFT.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 33 pages, 4 figures; v2: references fixed; v3: figure updated

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: CFT-Inspired Two-Horizon Thermodynamics as a Diagnostic for the Bi-Hair Organization of NUT Charge
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: After decades without a fully self-consistent thermodynamic formulation, recent proposals for Lorentzian Taub-NUT spacetime have yielded several inequivalent descriptions, each satisfying its own first law and Smarr relation, leaving unresolved which formulation is physically preferred. In this Letter, we introduce a two-horizon diagnostic whose left- and right-moving thermodynamic temperatures are fixed via the harmonic mean relations before the thermodynamic variables are chosen. For uncharged Taub-NUT spacetime, the left-moving first law closes with the mass and NUT charge, whereas, within the restricted homogeneous class examined here, the right-moving first law requires an additional thermodynamic secondary hair $J_n = mn$. This result supports a bi-hair thermodynamic organization of the NUT parameter through $N = n$ and $J_n = mn$. Furthermore, this two-horizon framework offers a new opportunity toward addressing similar thermodynamic non-uniqueness in other two-horizon NUT-charged systems when the first law and Smarr relation alone do not identify a physically preferred formulation.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: General non-extremal rotating charged AdS black hole solutions with four independent charge parameters in $D=4$, STU gauged supergravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present an exact solution for generic non-extremal rotating, charged black holes with a negative cosmological constant in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2, U(1)^4$ gauged supergravity. This general non-extremal solution contains seven independent parameters related to the mass, rotation, two electric and two magnetic charges, as well as a nonzero cosmological constant. It generalizes the four-dimensional Cvetič-Youm black hole solution to the gauged supergravity case. We anticipate that this is the only regular black hole solution in four-dimensional gauged STU model without any Misner string singularity and/or C-metric-like conical defect on the symmetry axes. We also investigate its thermodynamic property and give the Killing-Stäckel tensor responsible for the separability of Hamilton-Jacobi and massless Klein-Gordon equations. Various special cases related to the known solution are discussed, and its BPS limit is also analyzed. Our solution provides a new background to test the AdS$_4$/CFT$_3$ correspondence and to study the microscopic entropy via extremization of the BPS index.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum cosmological perturbations in bouncing models with mimetic dark matter
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We calculate the power spectrum of cosmological perturbations originated from quantum vacuum fluctuations in bouncing scenarios proposed in Ref.~\cite{chamseddine2014cosmology} in the framework of mimetic cosmology. We show that all physically relevant models produce scale-invariant spectral indices and amplitudes compatible with observations, provided that the bounce occurs at length scales $t_0$ inside the physically reasonable interval $10^5 l_p < t_0 < 10^9 l_p$. We also show that by slightly modifying the scalar field potential proposed in Ref.~\cite{chamseddine2014cosmology}, we can obtain the observed red-tilted spectral index, with the same amplitude constraints. The underlying theory contains instability problems yet to be solved. However, the methods we constructed and the results we obtained may be sufficiently general to be applied to the infrared limit of some yet to be constructed healthy mimetic cosmology, providing reasonable bouncing cosmological models without the need for any background quantum effect.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Chiral and deconfinement thermodynamics of the Polyakov-quark linear sigma model with and without charm quark: an SU(3) versus SU(4) comparison
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Using the Polyakov-loop extended linear-sigma model (PLSM), we investigate strongly interacting matter at finite temperature and baryon density by comparing the three-flavor (u,d,s) and four-flavor (u,d,s,c) formulations on equal footing, with the aim of isolating the thermal contribution of the charm quark. The model describes chiral dynamics through explicit and spontaneous symmetry breaking and reproduces the vacuum spectra of scalar and pseudoscalar mesons. Confinement is incorporated through a logarithmic Polyakov-loop potential calibrated to the continuum lattice-QCD equation of state (EoS). Within the mean-field approximation, we calculate light-, strange-, and charm-quark condensates, the Polyakov loop, and bulk thermodynamic observables, including pressure, trace anomaly, and entropy density, over broad ranges of temperature and baryon chemical potential. We also determine the chiral and deconfinement pseudocritical boundaries and represent them as phase boundaries and three-dimensional order-parameter surfaces. After tuning the Polyakov sector to lattice-QCD pressure and trace-anomaly data, the resulting entropy density agrees with HotQCD 2+1(+1)-flavor results throughout the crossover region. At zero baryon density, the non-strange condensate melts at Tc = 210 MeV in SU(3) and 218 MeV in SU(4), with curvature parameters kappa=0.018 and 0.017. Because mc>>Tc, charm remains thermally suppressed across the crossover. After normalization to the corresponding Stefan-Boltzmann limits, the SU(3) and SU(4) EoS nearly coincide below T~2Tc. Charm mainly contributes through a higher ideal-gas limit, a gradual high-temperature tail, and the flavor ordering u,d->s->c. For all baryon chemical potentials accessible within mean-field theory, the hadron-parton transition remains a smooth crossover.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 15 pages, 7 figures, 1 table submitted to Physical Review C

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Schwarzschild Ringdown Time Prescription on Critical Kerr Plunges
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: For a Schwarzschild plunge, constant-amplitude quasinormal-mode convergence has been tied to the source's advanced time at $r=0$, lying $9.435M$ after the $(2,2)$ strain peak. On real prograde critical Kerr plunges, $P(r_-)<0$ forces the ingoing time $v$ to diverge logarithmically at the inner horizon while $u_K$ stays finite. Matching $v$ to $-u_K$ at the unique interior zero $P(r_0)=0$ yields a parameter-free onset hierarchy $(u_{\rm H},u_{r_0},u_{\rm C})$ that recovers $9.435M$ as $a\to 0$ and predicts two-stage residual decay and frequency locking at $(6.85M,11.35M,13.35M)$ on an $a/M=0.9$ eccentric plunge.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table, including Supplemental Material

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quasinormal Modes and Excitation Factors of a Parity-Symmetric Beyond-Horndeski Black Hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study scalar, electromagnetic, and Dirac perturbations of an asymptotically flat black hole in parity-symmetric beyond-Horndeski gravity. The quasinormal spectrum is computed with very-high-order WKB expansions and Padé resummation, with Cesàro means used to diagnose internal convergence. The dominant modes are independently tested by time-domain evolution with Prony extraction and by Chebyshev pseudospectral collocation; the latter also provides systematic frequency scans in both the metric-scale and physical ADM-mass normalizations. Excitation factors are obtained separately from Green-function residues by complex-contour integration. In the fixed metric-scale normalization, approaching Schwarzschild generally increases both the oscillation frequency and damping rate, whereas stronger deformation shifts the modes toward lower frequencies and weaker damping. In ADM-mass units, the mildly deformed solutions remain close to Schwarzschild, while the most deformed sector becomes enhanced and nonmonotonic because the asymptotic mass itself varies strongly. The independent methods agree very well, however the sixth-order WKB approximation used in [G. Antoniou, T. D. Pappas, P. Kanti, Phys. Rev. D 112, 084013 (2025)] is insufficient in certain regions of the parameter space: the fundamental-mode discrepancy reaches nine percent in the damping rate and the first-overtone discrepancy can be of order unity. The Schwarzschild excitation factors are recovered. In the strongly deformed regime, their magnitudes can differ from the Schwarzschild values by more than two orders of magnitude in the asymptotic tortoise-coordinate convention. We show that this large effect is predominantly due to the deformation-dependent displacement of the potential barrier in the tortoise coordinate: when its maximum is used as the origin, the excitation factors exhibit much more modest deviations.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Unruh-like effects and correlation harvesting between particle detectors in uniform motion in (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study Gaussian-switched Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the (2+1)-dimensional Minkowski vacuum and following four classes of uniformly accelerated trajectories: linear, catenary, cusped, and circular motion. We first determine how the single-detector transition probability and effective temperature depend on acceleration and the torsion-to-acceleration ratio $\bar{b}$, whose continuous variation connects these four trajectory classes. We find that both quantities generally increase with acceleration, while their dependence on $\bar{b}$ can become nonmonotonic depending on the energy gap. We also examine a correlation-harvesting protocol by two detectors following horizontally displaced copies of the same trajectory. Increasing acceleration or separation generally suppresses the harvested concurrence and quantum mutual information, but the extent of suppression at fixed acceleration depends strongly on the trajectory class. For each of the four trajectory classes, we identify regimes of genuine entanglement harvesting in which vacuum correlations alone suffice to entangle the detectors, while the communication contribution alone cannot overcome local noise.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A discrete series gauge field at the late-time boundary of $dS_4$
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the free Maxwell field on the planar patch of four-dimensional de Sitter spacetime ($dS_4$). We review its bulk canonical quantization in the Bunch-Davies vacuum, and we give a representation-theoretic viewpoint by studying the transformation properties of single-particle states under infinitesimal dS transformations. By taking the late-time limit, we identify two late-time operators with scaling dimensions $Δ=1$ (leading) and $Δ=2$ (subleading). We introduce CFT-inspired inner products invariant under the dS group ($SO(4,1)$) for states created by late-time operators acting on the Bunch-Davies vacuum. We explain how the unitary discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ associated with the photon are furnished by both operators, in contrast with the Maxwell field on $AdS$ where the $Δ=1$ operator corresponds to a non-normalizable mode. We also explain how the corresponding discrete series representations of $SO(4,1)$ split into a direct sum of representations corresponding to two helicities $+1$ and $-1$. This is achieved by taking advantage of the dS invariance of the self-dual and anti-self-dual sectors of the photon field strength. In our outlook, we draw inspiration from a recent proposal for the microscopic description of $dS_4$ higher-spin gravity where conformal gauge fields in 3 dimensions play a central role, and we investigate a possible connection of the $Δ=1$ late-time operator with a conformal spin-1 gauge field in 3 dimensions.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 43 pages = 39 pages + references. v2: Misprint in normalization of late time operators fixed. Missed terms in eqs. (2.7) and (7.9) inserted. Other minor misprints fixed. Matches published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)ρ(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(χ)\rangle =\langle ρ(χ)\rangle \langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $χ$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $σ_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(χ)=\langle σ_{DM}^2\rangle$. We investigate the cosmological implications of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter, and we conclude that this scale-dependent equation of state dark matter cannot be the sole component of dark matter in the Universe. Also the second aim of this work is to provide a sufficient explanation for the question why $K_0$ changes for each galaxy, where $K_0$ is the value of $K(r)$ at intermediate and large radii from the core of the galaxy. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of having distinct dark matter components which cluster differently, and thus controlling differently the dynamics of the Universe at various scales. Scale-dependent equation of state dark matter can control the galactic scales, while another component can dominate at cosmological scales and thus control the Universe at cosmological scales.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The shadow of rotating FJNW metric
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the astrophysical aspects of the rotating Fisher-Janis-Newman-Winicour (FJNW) metric recently derived in [1]. The Hamilton-Jacobi equation is used to obtain the shadow of the rotating FJNW metric. We find that increasing the angular momentum parameter a and the metric parameter γleads to an increase in the size of the shadow. Finally, we study the deflection angle of light in the rotating FJNW spacetime.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Anti-de Sitter charges and maximal Cauchy hypersurfaces
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct conserved charges of asymptotic symmetries for negative-cosmological-constant vacuum spacetimes from the Neumann data for the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints on maximal conformally-compact Cauchy hypersurfaces. This gives a general and canonical initial value treatment of charges for vacuum spacetimes with timelike conformal boundary.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Fully constraining the neutron star equation of state requires combining observations from various channels that probe different density regimes. We perform a joint multiprobe inference of the equation of state using gravitational-wave observations from binary neutron star mergers, NICER mass-radius measurements of X-ray pulsars, and radio timing mass measurements of massive pulsars. We constrain the parametrized equation of state and perform Bayesian model selection among a set of candidate equations of state. The joint analysis yields a radius of $R_{1.4} = 11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83} \, \rm km$ for a canonical $1.4 \, M_\odot$ neutron star, and a maximum non-rotating neutron star mass of $M_{\rm max} = 2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23} \, M_\odot$ with $90\%$ credible intervals. Gravitational-wave and NICER observations constrain the equation of state at low to intermediate densities, while massive pulsar observations constrain it at high densities by requiring the equation of state to support the observed neutron star masses. We find no simple correlation between the stiffness of an equation of state and Bayesian evidence across different observational probes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Removability criterion for radiative corrections to the Starobinsky attractor in weakly nonlocal gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work, we investigate how the one-loop running of local couplings in weakly nonlocal, super-renormalizable completions of $R+R^{2}$ gravity affects the predictions of the Starobinsky model. Our study is motivated by the larger scalar spectral index $n_s$ preferred by recent data. For a canonical inflaton at first order in slow roll, we derive the response of the observables to an arbitrary fractional deformation $Δ$ of the Einstein-frame potential $V$. We find that it is governed by $\mathcal{R}[Δ]=(V/V')Δ'$, and that the shift of the logarithm of the slow-roll parameter is twice the logarithmic derivative of the trajectory average of $\mathcal{R}$. This provides a test which requires one differentiation only. Deformations with constant $\mathcal{R}$, which we call removable, change the E-model exponent and shift $n_s$ at $O(\ln N/N^{2})$ only, where $N$ is the number of $e$-folds, while $\mathcal{R}\propto N^{k}$ gives $Δn_s=[2k^{2}/(k+1)]\mathcal{R}/N$. When the running is improved at the Einstein-frame Hubble rate, the renormalization-group time is half the logarithm of the tree-level potential and the gravitational flow is removable. Under a naturalness condition, a matching to the nonlocality scale yields $|Δn_s|\lesssim3\times10^{-4}$, a factor of about $30$ below the shift preferred by the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). However, for a scale tied to the Jordan-frame curvature, the same flow is not removable and $Δn_s\simeq K/3$, where $K$ is a linear combination of the running parameters. Removability is a property of the flow together with the scale prescription. None of the deformations proposed since ACT DR6 that raise $n_s$ to the preferred value is removable. These results hold within a projected truncation of the local couplings and a first-order improvement of the potential.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 42 pages, 5 figures, 8 tables, substantially revised, and references added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A wormhole with two black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We report on a new three-parameter stationary solution of the four-dimensional vacuum Einstein equations, which describes a Lorentzian wormhole harboring two antipodal co-rotating black holes. These are hung from one of the two spacelike infinities by two semi-infinite cosmic strings with positive or negative tension. We evaluate the Komar masses and angular momenta of the two black holes, and check that these obey the usual Smarr relation, as well as the generalized first law for a system of collinear black holes and cosmic strings. While free from Misner strings, this spacetime allows closed timelike curves within a bounded volume. The metric also admits a naked ring singularity for almost all values of the parameters.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: EMRI Dephasing from a Torsion-Inspired Near-Zone Kerr Deformation: Motivated by Spin-Polarized Dark Matter
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive probes of weak conservative perturbations in the strong-field region of massive black holes. We study a phenomenological EMRI model motivated by Einstein--Cartan gravity in which a spin-polarized dark-matter spike is described by a Weyssenhoff fluid. After torsion is eliminated algebraically, the local spin contribution contains a repulsive exterior source $U_{tt}^{\rm spin}\propto-σ_0^2/r^3$. Solving the corresponding static linearized field equation, however, does not produce a global $1/r^3$ metric perturbation; the response contains a mass renormalization, a logarithmic $r^{-1}$ tail, and an $M/r^2$ term. We therefore introduce $g_{μν}^{\rm eff}=g_{μν}^{\rm Kerr}+αh_{μν}^{\rm eff}$ only as a local near-zone matching ansatz, not as a complete rotating Einstein--Cartan black-hole solution. Within this torsion-inspired deformation we compute circular equatorial inspirals and analytic-kludge waveforms. The fiducial model can produce large phase shifts in an idealized adiabatic calculation, but the forecast is optimistic and does not include a full LISA/Taiji response, Teukolsky/self-force fluxes, eccentricity, inclination, or high-dimensional parameter degeneracies. The results should be read as constraints on an effective near-zone operator rather than as a prediction of minimally coupled Einstein--Cartan dark matter.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Superluminal propagation in the magnetic NED reconstruction of the extremal Dymnikova black hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
We reconstruct the magnetic nonlinear electrodynamics (NED) source of the
  Dymnikova geometry on the branch \(\Iinv>0\) and analyze its
  electromagnetic perturbations on the fixed background. The reconstruction
  does not admit a Maxwell limit. The extraordinary characteristic cone
  gives a transverse speed \(v_\perp^2=(3u-5)/2\), with \(u=r^3/P^3\),
  which becomes superluminal for \(r>r_{\rm lum}=(7/3)^{1/3}P\). The
  principal system is pointwise hyperbolic in the finite exterior
  \(r\ge r_e\), with positive local quadratic energy, but not uniformly
  hyperbolic up to spatial infinity. The radial effective potential admits
  an exact reduction, \(V_{\rm em}=f\ell(\ell+1)\mathcal{A}/r^2+ff_{,r}q
  +f^2(q_{,r}+\frac34q^2)\), behaves as \(V_0\proptoε^2\) near the
  horizon, and grows as \(27r^4/(4P^6)\) at infinity. It is numerically
  positive on a fine grid up to \(r=50P\). The Dymnikova reconstruction
  does not satisfy the hypotheses of the Tomizawa--Suzuki theorem, since it
  lacks a Maxwell limit, yet it still produces superluminal extraordinary
  photons. The reconstructed NED branch is therefore mathematically
  consistent as a source of the Dymnikova background, but not causally
  acceptable with respect to the physical metric in the asymptotic region.
  The global positivity of the effective potential and the quasinormal
  spectrum are left as open problems.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exactly solvable Brill waves: explicit gravitational-wave initial data with trapped surfaces
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Vacuum initial data for pure gravitational waves on $\mathbb{R}^3$ (Brill waves) have so far been obtained only numerically. Here a one-parameter family is solved exactly: in toroidal coordinates the constraint separates, and a suitable seed function makes every mode equation hypergeometric. The data are real analytic and asymptotically flat and exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.8048\ldots$; their mass is an explicit series with a pole at $k_c$. Near $k_c$ the data provably contain trapped surfaces and an apparent horizon. A scaling symmetry yields further solvable families, one of them elementary.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures, 1 table. Companion paper: arXiv:2610.16773

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Entanglement, equivalence principle, and HBAR entropy, in a new bumblebee black hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate quantum correlations, atomic excitation, and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) entropy near a recently proposed bumblebee black hole with spacelike or lightlike Lorentz violating vacuum configurations. Using localized scalar field packets and the near horizon Rindler correspondence, we evaluate the logarithmic negativity and mutual information as functions of observer position, packet frequency, and geometric deformation. Configurations with the same geometry yield identical correlation measures. Positive geometric deformations partially counteract entanglement degradation, with the largest differences occurring at low frequencies. We also compute the excitation probability of a freely falling two level atom using the time coordinate normalized at spatial infinity. At leading near horizon order and within the frequency hierarchy adopted, its thermal factor agrees with the local flat spacetime acceleration radiation result. Finally, we derive the HBAR entropy flux and its relation to the radiative horizon area loss using the canonical conserved energy. The area coefficient depends on the causal character of the vacuum even for configurations with identical geometries: the spacelike case acquires a factor set by the bumblebee coupling, while the lightlike case gives the usual one quarter coefficient. These coefficients reproduce the corresponding thermodynamic entropy factors.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages and 5 figures -- version accepted for publication in Physics Letters B

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Relativistic Hydrodynamics as an Intersection Problem
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Ideal relativistic hydrodynamics admits a covariant description as an intersection problem in a symplectic space associated with spacetime. The independent fields are differential forms of degrees 0,1,3,4. Spacetime diffeomorphisms and shifts of the momentum one-form act Hamiltonianly; the zero locus of their moment map is a coisotropic subvariety encoding the transport equations. The spacetime metric and equation of state determine a Lagrangian submanifold, whose intersection with the coisotropic subvariety is precisely the Lichnerowicz--Carter system. We explain the geometric meaning of the canonical flow parameter, derive circulation and Ertel invariants directly from the constraints, and identify energy--momentum conservation with covariance of the constitutive Lagrangian. The nonrelativistic limit and a relation of entropy-level helicity to split Calabi--Yau geometry are briefly indicated.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitomagnetic Frame Memory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
We investigate the response of spatially separated spinning test particles to a finite-duration plane gravitational wave in the proper detector frame, {working to linear order in the wave amplitude.}
  Using Fermi normal coordinates and the gravitoelectromagnetic decomposition of the local metric, the spin evolution is governed, at leading order in the distance from the reference world-line, by the magnetic part of the Riemann tensor. A finite curvature profile with a non-vanishing gravitomagnetic pulse area induces a residual relative rotation of the spins, proportional to the time integral of the local gravitomagnetic field. The resulting change persists after the curvature has vanished and may be interpreted as a local frame-memory observable. This effect has the structure of a velocity-type memory of finite plane-wave curvature profiles and provides a direct operational probe of the integrated magnetic part of spacetime curvature.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Accepted for publication as a Letter in Physical Review D

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analytic Brill wave initial data with trapped surfaces
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Since Brill's work of 1959, the conformal factor of finite-amplitude Brill waves, the axisymmetric and time-symmetric vacuum initial data on $\mathbb{R}^3$ that describe pure gravitational radiation, has been obtained only numerically, up to the most recent studies. Here an explicit one-parameter family of such data is constructed; the data are real analytic and asymptotically flat, with trivial topology and a single end. The free metric function is a closed-form combination of elementary functions and a dilogarithm. The data have the toroidal conformal symmetry of Beig and Husa, and a change of variable of Natanzon type reduces every mode equation to the Gauss hypergeometric equation, so that the conformal factor is a series with explicit Gamma-function coefficients. A ground-state identity gives a sharp existence criterion: complete, asymptotically flat data exist precisely for $k<k_c=0.80480168\ldots$, and the explicit series is identified with the unique variational solution. The ADM mass is an absolutely convergent digamma series, with $m/a=πk^2/10+O(k^3)$ for small amplitudes and an explicit residue at its critical divergence. Sufficiently strong waves contain trapped surfaces: it is proved that for $k$ close to $k_c$ the rescaled conformal factor converges to an explicit function and explicit tori and spheres become outer trapped, so that the data contain an apparent horizon. A numerical search, restricted to equatorially symmetric star-shaped surfaces, finds marginally trapped (minimal) spheres, which appear in a fold near $k=0.7670$. A scaling symmetry of the mode problem generates further solvable families, whose simplest member has the elementary seed function $q=\frac12\log[1+4a^2ρ^2/(ρ^2+z^2+a^2)^2]$. No thin-torus or weak-field approximation is used.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Numerical Integration of Geodesic Motion in Non-Schwarzschild Spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: This contribution presents a method for numerically solving geodesic motion in Wolfram Mathematica applied on a system consisting of a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a thin Vogt-Letelier disk. While geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime is fully integrable due to its high degree of symmetry, the addition of a disk breaks the spherical symmetry and leads to a weak-integrable dynamical system. Particular attention is paid to the treatment of particle trajectories near the thin disk, where discontinuities in the derivatives of the metric may affect numerical stability and the conservation of integrals of motion. Several numerical treatments of disk crossings were implemented, arriving to a method based on the re-normalization of the four-velocity. The phase-space of the system is investigated using Poincaré sections and rotation number spectra.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Wavelet-domain flow-matching posterior estimation for LISA signals with data gaps
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) data stream will contain scheduled and unscheduled gaps, which break the stationarity of the instrumental noise and invalidate the standard frequency-domain likelihood. Amortized simulation-based inference (SBI) avoids explicit likelihood evaluations, but its application to months-long observations requires compressing high-dimensional, gapped time series while preserving information about source parameters. We develop an end-to-end amortized posterior estimation pipeline: the gapped data are mapped to noise-scaled Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) wavelet coefficients and summarized by a convolutional-Transformer network, trained jointly with a flow-matching (FM) posterior estimator, with optional importance-sampling correction. For a LISA-like signal observed for 3 months, the amortized FM posteriors are well calibrated on simulated observations whose waveforms and gaps were not seen in training. The FM posteriors agree closely with the benchmark, the posteriors from parallel-tempered Markov chain Monte Carlo (PTMCMC), although they exhibit moderately greater dispersion. Importance sampling efficiently reweights the FM posterior, achieving close agreement with the benchmark at modest additional cost.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Brans Dicke scalar-tensor gravity and unimodular FRW cosmology with Coleman-Weinberg potential
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: As an alternative gravity theories with respect to General Relativity, the Brans-Dicke scalar-tensor model is well known, in which the Brans-Dicke parameter the controls the best fit observational, and so its cosmological model is studied in the literature well. On the other side, the Coleman-Weinberg self-interaction scalar field potential coming from radiation corrections of Feynman diagrams is used to describe the best fit cosmic inflation phase and reheating phase. We study inflation in unimodular Brans-Dicke gravity with a Coleman-Weinberg potential. We investigate the observational constraints on the Brans-Dicke parameter \(ω\) and identify its allowed range in light of current cosmological data. Also, in the slow-roll regime, we derive inflation parameters and study the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ in terms of the model parameters, and determine the region of the parameter space allowed by observations. Comparing these predictions with the P-ACT-LB-BK18 constraints, we find that the model is consistent with the data at the $95\%$ CL level for $77\lesssimω\lesssim1148$ and within the $ 68\% $ CL for $134\lesssimω\lesssim272$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes in Einstein-phantom scalar-Gauss-Bonnet theory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the radial stability of nonlinearly scalarized black holes found in Einstein--phantom scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial and exponential couplings. Two branches of lower and primary are found for phantom scalarized black holes. The coupled scalar--metric perturbations reduce to a Schrödinger-type equation, after eliminating redundant metric perturbations. The lower branch including the pure quartic solutions has one growing mode, while positive zero-energy solutions for the primary branch could establish stability through the $S$-deformation method. Stable primary solutions are found for the exponential coupling. Also, we explore the connection between radial stability and thermodynamic analysis for two branches. Furthermore, we show that canonical scalarized black holes obtained from Einstein--scalar--Gauss--Bonnet theory with polynomial coupling reveals unstable lower and stable primary branches.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Geodesic Route toward Holography beyond AdS: Tessellating the Schwarzschild Black Hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In vacuum anti-de Sitter (AdS) space, the geometry admits a perfect tessellation by a geodesic network. This tessellation characterizes the background exactly, and a partial entanglement entropy (PEE) tensor-network toy model of AdS/CFT can be defined on it. It has so far been unclear whether this construction can be extended beyond vacuum AdS. In this paper we take the first step in this direction. We show that the exterior region of the Schwarzschild black hole and its Einstein--Rosen bridge are perfectly tessellated by a specific geodesic gas emitted from the boundary, so that Crofton reconstruction holds in these regions. We then prove that such a geodesic tessellation and the Crofton reconstruction it defines extend to more generic Riemannian manifolds. This allows us to construct a PEE tensor-network model of holographic duality on more generic geometric backgrounds. In the case of the PEE tensor-network model for the Schwarzschild background, we can concretely realize the Bekenstein--Hawking entropy, the Ryu--Takayanagi formula and the ER=EPR proposal. Our approach opens a new route towards holographic toy models beyond AdS/CFT.
