High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Kerr Metric in Canonical Harmonic Coordinates to All Orders
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We give in closed form the transformation from Boyer--Lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric, to all orders in Newton's constant and in the spin. This is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the MPM prescription and by the harmonic-gauge Einstein recursion sourced by the Kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. The chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the Cook--Scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. The proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom. Rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-Minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. This sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an MPM gauge moment. The exact chart selects the representative in which this third-PM homogeneous mode vanishes; imposing the same condition on the recursion removes the only residual ambiguity and fixes its solution uniquely. As a consequence, the canonical MPM iteration needs no finite-part regularisation and no harmonicity correction at any order. We give the exact gothic metric and the post-Minkowskian coefficients in closed form through fifth order, where an arctangent function first appears at fourth order. We find agreement with recent canonical MPM and amplitude-based results at fourth order, and we verify the construction in exact arithmetic through fifth order and twelfth order in the spin, with code made publicly available.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 36 pages. Codes available at Github https://github.com/pierrevanhove/kerr-metric-harmonic and Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/24397114

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Black hole equations of state and response functions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We systematically develop a framework for equilibrium thermodynamics in terms of thermodynamic representations, which are choices of thermodynamic potential and independent variables, one from each conjugate pair. In each representation, equations of state arise from first derivatives of the potential and response functions from its second derivatives. We apply this framework to ideal gases and to Schwarzschild black holes in a spherical cavity in various representations, interpreting the cavity area and its conjugate surface pressure as the thermodynamic volume and pressure of a holographically dual system. For this quasi-local Schwarzschild black hole, stability depends on the thermodynamic representation, or equivalently on which variables are held fixed under equilibrium perturbations. The large black hole branch is thermally stable at fixed volume but mechanically unstable under isothermal compression, while the system is mechanically stable under adiabatic compression everywhere. At fixed pressure, the black hole is thermally unstable throughout the physical state space. We also find that the thermal expansion coefficient is negative everywhere and show that isenthalpic expansion always cools the black hole. More broadly, the framework provides a systematic route to deriving equations of state and response functions for a wide class of black hole systems using quasi-local gravitational thermodynamics.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Published version: minor improvements. 31 pages + 2 appendices; 5 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Banana D-modules
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the holonomic $D$-module whose solutions are generic-mass banana Feynman integrals with complex propagator powers and spacetime dimension. We call this the banana $D$-module. Two properties of the banana $D$-module are studied: its holonomic rank and the irreducibility of the monodromy representation. This is achieved by relating the banana $D$-module to Lauricella $F_{C}$ hypergeometric systems. Further, we expand the generic-mass banana Feynman integral and the associated discontinuity integral in terms of series solutions. Finally, we analyze the Pfaffian system arising from the banana $D$-module and construct an explicit $d\log$ representation in the equal-mass specialization.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_k$: matching $A(k)$ in ABJM free energy
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The function $A(k)$ appearing in the large $N$ expansion of free energy of ABJM theory on $S^3$ is known exactly from localization. An earlier calculation of the 1-loop partition function of 11d supergravity on $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb Z_k$, based on the standard KK spectrum on $S^7$, did not reproduce it. We identify a missing 1-loop supergravity contribution as that of the 3-form field fluctuations built from square-integrable harmonic 2-forms on Euclidean $\mathrm{AdS}_4$ tensored with $S^7$ modes, which are not captured by the KK spectrum. Adding it to the KK tower contribution expressed in terms of superconformal characters and applying the $\mathbb{Z}_k$ projection, the total expression simplifies, and its evaluation in a zeta-function prescription reproduces the expression for $A(k)$. We also apply a similar approach to the 3d ADHM theory whose M-theory dual is the orbifold $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^7/\mathbb{Z}_p$, which has singularity along the fixed locus $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times S^3$, supporting a 7d $SU(p)$ vector multiplet. Adding the localized KK modes of this multiplet to the $\mathbb{Z}_p$-projected supergravity spectrum gives a 1-loop free energy that reproduces the ADHM localization counterpart of $A(k)$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 44 pages. v2: minor improvements, added argument in sec. 5 fixing the k-independent constant

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Conservation law of super-Lorentz charges across spatial infinity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Under assumptions compatible with generic gravitational scattering, the vacuum relativistic gravitational field is entirely determined at leading order in the large radius expansion at spatial infinity by its supermomentum, its dual supermomentum and its global supertranslation frame. At subleading order, the gravitational field is determined by three additional sets of charges: the super-Lorentz charges, the leading mixed tail/ peeling-breaking charges and the leading peeling-breaking charges. In this work we provide a proper-supertranslation-invariant definition of these charges in terms of asymptotic Bondi-Sachs fields as well as a corresponding proper supertranslation and logarithmic translation invariant definition of these charges in terms of Beig-Schmidt fields. Using the properties of homogeneous and inhomogeneous solutions to relevant wave equations over the boundary de Sitter spacetime at spatial infinity, we derive the conservation law of super-Lorentz charges between the future and past of spatial infinity. We obtain that the super-Lorentz aspects are non-locally defined from the Bondi-Sachs fields.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 57 pages, 1 figure, revised version. This version matches with the published version, which corrects earlier errors and typos

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in gravitational-wave observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, extracted from the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions with power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, where slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed by local matter and geometry without an external clock. In this regime, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, rigorously justifying the standard practice of computing the scalar-induced gravitational-wave energy spectrum from this kernel.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 51 pages, 6 figures; revised abstract and introduction, presentation improved

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Probing Topological Phases in a Strongly Correlated Ladder Model via Entanglement
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: This work examines the interplay of band topology and interactions in a spinless two-leg ladder with $p$-wave-like inter-orbital hybridization. In the non-interacting limit, the model hosts three topologically distinct insulating phases, denoted by $A$, $B$, and $C$. Combining density-matrix renormalization group calculations with low-energy theories of the critical lines yields the interacting phase diagram for an inter-orbital density-density interaction. The $A$-$C$ boundary contains two Dirac valleys and has central charge $c=2$ in the free theory. In the presence of interaction, the exact reflection symmetry pins the $A$-$C$ boundary to its free-theory location, while the critical theory evolves to $c=1$ and the edge entanglement entropy changes from $2\ln 2$ to $\ln 2$. The $B$-$C$ boundary contains a single Dirac mode and shifts quadratically with interaction strength through second-order self-energy corrections involving virtual heavy modes, while retaining its $c=1$ critical structure. Charge conservation and antiunitary many-body chiral symmetry give an interacting $\mathbb{Z}_4$ classification. This distinguishes the two interacting topological phases despite their identical lowest entanglement-spectrum degeneracy. The boundary response is governed by the symmetry and operator content of its critical theory and the symmetry-protected topology of the adjoining phases.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Analytical calculations and explanations are added. (23 pages, 14 figures, 7 appendices)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Polarized IKKT holography: bulk realization of BPS operators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the holographic imprint of polarization in the lowest BPS multiplet of the IKKT matrix model. On the matrix model side, the deformation requires operator mixing and broken-symmetry Ward identities to organize the surviving operators into an irreducible atypical multiplet of the $F(4)$ superalgebra. In the bulk, we use one-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity to identify the analytic half-BPS background with $F(4)$ symmetry whose boundary behavior matches the IKKT polarization. We solve the linearized bosonic and fermionic equations around this background and its undeformed counterpart exactly, and extract the independent asymptotic data. The supersymmetry transformations of these data reproduce the matrix model multiplets, thus establishing a bulk realization of this BPS operator structure.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The $a$-function in fractional dimensions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider the $β$-functions for both scalar, and supersymmetric chiral scalar, field theories with a general $n$th-order self-interaction, in their critical dimensions, which are in general non-integer. We perform a full computation up to fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case, and a partial one in the scalar case. We then demonstrate the existence of an $a$-function, related to the $β$-functions by a gradient flow with a positive-definite metric, through fourth order in the coupling in the supersymmetric case; and show that all our fourth-order results in the scalar case are consistent with a similar property holding there too.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: From Self-Dual to Physical $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$: Anomalies, Boundary Stokes Phenomenon, and Global Structure of $θ$-vacua
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We introduce a two-coupling generalization of $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ model that continuously interpolates between the self-dual ($ε=0$) and the physical ($ε=g$) theories as a useful nonperturbative tool. At $ε\neq g$, this model possesses a chiral imbalance, which may be viewed as a real topological deformation (imaginary-$θ$). We demonstrate that exact quantum equivalence between first- and second-order formulations strictly requires a topological counterterm sourced by a bosonic chiral anomaly. Solving this deformed theory at large $N$ yields two primary results. First, we analytically determine the nonperturbative vacuum structure of the self-dual theory, a self-dual vacuum with a dynamically generated field-strength condensate. Second, we resolve a fundamental paradox where saddles with $(θ+ 2πn) \sim O(N)$ ($n$ is branch number) spuriously yield lower energy densities than the physical ground state. Because the effective action possesses an essential singularity at $F=0$, we show that the Lefschetz thimble analysis must be generalized to include boundary thimbles. A boundary Stokes phenomenon renders the problematic saddles topologically inactive, fully restoring the validity of the large-$N$ expansion for strongly coupled theories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Vertex Operator Algebras in Lean: a formal library and its companion book
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We present LeanVOA, a Lean 4 library for the theory of vertex operator algebras (VOAs), together with a companion book that sets each formalized result next to its textbook statement. The library constructs the Moonshine module $V^
atural$ and proves, with no hypotheses, the Conway-Norton moonshine conjecture for every automorphism of $V^
atural$ (Borcherds' theorem), along Borcherds' route through the Monster Lie algebra. It identifies $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ with a formal model of the Monster taken from the AxiomMath library for the classification of finite simple groups. A separate package in the repository imports that library's generation theorem for the model and proves, with no hypotheses, that $\mathrm{Aut}\,V^
atural$ is isomorphic to the model, compatibly with the Griess algebras, and that moonshine holds for every element of the Monster. It also formalizes Zhu's modular invariance, Huang's tensor categories with the Verlinde formula, the Gannon-Rayhaun classification of $c=1$ VOAs, and classical freeness of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ (Arakawa-Dai) and of the minimal models $M(2,2m+3)$ (van Ekeren-Heluani). It also contains new results: graded first-order rigidity of all Virasoro minimal models and of $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ at every admissible level; classical freeness of $L_{-3/2}(\mathfrak{sl}_3)$, and of the other members of the Deligne series under stated assumptions; and a proof that graded unitarity of the boundary admissible $L_k(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ implies that of the minimal models $M(2,2n+1)$. The library declares no axiom of its own. This note announces release v1.1, which moves the whole library to Lean v4.35.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 8 pages. Code and short version: https://github.com/Fedor-Popov/Lean_VOA (v1.1); book: https://fedor-popov.github.io/Lean_VOA-book/. v1.1: the whole library moved to Lean v4.35

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Casimir effect in Gribov-Zwanziger theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider Yang-Mills theory with two infinite parallel plates, separated by a distance \(L\), that are perfect magnetic conductors (PMC) or perfect electric conductors (PEC). Recently, it was shown that the Gribov copy problem persists in such a setting. We then study the Gribov-Zwanziger (GZ) action in the presence of those boundaries using functional integral methods. Lagrange multiplier fields allow one to lift the boundary conditions into the action, after which the boundary modifications to the gluon propagator can straightforwardly be determined. In the PEC case, we provide evidence that, even when translation invariance is (partially) broken, the usual horizon term in the GZ action still restricts the functional integral to the Gribov region. We compute the Casimir energy for GZ with PMC or PEC plates, both directly from the functional integral and from the energy-momentum tensor, obtaining consistent results. We compare our analytical results with recent lattice data, in both 4D and 3D. A priori, one might expect that the boundary-modified gluon propagator introduces new \(L\)-dependencies into the GZ gap equation. This would make the Gribov mass \(γ\) dynamically dependent on \(L\), implying an interesting interplay with the Casimir energy. However, we show that no such dynamical \(L\)-dependence occurs within the current approximation.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Spin-Torsion Coupling: Vector and Scalar Torsional Potentials of Chiral Spinor Currents
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We investigate integral representations of torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents within a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometric framework. Starting from the coupling between spinorial currents and axial torsion, we construct screened Green-kernel solutions and examine their relation to antisymmetric tetradic perturbations and contorsion.
  Particular attention is devoted to stationary toroidal configurations, for which the magnetic-type dipole moment vanishes while a nonzero toroidal moment and effective circulation remain. The dependence of these quantities on Yukawa screening is analyzed, together with their implications for an Aharonov-Bohm-like geometric structure.
  We further introduce a mixed-chirality source describing an effective connection between oppositely polarized domains and investigate the corresponding flip-sector integral. The dynamics of massive Majorana neutrinos in an axial background is then examined, distinguishing chiral mixing from helicity oscillations and identifying the role of transverse torsional components.
  The resulting framework connects spinorial sources, finite-range torsional potentials, toroidal geometry, and neutrino spin dynamics, while providing a mathematical basis for further investigations of torsional transport and observable effects.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quasi-local form for $α$--$z$ Rényi QNEC from fixed-ray escorts
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Rényi divergences generalize relative entropy and measure the distinguishability of quantum states, but their relation to energy and entanglement entropy is less direct than for ordinary relative entropy. We introduce and study an energy--entropy relation for Rényi divergences by making use of an integral representation that expresses the $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence as an average of ordinary relative entropies of auxiliary escort states constructed from the excited state and the reference state. The integral representation gives energy--entropy decompositions, averaged entanglement laws and energy bounds in regulated quantum field theory (QFT). We further obtain a quasi-local expression for the diagonal second null shape variation of the $α$--$z$ Rényi divergence of an excited state relative to the QFT vacuum. This expression contains a transport term because forming an escort after restricting to a smaller region generally differs from restricting an escort formed beforehand. The conjectural $α$--$z$ Rényi quantum null energy condition (QNEC) then gives a lower bound on the null energy density of the average escort state. As in the ordinary QNEC, the bound involves a second null variation of von Neumann entropy, here averaged over the escort ensemble. We verify the conjecture for an exactly solvable family of coherent excitations of a free scalar field throughout the finite-divergence part of the upper data-processing region. For this family, the sandwiched Rényi divergence at fixed $α>1$ has a positive diagonal second null shape variation that is entirely accounted for by the transport term. We also show that escort formation commutes with the reduced encoding channel in finite-dimensional operator-algebra quantum error-correcting codes with exact complementary recovery.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 45 pages; v2: several clarifications added; improved abstract and introduction; results unchanged

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gauging background isometries of the ILST null string
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a general gauging of a subalgebra, $\mathfrak h$, of the isometries $\mathfrak g$ of the background geometry for the ILST string (e-Print: hep-th/9307108 [hep-th]). We discuss which of the isometries in $\mathfrak g$ survive the gauging as symmetries. The gauged symmetry does not in general involve transformations of the vector density V. There is thus a corresponding contraction of the algebra of constraints as compared to the flat background and it no longer represent the full Carroll-Weyl algebra. This algebra of constraints is derived and discussed, partly in an appendix. The gauging of isometries sets the stage for a reduction, or quotient construction, leading to a new null string on the space of orbits of the gauge group. We illustrate this by deriving the ILST string in $AdS$ background as a quotient of a model in SO(d,2) background by a SO(d,1) isometry, in group space

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Neural variational Skyrmions as a topological benchmark: emergent symmetry, precision energies and KAN--MLP comparison
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We propose the three-dimensional Skyrme model as a topological benchmark for neural variational methods and construct fully three-dimensional Skyrmions with baryon number $B=1,\ldots,4$ without imposing a symmetry ansatz, with high precision. For $B=2,3,4$, the relaxation of these Skyrmions starts from $B$ unit-charge lumps with random positions and orientations, which carry no symmetry information. The known toroidal, tetrahedral, and cubic Skyrmions nevertheless emerge spontaneously. The resulting variational energies for $B=1,\ldots,4$ lie slightly below the published reference values. The neural method highlights the high accuracy for retaining the topological charge, differing from $B$ by at most $10^{-6}$ in the highest-precision solutions. Our numerical method goes through physical constraint tests such as the Derrick virial relation and the Faddeev--Bogomolny bound, together with evaluation / verification through independent quadratures and resolution sweeps. We then compare Kolmogorov--Arnold networks (KANs) with multilayer perceptrons (MLPs) in more than a thousand training runs, both with and without a rational-map ansatz. With default settings, KANs appear markedly superior, but most of the gap disappears once the MLP activation function and learning rate are tuned. KANs remain more parameter-efficient and more robust at fixed epoch budget, while MLPs with the tuned activation function perform at least as well at fixed wall-clock time. We also argue that continuous gradient descent cannot smoothly change the topological sector of our neural field, clarifying the origin of topological freezing observed in our neural variational solvers. Our results on the neural methods applied to Skyrmions pave a research ground for AI-agentic benchmarks for classical topological solitons, toward AI-assisted soliton physics.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 32 pages, 6 figures, 12 tables. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24390286

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Pairing and modular: Generalized electrons and quasiholes inside the $\boxtimes$ of topological orders
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the relationship between the pair creation mechanism in physics and the pairing ($\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}$) in mathematics, focusing on the modular and algebraic properties. We provide a way to couple two topologically ordered systems, $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{A'}$ sharing the common (non-group-like) structure $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}=\overline{\mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}}$, through the nonabelian anyon analog of the pair creation mechanism denoted as $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}=\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}\boxtimes \mathbf{A'}_{\text{ub}}$. We identify $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the generalized version of electron operators in general topological orders or hidden current with (half-)integer spin involving the conformal embeddings. We provide a way to construct $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$ as the hidden topological operator and identify $\mathbf{A}\boxtimes_{\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub}}}\mathbf{A'}$, a general class of topoloical orders, as the $\mathbf{A}_{\text{ub},\boxtimes}$-extended symmetry topological field theory. We also conjecture a series of underlying (unexplored) modular invariants, connecting the conformal embedding and the pairing.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Fractionalized Fermi liquids and the cuprate phase diagram
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We review a theoretical framework for the cuprate superconductors, rooted in a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*) description of the intermediate-temperature pseudogap phase at low doping. The FL* theory predicted hole pockets each of fractional area $p/8$ at hole doping $p$, in contrast to the area $p/4$ in spin density wave theory. Magnetotransport measurements, including observation of the Yamaji angle, show clear evidence of hole pocket quasiparticles which can tunnel coherently between square lattice layers, and are consistent with the FL* description.
  The FL* phase of a single-band model is described using a layer construction with a pair of ancilla qubits on each site: the Ancilla Layer Model (ALM). Fluctuations are described by the SU(2) gauge theory of a background spin liquid with critical Dirac spinons. A Monte Carlo study of the thermal SU(2) gauge theory transforms the hole pockets into Fermi arcs in photoemission. One route to confinement of FL* upon lowering temperature yields a $d$-wave superconductor via a Kosterlitz-Thouless transition of $h/(2e)$ vortices, with nodal Bogoliubov quasiparticles featuring anisotropic velocities and vortices surrounded by charge order halos.
  Increasing doping from the FL* phase in the ALM drives a transition to a conventional Fermi liquid (FL) at large doping, passing through an intermediate strange metal regime. We formulate a theory of the FL*-FL metal-metal transition without a symmetry-breaking order parameter, using a critical quantum `charge' liquid of mobile electrons in the presence of disorder, developed via an extension of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model to two spatial dimensions.
  At low temperatures, and across optimal and over doping, we address the regimes of extended non-Fermi liquid behavior by Griffiths effects near quantum phase transitions in disordered metals.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 101 pages, 43 figures. Review article based on lectures by SS at Boulder, Trieste, Hong Kong, with links to lecture videos. Comments welcome. v3. Introduced terminology of Ancilla Layer Model (ALM). v4. Added additional QMC results on variable exponents in Griffiths phase; v7. Updated results on quantum oscillations

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Constraints on the volume enclosed by Fermi surfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: A fundamental property of a Fermi liquid (FL) is that the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by $ρ$, the total density of electrons. In a fractionalized Fermi liquid (FL*), the volume enclosed by the Fermi surface is determined by the same expression after $ρ$ has been shifted by a quantized amount, most commonly to $ρ-1$ (we assume spin rotation invariance, for simplicity). The FL* shift is related to the quantized symmetry fractionalization data of a quantum spin liquid, whose fractionalized spinon excitations are present alongside the Fermi surface quasiparticles. In this review article, we establish the FL* Fermi volume by generalizing the original Luttinger proof for FL to parton gauge theories of the quantum spin liquid and FL*. We also discuss Oshikawa's flux insertion arguments for FL, and their extension to FL*, including a discussion of gapless spin liquids.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 24 pages, 5 figure. For the Special Centenary Issue of the Indian Journal of Physics, Recent Trends in Condensed Matter Physics

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Thermal photon production in massless boost-invariant gases: hydrodynamization without thermalization
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study hydrodynamization and thermalization in ultrarelativistic heavy-ion collisions using relativistic kinetic theory. Modelling the quark-gluon plasma as a classical gas of massless particles undergoing a boost-invariant longitudinal expansion, we solve the Boltzmann equation in the relaxation-time approximation via a semi-analytical method based on the method of moments. We show that the energy-momentum tensor is well described by relativistic fluid dynamics even when the system is far from local equilibrium. The single-particle distribution function, on the other hand, is not well approximated by a hydrodynamic truncation, suggesting that the onset of hydrodynamic behaviour does not require thermalization. We then quantify how the departure from equilibrium affects the emission rate of thermal photons in the forward scattering approximation, and show that non-equilibrium corrections beyond the hydrodynamic limit can have a significant impact on this observable.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $η$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: On the Casimir effect with mixed dynamical edge mode and perfect electromagnetic conducting boundary conditions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the Casimir effect for a parallel plate setup with one plate with dynamical edge mode (DEM) boundary conditions, and one plate with perfect electromagnetic conductor (PEMC) boundary conditions. In order to restore BRST invariance, new edge fields are introduced on the DEM plate. We then lift the boundary conditions into the action using Lagrange multiplier fields, and integrate out the bulk fields to obtain a non-local effective boundary theory from which we compute the Casimir energy. The resulting Casimir force is identical to a PMC-PEMC setup, implying that, from the point of view of the Casimir effect, a DEM plate is equivalent to a PMC plate. We also include a detailed derivation of the general functional method used to compute the Casimir energy from the partition function.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 17 pages, 2 figures. v2: version accepted for publication in Annals of Physics

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $λ$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|λ|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|λ|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|λ|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|λ|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Examples of infinitesimal Gribov copies in the presence of planar boundaries, and an emergent boundary gauge invariance in Yang-Mills theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: First, we explicitly construct zero-modes of the Yang-Mills Faddeev-Popov operator in the presence of two parallel plates, with either perfect electric (PEC) or perfect magnetic (PMC) boundary conditions imposed. This establishes the existence of infinitesimal Gribov copies with finite action, and even finite L_2-norm, in Yang-Mills theory with non-trivial interfaces. We adapt Henyey's construction, although the boundary configuration imposes extra restrictions on the ansatz for the gauge field. Second, we discuss the phenomenon of an emergent boundary gauge invariance for PEC and PMC plates in Yang-Mills theory. This shall be important when applying the Gribov-Zwanziger procedure to parallel plate setups, of relevance for non-perturbatively studying the non-Abelian Casimir effect in the future.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 16 pages, 6 .jpg figures. v2: version accepted for publication in JHEP

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model. We work at $θ= π$ and at a bare fermion mass exceeding the critical value; in this regime, there are two degenerate vacua, and the $e^+$ and $e^-$ particles are realized as soliton states interpolating between them. We carefully explain how to find and characterize such soliton states using infinite tensor network methods, and then exhibit real-time simulations of their collisions. These collisions involve the formation of an energetic flux string, and we demonstrate that our final states are superpositions of elastic and string-breaking trajectories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum Metric and Nonlinear Hall Effect of Photons
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Using the path-integral formalism, we show that photons possess a nontrivial quantum metric in momentum space. We derive the semiclassical action and equations of motion by taking into account the quantum metric. In media with a spatially varying refractive index $n(\mathbf{x})$, the quantum metric induces a shift in the trajectory of light at second order in spatial gradients of $n$, whose transverse component may be regarded as a nonlinear Hall effect of light. The quantum metric also gives rise to corrections to photon propagation relevant to gravitational lensing in curved spacetime at second order in wavelength, including a gravitational nonlinear Hall effect arising from the interplay between the geometry of position space and that of momentum space.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 6 pages; v2: several equations corrected; optical observability estimate and discussion added; clarifications and references added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Type-IV 't Hooft Anomalies on the Lattice: Emergent Higher-Categorical Symmetries and Applications to LSM Systems
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: 't Hooft anomalies impose fundamental constraints on quantum matter and often lead to emergent symmetry structures upon gauging. We analyze a lattice model with four global symmetries realizing a mixed anomaly described by $\sim a_1\wedge a_2\wedge a_3\wedge a_4$, where the $a_i$ denote background gauge fields for the global symmetries. Through explicit lattice gauging, we demonstrate the emergence of higher symmetry structures, including 2-group, non-invertible, and higher fusion categorical symmetries. We also provide a field theoretical understanding of these results. Applying this framework to systems with Lieb-Schultz-Mattis anomalies, obtained by promoting part of the internal symmetries to translational symmetries, we demonstrate that modulated (dipole) symmetries and non-invertible translation symmetry arise as direct counterparts of those in systems with purely internal type-IV anomalies. Importantly, we uncover a qualitatively new feature absent in previously studied modulated symmetries and non-invertible translation: their realization can become intrinsically defect-dependent. In particular, the emergent symmetry structure changes depending on whether symmetry defects are present. This work establishes a concrete lattice realization of mixed anomalies and reveals a rich structure of emergent symmetries, thereby clarifying their role in constraining quantum phases of matter.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 48 pages, 17 figures, v2: Added a discussion of non-invertible translation symmetry and references

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Beyond the Peak: Constraining early dark energy with the damping tail
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Early dark energy is commonly characterized by the amplitude and location of its primary energy-injection peak. We show that its post-peak evolution, which we call the \emph{EDE tail}, provides an additional observable probe of the underlying scalar dynamics and can materially affect its ability to alleviate the Hubble tension. We construct a simple phenomenological framework in which distinct regions of a multiscale scalar potential govern the dynamics at different field scales. As a representative realization, we consider a potential that combines axion-like and $α$-attractor-like regimes, thereby allowing the EDE tail to be reshaped through reflection and asymmetric oscillations. Confronting this framework with cosmic microwave background, baryon acoustic oscillation, and supernova observations, we find an improved fit to the high-$\ell$ CMB data together with a higher inferred bestfit $H_0$. Our results show that the EDE tail retains observable information about the underlying scalar potential that is not captured by the conventional peak parameters alone. This provides a complementary route for constructing and observationally distinguishing EDE scenarios, and potentially for further alleviating the Hubble tension.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Obstruction to local entropy laws on arbitrary black-hole cuts in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study local entropy laws on arbitrary cuts of event horizons in five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity, treated as an exact theory. No covariant local entropy can both reproduce the stationary black-hole entropy and be nondecreasing between every ordered pair of cuts, provided its density is smooth on an invariant open set of off-shell metric and cut jets containing a flat planar cut and every cut used in the argument. No global bound on derivative order is assumed. The counterexamples to the second law are vacuum black holes perturbed by a gravitational wave, with a strongly hyperbolic formulation near the relevant horizon interval and its stationary future. Shear makes the intrinsic curvature of a cut depend on its bending. The stationary entropy fixes the coefficient of this curvature term, and local corrections cannot cancel its response to cut bending. The obstruction appears at second order in wave amplitude on a smooth horizon, without a merger or topology change.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Perturbative $S$-matrix Unitarity in Higher-Derivative Theory of Fermions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a higher-derivative fermion theory with four-Fermi interactions. In quantum field theory, it is conjectured that good high-energy behavior of tree-level scattering amplitudes implies renormalizability, a notion referred to as the tree-unitarity criterion. To investigate whether this criterion is satisfied in a higher-derivative fermion theory, we examine the structure of the $S$-matrix in detail. Owing to the higher-derivative kinetic term, the mass dimension of the spinor field differs from that of a conventional fermion, rendering four-Fermi interactions renormalizable at the cost of introducing ghost states. We show that, unlike bosonic ghosts, fermionic ghosts inevitably give rise to negative-norm states regardless of the sign of their energy eigenvalues. We further demonstrate that, in contrast to conventional four-Fermi theories, the higher-derivative four-Fermi theory satisfies perturbative $S$-matrix unitarity. In light of the tree-unitarity criterion, these results provide supporting evidence for the renormalizability of higher-derivative fermion theories and generalize our previous findings on higher-derivative scalar theories to the fermionic case.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Energy and Charge Transmission at Conformal Interfaces: Relations and Bounds
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Symmetry constrains how independently energy and charge can pass through a conformal interface. For interfaces between Wess--Zumino--Witten (WZW) models $G_{k_L}$ and $G_{k_R}$ preserving the diagonal affine algebra, we derive an exact relation between the energy and charge transmission coefficients, $c_{LR}=2(\dim G)k_{LR}/(k_L+k_R+2h^\vee)$. Together with positivity of outgoing energy, this relation excludes complete energy transmission at unequal levels. With additional bulk degrees of freedom, the equality is replaced by bounds controlled by the coset central charges. Complete transmission from a lower-level WZW model then imposes a lower bound on the coset central charge on the other side. In linear response, the relation fixes the ratio of thermal to charge conductance to the harmonic mean of the two bulk ratios, independently of the interface, while coset sectors bound the thermal conductance at fixed charge conductance. This interface-independent ratio is a generalized Wiedemann--Franz law for conformal interfaces between WZW models. The charge transmission coefficient $k_{LR}$ also governs equilibrium charge fluctuations and fixes the leading quadratic dependence of the boundary-condition-changing operator's scaling dimension on the rotation angle.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Calabi-Yau at 50: mathematical discovery in the age of AI
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Using the golden jubilee of Yau's proof of the Calabi conjecture as a spring-board, we discuss how the dataset of Calabi-Yau manifolds brought together mathematicians and physicists since the 1980s, and then further brought in the world of machine-learning and AI since 2017. We give a historical account on the growth of the field of ``AI-assisted mathematics'' in the last decade, and comment on what culminated in 2026 as perhaps the most dramatic year in the history of mathematics since Euclid.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 27 pages. Based on invited talk at "Calabi-Yau at 50: The Legacy and Future", held at Tsinghua University in September, 2026

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: IR/UV mixing from higher-order interactions in a Scalar Field
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The observed vacuum energy lies far below the usual quantum-field-theoretic estimate. We construct a preferred-frame reduced scalar Hamiltonian in which a nonlocal quartic field derivative interaction produces a wavevector dependence proportional to $|\vec k|^8$ for modes below a smoothly defined scale. Within the quartic oscillator regime, the ground-state energy and excitation gaps are $\propto |\vec k|^{8/3}$. The preferred frame is characterized by a timelike clock-field background. The Planck energy is reached at a substantially smaller value of the spatial wavevector due to its supra-linear mode-energy dependence. The proposed interaction is instantaneous in the preferred frame and yields a Hamiltonian bounded below. Normalizing the peak of the ground-state energy to the Planck scale, together with Cohen-Kaplan-Nelson (CKN) saturation, applied as a matching recipe rather than as an {\it {ab initio}} calculation, fixes the cutoff scale at $k_G\sim k_{Pl}^{1/3}k_{box}^{2/3}$. Modes above the smooth cutoff scale retain their ordinary scalar dynamics. We assume that the interaction-induced ground-state energy shift gravitates, as do other contributions. CKN saturation is imposed on the total vacuum energy, comprising this shift and the other vacuum contributions. Identifying the inferred infrared scale phenomenologically with the cosmic event horizon reproduces the holographic-dark-energy relation $ρ_{vac}\propto\frac{M_{Pl}^2}{R_h^2}$, provided the coupling tracks the horizon; the resulting holographic fluid has $w_0\simeq-0.89$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Directional Anisotropic Sensitivity Curves for Pulsar Timing Arrays
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: After two decades of observations, pulsar timing array collaborations have reported strong evidence for a stochastic gravitational wave background, most likely sourced by an inspiraling population of supermassive black hole binaries. Because that population is finite, anisotropy in the background is inevitable, producing hotspots on the sky that track the loudest binaries. Building on the Fisher formalism for anisotropic backgrounds, we recast the directional Fisher information as effective sensitivity curves on the sky, distinguishing the radiometer and full-Fisher estimators, along with a sky-weighted curve that reduces the anisotropic sky to a single spectrum and recovers the standard isotropic curve in the isotropic limit. We implement five sky-decomposition bases: pixel, spherical harmonic, square-root spherical harmonic, radiometer, and principal-map. We demonstrate the framework on a simulated array modeled on the International Pulsar Timing Array: characterizing the angular response, analyzing the Fisher structure, quantifying the detectability of injected anisotropic hotspots, and forecasting future-array sensitivity. The framework is released as an extension to the sensitivity software package hasasia.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A High Precision Transformer model for precessing binary black-hole merger waveforms calibrated to numerical relativity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present a Transformer model for merger-centered gravitational waveforms from precessing binary black holes. Given the mass ratio and two three-dimensional spin vectors, the network predicts 512 quintic B-spline coefficients for all 21 signed spin-weighted spherical-harmonic strain modes through $\ell=4$ on $[-1620,160]M$ ($M$ being the total binary mass), enforcing binary-exchange and equatorial-reflection equivariance and yielding $C^4$ time-domain waveforms with exact parameter and temporal derivatives via automatic differentiation. The model is pretrained jointly on numerical-relativity (NR) waveforms from the SXS and RIT catalogues together with synthetic NRSur7dq4, SEOBNRv5PHM, and perturbative waveforms, and fine-tuned on SXS strain data. On 109 SXS evaluation waveforms (106 physical systems) over $[-1500,100]M$, it achieves a mean balanced relative strain error of 0.0305 and a mean finite-window detector mismatch at $120\,M_\odot$ of 0.1536%, outperforming SEOBNRv5PHM, NRSur7dq4v2, and IMRPhenomTPHM across common support, with compiled batched float64 inference reaching 445 waveforms/s on an A100 GPU.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 24 pages, 11 figures, 9 tables; ancillary files include the NR dataset membership and exposure tables; inference code and weights at https://github.com/jdong745/merger-transformer

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Kinetic moment estimates and a one-sided Lyapunov barrier for the relativistic fermionic Michie-King equation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the cutoff Ruffini--Argüelles--Rueda (RAR), or relativistic fermionic Michie--King, equation of state along an equilibrium family with fixed Tolman--Klein invariants. Three kinetic moments give exact formulas for both the pressure-to-density ratio and the derivative of pressure. Cauchy--Schwarz yields a global relation between these two quantities. It implies vertical vector-field domination of the associated Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff system by the linear equation of state $P=ρc^2/\sqrt3$ in the physical wedge $0<y\leq3x$. We construct a filled, one-sided version of the Bors--Stańczy Lyapunov barrier and check every boundary. This controls all outward excursions, including those after a lower exit from a Lyapunov sublevel. For regular configurations the resulting explicit Lambert bound is $2Gm(r)/(rc^2)<0.6879212521$. Using the diagonal where this ratio has a stationary value sharpens the bound to $0.6734385929$. The argument is conditional on a regular TOV configuration and does not require a separate finite-radius existence theorem. We also identify and correct a logarithmic coefficient in the previously used explicit linear-comparator formula.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $φ_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $φ_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dynamical tidal response of neutron stars: From effective field theory to gravitational waveforms
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the fully relativistic dynamical tidal response of neutron stars up to second order in the frequency. Combining the worldline effective field theory for extended gravitating bodies with perturbation theory of relativistic stellar models, we derive the tidal deformation induced by an external time-dependent field, including a universal logarithmic running term. In the effective theory, we work in dimensional regularization and, through a consistent matching procedure, obtain for the first time the complete leading-order dynamical tidal corrections to both the conservative dynamics and the gravitational-wave signal of compact binaries, including the scheme-dependent finite terms in addition to the running. We show that, in the relativistic regime, dynamical effects cannot be fully captured by mode excitations alone. The magnitude of the additional contribution depends on the stellar compactness, the equation of state, and the running term. Dynamical Love numbers are significantly enhanced with respect to their static counterparts for relatively small compactness. As a result, although they formally enter the gravitational-wave phase at eighth post-Newtonian order, dynamical tidal effects yield a nonnegligible contribution during the late inspiral. Using a Fisher-matrix analysis, we show that third-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope could measure dynamical Love numbers for a range of neutron-star masses and equations of state. Conversely, neglecting these effects can lead to significant biases in the inference of static Love numbers, and hence on the nuclear equation of state. Our results highlight the importance of dynamical tidal effects for high-precision gravitational-wave modeling with future detectors.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 31 pages, 9 figures. v3: fixed typo in waveform derivation; main conclusions unaffected

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. With unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional MCMC posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. When marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. Under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. We test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. We find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. Finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a LISA global fit.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: What determines the properties of Population III binaries?
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Population~III binaries may provide a gravitational-wave probe of the first stellar populations. Uncertain initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions complicate predictions of their remnant masses, birth orbits and formation spins. Varying these model evolutionary parameters (MEPs) jointly is needed to identify which MEPs shape each property and whether their effects persist among binaries that merge. We use \textsc{StarTrack} to evolve $2\times10^6$ initial binaries per model across 1152 configurations spanning eight MEPs. To our knowledge, this is the largest grid of Population~III isolated-binary population-synthesis models to date by number of distinct parameter configurations. We compare the properties and correlations of all binary black holes (BBHs) with those of systems that merge within the adopted age of the Universe. The all-BBH (merging-BBH) model medians span $34.3$--$171.0 M_{\odot}$ ($23.1$--$94.8 M_{\odot}$) in total mass, $0.039$--$0.106$ ($0.018$--$0.129$) in effective aligned spin $χ_{\mathrm{eff}}$ at formation, and $0.075$--$0.639$ ($0.039$--$0.983$) in birth eccentricity. Merger selection also changes correlations between BBH properties and the combinations of MEP values and prescriptions associated with them. We use variance-based sensitivity analysis to quantify how the initial binary parameter distributions and evolutionary prescriptions affect the predicted BBH properties.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages, 5 figures. Abstract abridged for arxiv

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Disrupted stars and captured compact objects: Combining observations from multiple messengers to infer the population of massive black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Massive black holes (MBHs) are found in galactic centres, but their formation and evolution remain elusive. Tidal disruption events (TDEs) and extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) both arise from stellar dynamics in the nuclear star clusters around MBHs, and are observed with electromagnetic surveys and gravitational waves, respectively. To overcome the scarcity of coincident detections, we formulate how to combine gravitational-wave detections from LISA-EMRIs with observations from ZTF-TDEs to measure properties of the MBH population. Building on two-dimensional Fokker-Planck simulations of EMRIs and TDEs, we model how their populations are affected by the MBH-host scaling relation, the nucleation fraction and the MBH occupation fraction, and analyse the resulting catalogues using joint hierarchical inference accounting for their individual selection biases. With current ZTF-TDE detections, we can already identify combinations of MBH formation favoured by and consistent with the observed TDE population, and derive corresponding predictions for the EMRI population detectable by LISA. Across a range of astrophysical assumptions, the ratio of detectable TDEs to EMRIs is high: ZTF detecting 2.7-84.3 times as many TDEs as LISA detects EMRIs. TDEs, through their numbers, set the shared mass and redshift distributions: LSST constrains the characteristic MBH mass to a 90% credible width of 0.31 dex and the power-law index of the redshift evolution to a precision of 0.11. EMRIs make up ~3.4% of the joint catalogue, yet carry more information than the whole ZTF sample and are the only probe of MBH spin and orbital eccentricity. TDEs will constrain the abundance of low-mass MBHs before LISA flies, while EMRIs will measure properties that electromagnetic surveys cannot. EMRI and TDE observations offer complementary insights into MBH growth and evolution that neither can provide alone.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational Landscapes: black holes with linear equations of state in asymptotically safe gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study black holes with linear equation of state within the framework of asymptotically safe gravity. This study extends previous work on gravitational collapse in asymptotically safe gravity (that has been done for a dust fluid) by considering into account the pressure of stellar matter. We derive modified field equations containing the running gravitational coupling and the cosmological constant as functions of energy density. The interior space-time of collapsing star is modeled by the Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric, while the exterior is described by a static spherically symmetric space-time. Different equations of state from ordinary matter to exotic phantom energy are considered to investigate their impact on black hole structure and horizon formation. Our results illustrate that asymptotically safe gravity can introduce non-singular black hole solutions under specific conditions. These results provide new insights into black hole physics and the avoidance of singularities within the asymptotically safe gravity framework.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Matching second-order classical and 1-loop quantum tensor power spectra in de Sitter spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Large corrections to the inflationary tensor power spectrum have been speculated to emerge either as second-order scalar-induced classical effects, or as 1-loop quantum corrections. These two sources are not independent of each other. Choosing the example of a massless minimally coupled scalar field, we show how the full 1-loop result can be divided into its classical and vacuum parts. Working first in dimensional regularization, we show that the classical part is IR divergent, with IR referring to small comoving momenta that have an influence for a very long time. In the full 1-loop quantum result, these divergences cancel. Introducing then a momentum cutoff that permits for a numerical evaluation of the classical contribution, we show that the IR sensitivity manifests itself as a cubic divergence. We suggest a procedure of "non-perturbative renormalization" for extracting physical information not affected by the divergence. If this can be implemented in realistic systems, it could consolidate numerical studies of inflationary scalar-induced gravitational waves.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 41 pages. v2: comments on the KLN theorem, and on pitfalls of the classical approximation (in appendix D)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Coronagraphic time-delay interferometry: fundamental steps towards concrete applications
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is a future space-based gravitational wave (GW) observatory. Central to LISA data analysis is time-delay interferometry (TDI), which reduces otherwise overwhelming laser frequency noise. In previous work, we explored coronagraphic TDI, a sky-dependent null-stream channel which cancels the GW signal of a point-like source when pointed at its sky position. Because this property relies only on the geometric response of LISA, coronagraphic TDI is a candidate for model-agnostic sky localization. Here, we address three challenges which arise when analyzing realistic LISA data: (i) spacecraft motion; (ii) signal superposition; (iii) instrumental noise. We derive a second-generation coronagraphic TDI variable and its analytic noise model, and show that it reduces laser frequency noise in the presence of spacecraft motion while still recovering the position of the source. Using pairs of Galactic binaries (GBs), we find that sources can be localized independently provided they do not overlap in frequency, even when they share the same sky position, whereas sources overlapping in frequency can only be localized if one dominates by a factor of ~100 in amplitude. This is confirmed by the analysis of a simulation containing a massive black hole binary and 49 verification GBs. Finally, we introduce a statistical test based on the analytic noise model, which provides well-calibrated confidence regions for the sky position of the source. Applying it to GBs in the presence of instrumental noise, we find that the geometric response alone only weakly constrains the sky position: even at signal-to-noise ratios of order 10^4, 90% confidence regions span ~10^3 deg^2. These are fundamental steps towards applications of coronagraphic TDI to LISA data, such as sky localization and glitch discrimination, which we discuss.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Jet launching from the Kerr black hole magnetosphere: An electrogeodesic approach
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The launch of relativistic jets of plasma on astrophysical to cosmological scales is observed in a variety of astrophysical sources, from active galactic nuclei to X-ray binaries. While these jets can be reproduced by general relativistic magneto-hydrodynamics (GRMHD) and particle-in-cells (GRPIC) simulations of the dynamical Kerr magnetosphere, the development of analytic models to describe the physics of the jets has remained limited. A key challenge is to analytically describe the individual trajectories of accelerated charged particles, which ultimately build up the jet and emit radiation. In this work, we provide a first simple but fully analytical model of jet launching from the Kerr magnetosphere based on the motion of charged particles. To that end, we use the integrability of electrogeodesic motion in the Kerr monopole magnetosphere to study the ejection of charged particles near the poles. This enables us to derive (i) a criterion for the rotation axis to constitute a stable latitudinal equilibrium position, thereby representing an idealized jet, (ii) the expression for the magnetic frame-dragging effect, and (iii) the condition for an asymptotic observer to measure blueshifted particles emanating from the black hole surroundings. Our study reveals that particles can be accelerated only in a specific region whose maximal radius depends on the spin and magnetization of the black hole. We further show that these results extend to the split-monopole Kerr solution by a redefinition of the angular momentum of the charged particles. Alongside these results, we provide a detailed review of the construction of test magnetospheres from (explicit and hidden) symmetries of the Kerr geometry and the condition for the separability of the electrogeodesic motion in a test magnetosphere, which serves as a basis for the model studied in this work.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 37 pages, 4 figures, References and clarifications on the relation to the split-monopole solution added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Effective theory of quantum black holes with Kretschmann scalar
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the thermodynamics, quasinormal modes (QNMs), and shadows of the effective theory of quantum black holes (BHs) by expanding the physical constants in terms of the Kretschmann scalar. The resulting effective metric can contain two horizons, which is typical for a quantum-corrected Schwarzschild spacetime. The second-order corrected metric only shifts the first-order corrected metric, allowing investigation of IR phenomena from the pure first-order corrected one. From a thermodynamic point of view, the metric leads to a stable cold remnant with zero entropy, compatible with the third law of thermodynamics. In the perturbation regime, we use massless scalar perturbations to extract the effective potential, QNMs, graybody factor, and total absorption cross section. We show that double-horizon BHs have a double light ring in the potential, and for a certain value $Ω/χ^2=0.01,$ the QNMs are similar to the GR case since the horizon is Schwarzschild-like. We also tested the correspondence between the QNMs and the graybody factor, and our results still hold with an error far below $1\%$. Our results also conclude that the higher the frequency, the bigger the cross-section area. For the optical observables, we observe that the opposite sign of $Ω$ leads to distinct behavior of the BH's photon sphere and shadow radius. The Sagittarius A* shadow radius upper bound from the Event Horizon Telescope observation in the $2σ$ and $1σ$ significance set the upper limit of the quantum parameter $Ω$ to $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.3649$ and $Ω/χ^2 \lesssim 0.0105$, respectively.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 12 pages, 15 figures, under review in European Physical Journal C

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Test of gravitational redshift by optical clocks at different latitudes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: General relativity predicts that frequency comparisons between clocks are affected by both gravitational and kinematic time dilation. While the kinematic contribution has been tested with high accuracy, experimental tests of the gravitational redshift remain comparatively less stringent. Here, we measure the frequency shift between two Earth-fixed optical atomic clocks at different potentials and compare it to the redshift predicted by general relativity using independent geodetic measurements. The observed shift agrees with the prediction, testing the gravitational redshift at the $4.6 \times 10^{-5}$ uncertainty level, improving ground-based tests by a factor two. Previous ground-based tests separated the clocks mainly vertically. For clocks at different latitudes, their height difference is governed not only by the gravitational potentials at their locations but also by the centrifugal potentials caused by Earth's rotation. As both contributions can partially cancel, the gravitational contribution can be considerably larger than their height difference suggests. In this work, a separation of the clocks by $4^\circ$ in latitude enhances their sensitivity to a gravitational redshift violation threefold, to the equivalent of an approximately 1200 m difference in height for small latitudinal separation. Our results establish Earth's rotation as a so far unexploited resource for advancing ground-based tests of the gravitational redshift towards the sensitivity of previous space-based experiments.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Shape wall: Constraints on late-time solutions to the Hubble tension from the dimensionless expansion rate
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The standard "no-go theorem" against late-time solutions to the Hubble tension is essentially a normalization wall, since Baryon Acoustic Oscillation (BAO) measurements constrain the product $H_0r_d$, with $r_d$ the sound horizon at baryon drag. However, late-time solutions (which keep $r_d$ fixed) are tightly constrained not only by the BAO normalization $H_0r_d$, but also by the shape of the expansion history, i.e. the dimensionless expansion rate $E(z) \equiv H(z)/H_0$. We show that, if $r_d$ and the acoustic angular scale $θ_s$ are fixed, an increase in $H_0$ needs to be matched by an equal fractional increase in the dimensionless distance integral $I \equiv \int dz/E(z)$: $δH_0/H_0 \simeq δI/I$. We use this to quantify the "shape wall" set by relative distance constraints on $E(z)$, which we reconstruct nonparametrically, using Gaussian Processes and the latest unanchored Type Ia Supernovae (SNeIa) and BAO data. In our most conservative analysis using PantheonPlus SNeIa and DESI DR2 BAO data, we find a maximum fractional increase in $H_0$ of $\lesssim 2\%$, falling well short of the $\gtrsim 8\%$ required to solve the tension. This shape wall holds even in the presence of early-time new physics, and limits the maximum increase in $H_0$ which can be contributed by late-time modifications to $E(z)$ at fixed $θ_s$. Therefore, late-time modifications, whether invoked alone or alongside early-time new physics, face not only the well-known normalization wall, but also a stringent percent-level shape wall.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 25 pages, 19 sub-figures arranged into 5 figures, many references. v2: additional references added, included a new Fig. 1 providing a very useful graphical summary of the main idea (many thanks to William Giarè! Please check out his extremely useful repository at https://github.com/williamgiare/wgcosmo/ on Github). v3: minor change to title, version accepted for publication in PRD

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Kerr Metric in Canonical Harmonic Coordinates to All Orders
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We give in closed form the transformation from Boyer--Lindquist coordinates to the canonical harmonic coordinates of the Kerr metric, to all orders in Newton's constant and in the spin. This is the canonical harmonic chart selected by the MPM prescription and by the harmonic-gauge Einstein recursion sourced by the Kerr multipoles, with the residual homogeneous freedom fixed by the boundary conditions. The chart is the real, time-reversal-covariant combination of the two radial harmonic functions underlying the Cook--Scheel coordinates, which differ from it by a definite residual harmonic transformation. The proof rests on a classification of the residual harmonic freedom.
