Rotational covariance, parity, time reversal and analyticity in the spin allow a decaying homogeneous solution beyond the linear field only in the spatial components at third post-Minkowskian order, with angular degree $\ell=p+2$ at spin order $a^p$. This sector is a pure gauge mode, equivalent to an MPM gauge moment. The exact chart selects the representative in which this third-PM homogeneous mode vanishes; imposing the same condition on the recursion removes the only residual ambiguity and fixes its solution uniquely. As a consequence, the canonical MPM iteration needs no finite-part regularisation and no harmonicity correction at any order. We give the exact gothic metric and the post-Minkowskian coefficients in closed form through fifth order, where an arctangent function first appears at fourth order. We find agreement with recent canonical MPM and amplitude-based results at fourth order, and we verify the construction in exact arithmetic through fifth order and twelfth order in the spin, with code made publicly available.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 36 pages. Codes available at Github https://github.com/pierrevanhove/kerr-metric-harmonic and Zenodo https://zenodo.org/records/24397114

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black hole equations of state and response functions
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We systematically develop a framework for equilibrium thermodynamics in terms of thermodynamic representations, which are choices of thermodynamic potential and independent variables, one from each conjugate pair. In each representation, equations of state arise from first derivatives of the potential and response functions from its second derivatives. We apply this framework to ideal gases and to Schwarzschild black holes in a spherical cavity in various representations, interpreting the cavity area and its conjugate surface pressure as the thermodynamic volume and pressure of a holographically dual system. For this quasi-local Schwarzschild black hole, stability depends on the thermodynamic representation, or equivalently on which variables are held fixed under equilibrium perturbations. The large black hole branch is thermally stable at fixed volume but mechanically unstable under isothermal compression, while the system is mechanically stable under adiabatic compression everywhere. At fixed pressure, the black hole is thermally unstable throughout the physical state space. We also find that the thermal expansion coefficient is negative everywhere and show that isenthalpic expansion always cools the black hole. More broadly, the framework provides a systematic route to deriving equations of state and response functions for a wide class of black hole systems using quasi-local gravitational thermodynamics.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Published version: minor improvements. 31 pages + 2 appendices; 5 figures

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraints on Schwarzschild Black Hole in a Generalized Dehnen-Type $(1,4,γ)$ Dark Matter Halo via the S2 Star Orbit around Sgr A$^\star$
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The distribution of dark matter (DM) halo around supermassive black holes (BHs) may leave observable imprints on stellar dynamics near galactic centers. Motivated by this, we investigate the orbital motion of the S2 star in the spacetime of a recently derived generalized Schwarzschild BH solution embedded in a Dehnen-type $(1,4,γ)$ DM halo, considering it as a possible model for Sgr A$^{\star}$ at the center of the Milky Way. Unlike previous studies restricted to specific values of the halo parameter $γ$, the present solution describes the fully generalized case with arbitrary $γ$. We derive the corresponding equations of motion and obtain the associated pericenter shift over one orbital period. Using observational data of the S2 star, we constrain the parameters of the Schwarzschild--Dehnen BH-DM system through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis. Our MCMC analysis provides constraints on the parameter $γ$ of the generalized Dehnen-type DM halo. The posterior medians of $γ$ with 68% credible intervals are $γ=0.652^{+0.435}_{-0.446}$ and $γ=0.771^{+0.486}_{-0.522}$ for Dataset 1 from Do et al. and Dataset 2 from Gillessen et al., respectively. The corresponding one-sided 95% upper credible limits are $γ<1.238$ and $γ<1.389$. If the halo is instead normalized to the observed local dark-matter density at solar distance, $ρ_{\rm DM}(8\,\mathrm{kpc})\simeq0.01\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-3}$, the 95% upper limits become $γ<1.949$ and $γ<1.931$ for Dataset 1 and Dataset 2, respectively. The analysis shows that the S2 orbital motion provides constraints on the parameter $γ$ of the DM halo profile, while the characteristic halo density $ρ_s$ and scale radius $r_s$ exhibit a strong degeneracy and remain sensitive to the adopted prior ranges.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Conservation law of super-Lorentz charges across spatial infinity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Under assumptions compatible with generic gravitational scattering, the vacuum relativistic gravitational field is entirely determined at leading order in the large radius expansion at spatial infinity by its supermomentum, its dual supermomentum and its global supertranslation frame. At subleading order, the gravitational field is determined by three additional sets of charges: the super-Lorentz charges, the leading mixed tail/ peeling-breaking charges and the leading peeling-breaking charges. In this work we provide a proper-supertranslation-invariant definition of these charges in terms of asymptotic Bondi-Sachs fields as well as a corresponding proper supertranslation and logarithmic translation invariant definition of these charges in terms of Beig-Schmidt fields. Using the properties of homogeneous and inhomogeneous solutions to relevant wave equations over the boundary de Sitter spacetime at spatial infinity, we derive the conservation law of super-Lorentz charges between the future and past of spatial infinity. We obtain that the super-Lorentz aspects are non-locally defined from the Bondi-Sachs fields.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 57 pages, 1 figure, revised version. This version matches with the published version, which corrects earlier errors and typos

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in gravitational-wave observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, extracted from the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions with power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, where slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed by local matter and geometry without an external clock. In this regime, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, rigorously justifying the standard practice of computing the scalar-induced gravitational-wave energy spectrum from this kernel.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 51 pages, 6 figures; revised abstract and introduction, presentation improved

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Inpainting to search for premerger massive black hole binaries in realistic LISA datasets
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A key science target of the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) is to carry out multi-messenger observations of massive black hole binaries, observing the merger simultaneously in gravitational waves and with electromagnetic observatories. Identifying that a merger is happening and providing an updating estimate of the sky location in the hours, days and weeks before the merger is critical to enable electromagnetic observations of the merger event. In this work we demonstrate and compare two methods for premerger identification of massive black hole binaries; a zero-latency filter approach and, for the first time, an approach using an ``inpainting'' technique. We apply these methods to the LISA Data Challenge dataset 2a--Sangria-HM--and demonstrate the successful recovery of the 14 signals in the dataset that we expected to be identifiable at least half a day before merger. We show that the inpainting method can identify premerger signals even when gaps are present in the data, demonstrating the recovery of a signal even when 3 day-long data gaps are added to the 14 days preceding merger. Finally, we explore the challenge of overlapping signals, using a region of overlapping signals in the Sangria-HM dataset, all of which merge within a 10-day window, and show how removing signals that have been confidently identified from the data allows us to identify quieter signals in the same period.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: BMS Charges from Null Hypersurfaces
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show how the gravitational dynamics, phase space and Noether charges of the BMS group at future null infinity $\mathscr{I}^+$ can be derived as limits of their analogues on null hypersurfaces at finite distance. The Bondi mass-loss and angular-momentum evolution equations arise as limits of the Raychaudhuri and Damour constraints. The Ashtekar--Streubel (aka Wald--Zoupas) symplectic potential arises as a specific member of a two-parameter family of null-boundary symplectic potentials, corresponding to the Dirichlet (aka canonical) polarization, while the other members differ by field-space exact terms, leading to the same radiative pre-symplectic structure but potentially different BMS fluxes. Deriving the BMS charges requires additional care, since BMS generators extended into the bulk are generally not tangent to the null hypersurfaces. After accounting for this and the associated anomalies, the renormalized canonical charges still contain an additional soft contribution. The prescription of a covariant boundary Lagrangian determines a corner improvement that removes this term and recovers the standard BMS charges.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Spin-Torsion Coupling: Vector and Scalar Torsional Potentials of Chiral Spinor Currents
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
We investigate integral representations of torsional fields sourced by chiral spinor currents within a weak-field, Ricci-flow-inspired geometric framework. Starting from the coupling between spinorial currents and axial torsion, we construct screened Green-kernel solutions and examine their relation to antisymmetric tetradic perturbations and contorsion.
  Particular attention is devoted to stationary toroidal configurations, for which the magnetic-type dipole moment vanishes while a nonzero toroidal moment and effective circulation remain. The dependence of these quantities on Yukawa screening is analyzed, together with their implications for an Aharonov-Bohm-like geometric structure.
  We further introduce a mixed-chirality source describing an effective connection between oppositely polarized domains and investigate the corresponding flip-sector integral. The dynamics of massive Majorana neutrinos in an axial background is then examined, distinguishing chiral mixing from helicity oscillations and identifying the role of transverse torsional components.
  The resulting framework connects spinorial sources, finite-range torsional potentials, toroidal geometry, and neutrino spin dynamics, while providing a mathematical basis for further investigations of torsional transport and observable effects.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Relativistic Newton's Third Law for Binaries in Environments
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We derive the relativistic form of Newton's Third Law governing the interaction between intermediate- and extreme-mass-ratio inspirals and surrounding relativistic matter fields. Working within a two-parameter expansion, we rewrite the evolution of the secondary's orbital elements in a form resembling the integrated forces acting on the environment, avoiding the need to calculate any gravitational perturbations sourced by the dynamical matter content. Using the retarded and advanced Green's functions, we obtain both instantaneous and orbit-averaged laws relating the rate of change of the secondary's orbital energy and angular momentum to that of the matter and the gravitational-wave fluxes at that order. Our results clarify and correct the mixture of ad hoc balance prescriptions currently employed in the literature, providing first-principles forcing functions for the secondary's orbital elements in two ready-to-use forms: a leading-order formulation suitable for fast evaluation with complex relativistic matter simulations, and a first-post-adiabatic formulation of the energy and angular-momentum evolution in environments that are stationary and axisymmetric at leading order.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Parameter Estimation on LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA O4a Binary Merger Triggers with Sub-solar Mass Components
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA collaboration has reported the results for searches for sub-solar mass components in compact binary coalescence during observing run O4a. No detection candidates were identified, but the most significant seven triggers were reported. We present the results of Bayesian parameter inference on these triggers. Five of the triggers show agreement between the Bayesian parameter estimation and the search pipeline trigger. Our results show that three of the triggers may contain a possible sub-solar mass component. Parameter estimation indicates that the other two events, if real, would be neutron star - black hole binaries. The remaining two triggers do not provide informative parameter estimation. We also study three O4a compact binary coalescence triggers, and one O3 trigger, that have been noted by three other groups, and our parameter estimation indicates that three of these may contain a sub-solar mass component. We study the data quality associated with these triggers. Finally, we discuss the challenges for parameter estimation on compact binary coalescence events containing a sub-solar mass component: long signal duration, possible small chirp masses, possible small mass ratios, and data quality issues over potentially hundreds of seconds of data.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Efficient Analysis of Numerous Galactic Compact Binaries via the Free-bin Scheme
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Global analysis of Galactic compact binaries (GCBs) for space-based gravitational-wave detectors is computationally demanding in the high-frequency region (above $\sim$10 mHz), where resolvable signals are sparse but frequency samples are numerous. We propose a free-bin scheme that evaluates the nontrivial likelihood only in movable frequency windows centered on sampled signal frequencies. The method preserves the joint-likelihood structure by replacing only the signal-containing regions of a precomputed null likelihood, and avoids the fixed-bin edge effect by construction because the windows follow the sampled frequencies. In a simulated TianQin dataset containing 193 GCBs, 192 injected sources are recovered with waveform fitting factors above 0.99. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that the free-bin and conventional full-band likelihood implementations yield identical results when the same finite-length local waveforms and numerical settings are used. Computational benchmarks show that the acceleration is primarily controlled by the fraction of the frequency domain covered by the merged signal windows and decreases as this coverage increases.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures. Published in Physics Letters B

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and geodesic completeness relative to vacuum, finding in general that coupling to matter does not eliminate the existence of theories with regular solutions.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A covariant analysis of massless Dirac fields in LRS spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the massless Dirac field in locally rotationally symmetric (LRS) spacetimes using a covariant spinorial-fluid representation, with the spinor current and spin direction aligned with the LRS frame. When the current has both vorticity and sheet twist, characterized by a constant ratio $λ$, the LRS integrability condition relates evolution and propagation derivatives, reducing the field equations to an ordinary differential system that can be integrated exactly. The integrability of the chiral angle forces the heat flux to vanish and the source to saturate the null energy condition along the two radial null directions. A constant boost in the radial Lorentzian two-plane maps the spinor current to a canonical congruence, which is stationary (LRS~I) for $|λ|>1$ and irrotational and geodesic (LRS~III) for $|λ|<1$. In this frame, the local metric is reconstructed in the Goode--Wainwright--Van den Bergh canonical form. For $|λ|>1$ the energy density is positive, and the metric is locally isometric to the horizonless charged Taub--NUT (Brill) metric: in the polar representation, the massless Dirac field supplies a stress--energy tensor algebraically identical to that of the Brill electromagnetic field, with no Maxwell field present. For $|λ|<1$, the energy density is negative and the metric is the hyperbolic ($k=-1$) charged NUT metric with a formal negative squared-charge parameter, whose homogeneous slices are of LRS Bianchi type~VIII.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dark Energy Based on Modified Gravity: Where the Future Lies?
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Based on current observational data, there is a strong possibility that dark energy was in a phantom regime in the near past, and a transition from a phantom to a quintessential regime may have occurred. Since then, many scenarios compatible with the DESI data have been proposed. In particular, there exist several realistic models in the framework of $F(R)$ gravity. In this paper, we show that such realistic models of $F(R)$ gravity may produce an anti-gravity or ghost graviton in the future. The problem could be avoided by further changing the parameters and fine-tuning the initial conditions, but we propose to introduce a potential barrier of the scalar field for the small scalar curvature region, which prevents the Universe from evolving into the anti-gravity or having a ghost graviton region, without the fine-tuning of the initial conditions. We also discuss how this regime can be tested using peculiar velocity and kSZ effect probes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Microscopic Cosmological Backreaction of an Ultralight Majoron Coupled to a Coherent Hidden Pseudo-Dirac Ensemble
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We develop a microscopic framework for the cosmological backreaction of a hidden pseudo-Dirac fermion ensemble derivatively coupled to an ultralight Majoron. Starting from the effective action, we derive the exact operator Ward identity for the pseudo-Dirac current and the associated microscopic energy-transfer law. For a thermal density matrix prepared at a finite initial time, we calculate the subsequent collisionless, linearized coherence response without assuming continued thermal equilibrium or introducing phenomenological dissipation. The finite-time retarded solution retains the initial boundary transient and nonlocal memory contribution, allowing us to assess the validity of the leading local adiabatic approximation and distinguish reversible coherent energy exchange from dissipative friction. For a subdominant Majoron benchmark evolving in a prescribed FRW background, the local energy-transfer rate changes sign, while the present-day fractional velocity correction is only $+5.23\times10^{-53}$. A convergence-tested numerical comparison, including the initial transient and memory contribution, bounds the difference between the retarded and local fractional velocity corrections to less than $6.78\times10^{-17}$ of the local correction. Within the linearized, collisionless positive-energy two-state approximation, these results demonstrate that the microscopic backreaction does not produce significant Majoron freezing for the benchmark considered, while leaving open different behavior in other parameter regimes or preparation histories.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Type-II quasinormal modes of dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg AdS black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this paper, we investigate Type-II quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a magnetically charged dilaton--Euler--Heisenberg black hole in anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetime. The Type-II includes coupled gravitational, dilaton and electromagnetic perturbations. Its coupled equations are derived for $\ell=0,1,2$ modes and the QNM frequencies are calculated by employing direct integration and Chebyshev pseudospectral methods, giving consistent results. For nondegenerate dipole ($\ell=1$) mode at fixed curvature, the nonlinear correction starts at order $Q^2$ for electromagnetic-led branch and at order $Q^4$ for scalar-led branch. In this case, stronger AdS curvature enhances reduction of the electromagnetic-led real frequency for positive coupling, while gravitational-led quadrupole real frequency changes weakly with charge. As the curvature weakens, the dipole frequencies approach the AdS normal-mode scale and their damping decreases. We find that all modes computed have negative imaginary parts for nonextremal black holes, implying this black hole is stable against Type-II perturbations. Furthermore, we explore the connection between thermodynamic phase transition and QNMs for $\ell=0$ dilaton. For a subcritical isobaric process, the QNM real frequency of $\ell=0$ dilaton decreases with increasing temperature of small black holes, while it increases with increasing temperature of large black holes. At coexistence, the damping rate for large black holes is about 4.28 times that for small black holes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Imprints of screened dark energy on nonlocal quantum correlations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate how screening mechanisms, reconciling light scalar fields driving cosmic acceleration with local fifth force constraints, can be probed via their impact on nonlocal quantum correlations between entangled spin pairs, whose evolution on a curved background is affected by General Relativity (GR) and screened modified gravity effects. We consider a gedankenexperiment featuring a pair of massive, spin-$1/2$ particles orbiting the Earth, evaluating their nonlocal correlations through spin observables associated to the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. Using a general formalism developed earlier for curved space-time spin evolution, we compute the effects of screening on the CHSH inequality, finding its degree of violation to be suppressed relative to the flat space-time case. Applying this formalism to the chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton mechanisms, we identify currently unconstrained regions of parameter space where the screening contribution is comparable to that of GR. While detecting these effects will be challenging, our work provides a proof-of-principle for testing screened dark energy through quantum nonlocality.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 24 pages, 3 figures (6 subfigures in total); v2: typos corrected, references added, accepted for publication in Physical Review D; v3: further typos fixed; v4: minor notational corrections; v5: corrections and updated figures, symmetron and dilaton results revised

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Bounds on screened dark energy from near-Earth space-based measurements
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We test screened dark energy with near-Earth, space-based measurements. In a post-Newtonian framework, we compute leading corrections to geodetic precession (Gravity Probe B), LAGEOS-2 pericenter advance, and the Sagnac delay in a prospective orbital configuration, yielding bounds on chameleon, symmetron, and dilaton models. LAGEOS-2 sets the strongest Earth-orbit limits on symmetron and dilaton, while a Sagnac setup at the projected sensitivity of state-of-the-art space clocks gives the tightest chameleon constraint. These results show that low-density, space-based experiments sensitively probe screened dark energy and exclude previously allowed parameter space. Notably, at an assumed delay precision of $\mathcal{O}\big(10^{-19}\big)$, a Sagnac test would exclude the entire chameleon parameter space considered.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures (4 subfigures); v2: typos corrected, clarifications and references added, accepted for publication in Physical Review Letters; v3: corrections and updated figures, conclusions unchanged

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quantum Metric and Nonlinear Hall Effect of Photons
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Using the path-integral formalism, we show that photons possess a nontrivial quantum metric in momentum space. We derive the semiclassical action and equations of motion by taking into account the quantum metric. In media with a spatially varying refractive index $n(\mathbf{x})$, the quantum metric induces a shift in the trajectory of light at second order in spatial gradients of $n$, whose transverse component may be regarded as a nonlinear Hall effect of light. The quantum metric also gives rise to corrections to photon propagation relevant to gravitational lensing in curved spacetime at second order in wavelength, including a gravitational nonlinear Hall effect arising from the interplay between the geometry of position space and that of momentum space.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 6 pages; v2: several equations corrected; optical observability estimate and discussion added; clarifications and references added

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Fractal phase structure of QCD under imaginary rotation
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We show that in hot QCD rotating at an imaginary angular velocity $\tildeΩ_I$, the angular velocity selects not only the temperature of the bulk but whether charge conjugation $C$ is broken there. For QCD at temperature $T$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $θ$, with $\tildeΩ_I/2π=p/q$ in lowest terms, the bulk far from the rotation axis is in the same thermal equilibrium state as nonrotating QCD at temperature $T/q$ and imaginary quark chemical potential $θ'=qθ+π(p+q+1)$; this follows from the Euclidean boundary conditions and locality alone, and holds nonperturbatively whenever the equivalent nonrotating system has a finite correlation length. Consequently, even at zero quark chemical potential, the bulk is placed at the Roberge-Weiss (RW) point whenever $p$ and $q$ are both odd, and $C$ is spontaneously broken there for $T>qT_{\rm RW}$, with $T_{\rm RW}$ the RW endpoint temperature. The bulks at $\tildeΩ_I=2π/3$ and $4π/3$, for example, are both at temperature $T/3$, yet only the former can break $C$. The set of imaginary angular velocities at which $C$ is broken has a fractal structure: raising $T$ adds rationals of ever larger denominator. At irrational $\tildeΩ_I/2π$ the bulk corresponds to zero-temperature QCD at any $T$ and remains confined.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Lattice Configuration Generation with a Self-Learning Diffusion Model
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We show that a diffusion model for lattice field theory can be trained by self-learning, without configurations from a separate simulation, and used as the generator of an exact Markov chain. Training starts from exact samples at $β=0$, and along a ladder of couplings the model's own chain at each coupling, weighted by the action difference, trains the score at the next. A Metropolis-Hastings test on each proposal and its noising path keeps the sampled distribution exact for any network, so that network errors affect only the acceptance and autocorrelation times. In the two-dimensional compact XY model up to $β=1$, on the high-temperature side of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition, ladders at $L=4$ and $8$ reproduce exact and reference values of the energy density and helicity modulus at every coupling, and the generator trained from $β=0$ at $L=8$ has the same acceptance as one trained on an exact chain at $β=1$. The acceptance follows the relation known from hybrid Monte Carlo, with terms set by the number of noise levels and by the network error per site, and a network trained at $L=4$ generates up to $L=16$ when the number of levels grows with the volume.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Information geometry of continuum limits in lattice field theory: The Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: When the Boltzmann weight is nonnegative, the actions of a lattice field theory form a statistical manifold, whose Fisher metric gives the number of measurements needed to distinguish two nearby actions. For the two-dimensional lattice Gross-Neveu model with Wilson fermions in the large-$N$ limit, we study the continuum limit, in which the lattice spacing $a$ goes to zero at fixed mass gap $Λ$, through the Fisher metric of the distribution of the auxiliary field $σ$. The renormalization condition fixes an expectation coordinate, and dimensional transmutation becomes an exponential relation between it and a natural coordinate. The main result is that the $a\to0$ limits differ between the Fisher metric of the long-distance modes, whose momenta are fixed in physical units, and that of the full $P(σ)$. In the former, the infinitely many irrelevant directions that change the kinetic term locally shrink relative to the mass-term direction to order $aΛ\log(1/(aΛ))$ or smaller, and several modes together leave only the two directions $(Λ,m)$ of the continuum theory. In the latter, the kinetic-term directions shrink as fast as the mass-term direction, and the difference in the regularization remains in lattice-scale correlations. In the eight-dimensional space of local deformations examined numerically, the one exception is the deformation that only adds a contact term to the propagator, which as $a\to0$ becomes indistinguishable from a change of $1/g^2$ in both metrics. In the Fisher metric of the full $P(σ)$, the curvature of the coupling plane at fixed kinetic term diverges as $(1/2)\log^2(1/(aΛ))$, not as the correlation volume often assumed in thermodynamic geometry, and the critical point lies at infinite distance in this plane.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 40 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. v2: revised throughout; added a maximum-entropy reading of the renormalization condition (Sec. III), the finite-N condition (Sec. IV C), the eigenvalues in a normalized basis (Appendix C), and the finite Fisher length of smeared long-distance fields (Sec. IV E)

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Optimised 8th-Order Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Quantum Simulation
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Simulating quantum dynamics in many-body systems is one of the most promising applications of quantum computers. Product formulas are a natural choice for this task, since they map directly onto quantum gates, and increasing their order $n$ could lead to reduced gate depths, provided the parameters are chosen efficiently. So far, schemes beyond $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order have only been built as compositions of second-order schemes, while more general product formulas are known only up to $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. In this work, we extend our optimisation framework to order $n = 8$, and find both more efficient compositions and the first $8^{\textrm{th}}$ order general schemes. Our formulas improve on the theoretical efficiency of the state-of-the-art schemes by Morales et al and we recommend two schemes explicitly. In simulations of the Heisenberg XZ chain one of our recommended schemes always outperforms those by Morales et al, though it is not always the same scheme that performs best. More generally, we observe that for Hamiltonians split into many non-commuting operators the uniformity of a Trotter decomposition becomes the main indicator of a scheme's performance. To assess the schemes' use on quantum hardware, we simulate noisy circuits with our new Qiskit plugin qiskit-omelyan. At current noise levels, the Leapfrog scheme remains the best choice, but as noise rates decrease toward fault tolerance, our recommended schemes become competitive.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Sampling non-abelian lattice gauge theories with diffusion models
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We present gauge-equivariant diffusion models as samplers for lattice gauge theories (LGTs). Using lattice gauge-equivariant convolutional neural networks (L-CNNs) and the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA), we are able to accurately sample two-dimensional U(2) field configurations and show first promising results for four-dimensional SU(3). Our two-dimensional models extrapolate remarkably well to larger inverse couplings than originally trained on. We confirm this by comparing observables to analytically known values and to hybrid Monte Carlo results.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 7 pages, 4 figures, contribution to the Proceedings of the 22nd International Conference on QCD in Extreme Conditions (xQCD 2026), 14-17 July 2026, Busan, Korea

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Solving fermionic sign problems with physics-informed kernels
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We extend the generative sampling approach with physics-informed kernels (PIKs) [1,2] to a general class of physics systems with complex distributions and a structure also encountered in fermionic systems. The resolution of sign problems of generic weighted sums of complex Gaußian distributions with the PIK approach is central to this application. In a first step, PIKs map a real normal distribution to such a weighted sum, and this procedure is called the PIKfan. The PIKfan has the sampling cost of a real normal distribution. In a second step, this weighted sum is evolved with a second PIK into the distribution of the theory at hand. In combination, we reduce the sampling task for a general class of complex systems to a Gaußian one, and the main computational task is that of computing the PIK. We illustrate the approach with the one-site Hubbard model at arbitrary chemical potential and with $φ^4$-deformed extensions of it.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Operator Learning for Spectral Reconstruction from Euclidean Correlators
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: In this work, we propose a novel supervised machine-learning-based strategy for extracting smeared spectral functions from Euclidean correlation functions. The strategy revisits the numerically ill-posed spectral reconstruction problem within the framework of Operator Learning through the use of DeepONet-like architectures. To illustrate the method, we construct an ensemble of neural networks trained on mock data generated from Gaussian Processes containing different levels of prior knowledge. This ensemble is then employed to estimate the systematic uncertainty associated with the fact that a neural network provides only an approximation to the target operator. The procedure is fully validated on previously unseen noisy mock data. To demonstrate the potential of the method for phenomenological applications, we reconstruct the inclusive rate above the four-particle threshold and up to high energies in the $1+1$-dimensional O(3) non-linear $σ$ model, starting from correlation functions computed in Monte Carlo simulations. The final result is consistent with the known analytic spectral density and, compared with the state-of-the-art Hansen-Lupo-Tantalo algorithm, exhibits a significant reduction in the total uncertainty even under mild physical assumptions encoded in the training set. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to more phenomenologically relevant observables in lattice QCD.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 37 pages, 20 figures, 5 tables. Revised version accepted for publication in PRD

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Electromagnetic pion mass splitting using a Pauli-Villars-regulated photon propagator
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We present a lattice QCD calculation of the charged-neutral pion mass splitting $M_{π^+} - M_{π^0}$ at $\mathcal{O}(α_\mathrm{em})$ using a recently proposed framework based on a Pauli-Villars (PV) regulated photon propagator defined in the continuum and infinite-volume limit, with $Λ$ acting as an additional UV cutoff scale. This formulation, when combined with a dedicated treatment of the elastic contribution, avoids power-law finite-volume effects on electromagnetic mass shifts. We perform the calculation using CLS ensembles, studying finite-volume effects, the continuum limit and the extrapolation to the physical point for several values of the scale $Λ$. By means of the Cottingham formula, we further decompose the result into elastic and inelastic contributions at fixed $Λ$. Our final result, after removing the cutoff scale $Λ$, is $M_{π^+} - M_{π^0} = 4.56(22)$ MeV, in good agreement with the experimental measurement. Our complete calculation demonstrates that, for a mass splitting not requiring any counterterms, the formalism can be implemented successfully, whilst also offering useful insights into the computation of electromagnetic corrections to other observables.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 32 pages, 13 figures, 5 tables. Revised version accepted for publication in JHEP

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Efficient Trotter-Suzuki Schemes for Long-time Quantum Dynamics
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Accurately simulating long-time dynamics of many-body systems is a challenge in both classical and quantum computing due to the accumulation of Trotter errors. While low-order Trotter-Suzuki decompositions are straightforward to implement, their rapidly growing error limits access to long-time observables. We present a framework for constructing efficient high-order Trotter-Suzuki schemes by identifying their structure and directly optimizing their parameters over a high-dimensional space. This method enables the discovery of new schemes with significantly improved efficiency compared to traditional constructions, such as those by Suzuki and Yoshida. Based on the theoretical efficiency and practical performance, we recommend two novel highly efficient schemes at $4^{\textrm{th}}$ and $6^{\textrm{th}}$ order. We also demonstrate the effectiveness of these decompositions on the Heisenberg model and the quantum harmonic oscillator, and find that for a fixed final time they perform better across the computational cost. Even when using large time steps, they surpass established low-order schemes like the Leapfrog. Finally, we investigate the in-practice performance of different Trotter schemes and find the decompositions with more uniform coefficients tend to feature improved error accumulation over long times. We have included this observation into our choice of recommended schemes.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 28 + 7 pages, 11 figures, 5 tables and 1 animation; v2 (published version): Added scheme comparison table and fixed grouping mistake, v3: fixed origin point typo, v4: fixed mistake in Eq.(27)

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: From Resonance Properties to High-Energy Behavior: The $R$ Ratio from Lattice QCD
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We investigate resonance properties and inclusive spectral behavior through Bayesian reconstruction of the $R$-ratio from Euclidean lattice correlators near the physical pion mass. Without additional Gaussian smearing, the reconstructed spectrum already captures the smooth high-energy behavior observed in experiment. Direct integration of the $ρ$ peak determines $f_ρ$ with approximately $1\%$ statistical precision and close agreement with the experimental reference, providing access to resonance properties without resolving individual finite-volume levels. With a common Gaussian width of $σ=0.6$~GeV, the lattice and experimental $R$-ratios show good overall agreement over $0.25$--$2.50$~GeV. Comparisons among ensembles with spatial extents up to approximately $10$~fm demonstrate that finite-volume effects can be controlled across these complementary observables. These results demonstrate a unified framework for studying resonance and inclusive physics from lattice QCD, with potential applications to other hadronic channels, inclusive decay rates, and hadronic tensors.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: From Self-Dual to Physical $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$: Anomalies, Boundary Stokes Phenomenon, and Global Structure of $θ$-vacua
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We introduce a two-coupling generalization of $\mathbb{C}P^{N-1}$ model that continuously interpolates between the self-dual ($ε=0$) and the physical ($ε=g$) theories as a useful nonperturbative tool. At $ε\neq g$, this model possesses a chiral imbalance, which may be viewed as a real topological deformation (imaginary-$θ$). We demonstrate that exact quantum equivalence between first- and second-order formulations strictly requires a topological counterterm sourced by a bosonic chiral anomaly. Solving this deformed theory at large $N$ yields two primary results. First, we analytically determine the nonperturbative vacuum structure of the self-dual theory, a self-dual vacuum with a dynamically generated field-strength condensate. Second, we resolve a fundamental paradox where saddles with $(θ+ 2πn) \sim O(N)$ ($n$ is branch number) spuriously yield lower energy densities than the physical ground state. Because the effective action possesses an essential singularity at $F=0$, we show that the Lefschetz thimble analysis must be generalized to include boundary thimbles. A boundary Stokes phenomenon renders the problematic saddles topologically inactive, fully restoring the validity of the large-$N$ expansion for strongly coupled theories.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Casimir effect in Gribov-Zwanziger theory
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We consider Yang-Mills theory with two infinite parallel plates, separated by a distance \(L\), that are perfect magnetic conductors (PMC) or perfect electric conductors (PEC). Recently, it was shown that the Gribov copy problem persists in such a setting. We then study the Gribov-Zwanziger (GZ) action in the presence of those boundaries using functional integral methods. Lagrange multiplier fields allow one to lift the boundary conditions into the action, after which the boundary modifications to the gluon propagator can straightforwardly be determined. In the PEC case, we provide evidence that, even when translation invariance is (partially) broken, the usual horizon term in the GZ action still restricts the functional integral to the Gribov region. We compute the Casimir energy for GZ with PMC or PEC plates, both directly from the functional integral and from the energy-momentum tensor, obtaining consistent results. We compare our analytical results with recent lattice data, in both 4D and 3D. A priori, one might expect that the boundary-modified gluon propagator introduces new \(L\)-dependencies into the GZ gap equation. This would make the Gribov mass \(γ\) dynamically dependent on \(L\), implying an interesting interplay with the Casimir energy. However, we show that no such dynamical \(L\)-dependence occurs within the current approximation.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: The index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators: I
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: This is the first of a series of papers which will be devoted to a study of the index of mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on closed Riemannian manifolds. The aim of the series is to discretise the index of the Dirac operator. On flat tori, this is achieved by the Wilson--Dirac operator of lattice gauge theory on a regular lattice. On a general closed Riemannian manifold, however, no regular lattice is available. As an intermediate step between the continuum Dirac operator and its discretisations, we introduce mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators on any closed Riemannian manifold, defined by integrating covariant differences over distances comparable to a fixed length scale. In this paper, we define the index of the mesoscopic Wilson--Dirac operators via spectral flow and prove that it agrees with that of the continuum Dirac operator at all sufficiently small scales. The proof rests on an elliptic estimate uniform in the scale and a Rellich-type compactness theorem. In the second paper, we shall pass from mesoscopic operators to discrete Wilson--Dirac operators.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Numerical tests of 5D APS $η$-invariant phases for 4D chiral fermions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We calculate the phase of a 4D chiral fermion determinant from the 5D Atiyah--Patodi--Singer (APS) $η$-invariant. We study the anomaly-free $SU(5)$ representation $\mathbf{10}\oplus\overline{\mathbf 5}$ on a four-torus, using gauge fields independent of one coordinate. For these backgrounds, the 4D phase can be calculated independently from a 3D Dirac spectrum. For an Abelian background embedded in $SU(5)$, two different 5D bulk extensions reproduce the 4D phase within $0.03\%$ in the tested heat-kernel extrapolations. One extension changes the spatial gauge field along the fifth direction and requires a coupled 5D spectral calculation. An independent single-charge check reproduces the Chern--Simons anomaly coefficient within $0.3\%$ using quadratic extrapolations. We also calculate 5D APS phases for non-Abelian backgrounds in the $SU(4)\times U(1)$ subgroup. For a background generating the full $\mathfrak{su}(4)$ algebra, the 5D phase with a fixed spatial field agrees with the independent 4D phase within $0.5\%$ over the six heat-kernel parameters examined. We further study a varying-field 5D extension for an embedded $SU(2)$ background. These results show that the 5D APS calculation reproduces a nonzero chiral phase after anomaly cancellation.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Examples of infinitesimal Gribov copies in the presence of planar boundaries, and an emergent boundary gauge invariance in Yang-Mills theory
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: First, we explicitly construct zero-modes of the Yang-Mills Faddeev-Popov operator in the presence of two parallel plates, with either perfect electric (PEC) or perfect magnetic (PMC) boundary conditions imposed. This establishes the existence of infinitesimal Gribov copies with finite action, and even finite L_2-norm, in Yang-Mills theory with non-trivial interfaces. We adapt Henyey's construction, although the boundary configuration imposes extra restrictions on the ansatz for the gauge field. Second, we discuss the phenomenon of an emergent boundary gauge invariance for PEC and PMC plates in Yang-Mills theory. This shall be important when applying the Gribov-Zwanziger procedure to parallel plate setups, of relevance for non-perturbatively studying the non-Abelian Casimir effect in the future.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 16 pages, 6 .jpg figures. v2: version accepted for publication in JHEP

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: String breaking in a (1+1)-dimensional $e^+e^-$ collider
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: In this paper, we develop a framework for studying solitons in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories using tensor networks, and we apply it to simulate $e^+e^-$ collisions in the massive Schwinger model. We work at $θ= π$ and at a bare fermion mass exceeding the critical value; in this regime, there are two degenerate vacua, and the $e^+$ and $e^-$ particles are realized as soliton states interpolating between them. We carefully explain how to find and characterize such soliton states using infinite tensor network methods, and then exhibit real-time simulations of their collisions. These collisions involve the formation of an energetic flux string, and we demonstrate that our final states are superpositions of elastic and string-breaking trajectories.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Lattice QCD determination of the $γZ$ box contribution to the proton weak charge
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the $γZ$ box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, $\square_{γZ}$, a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to $E=155$ MeV. At $E=0$, the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain $\square_{γZ}(0)=0.00411(9)$. Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of $Q_W^p=0.06987(50)$. The calculated energy dependence of $\square_{γZ}$ is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract $Q_W^p$.Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the $γZ$ box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Evidence for Y-shaped color confinement of fully heavy baryons
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: The geometry of color confinement in baryons remains a fundamental question in quantum chromodynamics. We investigate whether heavy-quark spectroscopy can distinguish a genuine three-body Y-shaped confining interaction from a sum of pairwise $Δ$-shaped interaction. Using a high-precision three-body Schrödinger solver, we perform a simultaneous analysis of experimentally measured bottomonium masses and lattice-QCD calculations of $Ω_{bbb}$ excitation energies. For each confinement scenario, interaction parameters are independently optimized against the combined spectra. We find that the Y-shaped potential provides a consistent description of both systems, whereas the $Δ$-shaped potential exhibits significant discrepancies. Our results provide spectroscopic evidence favoring a collective three-body confining interaction and establish triply-heavy baryon spectroscopy as a complementary probe of the nonperturbative geometry of color confinement.

Quantum Physics.title: Addressable gate-based logical computation with quantum LDPC codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum computing relies on quantum error correction for high-fidelity logical operations, but scaling to achieve near-term quantum utility is highly resource-intensive. High-rate quantum LDPC codes can reduce error correction overhead, yet realizing high-rate fault-tolerant computation with these codes remains a central challenge. Lattice surgery remains the main approach for addressable logical computation but at a cost of $\mathcal{O}(d)$ time overhead. Other approaches rely on low-rate code switching methods or high space overhead homomorphic CNOT. In this work, we introduce a gate-based protocol for addressable single- and multi-qubit Clifford operations on individual logical qubits encoded within one or more quantum LDPC codes. Our scheme leverages logical transversal operations via an auxiliary -- a Bacon-Shor code or an unrotated surface code -- to perform logical operations with constant time overhead enabled by teleportation. We demonstrate the implementation of an overcomplete logical Clifford gate set and perform numerical simulations to evaluate the error-correction performance of our protocol. Additionally, our scheme can also realize any joint Pauli product measurement natively. Finally, we observe that our scheme can be integrated with magic state cultivation protocols to achieve universal, gate-based, and fully addressable quantum computation.

Quantum Physics.title: Impact of structured noise on bosonic quantum error correction
Quantum Physics.summary: Bosonic quantum error correction relies on an accurate description of single-photon loss dissipation using an ideal annihilation operator, under which correctable loss errors act equivalently on different logical code states. In realistic weakly nonlinear bosonic modes, however, coupling to a structured environment can render photon loss Fock-state dependent, thereby modifying the effective dissipation operator and deforming the associated error space. Here, we experimentally investigate this effect in a three-dimensional circuit quantum electrodynamics system. By injecting spectrally engineered environmental noise into a weakly nonlinear oscillator, we observe pronounced frequency selectivity in the measured Fock-state dynamics. While the long-time transition rates converge to the Markovian limit, the transient dynamics display distinctly non-Markovian behavior, in quantitative agreement with a second-order time-convolutionless theory. By applying narrowband noise to a binomially encoded logical qubit, we further demonstrate Fock-state-dependent dissipation channels that drive logical states beyond the nominally correctable error space. These results establish structured environmental noise as a mechanism for deforming photon-loss errors in weakly nonlinear bosonic systems and highlight the need to incorporate realistic, state-dependent dissipation into the design and characterization of bosonic quantum error correction.

Quantum Physics.title: Perturbative Recovery of Stabilizer-Subspace Correlations for Quantum Computational Chemistry
Quantum Physics.summary: Stabilizer-based subspace methods can substantially reduce the quantum resources required for electronic structure calculations, but the resulting projection neglects Hamiltonian couplings to configurations outside the retained subspace. In this work, we introduce Stabilizer-Subspace Perturbation Theory (SSPT) to recover the associated correlation contributions, using the Contextual Subspace Variational Quantum Eigensolver (CS-VQE) as a representative application. The central idea is to exploit the Pauli terms eliminated by stabilizer projection as perturbative operators that generate an external manifold from the optimized reference state. Their energetic contributions are evaluated using an Epstein-Nesbet-type second-order correction or a resolvent-based formulation that retains couplings within the external space. By exploiting the factorized structure of the stabilizer-constrained reference state, the required matrix elements can be evaluated through Pauli expectation values on the reduced contextual register without explicitly reconstructing the full-space wave function. Molecular benchmarks demonstrate substantial reductions in projection-induced energy errors, allowing chemical precision to be achieved with fewer contextual qubits in several cases. These results establish stabilizer-guided perturbation theory as a promising strategy for improving the accuracy of resource-efficient quantum chemistry calculations.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Otto engine powered by an anisotropic Heisenberg XYZ model under independent local magnetic fields
Quantum Physics.summary: We study a quantum Otto heat engine whose working substance is an anisotropic two-qubit Heisenberg XYZ model. Independent local magnetic fields are used to control each spin individually. The influence of the longitudinal coupling, anisotropy, transverse coupling, and local fields on the net work output and efficiency is systematically examined. Reducing the longitudinal coupling is found to markedly improve both the maximum work and the peak efficiency. The engine performance reaches an optimum at a particular value of the anisotropy parameter. A local work analysis clarifies how work is produced during the cycle. Because of the asymmetric local fields and the intrinsic spin-spin interaction, the two qubits play markedly different thermodynamic roles; the interaction term itself contributes crucially to the total work. We further analyze the variation of quantum entanglement, quantified by concurrence, along the cycle. The results indicate that a pronounced change in entanglement between the hot and cold isomagnetic strokes is closely correlated with the efficiency enhancement. This work offers new insight into the operating principles and control of quantum Otto heat engines.
Quantum Physics.comment: 26 pages, 9 figures. All numerical calculations, symbolic verifications, and figure generation were performed using open-source Python libraries (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib). No proprietary commercial software was used in the production of this work. The complete Python source code is available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request

Quantum Physics.title: Privacy-Enhanced Distributed Sensing Network via Causal-Order Switching and Probe Squeezing
Quantum Physics.summary: As sensor networks become more interconnected, sensitive information sharing among multiple users poses potential risks of information leakage, making privacy protection a critical challenge. To address this challenge, we quantify network privacy using the maximum information leakage ratio (MILR) and propose a protocol that enhances privacy through causal-order switching and probe squeezing. Causal-order switching harnesses intrinsic network propagation dynamics for privacy encoding, while probe squeezing suppresses information leakage through quantum channels and increases the information available for estimating the global parameter. These mechanisms enable an asymptotic exponential enhancement on the privacy with the squeezing rate. We experimentally demonstrate this mechanism in distributed beam-tilt sensing using spatially structured light without requiring nonclassical light sources. Our work identifies intrinsic network propagation dynamics as a resource for privacy protection and opens a new avenue for continuous-variable sensing networks that combine high precision with enhanced privacy.
Quantum Physics.comment: 27 pages in total. Main text: 15 pages, 5 figures. Supplementary material: 12 pages, 8 figures

Quantum Physics.title: Attainable and unattainable gauge-dependent quantum precision limits in ultrastrong light--matter coupling
Quantum Physics.summary: In this paper, we study the gauge dependence of quantum precision in ultrastrongly coupled light--matter systems. The unitary between gauges carries the coupling $g$, so each truncation defines a different family. The quantum Fisher information traces an exact parabola across frames. Harmonic matter minimizes it at a universal $θ_\ast=Ω/(Ω+ω)$, set by the matter and cavity frequencies. Only the minimal-coupling bound is attainable. Frames differ by a factor $9.6$ with opposite trends. Diverging virtual-excitation gain at the Dicke point is a gauge artifact and saturates.

Quantum Physics.title: Efficient Spectra and Dynamics with Tangent-Space Chebyshev Tree Tensor Networks
Quantum Physics.summary: We present a tangent-space Chebyshev method (TaChe), which combines tree tensor network states with Chebyshev recursion and maximum entropy spectral analysis in a tree tensor network tangent space, for quantum many-body spectra and dynamics. Implemented tensor network state calculations in the tangent space of the ground state, the core advantage of TaChe is that it can substantially reduce the computational complexity, memory usage, and numerical instability associated with tensor network state compression. Implemented on the GPU platform, it produces accurate spectra with speedups of up to $46.8$ over the previous Chebyshev tensor network method and $13.7$ over one-site time-dependent variational principle propagation in the reported benchmarks. Applications to acetonitrile, thermal aggregate emission, finite-temperature charge transport on a \(6\times6\) lattice, and internal conversion in aggregates of up to 100 molecules demonstrate the efficiency and versatility of TaChe in simulating complex molecular systems.

Quantum Physics.title: Channel coding against quantum jammers via minimax
Quantum Physics.summary: We study classical communication over fully quantum arbitrarily varying channels, in which a jammer can prepare an arbitrary state entangled across channel uses. We formulate assisted codes as joint input-output maps and apply Sion's minimax theorem to exchange optimization over codes and jamming states at fixed message size. Combining this reduction with one-shot coding bounds and a generalized quantum asymptotic equipartition property yields a single-letter formula for the entanglement-assisted classical capacity, a single-letter formula for the shared-randomness-assisted capacity of classical-quantum channels, and a regularized formula for general quantum input channels. For entanglement assistance and for shared-randomness-assisted classical-quantum channels, we extend the capacity formulas to arbitrary jammer Hilbert spaces while keeping the sender and receiver systems finite-dimensional. The extension uses finite-dimensional approximations at each blocklength, a uniform bound on the change in coding error, and compact closures of finite-dimensional output-state sets. These arguments avoid de Finetti reductions and establish equality with the corresponding compound-channel capacities in these two settings.
Quantum Physics.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure, 1 table We solved the infinite-dimensional case in this version

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Subentropy: Subadditivity and Sharp Bounds on Discrimination Error
Quantum Physics.summary:
Subentropy gives a tight spectral lower bound on the accessible information of ensembles of pure states. We prove its subadditivity for arbitrary bipartite states in finite dimensions and derive a sharp relation between conditional subentropy and the minimum discrimination error. This relation strengthens a conjectured comparison with conditional min-entropy. Its inverse gives the strongest universal lower bound on the error determined only by conditional subentropy and the number of labels. Both main results follow from a comparison of conditional subentropy with the average subentropy of measurement posteriors, valid for mixed signal states and every finite measurement. We characterize all equality cases in these two results and bound posterior deviations near equality. We also determine the optimal Lipschitz constant in trace distance for conditional subentropy on classical-quantum states, including the exact constant when the quantum marginal is fixed. A determinant inequality strengthens subadditivity and proves strong subadditivity for classical distributions, while an exact counterexample shows that strong subadditivity fails for quantum states.
  Lean 4 proofs of all theoretical results are available at https://pratikpatil.io/lean/subentropy/

Quantum Physics.title: Combining Schrödinger and Heisenberg Evolution to Extend Quantum Many-Body Simulations
Quantum Physics.summary: Classical simulations of quantum many-body dynamics face complementary limitations: entanglement growth restricts state evolution in the Schrödinger picture, while operator spreading makes Heisenberg-picture calculations increasingly expensive. Here, we combine both approaches by evolving quantum states and observables independently and joining their dynamics through massively parallel tensor-network contractions. We implement this strategy using tree tensor networks and sparse Pauli propagation, extending evolution times beyond those reached by either method separately in our calculations. For a quench of the two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model at the critical field, we simulate the magnetization of an $11\times11$ open lattice up to $t=1.20$ by combining state and operator evolution over intervals $t_S=t_H=0.60$. We compare the dynamics with iPEPS, numerical linked-cluster expansion, and X-truncated sparse Pauli dynamics results. We also combine exact state evolution on small clusters with operator propagation on a larger lattice, improving agreement with iPEPS relative to cluster evolution alone. We further derive error bounds showing how the state can suppress operator errors and the evolved observable can reduce sensitivity to state errors.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum simulation of low-temperature impurity models
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum impurity models, which describe a small but strongly-interacting subsystem coupled to a large noninteracting bath, are the computational core of dynamical mean field theory and play an important role in simulating strongly correlated materials. We develop quantum algorithms for efficiently simulating these models at low temperatures and with high precision. For any impurity model on $n$ fermionic modes with fixed impurity size: (1) We give a quantum algorithm that prepares the thermal state at inverse temperature $β$ to precision $δ$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,β,\log(1/δ))$. This algorithm is the first to achieve both polynomial scaling in the inverse temperature and polylogarithmic scaling in the precision. When the Hamiltonian has an inverse-polynomial spectral gap, our quantum algorithm prepares its ground state to precision $δ$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log(1/δ))$. (2) We further give a quantum algorithm that prepares a purification of the thermal state in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,β,\log(1/δ))$. Using this purification, we estimate static and dynamical properties with error $δ$ in time polynomial in $n$ and $β$ and linear in $1/δ$ up to polylogarithmic factors, achieving the Heisenberg scaling. Our algorithms build on quantum Gibbs samplers, which are quantum analogues of Markov chain Monte Carlo methods. By using global jump operators instead of local ones, we avoid the $\exp(β)$ overhead commonly associated with quantum Gibbs samplers, making them efficient for impurity models even at low temperatures.

Quantum Physics.title: Observable-Level Expressivity in Fixed-Readout Quantum Neural Networks
Quantum Physics.summary: A central question in quantum machine learning is which functions of an input state a model can represent when its measurement is fixed by hardware or by experimental design. We address this question for quantum neural networks with a fixed readout observable, where the trainable pre-measurement dynamics determine the effective observable in the Heisenberg picture and the scalar output is the measured expectation value itself, without trainable affine post-processing. We characterize the reachable effective observables under three physical resource classes: unitary evolution, which preserves the spectrum of the readout; mixed-unitary evolution, which relaxes this to a majorization constraint while preserving the trace; and completely positive trace-preserving (CPTP) evolution, whose Heisenberg adjoint is unital rather than trace-preserving and therefore lifts the trace constraint inherited at the mixed-unitary level. The three reachable sets are a fixed-spectrum orbit, its convex hull, and an operator interval, and the inclusions are strict for any readout that is not proportional to the identity. The separation is witnessed locally: for a fixed Pauli readout $Z_j$ on an arbitrary number of qubits, the amplitude-damping observable $γ\id+(1-γ)Z_j$ lies outside the mixed-unitary level for every $γ>0$. We realize the CPTP level with a Stinespring-channelized circuit and derive closed-form loss floors, $4γ^2/3$ and $γ^2$ for the unitary and mixed-unitary levels and zero at the CPTP level, which the numerics reproduce within precision. Structured-observable, Rényi-moment and classification experiments illustrate how the hierarchy manifests in finite-depth ansätze. The results identify which spectral constraint each physical resource relaxes, framing reachable-observable classes as a resource for expressivity rather than an architectural advantage.

Quantum Physics.title: 500 Hz atom-atom entanglement distribution over metropolitan-scale fibers
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum networks and repeaters are among the most promising routes to scale up quantum information systems. Nevertheless, various aspects still require significant improvement to achieve practical realization. Multiplexing can enhance the performance in many fundamental steps, thus emerging as a critical strategy for the realization of quantum repeaters. Currently, a major bottleneck in realizing functional quantum repeaters is heralded entanglement distribution over longdistance elementary links, as neither of the two dominant protocols-single-photon nor two-photon interference-can simultaneously achieve high efficiency and strong robustness. Here, we address this challenge by experimentally realizing a method that unifies the efficiency and robustness. By harnessing two 15 * 15 quantum memory arrays, we generate remote matter-matter entanglement at a rate of 546 Hz over 20 km of fiber without active phase stabilization. This rate exceeds that of two-photon and single-photon schemes by factors of 75,932 and 23, respectively, establishing a new benchmark for entangling speed over metropolitan-scale distances and enabling semi-deterministic entanglement distribution. Inherently compatible with multiplexed quantum repeater architectures, our scheme offers a promising approach towards the realization of future high-performance distributed quantum systems.

Quantum Physics.title: Fracton Topological Holography
Quantum Physics.summary: Topological Holography (TH) is a framework of representing $(d-1)$-dimensional quantum systems with a $d$-dimensional sandwich, consisting of a topological order bulk, a gapped top boundary and a dynamical bottom boundary. Dualities and non-invertible symmetries are represented by the change of top boundary in the TH framework. Existing studies have focused on sandwiches with liquid topological bulk, in this paper we examine some fracton bulks, where we call the framework Fracton Topological Holography (FTH). In particular, the X-cube FTH induces the transverse field plaquette Ising model (TFPIM) version Kramers--Wannier duality, the duality between TFPIM and the two-dimensional $90^\circ$ quantum compass model, and the self-duality of quantum compass model. Haah's code FTH induces a duality of transverse-field generalized Ising models (TFGIMs). The two examples illustrate at least a part of type-I fracton (X-cube) and a part of type-II fracton (Haah's code) models can be used to construct FTH sandwiches. Moreover, we construct an explicit Sequential Quantum Circuit (SQC) switching the top boundary of X-cube sandwich, realizing the TFPIM version KW duality.

Quantum Physics.title: Landscape-Similarity-Guided Optimization in Divide-and-Conquer QAOA
Quantum Physics.summary: Divide-and-conquer strategies mitigate hardware constraints for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices by partitioning large interaction graphs into smaller, hardware-compatible sub-problems. However, this approach introduces a severe classical training bottleneck: a decomposition across $m$ boundary nodes generates $2^m$ distinct sub-problems that typically require independent optimization. In this work, we quantify correlations between reduced QAOA energy landscapes using a landscape-overlap measure $q$ and Pearson correlation $r$, and investigate their usefulness for parameter transfer. For $p=1$ on the studied long-range percolation graphs with $L=50$--$400$, the displayed $q(s)$ curves cross near $s\approx0.6$. This observation on finite systems does not establish a thermodynamic phase transition. Exploiting these correlations, we introduce Doubly Optimized QAOA (DO-QAOA), which fully optimizes one representative reduced instance and transfers its parameters to the remaining frozen assignments, with target-specific refinement when required. We evaluated DO-QAOA on more than 6,000 circuits under the realistic noise model, DO-QAOA uses approximately $285$--$386\times$ fewer quantum shots and has approximately $6.5$--$23.9\times$ shorter runtime than FrozenQubits, with equal or lower dataset-averaged Approximation Ratio Gap (ARG).

Quantum Physics.title: Remote Charging of Quantum Batteries via a Multimode Resonator
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the remote charging of a qubit battery by a qubit charger coupled through a finite multimode resonator. The charging protocol uses time-shifted coupling pulses that account for the spatial phases of the resonator modes. We compare the energy stored in the battery with its ergotropy, the maximum work extractable by a local unitary operation. In the single-excitation regime considered here, the battery stores energy at any nonzero excited-state population, but its ergotropy is positive only when that population exceeds one half. In the absence of loss, stronger coupling brings the battery above this threshold earlier, while the final charge remains nearly complete across the coupling range studied. For the parameters considered, qubit relaxation suppresses ergotropy more strongly than resonator loss at comparable decay rates. After the battery is disconnected, relaxation causes its stored energy to decay exponentially, yet its ergotropy vanishes at a finite time while half of its energy capacity remains occupied. For a fixed storage interval, disconnecting at the population maximum therefore preserves the most extractable work.

Quantum Physics.title: Positive-partial-transpose structure of completely entangled subspaces and their complements
Quantum Physics.summary: A completely entangled subspace (CES) contains no product vectors, so every state supported on it is entangled. Whether such a subspace can support states with positive partial transpose (PPT) is a more subtle question. The normalized projector onto a CES may be NPT even if there exist PPT states supported on the CES. We investigate this distinction using a semidefinite criterion that optimizes the smallest partial-transpose eigenvalue over all supported density operators. For two- qutrit states supported on CESs, this leads to a complete characterization: a CES supports PPT states exactly when it is four-dimensional and related by invertible local transformations to the complement of an unextendible product basis (UPB). We also establish restrictions on PPT states whose ranges contain only vectors of Schmidt rank at least three, ruling out their existence in $3\otimes n$, $4\otimes4$, and $4\otimes5$, and showing that any such state in $4\otimes6$ must have rank eight. An interesting structure emerges when two orthogonal completely entangled subspaces together span the full Hilbert space, which we term \textit{complementary CESs}. Explicit constructions in $3\otimes4$ demonstrate that both subspaces can support PPT entanglement even when their normalized projectors are NPT. In $4\otimes4$, we construct a complementary pair whose normalized projectors are themselves PPT entangled. These constructions offer an alternative route to obtaining PPT entangled states, beyond the familiar approach based on UPB complements.

Quantum Physics.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
Quantum Physics.summary: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.

Quantum Physics.title: Reconstructing Pure-State OTOCs from Forward-Time Linear Response
Quantum Physics.summary: We show that the connected out-of-time-ordered correlator (OTOC) of any pure state can be reconstructed exactly from commutator linear responses alone. The protocol requires no time reversal, no ancilla, no double copy, and no weak measurement: a unitary string pulse, forward many-body evolution, and a single local readout suffice. An average over a complete basis of pulse generators yields the OTOC exactly. We further show that the measurement can be made sparse by restricting the pulses to a fixed operator weight, which turns the truncation into an analytically controlled spectral filter: the deterministic bias can be computed before the experiment and cleanly separated from the statistical sampling variance. For Gaussian states, the finite-weight response is exactly proportional to the full OTOC after a known combinatorial rescaling. For quantum chaotic systems, the typical residual is suppressed as a power law in the sector size. Exact-diagonalization benchmarks in the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model and a nonintegrable Ising chain confirm these predictions.

Quantum Physics.title: Classification of Thouless pumps with non-invertible symmetries and implications for Floquet phases
Quantum Physics.summary: We study symmetry preserving adiabatic and Floquet dynamics of one-dimensional systems.
