High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Homotopy algebraic methods have become increasingly influential in the study of field theories. We consider semi-holomorphic Chern--Simons theory and its relation with the principal chiral model. The semi-classical equivalence of the two theories is expected on general grounds, as the principal chiral model arises by eliminating trivial pairs and gauge fixing. We construct this equivalence explicitly as an off-shell, cyclic quasi-isomorphism between the cyclic $L_\infty$-algebras governing the two theories, and show that it directly encodes the Lax connection. This provides a concrete example for studying integrability of a two-dimensional system through the homotopy algebraic lens.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v2: 27 pages, minor corrections, published version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Timelike Entanglement from Spacetime Density Matrices: A Lattice Realization
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a systematic framework for timelike entanglement in a two-dimensional free real scalar field, connecting spacetime density matrices with Lorentzian twist-operator correlators through independent microscopic and continuum calculations. Extending Gaussian diagonalization to generally non-Hermitian reduced operators, we determine their complete nonzero spectra in the generic regular case, together with all integer Rényi moments. The real-time replica construction relates these moments to twist correlators, with quantitative agreement in both magnitude and phase for the full four-point function on a circle, the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary two-point functions, and the massive form-factor predictions. In the massless continuum theory with Dirichlet boundaries, we further establish a finite causally connected window in which all integer moments are real, while the even moments are strictly positive for arbitrary initial states. For Gaussian states, all integer moments are strictly positive, and the resulting Rényi entropies are real. These results demonstrate that causal connectedness alone is not sufficient for a nonzero imaginary part of timelike Rényi entropy.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables $(ζ_1,ζ_2)$ built on the superalgebra $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ associated with the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli-Kyemba, the two dilation parameters $φ_1(p,q)$ and $φ_2(p,q)$ being meromorphic functions of two variables evaluated at $(p,q)$. The graded super-Fock space splits into four sectors: bosonic, $φ_1-$fermionic, $φ_2-$fermionic and bi-fermionic. In each of them we establish the diagonal representation of the density operator by means of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$derivative, angular integration and Berezin integration, and we give a unified compact form in terms of sectorial parametric functions. The total density operator is obtained in explicit form as the sum of the four sectorial contributions, and can be read as a mixture of the four sectors. We define the sectorial reproducing kernels, obtained from the resolution of the identity, we compute the matrix elements of the density operator in the super-coherent state basis, and we prove the hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties of the kernels, together with the series expansion of their diagonal values. An integral formulation relates the density operator, its density function and the reproducing kernel, the latter being the function associated with the identity operator. Berezin quantization in the bosonic sector yields the quantized operators associated with $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|^2$, $z^2$ and $\bar z^2$ and their mean values; the dispersions of the super-position and super-momentum operators show that the super-coherent states are intelligent states.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Dirichlet walls beyond JT gravity and their quantum group interpretation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We canonically quantize sinh dilaton gravity with finite Dirichlet boundary conditions. The reduced phase space is formulated in terms of the length of a two-sided spacelike geodesic in an effective AdS$_2$ geometry and its conjugate momentum. Canonical quantization leads to a finite-difference Schrödinger equation whose wavefunctions of the universe are given by $q$-hypergeometric functions. These furnish a quantum deformation of the hypergeometric wavefunctions of JT gravity. We further show that the finite cutoff Hamiltonian derived from the bulk analysis admits a natural interpretation as the reduced Casimir of $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{R}))$ acting on hyperbolic matrix elements. The two scattering wave solutions are hyperbolic matrix elements of the modular double $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))\otimes U_{\tilde q}(\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb R))$, and the wavefunction of the universe is their unique combination regular at vanishing length.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Superconformal mechanics from N-extended Euler-Calogero-Moser and Calogero models
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate two-particle variants of the N-extended Euler-Calogero-Moser and Calogero models. Oving to translational invariance, the center-of-mass degrees of freedom and the associated fermions decouple, yielding specific systems of superconformal mechanics. Additional bosonic spin variables are straightforwardly incorporated into the supercharges and the Hamiltonian. For the Euler-Calogero-Moser model, the two-particle supersymmetry exhibits an unexpected extension from $Osp(N|2)$ to $SU(1,1|N)$ superconformal symmetry, whereas the Calogero model reduces to purely $Osp(N|2)$ superconformal mechanics. Finally, we demonstrate that introducing a larger number of fermions into the system provides a consistent pathway to overcoming well-known pathologies with higher supersymmetries inherent to these framework.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 11 pages, version to appear in Phys. Lett. B

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quasi-Local Celestial Charges and Multipoles
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We extend Penrose's quasi-local mass definition to include higher-spin charges associated with the celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetries and relate them to traditional definitions of multipoles. The resulting formulae provide explicit expressions that can be computed on finite 2-surfaces, given a choice of null hypersurface. They yield a geometric definition of celestial symmetries and multipoles in generic spacetimes in terms of higher-valence solutions to the twistor equations. This, in turn, gives rise to natural flux-balance laws along the null hypersurface. We also present a first-principles phase-space derivation of these charges, starting from a twistor space action for self-dual gravity that can be identified with the standard gravitational asymptotic phase space at null infinity, performing a large gauge transformation analysis and using the Penrose transform to connect with the corresponding spacetime expressions. Finally, we formulate the spacetime analysis in the Plebanski gauge and relate the celestial symmetries to the integrability of self-dual gravity in the case of a self-dual background.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Chiral crossover responses in a magnetic field: Finite-$μ_5$ matching in the NJL model
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate how independent information at finite chiral chemical potential $μ_5$ constrains pseudocritical-temperature responses in the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model under a magnetic field. Vacuum calibration alone leaves the coefficient $c_r$ of the additional interaction $δΩ_r=c_rμ_5^2(M-m_0)^2$ undetermined. We compare soft-cutoff (SC) and Pauli-Villars (PV) vacuum regularizations, each combined with the direct treatment (D) or the magnetic finite-difference scheme (MFDS). The reference SC and PV treatments exhibit opposite finite-$μ_5$ responses already at $eB=0$. Matching the $eB=0$ scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio predicted by unitarized chiral perturbation theory gives $c_{\mathrm{SC}}=-0.07112$ and $c_{\mathrm{PV}}=0.22479$. Holding these coefficients fixed at $eB=0.1,0.2,0.4$ GeV$^2$ reduces the four-treatment spread of the normalized finite-$μ_5$-induced mass-inflection temperature change by factors of approximately $7.5$-$15.3$ at $μ_5=0.15$ GeV and $18.1$-$32.6$ at $μ_5=0.30$ GeV. For the distinct scalar-susceptibility peak-temperature ratio at $μ_5=0.15$ GeV, the spread decreases by factors of approximately $74$, $27$, and $14$ at the same magnetic fields, respectively. The reduction in regularization-dependent finite-$μ_5$ responses thus persists at the sampled nonzero magnetic fields without further matching.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Non-invertible Duality Defects in Four-Dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Lattice Gauge Theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider four-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ lattice gauge theories with generalized plaquette actions. These theories are known to exhibit dualities. We construct topological interfaces implementing these dualities by assigning a weight to each building block and proving topological invariance. At self-dual couplings, these interfaces become duality defects representing non-invertible symmetries. We also study center symmetry defects and their junctions with the duality interfaces and derive several crossing relations.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and Eöt-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the Eöt-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Group Theory and the CFT Distance Conjecture: $\mathcal{N}=2$ Tensionless Strings Have No (Co)Weight
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We perform a systematic survey of the Hagedorn behaviour at infinite-distance points in the conformal manifold of four-dimensional large-$N$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ Superconformal Field Theories admitting a Lagrangian description. Many properties of these theories can be understood in terms of the Lie algebra encoding the shape of their quiver. We find that in the overall-free limit, the Hagedorn temperature is determined by the largest eigenvalue of an affine or finite Cartan adjacency matrix. This defines two types of universality classes of theories sharing the same high-energy exponential growth of states characteristic of string-like spectra. The first and largest is the affine case, corresponding to orbifold and orientifold projections of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang-Mills, and all share the same temperature. The others fall into universality classes following an ADE classification with a temperature set by the dual Coxeter number, and can be obtained by deforming the affine case. Our results apply to all large-$N$ $\mathcal{N}=2$ quivers with any classical gauge symmetry, including those with matter charged beyond bifundamental representations. We further discuss the string-theoretic construction of these theories and some of the holographic implications, as well as how our methods extend to broad families of theories with less supersymmetry. We also consider limits where only part of the theory becomes free, and find lower and upper bounds on the exponential rate predicted by the CFT Distance Conjecture. Both these bounds and the Hagedorn temperature are set by the same eigenvalue, and when the quiver has a single gauge node the lower bound is saturated, giving a natural explanation for the three universality classes recently found in the literature.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: On the large N convergence of the supermembrane matrix model
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, the large N behavior of a supersymmetric matrix model is compared with its exact continuum description. We prove that the complete spectrum of a $SU(N)$ regularized compactified M2-brane theory in the semiclassical approximation converges, in the large $N$ limit, to the exact spectrum in the same approximation. To this end, we concentrate on the large $N$ limit of a supersymmetric matrix model describing a supermembrane with central charge on a toroidally compactified target space. We analyze, on the one hand, the supermembrane model formulated on a differentiable compact torus, with structure group given by the area-preserving diffeomorphisms, and, on the other hand, its associated regularized $SU(N)$ model. We emphasize in our analysis the structure of the local and global constraints of the regularized model, which generate the $SU(N)$ algebra and reproduce the area-preserving diffeomorphism algebra in the large N limit, together with the topological information associated with the central charge condition and the topology of the model. We explain the role of the central charge in the compactified supermembrane and how it allows a top-down $SU(N)$ regularization. It is known that its $SU(N)$ regularized model has a purely discrete spectrum with finite multiplicity. We prove that, in the semiclassical approximation, the spectrum of the Hamiltonian of the supersymmetric matrix model converges in the large-$N$ limit to that of the Hamiltonian of the supermembrane (M2-brane) with central charge.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $τ$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $τ$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: 70 years of Double-Logarithmic Approximation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Existence of Double-Logarithmic (DL) contributions to scattering amplitudes in QED was discovered by V.V. Sudakov in 1956 and total summation of DL contributions to electron-photon scattering resulted in appearance of famous Sudakov exponentials. Then, thanks to contributions of V.G. Gorshkov, V.N. Gribov, G.V. Frolov and L.N. Lipatov, the pattern of calculations in Double- Logarithmic Approximation (DLA) was constructed. Since then, DLA has become one of basic ways of describing various high-energy processes in the framework of QED, QCD and theory of EW interactions. In the present paper, we remind the history of DLA and present a brief overview of application of DLA to various objects like form factors, scattering amplitudes, DIS structure functions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 21 pp, 7 figures, multiple typos and misprints corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holomorphic Feynman diagrams in four dimensions and the quantum BPS ring
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute at all loop orders the kernels of the holomorphic Feynman graphs governing loop corrections to supersymmetry transformations and regularized operator products in the holomorphic twist of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=1$ supersymmetric gauge theories. Interpreting their current equations as those of an electrical network---with Schwinger parameters as resistances and holomorphic momenta as injected currents---we iterate series, parallel and star-triangle reductions on Schwinger space to obtain the fan, spider and cubic product-forest kernels at all loop orders. Assuming that twisting commutes with quantization for composite operators, we obtain every perturbative correction to the supersymmetry transformation in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, acting on operators with arbitrary holomorphic derivatives. Using the marked higher operations of Gaiotto, Kulp and Wu, we construct the quantum product and prove that on cohomology of the quantum supercharge it is associative, graded commutative and unital, furnishing the multiplication of the quantum BPS ring; in $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory every multi-graviton operator thus admits an explicit finite all-order completion. For the classical gauge groups, every perturbative differential image in the multi-trace ring vanishes upon Cartan restriction. In $\mathcal N=4$ Yang-Mills theory, we find new fortuitous classes and one-loop lifts across several gauge groups, no two-loop lift in the sectors tested, and rationally certified three-loop lifts in $SO(11)$, $SO(12)$ and $SO(13)$. The lowest example we find lies in the level-$34$ BMN sector of $SO(13)$. The glueball lifts in $SO(11)$ and $SO(13)$ remove the excess classical powers relative to their symplectic duals. Beyond $\mathcal N=4$, we find two-loop lifts in the Leigh-Strassler and $β$-deformations, and two- to four-loop lifts in abelian and $\mathcal N=2$ gauge theories.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 114 pages, 27 figures. v2 reports new three-loop BPS lifts for SO(11), SO(12) and SO(13) in N=4 Yang-Mills theory. It corrects citations, including the attribution of Proposition D.1 to Brandt (1993), expands the derivations and circuit diagrams, and updates the acknowledgments

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schrödinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method. Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Rotating Black Holes from Scaling Transformations in Horava Gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the scaling transformations that change the physical parameters of solutions in low-energy Horava gravity. In particular, we present a simple scaling transformation that generates rotating black-hole solutions in low-energy Horava gravity from known relativistic solutions. As explicit examples, we obtain "Doran-like" and "Kerr-Schild-like" rotating solutions in Horava gravity. We find that both solutions are horizon-penetrating, but their null horizons are not Killing horizons. We also find that, although their singularity structures differ from each other, chronology is protected in both solutions, as in the previously obtained Kerr-like solutions in Boyer-Lindquist coordinates.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Chaotic Dynamics around a Hairy Black Hole in Horndeski Gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the chaotic dynamics of a spinning test particle in a static, spherically symmet- ric hairy black hole (BH) in Horndeski gravity, using the Mathisson-Papapetrou-Dixon equations closed by the Tulczyjew-Dixon condition. Bound orbits are identified by fixing the angular momen- tum and setting the energy according to the effective potential, so that the accessible parameter range is bounded by a critical hair parameter, hcrit, which varies non-monotonically with the spin. We analyze the resulting chaotic behavior using Lyapunov exponents, Poincare sections, and re- constructed attractors. We find that the response of these indicators to scalar hair is orbit- and spin-dependent rather than universally monotonic. An analysis of orbital frequency ratios shows that, at physically maximal spin (S = 1), an approaching 2:1 azimuthal resonance overlapping a persistent 1:1 polar lock amplifies chaos, while the hair-driven erosion of potential saddles tends to suppress it. At non-physical spin (S = 1.5), the Lyapunov exponent decreases monotonically. Gravitational waveforms constructed via the quadrupole formula inherit the same state-specific pattern: the correlation between the two polarization modes varies non-monotonically with h, in step with the Lyapunov exponent. These results show that chaotic indicators respond to scalar hair in an orbit- and resonance-dependent manner rather than through simple monotonic suppres- sion, and identify the spin-dependent resonance structure as an essential ingredient for interpreting chaos around hairy black holes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Les Houches lectures on Spinfoam Path Integrals
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In these lecture notes for the Les Houches School on Loop Quantum Gravity 2025, which took place in September 2025, we give a pedagogical review of the basics of the spinfoam framework for a quantum gravity path integral. While spin network states in loop quantum gravity describe the quantum geometry of the 3d space as dynamical networks of entangled quanta of volumes, spinfoams define transition amplitudes for those spin networks using the reformulation of general relativity as an "almost-topological" field theory and tools from quantum BF theory and topological state-sums. The lectures were a short format of three times one hour and a half, only allowing to cover the basics and offer a glimpse of more advanced lines of research. We introduce spin foam path integrals for increasing spacetime dimensions starting with 2d BF theory, then build up to 3d quantum gravity with the Ponzano-Regge state-sum and the Turaev-Viro invariant, and finally the quantization of general relativity in four dimensions.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 49 pages; Lecture notes prepared for the Les Houches School on Loop Quantum Gravity 2025, https://sites.google.com/cstq.org/2025-lqg-blaumann-school; Slides on a brief history of spinfoams as Supplementary material; v2: signs and typos corrected in equations, added discussion on features of 4d spinfoam models

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Segre Classification as a Framework for Generating Exact Solutions in Static Cylindrical Spacetimes with Levi-Civita Matching
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The main objective of this article is to analyze cylindrically symmetric static spacetime based on the Segre classification, where each Segre type corresponds to a set of canonical forms of Ricci spinors represented by Newman-Penrose scalars. The surviving Segre types of trace-free Ricci tensor in the cylindrical geometry are $[1,(111)]$, $[1,1(11)]$, $[(1,1)11]$, $[1,111]$, $[(1,11)1]$, $[(1,1)(11)]$ and $[(1,111)]$. Different combinations of eigenvalues and eigenvectors formed via Segre classification aid in understanding the distribution of matter and energy within that particular kind. Solutions are presented for the isotropic type $[1,(111)]$, for the anisotropic type $[1,1(11)]$, where a new metric function is introduced, and for type $[1,111]$, where all three pressures differ and the Krori-Barua functions are used. They satisfy the physical and stability criteria, namely the Zeldovich condition, causality condition, energy conditions and adiabatic index. The types $[(1,1)11]$ and $[(1,11)1]$ have $ρ=-P_r$ and give dark energy like configurations in which the strong energy condition is violated in the core, the latter having the tachyonic fluid form of the energy momentum tensor. For type $[(1,1)(11)]$, a charged solution in the presence of a non-null electromagnetic field is obtained and joined to an electrovac exterior. Matching with the Levi-Civita exterior shows that the vanishing of the radial pressure at the boundary is equivalent to the Darmois conditions. The C-energy and the curvature invariants are evaluated for each solution, and the results are compared with earlier works.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The type-II double copy for relativistic Rindler fluids
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Within the Weyl double copy framework, we study a mixed single-copy construction for the Petrov type-II geometry of first-order relativistic Rindler fluids. Working on a common fixed flat Rindler background with consistent spinor conventions and a real field strength representation, we algebraically factorize the Weyl spinor into two symmetric rank-two Maxwell spinors and test the Maxwell equations and the zeroth copy scalar equation up to the first order in the relativistic gradient expansion. We separate the degeneration parameter from the gradient expansion parameter and analyze the continuous degeneration to the Petrov type-D and type-N branches as the complex shear and vorticity tend to zero, together with the preservation of the accuracy of the Maxwell and scalar field equations along each path. We also compare the relativistic construction with the nonrelativistic case.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Complete quasinormal modes of Type-D black holes. III. Reissner-Nordström spectra from zero to extremal charge
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Earlier calculations left open how gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of charged black holes recover the Schwarzschild spectrum and how the modes near algebraically special frequencies relate to the exact special solutions. We extend our Kerr analysis to Reissner-Nordström black holes by analytically continuing the ingoing horizon solution and locating the zeros of the incoming amplitude at infinity. For each of $\ell=2$ and $3$, we trace the first 42 overtone families from the Schwarzschild limit to extremality. The charge trajectories distinguish crossings of the negative imaginary axis from turns near it and separate the unconventional Schwarzschild modes from neighboring branches. At zero charge the polar algebraically special mode is a QNM. At extremal charge the exact axial special modes are total-transmission modes. Of the 84 families, 75 approach distinct extremal frequencies with finite damping, and nine approach zero frequency with vanishing excitation. At exact extremality we also compute, for the first time, gravitational QNMs on the unconventional Riemann sheet reached across the negative imaginary axis. At intermediate charge, the clearest resonant enhancement of both excitation factors occurs for the $\ell=3$ overtone pairs $(22,23)$ and $(23,24)$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Superheavy gravitational dark matter from runaway bubble collisions
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A stable particle that couples only through gravity is pair-produced in collisions of runaway bubble walls by graviton exchange. For a transition of duration $1/β$, a Dirac fermion reaches the yield $Y_X\simeq6.8\times10^{-3}(H/β)(T_{\rm reh}/M_{\rm P})^3$, where $H$ is the Hubble rate of the vacuum energy, $T_{\rm reh}$ the reheating temperature and $M_{\rm P}$ the reduced Planck mass. The yield is flat up to masses near $(H/β)M_{\rm P}/ν^2$, where $ν$ of order one sets the wall-field excursion. Gravity alone then gives dark matter up to about $10^{17}$~GeV at reheating temperatures far below its mass, where freeze-in fails.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 6 pages, 3 figures; Supplemental Material 11 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. Code: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24437869

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A hyperbolicity obstruction near regular charged centers
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A conserved charge creates a tension at a spherical center: the flux remains fixed while the area of the symmetry spheres shrinks. We ask whether curvature-dependent electromagnetic responses can reconcile bounded central curvature with hyperbolic propagation in four-dimensional Einstein gravity when both parity-even and parity-odd couplings are allowed. The background equations force a positive charge potential and its first curvature derivative to vanish at the central curvature endpoint. On branches with a positive electromagnetic kinetic coefficient and a positive effective gravitational coefficient, this endpoint flattening produces a physical extraordinary mode of the fully coupled equations whose squared angular characteristic speed is strictly below minus one at radii arbitrarily close to the center. Its characteristic cone has no hyperbolicity direction in common with the ordinary photon and graviton modes. The result requires no central curvature expansion, remains valid at points where the curvature Legendre Hessian vanishes, and extends to positive-definite mixing of finitely many Abelian fields. An exact analytic example with a nonlinear gravitational curvature sector admits a real, subluminal extraordinary photon cone near the center. In a fixed-action black-hole family, the obstruction extends outside the outer horizon over a near-extremal parameter interval.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 36 pages, 2 figures. Substantially revised and expanded version of v1; title changed

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Boundary spectroscopy of hidden near-horizon reflection
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A classical black hole horizon absorbs completely, and any deviation would be hidden in the bulk. For a scalar field in a rotating Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli exterior, we derive an exact boundary response of a corotating passive wall near the horizon. An Airy filter gives its spectrum, and positive energy excludes growing modes. On any frequency band the response identifies a constant wall impedance and the wall position, which enter orthogonally with weights determined by the spectral function. The boundary thus sees a reflecting wall, whereas a perfect absorber is exponentially hidden.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Main text 14 pages 3 figs; Appendix 4 pages 4 figs; v3 revisions, added a table summarizing the analysis framework and clarified the text. Main results & conclusions unchanged. Match published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Separability of coupled gravitational perturbations in Plebański--Demiański spacetimes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Recently, a major breakthrough in the separability of gravitational perturbations of the Kerr--Newman rotating charged black hole was achieved by Hintz [arxiv:2609.33661], and extended to non-zero cosmological constant Kerr--Newman-(A)dS black holes by Yoshida [arxiv:2610.20500] and Zhao [arxiv:2610.22274]. This method removes the need for the freezing approximation, wherein coupling to the electromagnetic degrees of freedom are ignored, at the price of a coupled set of equations in the gravitational radiative degrees of freedom. The key insight is to transform the coupled system of equations into a chiral form which is amenable to a modified matrix $R$-separation of variables. In this work we extend the construction to the most general type D electro-vacuum solution to the Einstein-Maxwell equations, with aligned matter and cosmological constant. The construction makes use of the conformal properties of the equations and we find a symmetry operator underlying the decoupling of the chiral system.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 10 pages: v2 minor typos fixed, additional refs

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Relic Neutrinos Probing Small Scale Primordial Non-Gaussianity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Relic neutrinos retain a record of electromagnetic entropy production after neutrino decoupling, probing primordial modes erased from the primary CMB. We derive the cubic photon number source from acoustic damping and its leading folded sensitive bispectrum window, with neutrino decoupling, thermalization, and acoustic coherence combined in a single response kernel. For excited initial states, this kernel filters the physical folded profile and yields a sharpness dependent transmission condition, directly connecting small scale primordial non-Gaussianity to relic neutrino capture rates.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages, 1 figure; your comments are absolutely welcome!

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Void inside the horizon: connecting the third-quantized vacuum to a classical spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the emergence of a classical spacetime from a quantum-gravitational vacuum within the framework of third quantization applied to the black hole interior. Following the canonical quantization of the Kantowski--Sachs spacetime, one can construct a wave packet that explains the classical interior of a Schwarzschild black hole. This wave packet should be extended to the classical singularity. To avoid this, one can introduce an analytic continuation and the Euclidean wave function. This is not an analytic continuation of the spacetime, but of the superspace. To give this a suitable meaning, it is reasonable to introduce the concept of the third quantization. In this aspect, the Euclidean analytic continuation of the superspace explains the on-shell trajectory connecting the third-quantized vacuum state to a coherent classical geometry. Finally, we discuss how nonlinear self-interactions and baby-universe wormhole couplings must be incorporated into the third-quantized action to dynamically drive this transition.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a repulsive interaction has the opposite effect. At larger coupling, the pure Yukawa contribution to the ionization power becomes increasingly important and can compete with the gravitational contribution, particularly for lighter mediators. Comparing continuum ionization with off-resonant bound-state mixing, we find that continuum ionization can halt superradiant growth at a substantially smaller Yukawa coupling. At their respective critical couplings, the Yukawa interaction provides the dominant contribution to cloud depletion in both channels. Finally, we calculate the phase correction to gravitational waves due to continuum ionization and characterize how the chirp-rate response varies with frequency near the thresholds at which successive orbital harmonics open continuum-ionization channels.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Modified gravity at large scales on quantum spacetime in the IKKT model
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The gravitational dynamics of 3+1 dimensional covariant quantum spacetime in the IKKT or IIB matrix model is studied at one loop, combining the Yang-Mills-type matrix action with the induced Einstein-Hilbert action. This combined action leads to interesting modifications of the gravitational dynamics at long distances, governed by modified Einstein equations including an extra geometrical tensor interpreted as ''mirage matter''. In particular we find extra non-Ricci flat geometric modes with a non-standard dispersion relation, with features reminiscent of dark matter and/or dark energy.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 27+10 pages, 4 figures. V2: harmonic gauge condition derived, improved presentation. V3: discussion of scales clarified

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Optical appearance and radial stability of thin-shell wormholes in fractional-power magnetic electrodynamics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate disk images of symmetric thin-shell wormholes in fractional-power magnetic electrodynamics and relate optical appearance to local radial stability. Finite magnetic self-energy fixes the seed mass and links the charge to the nonlinear scale. Transparent disks illuminate both exteriors, and independent Maxwell rays reach a static observer. For the standard Born--Infeld magnetic subset, static emitters are compared with circular motion outside the innermost stable orbit and an inward plunge below it. The wormhole--black-hole intensity difference separates light transmitted from the opposite disk from emission removed by throat excision. The illuminated inner edge depends on the admitted disk crossings rather than the throat radius alone. Increasing charge contracts the critical curve in the sampled family. Motion suppresses the face-on intensities and produces an azimuthal brightness contrast at inclination. A broad outer shoulder arises from partial compensation between decreasing emissivity and increasing circular frequency weights, before the profiles recover a decaying weak-field tail. All nine prescribed throats satisfy a local radial stability test for a calibrated modified cosmic Chaplygin law describing an effective exotic layer. An analytic identity establishes radial instability at the selected unstable photon orbit for any finite density-only constitutive slope. The resulting images relate transmitted radiation and emitter kinematics to the material support of the throat, providing a controlled comparison with the matched seed black hole.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Thin-shell wormholes from magnetic black holes in exponential electrodynamics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Transparent magnetic wormholes can share a black hole exterior while their supporting matter controls the response of the throat. We construct symmetric thin shells from the magnetic black hole of exponential nonlinear electrodynamics and derive their equilibrium stresses and linear radial stability criterion. Restricting the seed to its zero-bare-mass magnetic branch ties the charge and coupling along the fixed-mass family. In the sampled configurations, calibrated linear barotropic shells are unstable, whereas variable phantom and variable Chaplygin laws admit locally stable radial sectors. Explicit radius dependence strengthens the phantom restoring term; the Chaplygin response cancels the divergent inverse lapse contribution and permits stable sectors close to a non-extremal seed horizon. The surface density remains negative, although an inner interval satisfies the tangential null and intrinsic strong energy conditions. At the seed photon sphere, the two variable laws share an exact stabilization threshold. The complete radial averaged null energy remains negative even when the proper shell energy tends to zero. Numerical null geodesic imaging uses independent, minimally coupled light and transparent junctions, with celestial sources and rotating thin disks truncated at the ISCO. For observer-side disk emission with the prescribed ISCO truncation and a throat below the seed photon sphere, inclined images coincide with the seed black hole image. A throat above that sphere removes selected returning contributions while preserving much of the bright primary structure. Illuminating the opposite exterior adds inner disk arcs, but a central dark region can survive because the disk does not illuminate every transmitted direction. The resulting image degeneracy depends jointly on the retained null trajectories and the emitting support, rather than on the presence of a horizon alone.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Strong-deflection scaling in nearly symmetric thin-shell wormholes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The angular winding of a returning light ray can grow while the family of admissible impacts disappears. We characterize this competition near reflection symmetry in a static thin-shell wormhole joining Schwarzschild exteriors of slightly different masses. Exact shell-frame matching fixes the reflected interval, and a normal coordinate at each nondegenerate photon-sphere maximum gives a composite angular expansion with controlled error on compact interior channel intervals. The result remains valid when the throat distance divided by the mass contrast tends to zero, stays finite or diverges. For a throat distance proportional to a positive power of the fractional mass difference, the width exponent increases from one toward two and then saturates, while the logarithmic winding coefficient decreases from three toward two. Fixed-throat configurations retain their finite-distance amplitude and coefficient three. Reference-subtracted profiles connect the intermediate sector to finite and vanishing scaled throat positions. Independent quadratures test the scaling laws and resolve the slower convergence associated with changing scale ratios. The shrinking solid-angle aperture follows directly from the critical-impact gap. For an axial observer and a transparent test disk confined to the same exterior, the return-phase condition selects the admitted intersections; sampled near-symmetric configurations shift the first available global crossing to a later label. The closing aperture and increasing winding are therefore linked by the accessible radial extent, with disk access determined by the phase accumulated on the emitting segment.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Small-Throat Boundary Condition for the Tunneling Wave Function of the Universe
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose a small-throat prescription for the wave function of a closed universe in the semiclassical approximation, motivated by the idea that universe creation may be obtained as the decoupling, or pinch-off, limit of a tunneling geometry connected to another universe through a small throat. Instead of retaining the parent-universe side explicitly, we describe the remaining half-geometry by a minisuperspace model with boundary conditions imposed at the throat. To model the finite throat, we introduce a small radiation component parametrized by $ε$ in a closed minisuperspace model with a positive cosmological constant. The radiation term produces two turning points, an inner one $q_-\sim O(ε)$ and an outer one $q_+\sim H^{-2}$, where $q$ is the square of the scale factor. Our prescription imposes the Neumann condition $\dot q(0)=0$ on the classical solutions and restricts the initial size $q_i=q(0)$ to the small-throat domain $0<|q_i|<\sqrtε/H$. This domain contains the inner turning point $q_-$ and excludes the unsuppressed outer-turning-point saddle at $q_i=q_+$. We choose the steepest-descent lapse contour through the inner tunneling saddle in the semiclassical approximation. Taking the limit $ε\to0$ after this finite-throat saddle problem has been defined, the inner turning point approaches $q_i=0$, and the saddle action reduces to that of the standard tunneling saddle. Other choices of lapse contour can instead select Hartle-Hawking-type growing branches. In this sense, the tunneling exponent and outgoing WKB phase can be obtained as the limiting form of tunneling from an arbitrarily small universe, rather than by imposing a boundary condition directly at a vanishing geometry.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 10 pages, 4 figures; v2: Fig. 4 added, updated to the published version

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Observational Signatures of Exact Black Hole Solutions in a Dark Matter Halo
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work, we derive novel exact solutions describing Schwarzschild-like black holes (BHs) embedded in a Dehnen-type dark matter (DM) halo density profile and investigate their geometric, dynamical, and observational signatures arising from such geometries. We begin by analyzing the horizon structure and spacetime curvature invariants, as well as examining the energy conditions associated with the DM halo. Subsequently, we study the influence of the DM halo on both timelike and null geodesics in the resulting geometry. Finally, we obtain observational constraints on the DM halo parameters by comparing the model predictions with weak-field data from Mercury and the S2 star orbit, as well as with the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) shadow measurements of M87$^\star$ and Sgr~A$^\star$, combined with the corresponding EHT and GRAVITY measurements of the BH mass and distance. Using Bayesian inference and Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, we obtain the posterior distributions of the model parameters and derive 95\% upper limits on the DM halo parameters. For M87$^\star$, we obtain $ρ_s<11.83~M_\odot\,{\rm pc}^{-3}$ and $r_s<54.36~{\rm kpc}$. For Sgr~A$^\star$, the EHT, GRAVITY, and combined EHT+GRAVITY analyses give $ρ_s<31.56$, $16.76$, and $21.25~M_\odot\,{\rm pc}^{-3}$, respectively. We find that all three cases lead to similar constraints on $r_s$ for Sgr~A$^\star$. Our analysis provides valuable insight into probing the potential influence of DM halo environments on spacetime geometry and observable properties of astrophysical BHs, offering an alternative perspective on BH-DM interactions.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Imaging the two-sided black hole interior with four-point correlators
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose a boundary four-point function smeared with wavepackets, which probes local physics behind the horizon of a two-sided AdS black hole. At high frequencies, boundary wavepackets aimed at an interior bulk point travel along geodesics and scatter locally about the bulk point, factorizing the correlator into a flat-space like scattering amplitude. To obtain this configuration, we utilize a non-trivial time ordering of operators, and also use one state-dependent operator insertion moved halfway across the thermal circle. An interesting property of this observable is that it also probes features of nontrivial states: null shocks and matter shells behind the horizon show up as jumps in the observed signal as the bulk point crosses them, thereby imaging the black hole interior.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A source-based decomposition of thermal noise for mechanical system design
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Thermal noise limits the sensitivity of precision mechanical instruments. We present a thermal- noise formulation for lumped-element mechanical systems that writes the total displacement thermal noise at the readout as the sum of contributions from all dissipative elements. For each contribution, we separate the thermal force generated by the element from its transfer to the readout. This decomposition provides simple design rules for comparing contributions from elements in series and in parallel and identifying the dominant noise source. It applies to frequency-dependent dissipation and to elements at different steady temperatures under local thermal equilibrium. We use it to identify the frequency regimes in which parallel and series dissipation dilution reduce displacement thermal noise. We then use examples of a pendulum on a lossy support, a rotational flexure, and rigidly mounted lunar optics to show how support noise can dominate even when the support has little effect on the system dynamics. Finally, a feedback-controlled suspension illustrates how sensing and actuation noise can be included in the same displacement-noise budget.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Another Look at the Weak-Field Limit of Generalized Hybrid Metric-Palatini Gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the weak-field regime of generalized hybrid metric-Palatini theories, described by a generic function $f(R,\mathcal{R})$, where $R$ is the metric Ricci scalar and $\mathcal{R}$ is constructed from an independent torsionless connection. Linearizing the field equations about Minkowski spacetime, we show, without using the scalar-tensor representation, that the theory propagates the usual massless spin-2 mode and two massive scalar modes, with an effective gravitational coupling. The absence of tachyonic and ghostlike instabilities at the linearized level, together with the nondegeneracy of the scalar sector, is shown to impose algebraic restrictions on the derivatives of $f(R,\mathcal{R})$ evaluated on the Minkowski background, which generalize previously obtained conditions. The Newtonian limit for an extended static source is derived, yielding a gravitational potential with two Yukawa corrections whose amplitudes are fixed by the scalar residues, while finite-size effects are encoded in source-dependent form factors. We determine the conditions under which the usual Newtonian limit is recovered and derive the effective post-Newtonian parameter $γ_Σ$ governing light propagation. Finally, we compute the radial epicyclic frequency and the corresponding anomalous periapsis advance, and compare it with planetary precession data to constrain the parameters of a viable hierarchical scalar-mass regime.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Revised version accepted for publication in the European Physical Journal C (v3: fixed math rendering in abstract)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on General Relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. The model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial Misner--Sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to Einstein's equations. Going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. Our Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology (AFIC) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. The extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. Rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. This mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages, no figures, comments are welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Relaxation of Quantum Near-Extremal Black Holes. (I) Microcanonical States, Pruning of Quasinormal Modes, and the Aretakis Instability
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
The late-time relaxation of a near-extremal black hole is classically governed by an infinite tower of purely damped quasinormal modes. This poses a puzzle: the higher overtones decay at rates much larger than the energy $E$ of the black hole above extremality, so they would need black hole states below the extremal mass. We resolve it by including the quantum fluctuations that become large when $E$ falls below a scale $E_b$. We compute the retarded Green's function of a probe of conformal dimension $Δ$ in a black hole of fixed energy, and find that each classical mode splits into a pair of poles with real parts set by $E_b$. The perturbed black hole decays as an unstable quantum system, and a pair is a resonance, i.e., a quasinormal mode, only if its energy lies within the accessible black hole spectrum. This prunes the tower to finitely many modes, all damped faster than $Δ^2E_b$, and below $E=Δ^2E_b/2$ none is left. For generic $Δ$, the response of the black hole decays first as $t^{-2Δ}$ and finally as $t^{-3/2}$, with an exponential stage in between if $E\ggΔ^2E_b$.
  The same quantum effects bear on the Aretakis instability of extremal black holes, in which transverse derivatives of a perturbation grow without bound on the horizon. Like the tower of modes, it originates in the scale invariance of the classical throat, which the quantum fluctuations break. The $t^{-2Δ}$ decay, which is the boundary counterpart of the Aretakis growth, ends by $t\sim1/E_b$, when the throat ceases to be classical, and by then horizon derivatives have grown only to a finite value. Their unbounded growth is an artifact of taking the semiclassical limit before the late-time one, two limits that in quantum mechanics do not commute.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Split Ends: UV Physics branches Black Hole Hair
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Coupling a shift-symmetric scalar field to the Gauss-Bonnet invariant modifies black holes (BHs) via scalar hair. Here we consider this field to be the Goldstone of a complex scalar field with a symmetry-breaking potential. For BHs of a size comparable with the inverse mass gap, the gapped field tries to restore the symmetry close to the horizon, enhancing the departure from standard BHs. Moreover, BHs of the same mass can have up to three different horizon areas and surface gravities. This branching has profound consequences for BH physics, potentially observable in gravitational waves.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Bondi-Sachs formalism on past light cones and an analogue of the integral mass formula
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Following a proposal that the thermodynamic aspects of general relativity can be found in the evolution of the past light cones of arbitrary worldlines, we generalise the Bondi-Sachs formalism to these surfaces. The observer may accelerate and rotate their tetrad, the spacetime may contain matter and a cosmological constant, and no symmetry is assumed. We impose regularity conditions at the vertex of each light cone and along the polar axis, including general axial conditions that allow for shear. Given a suitable prescription for the stresses of matter, the Einstein field equations can then be integrated hierarchically from data on a single light cone, and the regularity at the vertex fixes all constants of integration. The solution reveals a universal property: to first order in the observer's proper time, the evolution of the metric and of the four-momentum crossing the light cones is independent of the specific behaviour of matter. As an application, we derive, for an observer immersed in matter, an analogue of the integral mass formula of black hole mechanics.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 31 pages, 2 figures. Presents part of the results of arXiv:2609.25477. v2: improved treatment of the axial conditions and minor corrections

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quantum black hole evaporation from thin shell collapse: a complete effective picture
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Quantum gravity is expected to play a central role in resolving classical singularities and providing a complete, predictive spacetime picture. In this paper, we develop an effective model inspired by loop quantum gravity that aims to fulfill this expectation, providing a unified description of thin shell collapse, black hole formation, evaporation, and remnant dynamics. The framework exhibits general validity, holding across different effective equations of motion, matter sources, and evaporation laws. Specifically, we incorporate backreaction within a quasi-static approximation, modeling the radiation as null dust and matching the ingoing and outgoing fluxes across an evaporation surface using the Darmois-Israel junction conditions. For an evaporation law governed by the Stefan-Boltzmann law, we find that the final stage of evaporation yields an extremal black hole extending into a new asymptotic region, featuring both event and Cauchy horizons. Conversely, under the Schwinger approach, no event or Cauchy horizons form, instead, a temporary dynamical trapped region emerges, and the resulting spacetime remains globally hyperbolic. Under this variant, our model predicts a horizonless null remnant escaping to future null infinity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Refined Rényi Entropy from Replica-Geometry Tensor Networks
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Holographic tensor networks are a central route to understanding the mechanism behind the holographic duality, but standard fixed-graph constructions with maximally entangled links face a structural obstacle. Their leading entanglement spectra are flat, so their Rényi entropies do not depend on the replica index. This is in sharp contrast with holographic conformal field theories, where a tensionful cosmic brane makes the refined Rényi entropy $n$-dependent. Capturing this replica dependence is therefore an important test of tensor-network descriptions of holographic entanglement. We construct an explicit family of replica-dependent geodesic graphs that reproduces this behavior while keeping the links maximally entangled. For each replica index $n$, geodesics are emitted from the replicated boundary with the same local, isotropic intersection measure. They perfectly tessellate the selected replica geometry, so the $n$-dependence of their intersection counts comes from the geometry. Tensor-network models on these graphs reproduce the cosmic-brane prescription for refined Rényi entropy by counting crossing threads. Their cross-copy endpoint density also agrees, in CFT$_2$, with a boundary reconstruction within the additive linear combination proposal, providing a check beyond the total entropy. In higher dimensions, we further obtain an analytic large-separation decay law for this density.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Schwarzschild-Kerr crossover of high overtone quasinormal modes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A slowly rotating black hole is close to a nonrotating one, but its highly damped quasinormal spectrum is not. The Schwarzschild approximation holds only up to overtone numbers of order $χ^{-4/3}$, where $χ$ is the dimensionless spin. We find that the frequency shift at this scale is a universal function, derived from the wave boundary conditions with an error estimate. It is given by the spectrum of a sextic oscillator, via the correspondence between ordinary differential equations and integrable models. It recovers the Schwarzschild $\log 3$ and organizes the singular Kerr coefficients.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: On the evidence of lensing in GW231123
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Just like light, gravitational waves may be gravitationally lensed by massive objects along their travel path, however, this has not been observed so far. GW231123 is the most massive binary black-hole merger observed to-date, and quasi-circular gravitational wave analyses infer high masses and spin parameters that are particularly sensitive to the waveform model used. Here we investigate whether gravitational lensing can account for these features. We model the signal as a superposition of multiple overlapping images of the same merger and find support for lensing across four waveform models. The lensing interpretation reduces the support for these high spins, bringing both the inferred spins and masses into closer agreement across waveform models. A comparison with a background of unlensed signals gives the lensing interpretation an estimated significance of $3.96^{+0.68}_{-0.30}σ$. This makes lensing a compelling interpretation of this event but is insufficient for a definitive claim.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: How to Play a Black Hole: Understanding Quasinormal Mode Excitation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Understanding the excitation of black hole quasinormal modes is essential for interpreting gravitational-wave signals and inferring black hole properties from them. In this work, we investigate the excitation of the quasinormal modes of Schwarzschild black holes under controlled probes. In the absence of a source, we find that broader initial data suppresses mode excitation, enhancing the relative contribution of the late-time tail, while data localized near the light ring strongly suppresses overtones relative to the fundamental mode. On the other hand, plunging sources give rise to two distinct ringdown stages, associated with scattered radiation generated during the particle's infall and with the particle crossing the light ring. Finally, we investigate how much of the signal is sourced from the strong-field region by switching off the source at some finite radius. The resulting waveform is exponentially close -- in cutoff radius -- to that of a standard infall. These results provide insight into the dependence of QNM excitation on the properties and dynamics of the perturbation, and offer a controlled setting in which to investigate the origin of black hole ringdown.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Free hyperboloidal evolution in 3D: gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Hyperboloidal evolution allows to reach future null infinity within numerical relativity simulations. This work extends the conformal compactification approach with BSSN/Z4 from spherical symmetry to full 3D simulations. This is the first free numerical hyperboloidal evolution in 3D with a common formulation of general relativity. In this first step, gauge waves and constraint-violating gravitational waves perturbing Minkowski spacetime are evolved nonlinearly and show that the implementation is reliable and signals can be successfully extracted at future null infinity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Kerr-black-hole worldline action to $\mathcal{O}(G^5)$
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We establish a worldline action which correctly reproduces Kerr-black-hole dynamics up to fifth order in Newton's constant in a physical post-Minkowskian counting. This encompasses operators up to second order in the Riemann curvature tensor and up to fourth order in the spin tensor. Doing so entails performing the full effective-field-theory computation of the amplitude for a gravitational-wave scattering off of a spinning compact object up to four-loop order, and matching the result to the predictions from linear black hole perturbation theory. Quadratic-in-curvature operators which must be added to match successfully include time-reversal anti-symmetric ones at linear and cubic spin orders, capturing absorption across the black hole horizon, and conservative quadratic-in-spin ones. As an immediate application of our action, we compute the leading-order change in spin magnitude, and reproduce the leading change in mass, for a Kerr black hole in a scattering event with a second compact body, considering a generic orientation of the black hole's spin.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $Λ$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Hidden Simplicity of the Classical Limit
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the classical limit of two-to-two massive-scalar amplitudes at all orders of perturbation theory. We compute these amplitudes in the probe limit for several theories: a family of scalar theories, electrodynamics, and $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity with half-BPS matter. We show that related multiple-emission classical amplitudes obey a simple factorization derivable from the usual factorization of quantum amplitudes. The classical factorization, which reflects the second-order nature of classical dynamics, holds in more general theories --- including gravity. We further show that both the multiple-emission and the two-to-two classical amplitudes have a simple organization in terms of weighted trees. This allows a recursive computation to all orders in the probe limit. The probe's trajectory emerges as a generating function of trees. The required boundary conditions are given by the Feynman $i \varepsilon$ prescription, leading to a novel worldline Green's function. In our approach, the rich classical dynamics arises from simple combinatorics.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Tidally Induced Coda: Double Transients from Black Hole-Star Binary Encounters with Massive Black Holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Dense stellar environments surrounding massive black holes (MBHs) provide a natural setting for dynamical interactions that can produce transient electromagnetic and gravitational-wave sources. In particular, the tidal field of an MBH can strongly perturb binaries undergoing close encounters with it, driving their internal orbits to extreme eccentricities. Here, we investigate the outcomes of such interactions for binaries composed of a stellar-mass black hole (BH) and a star. Using direct few-body scattering experiments with the code SpaceHub, we explore hyperbolic encounters between BH-star binaries and MBHs. We systematically quantify the probabilities of different dynamical outcomes as functions of the binary orbital parameters and MBH mass, with particular emphasis on a channel in which the tidally induced eccentricity triggers a micro-tidal disruption event ($μ$TDE), as the star is disrupted by its BH companion, followed by accretion of the stellar debris onto the MBH. We derive fitting formulae for the $μ$TDE cross section and for the time delay between the two resulting flares, finding that the latter can be a few months for an MBH of $10^6\,M_\odot$. These double transients offer a distinctive observational signature of $μ$TDEs. We estimate event rates ranging from a few to $\sim 100\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ within a luminosity distance of $40\,{\rm Gpc}$.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, 2 appendices. Submitted to ApJL. Code: https://github.com/Kkritos/smbh-binary | Data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24372716 | Animation of Fig. 2: https://youtu.be/g8_UbibAqKQ

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: On the existence of constants of motion for multipolar test-body dynamics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show that the conservative equations of motion of an extended test body, with force and torque sourced by spin-induced and adiabatic tidal multipoles of arbitrary order, are the flow of the Hamiltonian $H=-\tfrac12μ^2+μU$, where $μ$ is the body's kinematic mass and all multipoles enter through a covariant scalar potential $U$. For such bodies, a certain notion of mass and a spin norm are shown to be exactly conserved, at all multipolar orders and in any background. We then apply our framework to the Kerr spacetime, and construct extensions of the Carter and Rüdiger constants through hexadecapolar order (quartic in spin). They are found to exist if, and only if, the body's multipoles are those of a Kerr black hole. Together with the energy and angular momentum, they make the dynamics of a spinning test black hole in Kerr perturbatively integrable through that order. Lastly, at the next, quintic-in-spin order, an analytic criterion implemented numerically reveals that neither constant admits a continuation, for any conservative multipoles. In the conservative, test-body limit, black-hole binaries thus carry a dynamical hidden symmetry shared by no other compact objects, which persists to high multipolar order but ultimately breaks.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 7 pages + End Matter (2 pages) + Supplemental material (14 pages). 2 figures

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the $f$ mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the $f$-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Nonlinear Causality and Strong Hyperbolicity of Einstein-Israel-Stewart Theories of Transient Relativistic Fluid Dynamics
