General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present the first complete analysis of nonlinear causality and local well-posedness for a very general class of bulk and shear viscous theories of relativistic transient fluid dynamics, which encompasses (i) the original Israel-Stewart theory derived from entropy-current arguments, (ii) approaches derived from kinetic theory, and (iii) resummed gradient-expansion based formulations as particular subcases. Our work establishes, for the first time, simultaneously necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for causality, alongside sufficient conditions guaranteeing strong hyperbolicity, in the full nonlinear regime. These results are rigorously proven for both systems coupled to Einstein's equations featuring a dynamic metric and on a fixed background, with or without a cosmological constant, and include baryon conservation (in the absence of heat/diffusion currents). The conditions are purely algebraic, require no simplifying spacetime symmetry assumptions or a specific equation of state, and allow all transport coefficients to depend on the dissipative currents. We also demonstrate that the normalization, orthogonality, symmetry, and tracelessness physical constraints on the dynamical variables are properly propagated during the lifetime of the solutions. Our results provide a readily usable toolset with which one can investigate the domain of applicability of relativistic viscous fluid dynamics in numerical and phenomenological studies in heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Near-boundary and near-horizon momentum--Krylov response in noncommutative-inspired BTZ spacetime
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We compute the proper radial momentum of a massive probe falling into a Lorentzian-smeared, noncommutative-inspired BTZ black hole at fixed asymptotic mass, and use it as the growth rate of momentum--Krylov complexity. In the BTZ limit the accumulated complexity is $\mathcal{K}_0 = X(\coshτ- 1)$. With smearing, the initial growth coefficient is $F'_α(X)/4$, while the late-time exponent is the surface gravity $F'_α(x_+)/2$. The two depend differently on the smearing parameter, so the deformed response is not a rescaled BTZ curve; we show this analytically and confirm it numerically. For a distant release point the early response approaches BTZ, whereas the late-time rate does not. A BTZ black hole with the same Hawking temperature reproduces the response to within about ten percent, and the remaining difference is set by the early/late mismatch. A Gaussian mass profile gives the same picture. The horizon radius and the surface gravity vanish at the critical smearing with exponents $1/2$ and $3/2$. At fixed mass the boundary stress tensor coincides with that of BTZ, but the $z^3$ Fefferman--Graham coefficient and the lengths of boundary-anchored geodesics do not.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Matrix Multiverses Meet Multiple Mythologies
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present a model in which asymptotically de Sitter universes of various types, and de Sitter (dS) radii $R_n$, live in the interiors of black holes in a maximally entropic flat $p = ρ$ Friedmann-Robertson-Walker universe. These dS universes clearly have many quantum states. We argue that they decay and equilibrate with the maximal entropy universe on time scales of order $α_n R_n {\rm ln} (R_n /δ_n)$, where $α_n$ are model-dependent dimensionless constants and $δ_n$ are the initial distances between the shell, satisfying the Israel junction conditions, and the dS horizon. These are time-scales as viewed by a detector following a trajectory far from the would-be cosmological horizon. These times are all exponentially shorter than dS recurrence times, which have no meaning in this model. It is impossible for a detector inside one of the dS universes to determine whether it is actually part of such a structure. This model could be used as the basis for claiming that certain constants of nature or cosmological initial conditions were chosen to have mathematically unnatural values because other values could not lead to any form of intelligent life.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 16 pages, v2: corrected an error in Section 3 and Appendix A, revised the Introduction, and added further references

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Lyapunov Stability of a Schwarzschild Black Hole Surrounded by the Kiselev Anisotropic Fluid
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the geodesic structure and the stability of circular orbits around a Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a Kiselev anisotropic fluid, characterised by the equation-of-state parameter $ω$ and the normalisation parameter $N$. We consider six representative values, $ω=-1,-2/3,-1/3,0,1/3$ and $1$, over the admissible range of $N$ determined by the horizon structure, including the corresponding extremal limits. Using the effective potentials for null and timelike geodesics, we determine the photon sphere, the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) and the outermost stable circular orbit (OSCO), and examine their stability through coordinate-time Lyapunov exponents. The photon sphere is unstable for all values of $ω$ and $N$ considered. Its instability weakens with increasing $N$ for $ω\leq0$ and vanishes at extremality for $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, whereas it varies non-monotonically with $N$ for $ω=1/3$ and strengthens for $ω=1$. For $ω=-1$ and $-2/3$, stable circular orbits are confined between the ISCO and the OSCO, which merge at a critical value of $N$ beyond which no stable circular orbits exist. In contrast, for $ω\geq-1/3$ stable circular orbits exist at all radii beyond the ISCO, whose location varies with $N$. We also derive a closed-form expression for the squared coordinate-time Lyapunov exponent $(λ_t^T)^2$, valid for arbitrary $ω$, whose sign changes exactly at the ISCO and OSCO, so that the Lyapunov criterion reproduces the boundaries of stable circular motion. The Schwarzschild--de Sitter, mass-shifted Schwarzschild and Reissner--Nordström geometries are recovered as special cases, and the results may have implications for black-hole shadows, thin accretion discs and quasi-periodic oscillations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 17 pages, 12 figures, 6 tables, comments are welcome

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Schwarzschild-de Sitter space is not rigid
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Mean-Field Backreaction in Single-Field Inflation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The validity of linear perturbation theory and the role of backreaction in single-field inflationary models that enhance power at small scales have recently been under debate. We investigate scalar backreaction semi-analytically in a mean-field approach within the decoupling limit, considering popular models with a transient ultra-slow-roll (USR) stage or an oscillatory feature (OF) in the potential. We find that ultraviolet (UV) modes in the Bunch--Davies vacuum can substantially affect backreaction estimates unless removed by adiabatic subtraction. Our mean-field treatment can reproduce recent lattice results, but reveals a spurious sensitivity to UV contributions in some cases. This sensitivity is reduced in the OF model when copious particle production separates the amplified physical modes from the UV vacuum tail, making lattice results more reliable in this regime. In USR, instead, adiabatically subtracted spectra yield milder backreaction on the background evolution than previously inferred.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 52 pages, 11 figures. Improved comparison with lattice simulations in Section 5. Conclusions unchanged. References added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analytic $k$-essence Inflation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this work we develop a fully analytic $k$-essence inflation solution which is compatible with the observational constraints on inflation, without the need for the slow-roll assumption being imposed dynamically in the field equations. The analytic solution is obtained for a kinetic scalar sector of the form $K(X)= \frac{X^n}{X_s^{n-1}}$ and for the scalar field satisfying a tracking condition $\dotφ^2=γH^{-m}$. For this class of theories, the sound speed of the primordial curvature perturbations is constant, so no gradient instabilities occur in the theory. The Hubble rate, the scale factor and the scalar field can be analytically expressed as functions of the cosmic time, and the observational indices of inflation depend solely on the parameters $n$ and $m$. The resulting evolution is inflationary and it develops a pressure singularity a few $e$-foldings after the end of inflation. However, using qualitative and quantitative numerical arguments, we show that the pressure singularity is classically avoided when the matter fluids of radiation and cold dark matter are taken into account.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Diffusing the assumptions: towards realistic LISA stochastic component separation with physics-aware simulation-based inference
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Simultaneous global-fit inference of the numerous sources observed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) depends on accurate modeling of its stochastic components: instrumental noise, the Galactic foreground, and astrophysical or stochastic gravitational wave backgrounds (SGWB). Realistic features such as non-Gaussian transients and data gaps challenge traditional likelihood-based pipelines, creating an opportunity for simulation-based inference (SBI) to augment traditional analyses. Here, we present an SBI framework for LISA stochastic component separation built on the Simformer, a transformer trained with diffusion or flow matching that ingests the full time-delay interferometry cross-spectral matrix via a physics-aware embedding. We progressively relax standard simplifying assumptions on simulated 11.6-day datasets containing a loud foreground and a faint power-law SGWB. With unequal arms and per-link noise freedom, the networks match 17-dimensional MCMC posteriors after importance reweighting; full cross-spectra constrain each link's optical metrology noise amplitude to $1\%$. When marginalizing over glitches or massive black hole binary transients, estimation errors remain flat up to transient signal-to-noise ratios of several hundred, whereas ignoring them severely biases likelihood fits. Under time-varying spline noise levels, realistic glitch rates, and gaps up to one day long, posterior coverage remains nominal or conservative across $\sim 10^4$ simulations. We test coverage in the local neighborhood of a given observation by introducing a novel importance-weighted localized simulation-based calibration test. We find flow matching slightly better calibrated than diffusion in simpler regimes and observe modest gains from physics-aware template inputs. Finally, we outline how these networks can initialize the noise and stochastic blocks of a LISA global fit.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Fate of Vainshtein Screening for UV/IR Mixing with a $P(X)$ Higgs Classicalizer
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Classicalization is a non-Wilsonian framework in which an effective field theory self-completes above its strong-coupling scale by generating semiclassical objects that decay into many soft quanta, thereby realizing ultraviolet-infrared mixing. A key requirement of this mechanism is that the force carrier be lighter than the strong-coupling scale. A natural application would be to embed classicalization in the electroweak Higgs sector to address the little hierarchy problem. In this work, we investigate whether Higgs classicalization can occur within the $P(X)$ class of gauged k-essence and k-chameleon models. For classicalization to occur, the theory must support Vainshtein screening around a sharply localized source. Our results show that it fails to do so, even when one attempts to engineer a symbiosis with chameleon screening through a gauge kinetic function, owing to a strong-coupling breakdown inside the screening region. These $P(X)$ theories therefore fail to provide a suitable framework for Higgs classicalization. Nevertheless, we emphasize that our results, obtained for a specific class of models, should not be interpreted as a no-go theorem for Higgs classicalization.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Conservative tidal effects to third post-Minkowskian order in scalar-tensor theories
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Using worldline effective field theory, we compute the conservative finite-size contributions to the impulse and scattering angle of nonspinning compact binaries in massless scalar-tensor theories with a scalar-Gauss-Bonnet coupling through third post-Minkowskian (3PM) order. We retain the full velocity dependence at linear order in the tidal response coefficients. The calculation covers the scalar dipole and quadrupole and the electric, magnetic, and mixed quadrupoles and octupoles. Among them, the scalar dipole enters the dynamics already at third post-Newtonian (3PN) order, two orders before the gravitational quadrupole. At 3PM, the tidal correction to the angle also depends on the first scalar derivatives of the responses and contains terms linear in the Gauss-Bonnet coupling. The results reproduce the general-relativistic tidal angle and the post-Newtonian tidal dynamics through 5PN, and a test-body calculation confirms their leading order in the mass ratio, including the Gauss-Bonnet terms for a companion with vanishing sensitivity.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Analysis of LIGO glitches during the first part of the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: This paper presents an analysis of noise transients observed in LIGO data during the first part of the fourth observing run, using the unsupervised machine learning technique t-distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) to examine the behavior of glitch groups. Based on the t-SNE output, we apply Agglomerative Clustering in combination with the Silhouette Score to determine the optimal number of groups. We then track these groups over time and investigate correlations between their occurrence and environmental or instrumental conditions. At the Livingston observatory, the most common glitches during O4a were seasonal and associated with ground motion, whereas at Hanford, the most prevalent glitches were related to instrumental conditions.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: On the Fourier Analysis of the Einstein-Klein-Gordon System: Limiting Behaviour of the Fourier Coefficients
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We revisit the problem of computing the Fourier coefficients associated with the spherically symmetric massless-scalar field system in $(1+3)$ dimensions initiated in [10]. We rigorously derive computationally efficient formulas for these coefficients and then use them to establish their asymptotic behavior as the mode numbers tend to infinity, including the explicit determination of the leading-order coefficients. Our approach builds on the method developed in [12] and relies on two powerful algorithms for hypergeometric summation, due to Zeilberger and Gosper. These algorithms enable us to systematically derive first-order linear recurrence relations and obtain closed-form discrete antiderivatives respectively for intricate hypergeometric sequences that arise in our analysis.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Symmetry breaking Poincar{é}--Einstein metrics and non-extendable boundary Killing fields
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct Poincar{é}-Einstein metrics on $R^2xS^3xS^2xS^2$ which bifurcate from anti-de Sitter black holes whose horizon is the product of a B{ö}hm metric on $S^3xS^2$ with a round $S^2$ , and which break the rotational symmetry of the $S^2$ factor while keeping their conformal infinity. Some Killing fields of the conformal infinity therefore do not extend to the bulk, although $$π$^1(M, $\partial$M ) = 0$. The construction rests on two results of independent interest: the Lichnerowicz eigenvalues of B{ö}hm metrics on invariant transverse traceless tensors are simple (with at most two exceptional values), the lowest one tends to $-$\infty$$ along B{ö}hm's sequence with a gap to the next one tending to infinity; and large anti-de Sitter black holes in dimension nine with an Einstein horizon have no static $L^2$ perturbation of scalar type, which we prove with an explicit positive supersolution of the Kodama-Ishibashi master equation.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Detecting Frame Dragging Effect with Next-Generation Spaceborne Clocks in a LEO-DRO Satellite Configuration
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Our approach employs a satellite constellation comprising one satellite in low Earth orbit (LEO) and one satellite in distant retrograde orbit (DRO). This configuration is designed to enhance the sensitivity to the Earth's rotation-induced frame-dragging signal while providing a stable and gravitationally isolated frequency reference. We derive a complete relativistic formulation for the frequency comparison between LEO and DRO, incorporating the post-Newtonian metric, higher-order Earth multipoles, lunar and solar tidal potentials, and the gravitomagnetic vector potential. The frame-dragging signal is of order $10^{-20}$, a level that is becoming increasingly accessible with next-generation optical clocks. Recent advances in zero-dead-time strontium optical lattice clocks have demonstrated a fractional frequency instability of $2.9\times10^{-19}$ at an averaging time of 20,000~s, with an estimated one-day stability of $2.5\times10^{-19}$. With continued advances in clock stability, achieving fractional-frequency sensitivity at the $10^{-20}$ level appears feasible in the near term, potentially enabling the direct measurement of a frame-dragging signal of the same order. Such a measurement would constrain Earth's gravitomagnetic field, enabling future investigations of gravitomagnetic effects on Einstein clock synchronization.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational lensing and deflection angles of generalised Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole embedded in a warped braneworld background
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate null geodesics, deflection angles, and gravitational lensing by the generalized Ellis-Bronnikov (GEB) wormhole and its embedding in a five-dimensional warped braneworld (WGEB). The GEB geometry extends the standard Ellis-Bronnikov wormhole through a steepness parameter $m\geq 2$, which controls the throat profile while partially reducing the violation of the classical energy conditions. We derive analytic expressions for the weak- and strong-deflection angles and obtain the corresponding Einstein-ring and relativistic-image relations. The standard Ellis-Bronnikov results are recovered as the special case $m=2$, while for $m>2$ the strong-deflection angle exhibits a power-law divergence instead of the familiar logarithmic behaviour. For the warped five-dimensional geometry, we show that the extra-dimensional momentum modifies the effective impact parameter, and hence the deflection angle and image positions while leaving the location of the unstable photon orbit unchanged. We further derive generalized relations between relativistic and non-relativistic Einstein-ring radii. Our analysis shows that deflection/ring data alone cannot distinguish the effect of the warped extra dimension in WGEB scenario.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 38+8 preprint pages, Major revision, new anaytic results, provisionally accepted for publication in CQG

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to $\sim 7 \%$. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Central charges as black-hole hair in weakly coupled trace-anomaly gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study black holes in Gabadadze's weakly coupled effective theory of the gravitational trace anomaly, keeping both the Euler and the Weyl central charges. We prove that a constant anomalyon on any Ricci-flat geometry, the Kerr family included, solves the full theory if and only if the two central charges coincide. Otherwise, the black holes continuously connected to this branch carry scalar hair whose charge is fixed by the surface gravity, the horizon topology and the difference of central charges alone: maximally supersymmetric matter leaves black holes bald, the Standard Model and photon-dominated sectors produce hair of definite sign, and conformal collider bounds confine it to a universal window. Electric charge separates the two anomaly invariants: the hair reverses sign at a critical charge-to-mass ratio set by the ratio of central charges, its extremal value retains only the Weyl charge, and the Euler charge governs the near-horizon growth of the anomalyon. For every unitary matter sector, the hair regular at the event horizon diverges at the Cauchy horizon. Finally, once the higher-derivative Weyl operator is order-reduced, the background, the anomalyon-graviton mixing and all propagation speeds depend only on the difference of central charges, which extends the no-ghost and Laplacian stability conditions to the full anomaly.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Carrollian correlators in black hole perturbation theory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this note, we clarify the relationship between the two-point Carrollian correlator and massless scattering in a black hole background. It turns out that there are two types of Carrollian correlators at the null boundaries of each asymptotically flat spacetime. The correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+$ should be regularized by subtracting the flat-space analog, and it is the position space version of the reflection amplitude for massless scattering. On the other hand, the correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to the future horizon $\mathcal H^+$ is absent in flat space, and it is the position space version of the transmission amplitude. The poles of the Carrollian correlators are governed by null geodesics from $\mathscr I^-$ to either $\mathscr I^+$ or $\mathcal H^+$, and these geodesics define two classes of classical equations in Carrollian space. These equations relate the Shapiro time delay to the deflection angle and are determined purely by the boundary data. We find that, for small deflection angles, the time delay for the correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+/\mathcal H^+$ exhibits logarithmic/quadratic behavior. On the other hand, when the deflection angle is large, the time delay always increases linearly for both correlators. We further establish a relation between the low-frequency bulk scattering coefficients and the leading non-contact contributions at late times. The correlator from $\mathscr I^-$ to $\mathscr I^+$ features an inverse-square tail $τ^{-2}$ with an explicit angular distribution $K_2$. We have numerically confirmed this angle-dependent late-time tail.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Higher-Dimensional Slowly Rotating Black Holes in Nonlinear Electrodynamics
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study slowly rotating, nonlinearly charged black holes in arbitrary spacetime dimension $d \geq 4$, using a generalized Lense--Thirring ansatz. Working to linear order in the rotation parameters, we solve the Einstein--nonlinear electrodynamics (NLE) field equations for restricted theories ${\cal L}({\cal S})$ depending on single invariant. We provide an extension of the four-dimensional "No Go theorem" proven in ArXiv:2203.01919 and demonstrate the uniqueness of Maxwell theory in $d \geq 4$. Similar to four dimensions, it is proven that the standard rotation generating trick fails to produce full rotating solutions for any nontrivial NLE in higher dimensions. We identify a family of NLE theories admitting slowly rotating solutions with vector potentials encoding rotation effect in Maxwell-like manner; in four dimensions this reproduces the previously found RegMax theory, while in $d\geq4$ we obtain the corresponding electric potential in closed form and the associated Lagrangian implicitly as a function of the radial coordinate.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraining Regular Black Hole Models with the Effective Field Theory treatment of General Relativity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this paper, we present a method for using perturbative predictions from treating general relativity as an effective field theory to constrain non-perturbative approaches to quantum gravity in black hole contexts. We start by reviewing a known result from this framework, which estimates the first quantum corrections to the interaction energy of a static particle near a black hole. We then propose a way to test non-perturbative quantum black hole models - specifically those formulated as modified Schwarzschild metrics, also known as regular black holes - against this perturbative result. To illustrate, we apply our method to the Hayward metric, showing that it does not align with the perturbative prediction, and we identify the most general metric that can reproduce the expected result.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle ($Δ$) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the $Δ$. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The $Δ$ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of $30^\circ$ is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for $\sim550$ binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 74+9 pages, 48+7 figures. The Geometry Comparison Report and Executive Summary are publicly available at https://edms.cern.ch/project/CERN-0000291524 and https://edms.cern.ch/ui/file/3529996/0.1/GCR-EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY-v4.pdf

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Geometric distinguishability of two-source gravitational-wave signals from the extrinsic geometry of the single-source waveform manifold
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Overlapping gravitational-wave signals can produce strong degeneracies in which a multi-source waveform is accurately represented by a single effective source. We formulate this source-confusion problem geometrically by treating the family of single-source waveforms as an embedded manifold in the noise-weighted detector Hilbert space. We introduce the distance-to-manifold statistic, defined as the minimum residual obtained by fitting a waveform with the single-source model, and show that its squared value is directly related to the maximized likelihood difference between two-source and single-source hypotheses in the noiseless limit. For two sources with nearby parameters, perturbative minimization demonstrates that the effective single-source fit absorbs all leading tangent-space deformations. The first irreducible residual lies in the normal space of the waveform manifold and is governed by its second fundamental form. We validate our approach using a six-parameter frequency-domain inspiral model with a LISA-like time-delay-interferometry response. Direct optimization reproduces the predicted quartic scaling over the numerically resolved regime, while two-dimensional confusion-zone maps reveal strongly anisotropic distinguishability boundaries. These results establish extrinsic waveform-manifold curvature as a coordinate-independent diagnostic of local multi-source confusion and provide a practical framework for identifying parameter-space directions in which overlapping gravitational-wave sources are most difficult to resolve.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Accepted Manuscript online 18 November 2026. Published by IOP Publishing Ltd

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Quasi-Local Celestial Charges and Multipoles
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We extend Penrose's quasi-local mass definition to include higher-spin charges associated with the celestial $Lw_{1+\infty}$ symmetries and relate them to traditional definitions of multipoles. The resulting formulae provide explicit expressions that can be computed on finite 2-surfaces, given a choice of null hypersurface. They yield a geometric definition of celestial symmetries and multipoles in generic spacetimes in terms of higher-valence solutions to the twistor equations. This, in turn, gives rise to natural flux-balance laws along the null hypersurface. We also present a first-principles phase-space derivation of these charges, starting from a twistor space action for self-dual gravity that can be identified with the standard gravitational asymptotic phase space at null infinity, performing a large gauge transformation analysis and using the Penrose transform to connect with the corresponding spacetime expressions. Finally, we formulate the spacetime analysis in the Plebanski gauge and relate the celestial symmetries to the integrability of self-dual gravity in the case of a self-dual background.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and Eöt-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the Eöt-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Hybrid Stars with Post-Merger Rotation Profiles
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the effect of differential rotation on hybrid stars with the first-order deconfinement phase transition from hadronic to color superconducting quark matter. The differential rotation is introduced within a realistic, four-parameter phenomenological rotation law, in which the maximum angular velocity of the rotating configuration is shifted away from the center. We focus on two classes of differentially rotating solutions, namely quasi-toroidal (type C) and quasi-spherical (type A), and study the changes in the star global properties and angular velocity profiles due to the presence of a phase transition. We show that when increasing the angular momentum $J$ the turning points of the $J=const$ sequences shift towards lower energy densities, shrinking considerably the region where differentially rotating neutron stars with phase transitions exists. Interestingly, for both type A and type C solutions, the angular velocity profile is continuous throughout the star despite the discontinuity in the energy density. Moreover, we show that for the differential rotation law we study, at the crossing points where the mass-radius curves for different equations of state intersect, the rotational profiles of the solutions are very close despite large differences in the energy density profiles. This reveals a possible degeneracy between the post-merger remnant properties for models with and without phase transitions, emphasizing the need for complementary multi-messenger observables to distinguish between them.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 17 pages, 15 figures, Version accepted in Phys. Rev. D

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: For whom the Bell tolls: joint measurements and state updates in quantum field theory
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: State update rules and their behaviour in Bell tests play an important role in the study of measurement schemes and quantum information. We consider the state updates of the Fewster-Verch measurement framework for quantum field theory using their connection to the probability distribution of measurement outcomes. We focus on a set of observables of the form $A(f_i)^*A(f_i)$, where $A(f)$ is the (complex) smeared field operator for any theory induced by a formally hermitian, Green hyperbolic differential operator, and where the $(A(f_i))_{i=1, \dots, m}$ are assumed to be normal and mutually commuting. Under the assumption that these operators have a sufficiently nice representation on a bosonic Fock space, we derive the joint moment generating functional and the unique joint probability distribution for the observables $(A(f_i)^*A(f_i))_{i=1,\dots,m}$. As an application of these results, we construct a model of a Bell inequality test within quantum field theory using a recently developed coupled Proca-scalar model for polarization measurements. We show that our Bell test model can violate the CHSH inequality, approaching Tsirelson's bound for maximally entangled states in the limit where vacuum effects are perfectly rejected. These results show that the state update rules derived in the Fewster-Verch framework are compatible with strongly quantum correlations. They also support a viewpoint in which state updates should be understood in relation to available information.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter $1/p$, where $p$ is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity $e$, up to 10PN and $e^{20}$, extending beyond prior 6PN and $e^{16}$ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin $a$ and $e$, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in $e$. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For $a=0.9M$, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids ($\sim10^{-7}$) for $p\gtrsim20$ to $75$ as $e$ ranges from $0.1$ to $0.7$, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals: accessing generic orbits
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRI) are a significant gravitational wave source and a target for the upcoming LISA mission. Computations of the fluxes of conserved quantities, such as energy and angular momentum, are a critical part of modeling EMRI waveforms and can be performed using a frequency domain formalism to solve the Teukolsky equation. This requires computations of large numbers of mode amplitudes, many of which are negligible. However, it is unknown ex ante which can be safely skipped. We present a machine learning approach to estimate the dominant radial mode number as a function of the remaining mode numbers and apply it to reduce the number of unnecessary computations in EMRI flux calculation.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures, submitted to Proceedings of RAGtime 26-28: Workshops on black holes and neutron stars, Opava, Czech Republic

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Imprints of quantum space in the ringdown phase of Kerr black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate quantum-space corrections to the gravitational quasinormal modes (QNMs) of Kerr black holes within the framework of noncommutative geometry. The analysis employs a pseudo-semi-Killing Drinfeld twist, which preserves the classical Kerr geometry as an exact background solution while introducing nontrivial quantum corrections to linearized gravitational perturbations. Working to first order in the black hole spin and the quantum deformation parameter, including their mixed contribution, we derive a Schrödinger-like master equation for axial gravitational perturbations with a frequency- and spin-dependent effective potential. We compute the fundamental QNM frequencies using the WKB approximation and Leaver's continued-fraction method. Our results reveal corrections to the QNM oscillation frequencies and damping rates arising from rotation, pure quantum effects, and their interplay. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first systematic analysis of gravitational metric perturbations in a noncommutative Kerr black hole spacetime using a Drinfeld twist, extending prior work beyond the Schwarzschild case. Our findings demonstrate that quantum deformation effects alter both the oscillation frequencies and damping rates of quasinormal modes, with spin-quantum coupling introducing additional spin-dependent corrections to the Kerr QNM spectrum. Using a Kerr-anchored phenomenological prescription, we estimate the fractional frequency and damping-time shifts for selected merger remnants from the GWTC-3 and GWTC-5.0 catalogs. These estimates illustrate the potential signatures of quantum corrections in gravitational-wave ringdown.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Constraining dark energy with complementary probes of large-scale structure
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: To observationally pin down the nature of dark energy, it is essential to consistently model cosmological perturbations in the presence of dark energy alongside the background expansion and constrain this joint theory space with a large array of complementary probes. Here, we achieve this by constraining a model in the Effective Field Theory of Dark Energy (EFTofDE) framework by supplementing probes of the expansion history with several probes of large-scale structure: redshift space distortions (RSD) from DESI DR1, $3\times2$pt measurements from DES Y3, and the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect from cross-correlating CMB temperature anisotropies with galaxy number counts or CMB lensing. We demonstrate the complementarity of different probes which leads to strong improvements on constraints on DE perturbations. For our most constraining dataset combination that supplements CMB+BAO+SNe probes with DESI DR1 RSD, DES Y3 $3\times2$pt and ISW cross-correlations between CMB temperature and galaxy counts, we find an improvement in the Figure of Merit (FoM) for the DE perturbation parameters $\{c_B, c_M\}$ by a factor of 2.69. We show the phenomenological implications of these constraints by mapping them to the present-day values of the phenomenological functions $\{μ(z), Σ(z)\}$, where we see an FoM improvement by a factor of 3.37. We find a significant interdependence between the posteriors of $\{w_0, w_a\}$ and $\{c_B, c_M\}$, caused by the theoretical prior imposed by the gradient stability condition within the EFTofDE framework. Finally, we compute the significance of deviation from $Λ$CM for the EFTofDE model when constrained with CMB+BAO+SNe datasets, finding it to be at 2.9$σ$. This significance is nontrivially similar to the significance for the $w_0w_a$CDM model for the same dataset combination which we find to be 3.1$σ$.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages + appendices and references, 14 figures. v2: typos corrected, references added. v3: added minor clarifications, version accepted to PRD

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Longitudinal-dither wavefront sensing: Calibration-free measurement of mode mismatch
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Mode mismatch between a gravitational-wave detector and the beams injected into it lowers the power stored in the arms and the level of squeezing. Correcting it requires the complex amplitudes of the three second-order modes, measured on a calibrated scale with the cavity on resonance at its operating power. Here we present a method that obtains a signal proportional to the mismatch by moving the beam on the wavefront sensors already used for alignment control. A longitudinal dither of the cavity adds to the resonant mode a reference field, which reaches the sensors through the same signal chains and so calibrates both the scale of this signal and the Gouy phases of the sensors and actuators, with no external calibration. We demonstrate the method on an optical cavity held on resonance in its operating state at input powers of 2 W and 62 W. At 2 W it yields an optical model that agrees with independent measurements in the mode content, and with the layout model in the actuator Gouy phase within its uncertainty of about $1^\circ$. At 62 W the thermally induced change of the eigenmode is decomposed into waist-size and waist-position changes. The method requires only components that every controlled cavity already possesses and enables continuous in situ monitoring of the mode matching in the operating state.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Modeling the LISA response in the time-frequency domain
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Time-frequency methods are a promising approach to LISA data analysis. This paper presents a model for the LISA response directly in the time-frequency domain using the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer (WDM) transformation. The implementation is vectorized using JAX and can efficiently evaluate the response for batches of signals, achieving white-noise mismatches of $\sim 10^{-9}$ compared to existing implementations of the LISA one-arm response. Our results demonstrate that the LISA response can be modeled accurately and efficiently in the time-frequency domain, providing an important component of an end-to-end time-frequency LISA analysis framework.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Nonperturbative lattice simulation of the nucleation rate in thermal first-order phase transitions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We present a nonperturbative lattice study of vacuum decay through bubble nucleation in a three-dimensional real scalar field theory at finite temperature. The vacuum decay rate is computed by combining an expanded-ensemble multicanonical hybrid Monte Carlo approach, which samples the critical bubble configurations, with real-time Langevin dynamics, which follows the subsequent bubble evolution. We extrapolate the nucleation rate to the continuum limit and compare it with the corresponding one-loop perturbative prediction, finding a discrepancy of about 6.6%.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Quark and gluon gravitational form factors of the nucleon at next-to-leading order
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We compute the quark and gluon gravitational form factors $A$, $J$ and $D$ of the nucleon in three-point QCD sum rules at next-to-leading order in $α_s$ for the quark and gluon energy-momentum tensors (EMT), treating both at the same order in the $\overline{\rm MS}$ scheme. The nucleon EMT also tests the method, showing where the sum rules are reliable and why. Protected estimators of $D$ and of the trace form factor $\bar c$ require antisymmetric Borel moments, since none with equal Borel masses alone is protected. The $\mathcal{O}(α_s)$ corrections reduce $A_{\rm tot}$ by $32$--$40\%$, $J_{\rm tot}$ by $22$--$27\%$ and $|D_{\rm tot}|$ by $21$--$27\%$, since the perturbative share of the two-point function is much larger. The total form factors agree with lattice QCD for $1\le Q^2\le2.5$~GeV$^2$. At $Q^2=1.5$~GeV$^2$, $A_{\rm tot}=0.337\pm0.113$, $J_{\rm tot}=0.206\pm0.100$ and $D_{\rm tot}=-0.206\pm0.121$. $D$ is the most reliable result: its correlator is mostly perturbative, and its quark and gluon parts agree with the lattice. In $A$ and $J$, a local gluon-condensate term that does not fall with $Q^2$ is the largest, and their gluon shares are well below the lattice, possibly because the gluon EMT couples at this order only through gluon exchange and the condensate. A working region exists only near $β=1$, and the constant part of transitions cannot be separated within the Borel windows. The individual conservation identities deviate at one point by two standard deviations, consistent with a missing finite term in the $g_{μν}$ structure, and $\bar c$ is therefore given at leading order with condensates.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Hadron spectroscopy of QC2D at finite density
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We investigate the chemical-potential dependence of hadron masses in two-color QCD (QC$_2$D) at low temperature using lattice Monte Carlo simulations. We calculate all possible meson and diquark correlation functions, including disconnected diagrams, on a $32^4$ lattice at $T\approx40\,\mathrm{MeV}$. In the hadronic phase, we obtain a meson mass hierarchy similar to that of three-color QCD. After the superfluid transition, the ordering changes: the $σ$ and $a_1$ channels become lighter, while the pion mass increases with density. We also examine the diquark source dependence of the Nambu--Goldstone mode of $U(1)_B$ symmetry breaking and find an almost vanishing mass in the superfluid phase after extrapolation to zero source. Finally, we compare correlation functions for chiral partners and discuss indications of partial chiral-symmetry restoration. This contribution is based on our recent study of hadron spectra in dense QC$_2$D~\cite{Iida:2026dmw}.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Ab initio Complex Langevin computation of the roton gap for a dipolar Bose condensate
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We compute from first principles the dispersion relation of a finite-temperature dipolar Bose gas near the roton instability. Using a field-theoretic Complex Langevin (CL) approach, we access experimentally relevant atom numbers. We determine the roton excitation gap as a function of the s-wave scattering length under the conditions of the experimental study by Petter et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 122, 183401 (2019)] using erbium atoms. Our results show good agreement with experimental measurements close to the instability, in contrast to predictions of the standard approximate field theory based on the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE). While the eGPE agrees with our results far from the instability, we find that it quantitatively fails as the roton softens, where the CL result lies between the GPE and eGPE predictions. This deviation reveals limitations of the (extended) mean-field description and establishes Complex Langevin as a powerful tool for quantitatively accurate simulations of many-body quantum systems where quantum fluctuations and temperature play an essential role.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Hybrid Analog-Digital Simulation of the Abelian Higgs model
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: To investigate gauge theories with near-term quantum computers warrants exploration of nontraditional quantum simulators to find resource-efficient simulation protocols and ultimately access exotic features of different field theories, including unexplored regimes of the QCD phase diagram. In this work, using superconducting transmon qutrit processors, we formulate and implement a pulse-based, three-level, hybrid analog-digital simulation protocol of the (1+1) dimensional Abelian Higgs model (AHM) on two sites. Alongside this approach, we experimentally realize a gate-based implementation of the same model. Using the natural mapping of the three-level truncation of the transmon Hilbert space to the spin-1 truncated AHM, we observe real time dynamics of AHM field observables, which are analogous to electric field operators, with both protocols. For the analog-digital protocol, we engineer a Floquet simulation with a combination of local analog drives, driven modification of the natural interaction Hamiltonian of the two transmons, and dynamical decoupling pulses. For the digital protocol, we use a state-of-the-art qutrit processor to implement a Trotterized simulation of the model incorporating advanced error mitigation techniques. We further discuss the scalability of the two approaches, and their potential to be extended to the simulation of other model Hamiltonians. Our experiments demonstrate a viable platform for future studies of spin-1 and SU(3) based gauge theory models on current and near-term transmon qutrit processors.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Locality from Nonlocality: Symmetry Relocalization and Gauging of Lattice Dirac Fermions
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary:
Spatially nonlocal symmetries need not imply nonlocal gauge dynamics. Nonlocal canonical transformations make certain exact nonlocal compact symmetries of free lattice Dirac fermions onsite while retaining sufficient Hamiltonian locality for gauging. Symmetry relocalization yields exact or emergent gauge locality in 1D, 2D, and 3D, subject to lattice structure, topology, and anomalies.
  In 1D, a Hamiltonian-preserving transformation exchanges onsite vector and nonlocal spectral axial charges of a half-filled chain, enabling local gauging of each and exposing their mixed anomaly. Bosonization identifies momentum-winding T-duality, with a parity-projected operator flowing to a noninvertible topological defect. A nonperturbative norm-resolvent bound proves emergent dynamical gauge locality at finite chemical potential, while a doubled Chern-insulator parent reveals the duality's bulk origin and superconducting extensions reveal hidden compact symmetries.
  In 2D, the square $π$-flux Majorana model shares the Kitaev honeycomb model's single Dirac fermion and odd Pfaffian parity but supports sharp and exponentially local compact charges, the latter with nontrivial Chern topology. Relocalization retains Schwartz locality for asymptotically local gauging, while AIII/AII parents clarify bulk charge origin and parity-anomaly inflow. Two flavors yield compact $U(2)$, a quaternionic invariant, and asymptotically local non-Abelian gauging.
  In 3D, an exact mixed vector-axial flux response is derived, while a distinct model supports an exponentially local vector $U(1)$ charge with strong quaternionic topology. A nonlocal map makes the charge and Kramers symmetry onsite while preserving exponential Hamiltonian locality. For a compact $SU(2)$ Weyl doublet, a no-go theorem forbids translation-preserving Gaussian onsite relocalization retaining Weyl content and Hamiltonian locality.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Leading-order dynamical QED corrections to the thermodynamics of isospin-asymmetric QCD
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We present a first lattice calculation of the leading-order effect of dynamical photons on the thermodynamics of QCD at nonzero isospin chemical potential $μ_I$, across the onset of charged-pion condensation. In QCD this onset is a second-order transition, which dynamical photons are expected, on general grounds, to drive first order. However, a direct simulation is not possible since unequal quark charges render the QCD+QED action complex at nonzero $μ_I$. We therefore expand the free energy density $f$ in the electromagnetic coupling $e$ around $e=0$, where the sign problem is absent. The leading-order expansion coefficient, $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$, is the convolution of the photon propagator with the electromagnetic current-current correlator, which we measure with a newly proposed planar source on existing (2+1)-flavor pure-QCD ensembles at nonzero $μ_I$ and pionic source $λ$. At physical quark masses and a single lattice spacing, after extrapolating to vanishing $λ$, we find that $\partial^2 f/\partial e^2|_{e=0}$ is, within errors, independent of $μ_I$ below the onset and rises sharply across it.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 9 pages, 3 figures, talk presented at the 43rd International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice2026), July 26th - August 1st, 2026, University of Maryland, College Park, USA

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Non-Abelian Casimir energy in the Curci-Ferrari model through a functional approach
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Using functional integral methods, we investigate the non-Abelian Casimir energy in the Curci-Ferrari model, which offers an effective description of the infrared regime of Yang-Mills theory. We consider a 3+1D (resp.\ 2+1D) system of two infinite parallel plates (resp.\ wires) at a fixed distance from each other, with either perfect magnetic conductor (PMC) or perfect electric conductor (PEC) boundary conditions. Imposing the boundary conditions directly in the functional integral by the introduction of suitable auxiliary fields that act as Lagrange multipliers, we obtain a boundary effective action that captures the dynamics of this system. The Casimir energy is then computed both directly from the functional integral and via the energy-momentum tensor, providing equivalent results. We find that the Casimir energy for PEC and PMC conditions differs by a constant factor, which can be traced back to a van Dam--Veltman--Zakharov-like discontinuity (both in 3+1D and 2+1D). Lastly, we show that our analytical results are compatible with a variety of recent numerical lattice simulations of the non-perturbative Yang-Mills Casimir energy, in which a novel non-perturbative mass scale emerges.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Identifying the conformal window by chiral phase boundaries
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Once the number of massless fermion flavours reaches a critical value $N_f^*$, many-flavour QCD enters the conformal window, where chiral symmetry remains unbroken in the vacuum. At non-zero quark mass, chiral symmetry is explicitly broken, and thermal chiral crossovers can also occur for $N_f\geq N_f^*$. Their presence alone therefore does not distinguish a QCD-like theory from a mass-deformed conformal theory. They differ, however, in whether a thermal transition persists in the continuum chiral limit. To address this, we map out the chiral phase boundaries of unimproved staggered fermions in the bare lattice parameter space $(N_τ,β,am,N_f)$, comparing $N_f=7$ and $N_f=8$. Our results indicate that the thermal chiral transition persists in the continuum chiral limit for $N_f=7$, whereas the massless continuum theory with $N_f=8$ remains chirally symmetric in the vacuum. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the pseudo-critical surface for eight flavours observed for finite quark masses is consistent with conformal hyperscaling, providing further evidence that eight-flavour QCD lies within the conformal window and suggesting $7<N_f^*\leq8$.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 9 pages, Talk at the 43th International Symposium on Lattice Field Theory (Lattice2026) Subjects:

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Progress on finite temperature Sp(4) lattice gauge theory with matter fields
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We explore the finite temperature behaviour of the Sp(4) lattice gauge theory coupled to two dynamical Wilson fermions transforming in the fundamental representation. The continuum theory provides a realisation of composite dark matter within the Strongly Interacting Massive Particle (SIMP) paradigm. Its thermal phase transition in the early universe might have generated an observable relic stochastic gravitational wave signal. Evaluating the sensitivity of future gravitational wave experiments to this signal requires knowledge of the strength of the phase transition. We explore the two dimensional parameter space of the theory, defined by the bare fermion mass and inverse gauge coupling. For this exploratory study we focus on lattices with a small number of sites in the temporal dimension. We analyse the finite volume scaling behaviour of Polyakov loop observables. Specifically the scaling of the peak of the susceptibility, informed by multiple histogram reweighting, is used to discriminate between the presence of a phase transition or crossover. In the light fermion mass regime we find strong indications of a crossover, while for heavy fermions we find preliminary evidence of a first-order phase transition. These findings motivate further studies of the continuum limit for this and other Sp(2N) gauge theories.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Non-invertible Duality Defects in Four-Dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ Lattice Gauge Theories
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We consider four-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_N$ lattice gauge theories with generalized plaquette actions. These theories are known to exhibit dualities. We construct topological interfaces implementing these dualities by assigning a weight to each building block and proving topological invariance. At self-dual couplings, these interfaces become duality defects representing non-invertible symmetries. We also study center symmetry defects and their junctions with the duality interfaces and derive several crossing relations.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Pion scattering in finite volume within the Inverse Amplitude Method: Extension to moving frames
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We study the leading exponentially suppressed finite-volume corrections to $ππ$ scattering near threshold in moving frames. Using the one-loop Inverse Amplitude Method (IAM), we compute the $I=0$ and $I=2$ amplitudes in a box with total momentum $\vec P=2π\vec d/L$, including the left-hand cut and the $t$-, $u$-channel and tadpole contributions neglected in Lüscher's quantization condition. We derive the resulting correction to the near-threshold energy levels and measure its size relative to the Lüscher term. We find that it becomes comparable to the latter for $m_πL\lesssim 1.5$--$1.7$ at rest, and that it is larger in moving frames, reaching $m_πL\lesssim 2.8$ for $\vec d=[002]$. The corrections become negligible only for $m_πL\gtrsim 5$.
High Energy Physics - Lattice.comment: 5 pages, 2 figures. Contribution to the MESON 2026 proceedings

Atomic Physics.title: Exponential advantage in quantum observation with one extra qubit
Atomic Physics.summary: While quantum technologies promise to revolutionise how we observe the physical world, achieving substantial advantages with minimal overhead remains a central pursuit. Here, we show that augmenting a quantum machine with just one extra qubit yields an exponential advantage in probing quantum many-body dynamics. We propose an algorithm that uses this qubit to coherently interfere dynamical trajectories, simultaneously estimating exponentially many multi-time correlators with exponentially fewer evolutions than any ancilla-free scheme. Remarkably, this advantage holds even when the ancilla-free machine has unrestricted coherence time and arbitrary adaptive control, and persists even for a single correlator. We further prove that extending coherence time exponentially enhances observational power, establishing our protocol's optimality in both space and time. Finally, we numerically demonstrate our approach by predicting higher-order probe signals in a many-body system with orders-of-magnitude fewer experimental runs than previous methods. These results highlight the broad utility of our framework across quantum learning, sensing, and simulation.

Atomic Physics.title: 3D trapping of a meta-atom in an intensity minimum
Atomic Physics.summary: High-refractive-index particles have recently attracted a growing interest in optical manipulation, enabling to engineer optical forces through electromagnetic Mie resonances. Unlike standard silica particles, which exhibit trap frequencies mainly determined by material density, resonant meta-atoms formed by high-index particles enable qualitatively new trapping behaviors. In this work, we experimentally investigate the trapping of resonant silicon particles in an optical standing wave. A direct comparison of silicon and silica highlights the fundamental differences in their optical force scaling and trapping dynamics. Beyond conventional trapping at intensity-maxima, we demonstrate deterministic and stable three-dimensional trapping of silicon nanoparticles in optical intensity minima, a regime that remains inaccessible for silica particles. Drawing a mesoscopic analogy with blue-detuned atom trapping, our results establish meta-atoms as a versatile approach to further extend the optical manipulation tool box towards accessing novel trapping regimes e.g. in close proximity to a surface.

Atomic Physics.title: Computational Complexity and Energy Landscapes of Coulomb Crystals
Atomic Physics.summary: Simulated annealing is widely used to search for ground states of trapped-ion Coulomb crystals and of charges on a sphere (the Thomson problem). Elementary nonuniform bounds clarify the role of the input encoding. For identical ions in a fixed trap, unary ion count and a binary energy threshold define a decision problem in P/poly; NP-hardness would imply a collapse of the polynomial hierarchy. The same holds on the unit sphere. With unary ion count and logarithmic precision parameter, approximate configuration search on the sphere and in a fixed positive-definite harmonic trap admits a solution function in FP/poly. These advice bounds provide no uniform search algorithm. In simulations of up to 100 ions, the number of distinct minima found and the time to reach the best-known minimum both grow approximately exponentially. When ions are pinned to prescribed candidate sites, choosing which sites to occupy to minimize the Coulomb energy is NP-hard in two and three dimensions; a finite-precision promise version is NP-complete. All ions are identical, the interaction is bare Coulomb repulsion, and the hardness is carried by the site positions alone. We extend a previous inverse-square reduction to the Coulomb interaction by deriving its angular law, including the quartic field term, and sharpening two estimates. The construction is an array of quadrupoles whose common monopole term cancels from energy differences between legal configurations. Its energy landscapes exhibit large barriers between nearly degenerate minima. Barrier trees resolve this structure, and simulated annealing becomes trapped above the ground state in the cube example. At laboratory parameters, with individually tunable well depths, the encoding survives numerically on a half-filled square lattice. For Doppler-cooled strontium ions, this requires stiff wells a few to tens of micrometers apart, as in electrode trap arrays.

Atomic Physics.title: Precision Spectroscopy of a Trapped Ion Using a Bath of Ultracold Atoms
Atomic Physics.summary: We perform laser spectroscopy of a trapped ion that is not directly laser cooled. An ultracold atomic bath continuously cools the internal degrees of freedom of the ion to its hyperfine ground state via spin-exchange collisions, while a cotrapped $^{174}$Yb$^+$ ion sympathetically cools the external degrees of freedom. Successful laser excitation is detected via state-selective charge transfer following a collision with an atom and subsequent ion loss. As a demonstration of this spectroscopic technique, we probe the $6^2S_{1/2}\rightarrow 6^2P_{3/2}$ transition at 329 nm in $^{173}$Yb$^+$ and measure the magnetic and electric hyperfine interaction constants for the $6^2P_{3/2}$ state to be A = -241(1) MHz and B = 1460(8) MHz, respectively. Our results are in agreement with a previous measurement obtained in a hollow-cathode discharge experiment but are a factor of 6-9 more precise. The techniques demonstrated in this work may be extended to perform precision spectroscopy on ions with complex level structures, with applications in fundamental physics.

Atomic Physics.title: QED theory of scalar hyperfine interactions in HD$^+$
Atomic Physics.summary: HD$^+$ is the simplest heteronuclear molecular ion. It has been used to determine the proton-to-electron and deuteron-to-electron mass ratios, to test quantum electrodynamics, and to search for new interactions. All these applications rely on an accurate knowledge of its hyperfine structure, for which theoretical predictions have disagreed with several precise measurements. Here we calculate the two dominant hyperfine interactions, namely the couplings of the electron spin to the proton and deuteron spins, including the complete nonrecoil electronic relativistic and leading radiative corrections of relative orders $α^2$ and $α^3$, respectively, evaluated in the Born-Oppenheimer approximation. Nuclear-structure effects are suppressed by using the measured hyperfine splittings of atomic hydrogen and deuterium. The resulting couplings for 40 rovibrational states are about 18 times more accurate than the previous ones. They agree with the recent Penning-trap measurement in the ground state within the combined uncertainty of 65 Hz, i.e., 7 parts in $10^8$, and with a recent measurement in a rotationally excited state, whereas a discrepancy of $7.4(9)$ kHz persists for a vibrational overtone transition. Our results provide improved theoretical input for future determinations of the proton and deuteron masses from HD$^+$ spectroscopy.

Atomic Physics.title: Confidence-Aware Discriminative Readout of Neutral-Atom Arrays
Atomic Physics.summary: Fast and reliable detection is a central requirement for neutral atom quantum computers, yet fluorescence imaging remains a limiting step for rapid experimental cycling, large-scale array operation, and quantum-error-correction protocols. In this work, we demonstrate confidence-aware readout of $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ atoms in optical tweezers using a discriminative classifier. Rather than forcing each atom-site image directly into a hard binary outcome, the proposed readout produces a measurement reliability score. This score is produced by a logistic-regression classifier trained on features derived from both the total photon count and the spatial pattern of fluorescence at each site. The resulting classifier achieves the same readout fidelity with approximately half the imaging time. At an exposure of 10 ms, it achieves $99.83\%$ readout fidelity, comparable to the $99.82\%$ achieved by conventional photon-count thresholding at 20 ms. Importantly, the classifier score enables low-confidence outcomes to be converted into measurement-level erasures, leaving fewer residual unflagged errors at a fixed erasure budget. This improvement is further accompanied by strong false-positive suppression, which is important for downstream operations such as atom rearrangement where false positives can create target defects. Monte Carlo rearrangement simulations show that the reduced false-positive rate and confidence-based erasure conversion improve predicted defect-free assembly performance. This work establishes confidence-aware readout using a discriminative classifier as a practical paradigm for fast and scalable neutral-atom quantum computing.

Atomic Physics.title: Probing the Rung-Mott Insulator in Bosonic Two-Leg Ladders
Atomic Physics.summary: Mott insulators typically appear at integer densities, but certain lattice geometries or non-local interactions can stabilise Mott insulators at fractional densities. In this work, we study strongly interacting two-leg ladders using ultracold bosonic atoms around half-filling, and identify the rung-Mott insulating (RMI) phase through its characteristic rung occupation in site-resolved measurements. We probe its excitation spectrum via lattice modulation spectroscopy, and interpret the observed spectra using numerical simulations that include the driven dynamics, coupling to multiple excited states, and energy offsets. As with other Mott insulators, the RMI phase is characterized through its incompressibility, which we probe via a site-resolved analysis of densities and chemical potentials. Our results provide direct insight into the excitation dynamics of a strongly correlated ladder system, and pave the way for studying transport and further dynamical properties in low-dimensional quantum systems with programmable lattice geometries.

Atomic Physics.title: Perturbation of CO A1Π by a3Π should have been undetectable: detection, mechanism, and surprises
Atomic Physics.summary: A direct perturbation between the $a^3Π$ and $A^1Π$ vibrational levels of two electronic states that belong to the same electronic configuration of the carbon monoxide molecule should be unobservably weak because the vibrational overlap integral $\langle a^3Π,v' \mid A^1Π,v'' \rangle$ for their near-degenerate levels is extremely small. Yet level-shift and transition-intensity signatures of the $a^3Π(v = 13) \sim A^1Π(v = 2)$ perturbation are unmistakably present in the $^{13}\mathrm{C}^{18}\mathrm{O}$ isotopologue. A detailed study of, among others, the $A^1Π$ - $X^1Σ^+(2, 0)$, $B^1Σ^+$ - $A^1Π(0, 2)$, and $C^1Σ^+$ - $A^1Π(0, 2)$ spectra, obtained by the VUV- and Vis-FT complementary techniques in the energy regions of the six crossing points ($e$- and $f$-symmetry, $|Ω| = 0, 1, 2$) between the $a^3Π(v = 13)$ and $A^1Π(v = 2)$ states, reveal that the perturbation pathways are indirect, primarily facilitated by the $e^3Σ^-(v = 4)$ state, and that quantum mechanical interferences via its F1e and F3e components occur.

Atomic Physics.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
Atomic Physics.summary: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ acting on $\mathbb{N} \ge 3$ qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth $π$ pulses.
