Quantum Physics.summary: The recently proposed stochastic-quantum correspondence establishes a connection between general stochastic processes and quantum dynamics, in which stochastic transition probabilities admit compatible representations on a Hilbert space, known as quantum lifts. We ask how the predictive information represented by off-diagonal degrees of freedom in the quantum lift is encoded within the stochastic description. We introduce the notion of a family of context-dependent stochastic processes and show that their continuation probabilities encode this predictive information. In particular, suitable continuations allow the intermediate lifted quantum state to be reconstructed entirely from system configuration probabilities. This perspective also clarifies the nature of quantum measurement: active continuations make basis-dependent quantum probabilities accessible as configuration probabilities, while a separate physical interaction records the realized configuration and introduces measurement disturbance. Although the rooted quantum probabilities alone do not guarantee that every stochastic realizer of the idealized recording interaction faithfully records the system's pre-measurement configuration, we show that at least one faithful stochastic realizer always exists.
Quantum Physics.comment: 17 pages. This manuscript contains material previously presented in arXiv:2602.22095v3. The original manuscript is being reorganized into two separate papers and will be replaced by a shortened version

Quantum Physics.title: Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios with Agent-like Observers on Quantum Computers
Quantum Physics.summary: The Wigner's friend thought experiment raises the question of whether quantum theory can be applied consistently to systems that include observers. Extended Wigner's Friend Scenarios include spatially separate observers sharing entanglement. In the Local Friendliness (LF) framework, these scenarios lead to experimentally testable inequalities derived from Absoluteness of Observed Events and Local Agency, assumptions weaker than those needed for Bell inequalities. Their violation therefore has stronger implications, but LF tests are more experimentally challenging because they require an observer implemented as a quantum system. Drawing from the literature on artificial intelligence, we implement the "friend" with explicit agent-like functionality in a reversible quantum circuit. The agents store measurement outcomes, condition subsequent operations on stored information, and, in the most structured case, use Born-rule probabilities to bet on outcomes of their own future observations based on past observations. We study the circuits through ideal simulations, simulations using an IBM-device noise model, and experiments on the IBM processor ibm_marrakesh. Ideal simulations reproduce the maximal quantum violation of an LF inequality up to finite-shot fluctuations, while hardware runs show positive LF violations for all agents. These results are a step towards more sophisticated agent-like observer models in LF experiments on quantum computers. By focusing on functionality rather than size alone, this approach complements tests of quantum theory in the macroscopic regime and opens a direction for studying agents whose use of quantum theory is implemented within coherently controlled quantum dynamics.

Quantum Physics.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
Quantum Physics.summary: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their sensitivity to noise is expected to decrease exponentially with increasing separation between the Majoranas, a suppression known as topological protection. Kitaev chains engineered in quantum dot-superconductor arrays provide a tunable platform in which separated Majorana zero modes can emerge at the ends of the chain, even in two-site chains. These minimal-chain modes are known as poor man's Majoranas and retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron-hole character, but have only limited protection. A key outstanding challenge is to move beyond identifying such modes in electrical transport measurements and achieve coherent qubit control in the time domain. Here, we demonstrate a Majorana parity qubit by realizing coherent coupling between two-site Kitaev chains. Since total fermion parity is conserved, the system separates into global even and odd parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both manifolds with equal oscillation frequencies at the Majorana sweet spot, as predicted for isolated Majorana zero modes. We further show that the oscillation frequency and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in close agreement with our model for short, partially protected chains. Our results establish the first coherent control of a Majorana qubit, encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes in minimal Kitaev chains.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum optimization beyond qubit count by low-energy subspace sampling
Quantum Physics.summary: On current digital quantum devices, standard one-qubit-per-variable encodings restrict quantum optimization algorithms to problem sizes where classical solvers typically excel. To avoid this constraint, we introduce Quantum Subspace Sampling Descent (QSSD), an iterative heuristic that decouples the number of problem variables from qubit count, while preserving knowledge of the problem's global structure. QSSD drives the energy descent using a fixed-angle Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm as a low-energy sampler. As the angles are precomputed, each iteration requires just a single circuit execution. We test QSSD on IBM Heron and Nighthawk quantum devices with up to 152 qubits on instances of higher-order unconstrained binary optimization and Max-cut problems. On the largest instance with 10000 variables, QSSD reaches an approximation ratio above 0.95 with 100 circuit executions. We provide both exact and heuristic classical baselines, namely greedy, branch-and-bound solver, and simulated annealing. While our approach still does not match the performance of the best classical baseline, it shows promise in a slower runtime scaling with problem size given a fixed budget. This suggests a regime of large problems where subspace sampling on quantum devices could become competitive, as we also demonstrate how improvements in hardware will lead to better algorithm performance. QSSD is thus a practical heuristic for combinatorial optimization problems that helps bring quantum optimization a step closer to utility.

Quantum Physics.title: Optimal Trace Distance Estimation
Quantum Physics.summary: We present a trace distance estimator with optimal sample complexity. Specifically, the trace distance between two unknown $d$-dimensional quantum states can be estimated to within additive error $\varepsilon$ using \[ Θ\left(\frac{d^2}{\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\max\left\{1,\varepsilon^2\log^2(d)\right\}}\right) \] samples of each quantum state. This matches the lower bound of Wang (2026). The estimator combines tomography and polynomial approximation, with variance bounds from quantum Fourier analysis.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Capacity with Incoherent Codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Arbitrarily weak depolarizing noise drives the quantum capacity to zero in every input basis when the encoder is restricted to incoherent operations. Even one qubit cannot then be sent reliably: if the output is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability $\varepsilon\le1/2$, the entanglement fidelity is at most $1-\varepsilon/2$ at every block length. With unrestricted decoding, a single-letter formula gives the capacity with incoherent encoding as the maximum Holevo information over ensembles of basis states with identical environment outputs. For either incoherent or unrestricted encoding, imposing incoherent decoding reduces the capacity by at most a factor of two; this factor is optimal. We bound the fidelity of incoherent decoders and evaluate the capacities with incoherent encoding for multiqubit Pauli channels.

Quantum Physics.title: Controlled teleportation of an unknown qutrit and its control power
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose a controlled quantum teleportation protocol for an arbitrary unknown qutrit using a nonmaximally entangled channel, with Charlie holding a qubit and Alice and Bob each holding a four-level particle. With the aid of an auxiliary qubit, the receiver can recover the input state probabilistically with unit fidelity. We derive the overall success probability and show that it is independent of the input state. To quantify the controller's authority, we obtain analytical expressions for the optimal average teleportation fidelities with and without the controller's cooperation, keeping the sender's joint measurement fixed and averaging uniformly over pure qutrit input states with all measurement outcomes included. Their difference defines the control power of the protocol. For the shared states considered here, we determine a controller measurement basis that simultaneously maximizes the control power and the teleportation success probability for a given shared state. These results clarify the role of the controller's measurement in controlled teleportation with unequal local dimensions.

Quantum Physics.title: The infinite-dimensional extended Bloch representation
Quantum Physics.summary: In the extended Bloch representation (EBR) of quantum mechanics, the Born probabilities of a measurement with N outcomes are the relative volumes of N regions of a simplex-shaped abstract membrane, whose points represent the "hidden" measurement interactions. However, when N tends to infinity, the volumes vanish and the uniform membrane concentrates at the center of the unit ball. We show that this problem can be solved by renormalization: if the radius of the generalized Bloch ball grows like N, the distances of the measurement interactions from the facets of the simplex become independent exponential random variables. This is the only growth with a non-degenerate limit, and the limit membrane, which cannot live in the limit of the generalized Bloch space without privileging some of the outcomes, is the projective limit of the finite-dimensional membranes and, once renormalized, the only distribution compatible with the Born rule. For a pure point spectrum, the regions of the membrane become cones, the particle representing the state recedes to infinity, and the lines along which the membrane collapses become parallel. For a continuous spectrum, a further magnification yields a Poisson point process and the Born rule for probability densities. We also show that the uniform membrane is the only one compatible with the Born rule in finite dimension, and that the mechanism can be read, in every dimension, as a race between independent exponential clocks.

Quantum Physics.title: When Randomness Hides Quantum Simulation Errors
Quantum Physics.summary: Trotter formulas approximate quantum dynamics by discrete steps, but errors in measured observables can be much smaller than worst-case estimates. We investigate how this suppression depends on the degree of randomness in the input states. We show that the mean absolute observable-error bound for state 2-designs can be exponentially smaller in qubit number than the tight bound for state 1-designs. To characterize this error transition from 1-design to 2-design, we use the excess frame potential to quantify the ensemble's second-moment distance. We quantify departures from these random-state statistics through the frame potential, a measure of pairwise state overlaps, and identify the accessible observables most sensitive to the resulting deviations in mean-square error. Extending the analysis to a Hamiltonian trajectory whose frame potential decays as $1/T$ before saturation, we also obtain a sufficient $p$th-order Trotter number $\mathcal O(T^{1+3/(4p)})$ for evolution time $T$. These findings connect input-state statistics to the visibility of Trotter errors, giving a theoretical guarantee and foundation for practical quantum simulation.

Quantum Physics.title: Fourier analysis of quantum neural network with non-linear data embedding
Quantum Physics.summary: Fourier analysis has become a crucial tool for understanding the expressivity of Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) models, as well as an important indicator of barren plateaus. While existing literature has only studied angle-embedded VQCs in a noiseless environment, here we develop the Fourier analysis of VQCs with non-linear data embedding, with particular focus on amplitude embedding, as it provides a naturally compact encoding scheme. We first investigate a difference in the domain of input features that leads to a distinct expressivity of the zero-frequency Fourier coefficient. Assuming that the unitaries generated from the parameter space forms at least a unitary 2-design, we derive that, in integer-valued frequencies, the mean of the Fourier coefficients is concentrated at zero, and the variance is upper bounded by an inverse power-law function with respect to the infinity norm of the frequency. A numerical evidence of exponentially decaying pattern with respect to the frequency magnitude is also established, providing a frequency-perspective of viewing VQC model expressivity and its trainability. When a noise channel with unitary Kraus operators and probabilities $\{p_k\}$ is taken into account, the variance is further suppressed by a factor $\left(\sum_kp_k^2\right)^{Q}<1$ for $Q$ as the number of channel instances applied. Furthermore, we demonstrate and validate the analytical results through simulations, both noiseless and noisy, and contrast its expressivity against the angle-embedded Fourier features. We also examine the model's performance where target functions contains non-integer frequencies. Our results establish a rigorous Fourier framework for amplitude-encoded VQCs, offering both theoretical guarantees on expressivity, hence trainability scaling in the frequency domain, as well as practical simulations for deployment on noisy quantum devices.

Quantum Physics.title: Perfect state transfer in Grover walks on generalized Bethe trees
Quantum Physics.summary: We completely classify the generalized Bethe trees $B(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1})$ that exhibit perfect state transfer between vertex states in Grover walks. We prove that such a tree exhibits perfect state transfer if and only if it is a path or a uniform subdivision of either $B(2,3)$ or $B(1,2,3)$. We also determine all transferring pairs and the minimum transfer times.

Quantum Physics.title: Machine Learning-Based Quantum Error Mitigation for Bound-State Simulations
Quantum Physics.summary: Noise in quantum devices remains a major challenge for reliable quantum simulations, making quantum error mitigation an important tool for improving their accuracy. Machine learning-based quantum error mitigation (ML-QEM) provides a useful approach, but its performance depends on the training datasets and may produce reconstructed quantum states that are not physically valid. In this work, we introduce an ML-QEM framework that uses residual learning with convex projection to ensure that reconstructed density matrices satisfy physically valid density matrices. We study the effect of different training datasets and regression models using Haar-random and variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) ansatz states. We compare the proposed approach with conventional ML-QEM, readout error mitigation, and zero-noise extrapolation. The method is tested on IBM quantum hardware for three- and four-qubit simulations of the bound $Λ$-deuteron and $Λ$-$α$ hypernuclear systems, respectively. For the three-qubit system, ridge regression trained on VQE-ansatz states gives a ground-state energy of -0.134 MeV, close to the ideal value of -0.135 MeV, with a state fidelity of 0.999. For four-qubit system, kernel ridge regression gives ground-state energies of -3.014 and -3.045 MeV, with corresponding state fidelities of 0.995 and 0.998. These results show that physically constrained reconstruction, along with the choice of training datasets and regression models, can improve ML-QEM performance for the quantum simulations studied in this work.

Quantum Physics.title: Electron spin relaxation and coherence times of silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
Quantum Physics.summary: Color defect centers carrying electron spins in solid crystals like diamond and silicon carbide (SiC) are promising candidates for qubits and quantum sensors, with SiC material being particularly interesting due to its compatibility with the existing semiconductor technology. Here we investigated the electron spin properties of silicon vacancy centers (V1 and V2) both electron spin $S = 3/2$ in 4H-SiC in the temperature range $T=80-300$~K using electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR). The EPR spectrum shows central and satellite lines, where the former ones originate from V1 and V2 centers, as well as from unknown defect center X. The analysis of continuous wave EPR measurements revealed a spin concentration of $c_{\mathrm{V1}}=1.47\pm0.3\times10^{14}$, $c_{\mathrm{V2}}=5.6\pm1.12\times10^{13}$ and $c_{\mathrm{X}}=1.03\pm0.21\times10^{13}$ spins/cm$^{3}$. Additionally, electron spin coherence $T_2$ and relaxation times $T_1$ have been measured on the central and on the satellite spectral lines, resulting in longer $T_1$ and $T_2$ for the satellite transition, compared to the central one, with maximum values of $42.8\pm1.3$~ms and $0.708\pm0.004$~ms respectively at $T=80$~K. We reveal, that decoherence is mainly caused by nuclear and electron spin diffusion.

Quantum Physics.title: Approximate Decoherence, Recoherence and Records in Isolated Quantum Systems
Quantum Physics.summary: Using the framework of decoherent histories, we study which past events leave detectable records in isolated quantum systems under the realistic assumption that decoherence is approximate and not perfect. Using tools from quantum state discrimination, we establish asymptotically for a large class of (pseudo-)random histories how the strength of decoherence changes the number of reliable records, i.e., we quantitatively answer the question: when can approximate decoherence be approximated by exact decoherence? In addition, we reveal a clear decoherence structure for long histories based on a numerically exact solution of a random matrix model that, as we argue, captures generic aspects of decoherence. In particular, we observe strong recoherences for maverick histories that are statistical outliers with respect to Born's rule. From the perspective of the Many Worlds Interpretation, our results reveal a "branch selection problem" and shed light on the emergence of Born's rule and the theory confirmation problem.
Quantum Physics.comment: A few additional analytical results and a significantly improved presentation with a focused main text of 15 pages only. Total file: 41 pages, 21 figures and 195 references. Comments welcome!

Quantum Physics.title: Geodesic Efficiency of Counterdiabatic Charging in a Quantum Battery
Quantum Physics.summary: We investigate an open quantum battery consisting of a resonator acting as the energy-storage unit, a frequency-tunable two-level system acting as a controllable mediator, and an external coherent drive serving as the energy source. In the dispersive regime, the dynamics reduce to those of a driven harmonic oscillator with a tunable effective coupling. Starting from the vacuum state, the resonator remains in a coherent state under a Lindblad master equation describing photon leakage at zero temperature. We derive a counterdiabatic (CD) driving protocol that compensates for dynamical lag and ensures that the system follows the prescribed reference trajectory. As a result, the energy stored in the resonator increases monotonically without transient oscillations, allowing the battery to reach the target ergotropy at the prescribed final time $t_f$. The CD trajectory follows a geodesic in the coherent-state phase space and achieves near-unity geodesic efficiency over a broad range of pulse durations, whereas unassisted charging exhibits markedly lower efficiencies. Finally, we show that the CD protocol saturates the quantum speed limit for the charging process.

Quantum Physics.title: Second-order asymptotics for the quantum and private capacities of the erasure channel
Quantum Physics.summary: An erasure channel either delivers a quantum system intact or tells the receiver that it was lost. How much quantum information, or secret classical information, can a finite block transmit without assistance? We determine the optimal second-order coding rates for input dimension $d\ge2$, erasure probability $0<p<1/2$, and fixed infidelity (one minus fidelity) $0<\varepsilon<1$. For $n$ channel uses, the optimal base-two logarithmic code size is \begin{equation}\tag{A}\label{eq:abstract-rate} n(1-2p)\log_2d +2\sqrt{np(1-p)}\log_2d\,Φ^{-1}(\varepsilon) +O((\ln n)^2), \end{equation} where $Φ$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function and $Φ^{-1}$ is its quantile function. The square-root term is the second-order correction. This formula holds for entanglement transmission, entanglement generation, and private classical communication. Quantum error measures failure to preserve entanglement. Private error compares the actual output with a correctly decoded uniform message independent of an optimized environment state. The achievable Gaussian term and a matching quantum expansion below infidelity one half were established recently. We prove matching upper bounds for every fixed infidelity, including private communication, with the displayed remainder. The proof bounds one code's average performance across all loss patterns of a given size; binomial fluctuations then determine the Gaussian correction. It combines tests of correct and secret communication with tensor-product averaging and a classical polynomial identity. Arbitrary mixed encoders and collective decoders are allowed. Requiring the private error bound for every message preserves the Gaussian term. Fixing the ideal environment state to the actual marginal instead changes the quantile to $Φ^{-1}(1-\sqrt{1-\varepsilon})$. Thus the precise privacy criterion affects communication at second order.

Quantum Physics.title: Thermal state preparation with shallow quantum circuits
Quantum Physics.summary: Preparing thermal states on noisy quantum hardware requires circuits that remain shallow at low temperatures. Even when accurate classical state representations are available, compiling them into suitable circuits can be costly. We introduce PP-VarQITE, combining Pauli propagation with variational quantum imaginary-time evolution to determine circuit parameters entirely classically, with target temperatures encoded in the angles of a fixed circuit architecture. In numerical studies of Ising and frustrated Heisenberg models, we recover low-temperature energies and correlations using up to 100 qubits. Across the frustrated chain and two-dimensional lattice, our circuits are approximately two to ten times shallower than the lowest-depth circuits from sequential tensor-network compilation. These shallow circuits enable us to prepare a 48-site frustrated chain and a $7\times7$ Ising lattice using 96 and 98 qubits on the Quantinuum Helios trapped-ion quantum processor. We reproduce the development of dimer order and lattice-wide correlations from high to low temperatures, with the lattice circuits requiring at most 42 two-qubit layers. Through classical circuit design, we demonstrate low-temperature state preparation at circuit sizes beyond the practical reach of statevector simulation.
Quantum Physics.comment: 12 pages, 5 figures; supplementary material 26 pages, 14 figures

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum fields in a cold atomic simulator: relaxation and phase locking in tunnel-coupled 1D bosonic quasi-condensates
Quantum Physics.summary: We consider a prime example of simulating interacting relativistic QFT with cold atoms: the realisation of the sine-Gordon model by tunnel-coupled quasi-1D Bose gases. While experiments have shown that it can realise the sine-Gordon model in equilibrium, studies of non-equilibrium dynamics have revealed phase-locking behaviour that contrasts with predictions from sine-Gordon field theory. Here, we examine a one-dimensional field-theoretic model of the system and find that the phase-locking behaviour can be understood in terms of the longitudinal harmonic trap, and that the additional degrees of freedom observed in the experiment do not appear to play a significant role. Therefore, the experimental setup provides a good simulator of the sine-Gordon quantum field theory, even out of equilibrium, if the inhomogeneous background induced by the trap is taken into account. Furthermore, our results support the idea that modifying the longitudinal trap to a box shape should result in agreement with standard sine-Gordon dynamics. The main remaining open issues are accounting for 3D corrections and modelling the effect of the boundaries.
Quantum Physics.comment: 17 pages, 9 figures. v2: added new discussion to clarify some points. Added references. v4: added author contributions

Quantum Physics.title: QDMin: Coherent Quantum Minimum Finding over Parametrized Many-Body Hamiltonians
Quantum Physics.summary: Many questions about interacting quantum systems ask which member of a Hamiltonian family $H(\mathbf{q})$ has the lowest ground-state energy, rather than for the ground state of one Hamiltonian. A pointwise scan answers this with one many-body solve per candidate. QDMin (Quantum Deformation Minimum Finding) instead holds all $N_q$ candidates in a coherent register and searches them with a ground-energy threshold oracle, replacing $N_q$ solves by $O(\sqrt{N_q})$ coherent oracle calls. We identify static-field (Hubbard-Stratonovich) families as a broad class in which this minimum is a rigorous variational bound that the parent ground state does not reveal, and we make the oracle robust to imperfect ground-state preparation by fixed-point amplitude amplification. The measured search constant places the crossover against a pointwise quantum scan at $N_q \approx 220ξ^2$, where $ξ$ is the overhead of a coherent call. We test the search on realistic sd-shell (USDB) static quadrupole landscapes with up to $10^6$ grid points and on a Hubbard ring with competing orders. It pays where competing minima trap local descent, needing about four times fewer energy queries than multistart descent for oblate-prolate coexistence in $^{28}$Si, and not on smooth single-well landscapes. Circuit-level simulations validate the complete pipeline on a schematic model. The gain concerns the number of energy queries; any advantage of the quantum solver itself is separate.
Quantum Physics.comment: 29 pages, 7 figures. v2: substantially revised and extended. General-method framing (static-field families), overlap-robust threshold oracle, shell-model (USDB) and Hubbard examples, 2000-seed circuit-level statistics

Quantum Physics.title: Indistinguishability Theory for Identical Particles with Invariant Degrees of Freedom
Quantum Physics.summary: Identical particles have dynamically invariant labels in all setups where their degrees of freedom can be partitioned into two parts, which we call internal and visible, with the visible part subject to unitary evolution, while the dynamically invariant internal part accounts for the partial distinguishability of particles. We give the explicit form of the visible state in terms of the indistinguishability function, generalizing the standard symmetrization/antisymmetrization postulate for bosons/fermions with internal modes. The indistinguishability function on the symmetric group accounts for the permutation symmetry of the dynamically invariant label state and gives a self-contained description of the symmetry spectrum of the visible state. It is shown that the indistinguishability of single particles emitted independently from a stable source is completely characterized by the projective measures on the symmetry spectrum. We reveal a hierarchy of successive upper bounds on the projective measure of indistinguishability in terms of marginal projective measures. We point out an experimentally feasible way to get the upper bounds on the indistinguishability of an arbitrarily large number of single photons by direct experimental readout of their marginal projective measures. We also analyze the indistinguishability of coherent superpositions and convex mixtures and resolve a recently posed problem.
Quantum Physics.comment: 27 pages, no figures; two references added in the revision

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Coherence and Basis-Dependent Correlations in Quantum Systems
Quantum Physics.summary:
Quantum coherence and quantum correlations are two fundamental features of quantum systems and are closely related in various quantum information tasks. In general, due to the existence of correlations, the amount of coherence in a bipartite state should be no less than that in the reduced states. We focus on what types of states have an equal amount of coherence in the global state and the local states. For such states, the basis-dependent correlations (the difference between the coherence of a bipartite state and its reduced state with respect to a set of standard orthogonal local bases) vanish. Based on the Tsallis relative entropy coherence measure, we prove that block-diagonal product states exhibit vanishing basis-dependent correlations. Furthermore, we establish an equivalence between the absence of basis-dependent correlations and the block-diagonal product structure in a special case. We then consider the coherence measure based on quantum Fisher information and show that block?diagonal
  product states again lead to vanishing basis-dependent correlations, while in the two-qubit case the vanishing condition constrains the state to a broader block-diagonal-like product structure. These results provide a structural characterization of bipartite states with vanishing basis-dependent correlations under different coherence measures.

Quantum Physics.title: The gap persistence theorem for quantum multiparameter estimation
Quantum Physics.summary: One key aspect of quantum metrology, measurement incompatibility, is evident only through the simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters. The symmetric logarithmic derivative Cramer-Rao bound (SLDCRB), gives the attainable precision, if the optimal measurements for estimating each individual parameter commute with one another. As such, when the optimal measurements do not commute, the SLDCRB is not necessarily attainable. In this regard, the Holevo Cramer-Rao bound (HCRB) plays a fundamental role, providing the ultimate attainable precisions when one allows simultaneous measurements on infinitely many copies of a quantum state. For practical purposes, the Nagaoka Cramer-Rao bound (NCRB), or Nagaoka--Hayashi Cramer-Rao bound (NHCRB), is more relevant, as a lower bound when restricted to measuring quantum states individually. The interplay between these three bounds dictates how rapidly the ultimate metrological precisions can be approached through collective measurements on finite copies of the probe state. In this work we investigate this interplay. For full rank probe states, we prove that if the SLDCRB or HCRB cannot be saturated with measurements on a single copy of the probe state, then they cannot be saturated for any finite number of copies of the probe state. We demonstrate that these results do not necessarily hold for rank deficient states. As an application of this result, we show that it is impossible to saturate the HCRB for several physically motivated problems, including the simultaneous estimation of phase and phase diffusion. Finally, for practical purposes it is more relevant to study the rate at which the NHCRB converges to the HCRB. We prove that given $M$ copies of the probe state, the NHCRB converges to the HCRB at rate of at least $1/\sqrt{M}$.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum Tautochrone for photons and atoms
Quantum Physics.summary: The tautochrone problem, in which the travel time to a common point is independent of the starting position, has served as a foundational model in classical mechanics. Here we establish its quantum counterpart in engineered photonic waveguide arrays and atomic optical lattices, where nonuniform couplings drive photons and particles launched from different positions to converge simultaneously at a common site. Using higher-order correlation functions, we show that this quantum tautochrone effect holds for both bosons and fermions, with quantum statistics governing the character of the convergence: bosons converge onto the same site, while fermions, constrained by Pauli exclusion, gather at neighboring sites. For bosonic atoms, we further show how the tautochrone dynamics is shaped by lattice inhomogeneity, phase-space structure, and on-site interactions.

Quantum Physics.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
Quantum Physics.summary: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period. We distinguish between protocols that break the global ${\mathbb Z}_2$ symmetry by coupling to the order parameter and those that preserve it. These two classes of driving exhibit distinct scaling behaviors, with power-law exponents determined by the RG dimensions of the corresponding perturbations. We verify the proposed dynamic scaling theory through numerical simulations of both smooth single-frequency and discontinuous square-wave periodic drivings.

Quantum Physics.title: A quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder for robust anomaly detection at the LHC
Quantum Physics.summary: Model-agnostic searches for new physics at the Large Hadron Collider utilise unsupervised anomaly detection, where quantum and neuromorphic detectors represent potential approaches. We develop the first fully spiking variational autoencoder, a quantum-inspired spiking variational autoencoder (QSVAE), built on the quantum-inspired leaky integrate-and-fire (QLIF) neuron. In this work we recast the neuron from a measurement-based circuit to a differentiable computational unit. This neuron is benchmarked against other classical, spiking, and quantum models on an LHC di-jet latent space. We show that under noise perturbations the QLIF network retains $0.95$ of its clean accuracy, while accuracy retention for twelve classical models falls to $0.74$-$0.85$. The QLIF anomaly scores respond $3.5$-fold less to the noise perturbation than any of the control model's scores. We compare against a periodic classical control that reproduces the QLIF effect, isolating it to the $\sin^2$ membrane map. This membrane map is a native regulariser that decouples robustness from model capacity supplied by the qubit state space. We demonstrate this through several benchmarks and ablation studies to characterise the performance landscape of the quantum-neuromorphic model space.

Quantum Physics.title: Rydberg Constraint Ensembles for Nonnative Binary Optimization
Quantum Physics.summary: Rydberg blockade can exclude the configuration that minimizes a binary objective. We expand its finite penalties into a weighted ensemble of exclusion graphs. The full ensemble preserves the ground energy, and the interactions remaining on each graph set its local detunings. In simulations of two coupled squares, reversing a target coupling leaves the single-site energy slopes at uniform occupation unchanged, yet a collective mode of the residual interactions switches the favored diagonals from aligned to opposed. On 32 held-out twelve-site targets, the simulated probability of recovering a ground state in 128 shots averages 69.82\% with residual detunings and 24.31\% with a tuned uniform pulse. By scoring the pooled samples under the original objective, we can use these native layouts to search for ground states of a Hamiltonian that none implements alone.

Quantum Physics.title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
Quantum Physics.summary: While quantum protocols for oblivious transfer can be built from weaker assumptions than classical ones, the current protocols remain highly impractical due to stringent security bounds that demand a large amount of quantum communication. In this work, we propose an enhancement to quantum oblivious transfer protocols by leveraging zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs). At a high level, we modify the protocol such that the receiver proves that they are following honestly some crucial steps of the protocols, without revealing extra information to the sender. This yields a tighter security bound against a malicious receiver. For practical scenarios with a fixed security target, this approach reduces the amount of required quantum communication by one to two orders of magnitude, depending on the specific parameters. Furthermore, the benefits of our approach become particularly pronounced at higher qubit error rates, and our proposal even extends the maximum tolerable error rate of the quantum channel from approximately 3.5% to about 9%. The ZKP, however, introduces a substantial computational overhead, estimated to significantly exceed the acquisition time of the protocol, which is usually the primary bottleneck. To address this limitation, we also introduce a variant that serves as a tunable trade-off between the protocol with and without our modification. This enables precise adjustment of the computational overhead while still retaining significant, albeit moderately reduced, efficiency gains.

Quantum Physics.title: The role of composition rules in an axiomatic derivation of quantum mechanics
Quantum Physics.summary: Local discriminability and purification are two key axioms in an information-theoretic axiomatization of quantum mechanics as proposed by G. M. D'Ariano et al. (Quantum Theory from First Principles, 2017). Both of them refer to compound systems, the theory of which is rather directly assumed to be given by the tensor product structure. This structure, though well understood, should, however, be based on a more careful study of formal composition rules describing how local effects can be embedded into the compound effect space and how to reduce joint states onto subsystems. In that we follow the earlier work of T. Matolcsi, (Acta Sci. Math., 1975), and D. Aerts and I. Daubechies, (Helvetica Physica Acta, 1978), as summarized, e.g., in The Logic of Quantum Mechanics, 1981, by E. Beltrametti and G. Cassinelli. We also establish axioms of local discrimination stating that compound states can be told apart by local measurements the notion of which we also formally define. The purification axioms first introduced as axioms of quantum mechanics by D'Ariano et al. are also rewritten in a weaker form which we believe could be fruitful for future axiomatizations. These reformulations bring us closer to proper tensor product structures for joint state and effect spaces, so that the embedding map for states factors through the projective tensor product of the local state spaces and the embedding map for effects factors through the injective tensor product of the local effect spaces. We also discuss the case of multipartite composition axioms and associativity properties required in these settings.

Quantum Physics.title: Augmented Imaginary-Time Evolution of Neural Quantum States with Implicit Time Steps
Quantum Physics.summary: Finding the ground states of quantum many-body systems remains a central challenge in physics and quantum chemistry. Imaginary-time evolution (ITE) offers a natural, widely used route, but its convergence is typically asymptotic. Variational approaches restrict this evolution to parameterized manifolds, with neural quantum states (NQS) providing flexible representations commonly optimized via stochastic reconfiguration (SR). Their performance depends on the geometry of the variational manifold, the convergence properties of ITE, and the stability of finite-step explicit (forward) integrators. By exploiting local geometric information of the energy landscape, the recently introduced augmented imaginary-time evolution (AITE) can, in principle, reach the ground state in finite imaginary time. To exploit the accelerated convergence of AITE in NQS optimization, we first combine an implicit Euler step with Galerkin projection to derive an implicit SR scheme that permits large, stable steps and substantially outperforms conventional methods. We use it to formulate an implicit version of AITE and show that its acceleration persists under variational projection and finite-step integration with asymptotically quadratic convergence of the energy error. With finite sampling, implicit schemes yield consistent gains, and implicit AITE becomes increasingly advantageous.

Quantum Physics.title: Finite-time quantum equilibration from local correlations
Quantum Physics.summary: We study equilibration of a fixed subsystem coupled to an initially maximally mixed bath. We show that the worst-input mean-square error, maximised over observation windows of length $T$, is bounded from above and below by the mean square of a complete local autocorrelation on $[0,T]$. The constants depend only on the subsystem dimension, and no assumption on degeneracies of energies or energy gaps is required. Subtracting the stationary part of the correlation gives equilibration to the temporal state; retaining it gives thermalisation to the maximally mixed state. We then obtain explicit bounds for two static Hamiltonian families. A periodic spin-clock model thermalises on $O(n\log n)$ windows at fixed accuracy despite an exponentially small positive energy. A randomly dressed commuting model, with interaction range $O(\log N)$, has expected error $O(N^{-b}+T^{-1})$ while retaining an extensive family of conserved observables. We explain how the locally weighted spectrum determines these bounds.
Quantum Physics.comment: comments welcome; 9 pages main plus 16 supplementary, 2 figures, v2: substantially rewritten version with new results, v3: updated version with clearer presentation, v4: some minor clarification and more comprehensive supplementary note

Quantum Physics.title: Hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits for stabilizer codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum error correction is the art of protecting fragile quantum information through suitable encoding and active interventions. However, it is notoriously difficult to manipulate encoded quantum data without causing uncorrectable errors. Here, we introduce a mathematical framework for constructing hardware-tailored circuits that implement any desired Clifford unitary on the logical level of any given stabilizer code. We formulate this task as a discrete optimization problem that minimizes the number of CZ gates while naturally incorporating a parameterization of all Clifford stabilizers. Despite the intrinsic difficulty of the circuit compilation problem, our methods scale to at least $16$ physical qubits. Because our circuits require very few CZ gates, they provide excellent starting points for constructing fault-tolerant implementations using flag gadgets. Using a brute-force search, we develop several such flag gadgets, including weakly fault-tolerant logical Hadamard circuits for the $[[8,3,2]]$ code that require an unprecedentedly small number of physical two-qubit gates. Our work introduces both the mathematics and software for compiling hardware-tailored logical Clifford circuits. From a broader perspective, we turn away from the standard generator decomposition and instead focus on the holistic compilation of entire logical circuits, leading to significant savings in practice.

Quantum Physics.title: Magnetometry and slow light in PT-symmetric cavity optomechanics
Quantum Physics.summary: The generation of optical higher-order sidebands, which produces new frequencies with regular spectral separation, holds significant promise for applications in optical communication and quantum metrology. We investigate second-order sideband generation and tunable slow-fast light effects in a parity-time (PT)-symmetric cavity optomechanics and propose an enhanced magnetometer scheme. We demonstrate that the PT-symmetric structure, an external magnetic field, and the photon tunneling strength provide powerful and flexible control over both the second-order sideband efficiency, as well as the broadening and switching of slow-fast light propagation. Operating in the PT-symmetry-protected phases, our magnetometer based on the second-order sideband achieves a theoretical sensitivity at the picotesla level, surpassing the performance of previous optomechanical approaches. Our results offer new strategies for magnetic field sensing and optical transmission control, paving the way toward applications in quantum sensing and optical information storage.

Quantum Physics.title: Entanglement between distant spins in a polarized magnet forms a $d$-wave clover
Quantum Physics.summary: Spin-orbit coupling makes a polarized magnet a source of virtual spin-flip pairs. These pairs entangle distant spins: the symmetry of the coupling fixes the angular pattern, and the flips they leave behind end it at a distance of order the inverse spin-orbit angle. For a spin-1/2 square-lattice ferromagnet we prove, at leading order, a d-wave inverse-square law, 1.376 times the spin-wave amplitude, a clover-shaped entangled region, exact without the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya term, and that each spin's entanglement is entirely pairwise. Four qubits can test the d-wave signs at present error rates.
Quantum Physics.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, including End Matter; Supplemental Material (99 pages, 2 figures) appended. Code and data in the ancillary files

Quantum Physics.title: Transfer tensor description of driven inhomogeneous quantum systems
Quantum Physics.summary: The transfer tensor method (TTM) extrapolates open quantum system dynamics from short-time trajectories by encoding memory effects in a discrete hierarchy of transfer tensors. Standard TTM relies on time-translational invariance (TTI) of the dynamical maps, which is broken by time-dependent driving or coherent control. We generalize TTM to time-inhomogeneous and periodically driven systems with a two-time transfer tensor hierarchy $\mathcal{T}(n,k)$. For driving with period $t_0$, sub-stroboscopic sampling ($Δt = t_0/N_c$) restores a block TTI, $\mathcal{T}(n+mN_c, k+mN_c) = \mathcal{T}(n,k)$, so that only $N_c$ starting-time branches must be learned. Averaging over the driving phase (or start time), termed temporal homogenization, restores single-index TTI at the price of phase-induced memory that combines non-additively with that of static disorder. We study two systems. (i) In an inhomogeneously broadened two-level ensemble driven beyond the rotating-wave approximation (RWA), the phase-induced memory scales with the square of the Rabi coupling and the disorder-induced memory with the square of the inhomogeneous width. The phase-induced memory is frame dependent: in the drive's rotating frame it arises solely from counter-rotating terms and vanishes under the RWA, whereas in the lab frame it largely survives the RWA. (ii) In a driven tight-binding chain at the Dunlap--Kenkre condition, the clean chain is stroboscopically frozen, whereas sub-stroboscopic tensors show that dynamical localization is enforced by delayed, period-commensurate refocusing in the memory kernel, in contrast to the immediate backflow of Anderson localization. A generalized outgoing pseudoflux tracks the non-monotonic dependence of the spreading on disorder: moderate disorder breaks the refocusing and lets the particle spread over a larger but finite region, whereas strong disorder confines it.

Quantum Physics.title: Qubit-qubit-qutrit quantum correlations in $H \to f \bar f V$
Quantum Physics.summary: We perform an extensive analysis of the quantum correlations carried by the qubit--qubit--qutrit pure state arising in the decay of a massive scalar into a fermion--antifermion pair and a massive gauge boson, $H \to f \bar f V$, specialising to the Higgs boson decay $h \to τ^- τ^+ Z$. Working with the exact tree-level spin state and its systematic expansion around the massless-fermion limit, we obtain analytic control over the entire phase space: the bipartite entanglement measures, the genuine $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entanglement structure (the Miyake classification), as well as the Bell-inequality violations and the non-stabiliserness (magic) are all mapped and reproduced by compact formulas. The bipartite measures exhibit a monogamy-like trade-off between the fermion pair and the fermion--boson pairs. The state is genuinely $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ entangled over almost the entire phase space, most strongly in the collinear regions. We derive, for the first time, semi-analytical expressions for the tight $4 \times 4 \times 2$ Bell inequalities of the $2 \otimes 2 \otimes 3$ system, generalising the optimisation previously available only for three qubits, and find that the local-hidden-variable bound is violated over the entire phase space, reaching within a few per cent of the quantum bound at the upper endpoint of the di-tau mass spectrum. We further extend the stabiliser Rényi entropy and the non-local magic to systems with unequal local dimensions, and show that the near-endpoint state carries almost exactly one bit of non-local magic, which peaks at $\log_2 \frac{27}{7} \simeq 1.95$ in the collinear regions. The differential decay rate concentrates precisely in the most nonclassical region of the phase space.
Quantum Physics.comment: 53 pages, 14 figures, version published in Physical Review D

Quantum Physics.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
Quantum Physics.summary: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace, so that states are not described by density matrices in the algebra, and they have no pure normal states, such that the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

Quantum Physics.title: Inner sublattice competition: a minimal mechanism for reentrant localizations in Aubry-André lattice
Quantum Physics.summary: We construct a double mosaic Aubry-André (DMAA) model with two independent quasiperiodic potentials assigned to corresponding even and odd sublattices of the AA lattice, and show that the competition between them gives rise to multiple localization-delocalization transitions under single-parameter tuning. Such reentrant localizations are verified by comprehensive numerical characterizations including the inverse participation ratio, normalized participation ratio, fractal dimension, and real-space wavefunction distributions. Simulations based on a continuous polariton model yield consistent results, confirming the experimental feasibility of the predicted phenomena. This inner sublattice competition mechanism works in a minimal way for reentrant localizations without additional ingredients or dynamical modifications such as long-range hopping, mixed quasiperiodic and random disorder, or non-Hermitian gain and loss, offering a concise route to engineer reentrant localization based on the canonical AA lattice family.

Quantum Physics.title: Low-Degree Torus Approximations of the AND Function and $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ Circuits
Quantum Physics.summary: Torus polynomials, real polynomials evaluated modulo one, were proposed by Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao as a route to $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ lower bounds. We prove degree upper bounds for torus polynomials approximating a function on every input. First, for every $ε\in(0,1/4)$, $\mathsf{AND}_n/2$ has an $ε$-approximating torus polynomial of degree $O(\log(n/ε))$, improving the previous $O(\log^2(n/ε))$. This is optimal up to constant factors for inverse-polynomial error, by a lower bound of Krishan and Vishwanathan, and refutes two superlogarithmic-degree conjectures of Krishan and Sarma. Second, for every Boolean function $g$ computed by a depth-$d$, size-$s$ $\mathsf{AC}^0[m]$ circuit, $g/2$ has an $ε$-approximating torus polynomial of degree at most $C_m^d(\log s)^{\max\{1,μ-1\}d}\log(1/ε)$, where $μ$ is the number of distinct prime factors of $m$ and $C_m$ depends only on $m$. This improves the bound $(\log s)^{O_m(d^2)}(\log(1/ε))^{O_m(d)}$ of Bhrushundi, Hosseini, Lovett, and Rao, making the exponent of $\log s$ linear in the depth and the dependence on $\log(1/ε)$ linear. Both proofs sample terms of a Fourier expansion and approximate them by low-degree torus polynomials. A torus approximation of degree $D$ can be written as a linear combination of at most $(n+1)^D$ parities, called a periodic Fourier representation, which is known to give a non-adaptive measurement-based quantum computation with linear side-processing using one qubit per parity. Hence every $\mathsf{ACC}^0$ function can be computed with quasipolynomially many qubits and inverse-polynomial error probability on every input. Conversely, we prove that a periodic Fourier representation with $r$ parities and error probability $ε$ gives a torus approximation of degree $O(\log(r/ε))$, so the two notions are equivalent.

Quantum Physics.title: Toward light-controlled transverse Wigner ordering in attosecond electron beams
Quantum Physics.summary: Kinetic fluctuations and space-charge expansion hinder Wigner ordering in free-electron beams. Here we propose a laser-driven route toward transient, substrate-free Wigner ordering that combines photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) attosecond bunching, synchronized magnetic focusing, and spatial preconditioning. Classical relaxation and zero-temperature fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo trap benchmarks show that sixfold order survives quantum fluctuations from 1 T to sub-Tesla fields, defining ultrafast preparation targets.
Quantum Physics.comment: 25 pages (13 pages main text including 3 figures, plus 12 pages Supplemental Material)

Quantum Physics.title: Unified entropy entanglement
Quantum Physics.summary: The unified entropy as a generalization of the von Neumann entropy exhibits distinct diversity which contains the Tsallis entropy, the Rényi entropy, the von Neumann entropy as special cases. The unified-($r,t$) entropy entanglement with $0<r<1$ and $0< t\leq 1$ was shown to be an entanglement monotone in literature. In this paper, we explore unified-($q,s$) entropy entanglement with $q>1$ and $qs\geq1$ and show that it is also an entanglement monotone and that both of them are monogamous. Going further, we present a global multipartite entanglement measure (GlMEM) based on the unified entropy and it has two subclasses which are classified by the parameters $(q,s)$ and $(r,t)$. Consequently, from the view of the complete multipartite entanglement measure theory, we show that one of them is a complete multipartite entanglement monotone and is not only completely monogamous but also tightly completely monogamous, but the other one is even not complete. We also explore the genuine entanglement measures induced by the unified entropy and the relations with the bipartite entanglement and the global entanglement are discussed, respectively.
Quantum Physics.comment: 13 pages, 2 figures. Some results with gaps in the previous version are removed

Quantum Physics.title: Witnessing Magic (and other Quantum Resources)
Quantum Physics.summary: Motivated by measurements of quantum magic, we study the sampling cost of resource robustness ---a quantifier for a broad class of quantum resources--- by bounding the variance of optimal robustness witnesses. We first lower bound the samples required to estimate a state's resource robustness using Cramér-Rao bounds. We find that the number of measurements scales at least quadratically in the robustness for highly mixed states, and at least linearly in the generalized robustness for broad families of pure states, making it difficult to measure either robustness to low absolute error when the states are highly resourceful. We then derive two complementary bounds in terms of the geometry of witnesses, one of which is tight for a class of resource theories including coherence and bipartite entanglement. An additional hurdle occurs for tracking the onset of resource robustness along state-space trajectories: the integrated witness variance along a path is at least the squared resource gain over Fisher length, indicating that a state evolution with exponential resource gain necessarily goes through states for which the robustness cannot be measured efficiently. This hurdle does not occur when estimating robustness to fixed relative, rather than absolute, error. These results suggest that the ideal witness-based resource estimation task, for general resource theories, is the estimation of generalized robustness to low relative error on highly resourceful pure states.
Quantum Physics.comment: 10+4 pages; 1 figure; comments welcome, V2: additional references added

Quantum Physics.title: Validity and maximum violation of the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound for linear stabilizer codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Entanglement-assisted quantum codes protect quantum information with entangled pairs shared in advance, and the entanglement-assisted quantum Singleton bound of Brun, Devetak and Hsieh is the standard estimate of how many pairs they consume. Codes that violate it at large distance are known. For linear entanglement-assisted stabilizer codes, which include all qubit stabilizer codes of this kind, we determine when the bound holds and how far it can fail. The answer depends on how many qudits, together with the receiver's halves of the pairs, recover the logical qudits. If this number is less than twice the number of logical qudits, the bound holds, also for degenerate codes. If it is exactly twice that, the bound overstates the number of pairs by at most the length of the longest classical maximum distance separable (MDS) code of that dimension, minus the dimension. Codes carrying values and derivatives of polynomials on the projective line attain this maximum whenever the field size is at least that dimension and the MDS conjecture is known for it, which includes every prime and, by a recently announced result, every even field size. If the number is more than twice the number of logical qudits, the violation is bounded in terms of the lengths of classical codes of a given Singleton defect, and the bound is attained for one logical qudit. Apart from cited MDS lengths, the proofs are formalized in the Lean proof assistant.

Quantum Physics.title: Universal state merging for almost i.i.d. states
Quantum Physics.summary: In quantum state merging, Alice aims to transfer her share of a bipartite state to Bob while preserving the joint state with a purifying reference. For i.i.d. copies of $ρ_{AB}$, the optimal asymptotic net entanglement cost is $S(A|B)_ρ$ ebits per pair. We show that this cost is robust under deviations from exact i.i.d. structure. For every $R>S(A|B)_ρ$, a single sequence of one-way LOCC protocols, depending only on $ρ_{AB}$ and $R$, merges every weakly almost i.i.d. source along $ρ_{AB}$ with vanishing error. The net entanglement cost is at most $nR$ ebits for all sufficiently large blocklengths $n$. This guarantee also covers the Wasserstein and Mazzola--Sutter--Renner subclasses. Each class contains the exact i.i.d. source, so $S(A|B)_ρ$ is optimal for universal merging within each class. More generally, the same protocols achieve vanishing error whenever the two-pair marginal of the permutation-averaged source converges in trace norm to $ρ_{AB}^{\otimes 2}$.

Quantum Physics.title: Complex quasiprobabilities as measurable temporal interference
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum dynamics can encode interference information that conventional correlation functions leave unresolved. Here we show that the imaginary component of the extended Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability reveals dynamical distinctions absent from out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) formed from two repeated Hermitian observables at infinite temperature. We interpret its real and imaginary components as complementary quadratures of interference between many-body echo amplitudes. We prove that the imaginary component vanishes for every unitary evolution if either projective measurement has two outcomes, whereas nonreal values arise for generic unitary dynamics when it has at least three (e.g., spin-1 systems). We develop an algorithm to reconstruct the full quasiprobability from covariances of local probe signals over repeated preparations of randomised initial states, using forward evolution and probe readout only. In a spin-1 chain, a nonzero imaginary signal distinguishes a real Hamiltonian $H$ from $-H$ despite identical corresponding OTOCs, and identifies opposite sides of a pair-conversion resonance at short times while dipolar and quadrupolar OTOCs remain nearly unchanged. These results show how temporal interference resolves dynamical ambiguities and provides additional constraints for Hamiltonian inference.

Quantum Physics.title: Quasi-particle sector hybridization and the onset of chaos in spin ladders
Quantum Physics.summary: How quasiparticle numbers influence the emergence of quantum chaos is a fundamental question in interacting many-body systems. We investigate this interplay in a spin-$1/2$ XXZ ladder, where the strong-rung regime supports an approximate organization of many-body eigenstates into quasi-particle(triplon) number sectors. Using spectral statistics, triplon-based observables, and von Neumann entanglement entropy, we characterize the microscopic hybridization of triplon-number sectors as the leg coupling increases. We find that the crossover toward Gaussian orthogonal ensemble statistics shifts to weaker couplings with increasing system size, whereas the characteristic crossover scale associated with triplon-sector hybridization exhibits a much weaker size dependence. Furthermore, eigenstate-to-eigenstate fluctuations exhibit scaling consistent with the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis even while remnants of the strong-rung structure persist, suggesting that spectral chaos does not necessarily require complete sector hybridization.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization
Quantum Physics.summary: We introduce a quantum-echo Markov process for combinatorial optimization. Quantum dynamics based on quantum annealing (QA) or the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is used to engineer the transition kernel. Increasing the annealing time in QA or the number of layers in QAOA enables transitions to explore distant configurations while suppressing large energy changes. The Hamming-space delocalization originates from operator spreading, whereas the energy-space localization arises from a dynamically generated correlation. For optimization, we propose quantum-echo local optimization. For the ferromagnetic Ising chain, increasing the annealing time or circuit depth yields a nearly quadratic improvement in the dependence of the mean first-passage time on the inverse optimality gap compared with random single-spin flips. For the random Ising model, increasing these parameters initially improves optimization performance, whereas further increases degrade performance in QA and lead to saturation in QAOA. Quantum-echo greedy descent substantially improves the performance, highlighting the complementary roles of quantum dynamics in exploration and greedy descent in exploitation. These results establish quantum-echo dynamics as a framework for engineering structured transition kernels and provide a route to using finite-resource quantum many-body dynamics as a computational primitive for iterative optimization.

Quantum Physics.title: Ancilla-assisted multi-qubit quantum gates with polar molecules
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum error correction enables reliable quantum computation using imperfect physical gates, but its implementation often requires multi-qubit controlled-unitary gates $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ acting on $\mathbb{N} \ge 3$ qubits. Their direct realization is challenging, while decomposing them into standard one-qubit and two-qubit gates can increase circuit depth and error rates. Here, we present an ancilla-assisted scheme to directly implement $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(U)$ in optically trapped ultracold polar molecules. By appropriately selecting qubit states for the ancilla and data qubits, dark states can appear during two smooth $π$ pulses. This can generate a controlled-phase gate with the phase set by the relative phase between the pulses; notably, a single $2π$ pulse yields a $\text{C}_{\mathbb{N}}(Z)$ gate. Numerical analysis for a simple molecular spatial configuration demonstrates that the gate infidelity is dominated by qubit decoherence, yielding a $\text{C}_2(Z)$ fidelity of $0.996$ estimated with $T_2^\ast=1.5$~s and a gate duration of $T \approx 4\text{~ms}$. Furthermore, diabatic errors remain low, on the order of $10^{-4}$ for $\mathbb{N}=2,3$ and $10^{-3}$ for $\mathbb{N}=4$, even with dipole-dipole interaction strengths as low as $25\hbar/T$.

Quantum Physics.title: Eliminating Incompatibility in Quantum Multiparameter Estimation with Antiparallel Probes
Quantum Physics.summary: The simultaneous estimation of multiple parameters is fundamentally constrained by complementarity and measurement incompatibility, which limits the sensitivity of quantum measurement devices by preventing the symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) from being saturated. We show that antiparallel probe configurations can overcome this limitation when the dynamics of the parameter encoding preserve the said configurations. We characterise the quantum channels that satisfy this requirement and establish conditions under which such configurations exist and can saturate the SLD-CRB without compromising the quantum Fisher information, leading to a metrological advantage. For qubit probes, we prove that this advantage is present if and only if the encoding channel is unital. We extend this analysis to the two probe, finite dimensional qudit case by considering derivative reversal and transpose map based probe states, as well as more general multiprobe configurations. For each of these cases, we identify conditions under which an advantage exists. Our results establish connections between channel symmetries, probe configurations and the attainability of multiparameter precision limits.

Quantum Physics.title: Beyond Classical Minimax Rates: Quantum Sampling in Gradient-Based Simulation Optimization
Quantum Physics.summary: We study gradient-based search for a class of convex simulation optimization problems with gradients estimated from noisy outputs. With independent outputs, the optimal classical convergence rate for the expected objective gap is of order $O(N^{-2/3})$, where $N$ is the query budget. We apply quantum mean estimation to paired finite differences and progressively increase their estimation accuracy as the perturbations shrink, improving the convergence rate to $O(N^{-4/3})$. Furthermore, we show that coupling nearby evaluations improves the classical and quantum convergence rates to $O(N^{-2/(3-κ)})$ and $O(N^{-4/(3-κ)})$, respectively, where $κ\in[0,1]$ describes the variance reduction in paired outputs. Thus, quantum estimation halves the accuracy exponent in query complexity across coupling orders. Moreover, we establish matching lower bounds and show that these accuracy exponents are minimax optimal for fixed decision dimension, even when query locations and batch sizes are adaptive. Reconstruction from feasible differences retains the exponents when every simulation query must be feasible and accommodates boundary optima.

Quantum Physics.title: QuOptLab: Advancing Quantum Optics Experiments with an AI Agent
Quantum Physics.summary: Recent advances in AI-assisted theoretical research suggest that AI agents can contribute to research-level problems. Whether they can also advance experimental research by conducting experiments, analyzing the results, and proposing better experimental designs remains an open question. To address this question, we build a simulated quantum optics laboratory and integrate it with an AI agent in QuOptLab. The laboratory includes optical instruments, a robotic arm, and cameras, enabling the agent to carry out and iteratively refine experiments. We consider two complementary tasks: thin-film thickness measurement in free-space optics and edge-coupler design in integrated photonics. In the thin-film thickness measurement task, the agent repeatedly analyzes measurement results and revises its measurement method, including calibration and data analysis, reducing thickness-estimation error from 7.13 to 0.066~nm$^2$ over six epochs in a classical-interference run. For edge-coupler design, the agent iteratively proposes structural modifications, evaluates the resulting coupling performance, and uses the feedback to guide subsequent revisions, increasing simulated coupling efficiency from 85.81% to 91.98%.

Quantum Physics.title: Anomalous Hardening of a Fluctuation-Induced Gap
Quantum Physics.summary: In a mean-field picture, a gap opened by quantum fluctuations grows with them. This can fail if the fluctuating mode is critical and its displacement compensates its coupling to the degenerate states. A single parameter sets the gap response: above a universal threshold, the gap hardens as the critical fluctuations weaken. Whenever the parameter is nonzero, overcompensation beyond the critical point drives a secondary phase transition. In a quantum Rabi ring with synthetic flux, exact diagonalization shows the gap of a photonic Landau level rising by 15% as the critical variance falls by 25%.

Quantum Physics.title: Schur saturation and the Clifford ceiling in qudit CSS codes
Quantum Physics.summary: Orthogonality-type conditions (triorthogonality in the qubit setting and its prime-dimensional analogues), are the primary algebraic screening criterion for transversal non-Clifford gate constructions in CSS codes. In every known positive construction the certificate is accompanied by a non-Clifford logical gate, leaving open whether a CSS family can satisfy these conditions to arbitrarily high order while admitting no such gate. We answer this question for the class of symmetric spectral CSS codes $Q(A)=CSS(C(A),C(A))$ built from character evaluation on a finite abelian group $G$ with $\exp(G)\mid p-1$, $p\geq 5$ prime. The mechanism is the identity \[C(A)^\perp * C(A)^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^G,\] which we call Schur saturation of the dual code. It follows from the CSS self-orthogonality condition $A\cap(-A)=\varnothing$ and annihilates every local polynomial phase of degree $\geq 3$. The complete gate-group classification $S^{CSS}_{\leq p-1}(A)=C(A)^\perp \oplus C(Stab(A))$ shows that every strictly CSS-preserving local-diagonal transversal gate lies at level $\leq 2$ of the Clifford hierarchy, a structural bound we call the Clifford ceiling. The criterion extends to arbitrary CSS pairs satisfying $C_Z^\perp * C_Z^\perp=\mathbb{F}_p^n$; the LDPC instance $[[58,16,3]]_5$ is verified computationally. The false-positive character of the orthogonality certificates is sharpest in the Boolean toric family: these codes satisfy $\ell$-orthogonality for $\ell\leq p-2$, yet the non-Clifford sector collapses to zero. The flagship instance $[[64,56,3]]_5$ encodes $56$ logical ququints at rate $R=0.875$ with distance-$3$ protection, passes every orthogonality screening test, and yet admits no local-diagonal non-Clifford gate of any degree. The unique non-Pauli survivor is the uniform quadratic drive $Q_u$, fault-tolerant, logically nontrivial, and Clifford at level $2$, carrying no magic-state resource.

Quantum Physics.title: Coherence Transfer in Quantum Networks
Quantum Physics.summary: Detecting coherence transfer in complex quantum networks is challenging under uncharacterized experimental conditions and with limited access to the system. Here, we use the coexistence of static and dynamic coherence to derive a nonlinear criterion for coherence transfer. The criterion applies even when the verification capabilities of checkpoint nodes are uncharacterized. It requires only minimal one-network output analysis, up to the number of output state dimensions. Each output requires only two-setting measurements of state populations, regardless of the network size. The criterion is general for both spatial and temporal networks, including those with multiple coherence sources, and applies to quantum transport in solid-state nanostructures. Experimentally, using entanglement swapping, we transfer polarization-entangled pairs in four- and six-photon entanglement networks. The criterion provides experimental evidence of coherence transfer in multiphoton entanglement networks. Our findings provide a practical tool for investigating the presence, role, or function of coherence transfer in quantum networks.

Quantum Physics.title: Open Quantum Time Crystals without External Thermodynamic Resources: Go and No-Go Theorems
Quantum Physics.summary: Time crystals are phases of matter that spontaneously break time-translation symmetry. They have been ruled out in the ground and Gibbs states of isolated systems with only short-range interactions, yet they have been proposed and observed experimentally in nonequilibrium settings such as Floquet and open systems. However, existing proposals for time crystals in open quantum systems require an external supply of thermodynamic resources, such as work or energetic coherence. Whether coupling to an environment, without any such resource supply, can activate a time crystal absent in the isolated system remains open. We answer this question systematically through a Go theorem and a no-go theorem. The Go theorem answers it affirmatively: we construct an explicit model in which coupling a system to a zero-temperature Gibbs environment via a time-independent, energy-conserving interaction, with only short-range Hamiltonians, activates a time crystal in a stationary state that shows none in isolation. This coupling reproduces a Lindblad master equation satisfying three conditions---time-independent Hamiltonian and jump operators, time-translation covariance, and detailed balance---that hold in standard derivations unless thermodynamic resources are supplied externally. The no-go theorem shows that, for every Lindblad master equation satisfying these conditions and every stationary state, dissipation can never contribute to activation; only an environment-induced Hamiltonian term can. Indeed, the periodic two-time correlation function of any such time crystal coincides with that of the isolated system with the open-system Hamiltonian, the sum of the bare isolated Hamiltonian and the environment-induced Hamiltonian, in the thermodynamic limit. These results reveal both the possibility and the origin of time crystals in open systems without external resource supply.

Quantum Physics.title: Hybrid correlation generation with finite shared randomness
Quantum Physics.summary: Finite shared randomness can reduce the use of a prescribed two-qubit source in a hybrid model. Each party has two fixed binary projective measurements, and the protocol reproduces the resulting joint outcome distributions exactly. The parties choose their classical or quantum interfaces independently, without using the shared label, and keep their classical response functions fixed across branches. Eight labels suffice to preserve all feasible pairs of interface choice probabilities, and this bound is tight. The known classical four-label bound yields minimum-cost saturation. With an unrestricted label budget, the minimum source cost is zero if the target can be reproduced by a purely classical protocol, and one otherwise. For Werner states with identical orthogonal measurement pairs, the exact minimum source cost is obtained for every label budget. The three-label cost jumps at visibility $\frac{2}{3}$. Four labels give zero cost at every visibility. In a family of separable states, the two-label cost varies nonmonotonically with local bias while the full correlation tensor remains fixed. The distributed sampling analysis gives the minimum source cost at each label budget and the minimum worst-case total variation error for classical protocols with at most two shared labels.

Quantum Physics.title: ffsim: faster simulation of fermionic quantum circuits
Quantum Physics.summary: We present ffsim, an open-source software library for fast simulation of fermionic quantum circuits. ffsim exploits conservation of particle number and the z component of spin, symmetries present in a wide range of fermionic systems, to dramatically reduce memory usage and simulation time compared to general-purpose quantum circuit simulators. Compared to FQE, a library with similar functionality, ffsim differs in software design and is faster on a representative set of simulation benchmarks. Beyond state vector evolution by basic fermionic gates, ffsim offers a number of additional features including variational ansatzes, Hamiltonian time evolution via Trotter-Suzuki product formulas, efficient sampling of Slater determinants, seamless integration with Qiskit and PySCF, and comprehensive documentation. We demonstrate ffsim's capabilities on scientific applications, including a 64-qubit Hubbard model with 8 electrons. ffsim's source code and documentation are available via https://github.com/Qiskit/ffsim.

Quantum Physics.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems.
