We argue that the holographic duals are pseudo-Hermitian and $PT$-symmetric theories. Wormhole solutions also admit an interpretation as the low-energy theory of two stacks of branes and anti-branes after tachyon condensation. The wormhole is then dual to an entangled state of two copies of the theory that lives on a stack of branes. We present some evidence by computing the mutual information between the theories at each boundary and by identifying the Goldstone bosons associated with the breaking of the two copies of Poincaré symmetry to their diagonal subgroup.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 29 pages + appendices and references, 2 figures, calculation of the spectrum corrected, one of the wormhole solutions found to be unstable, the other wormhole solutions remain stable

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Baker-Akhiezer functions for Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
The Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system is a counterpart of the trigonometric Ruijsenaars integrable system (associated with the root system $A_n$) for the root system $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$. It depends on the standard Macdonald parameters $q$ and $t$ as well as the Koornwinder (Askey-Wilson) parameters $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$. Different specializations of the parameters connect it to the other classical root systems from the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family.
  The eigenfunctions of the Koornwinder-van Diejen integrable system are the symmetric Koornwinder polynomials; for certain values of the parameters $t$, $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ they coincide with the sum over the Weyl group of the Baker-Akhiezer functions introduced by O.A.\,Chalykh for the classical root system $BC_n$. The main idea behind this paper is to elucidate Chalykh's formalism and apply it to other affine root systems. We define Baker-Akhiezer functions for all root systems in the $(C_n^\vee, C_n)$ family. We also present some explicit expressions for Baker-Akhiezer functions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Attractors and initial-condition sensitivity in Horndeski cosmologies
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study whether nearby homogeneous cosmological histories approach or move away from the Genesis and contracting solutions. We also determine how an uncertainty in the scalar velocity at a later stage affects the inferred initial velocity. In the Genesis models, including the gravitational dynamics can substantially change this relation. We find that convergence of homogeneous solutions can occur even around backgrounds with unstable perturbations, and therefore attraction of the background is not sufficient to establish that a cosmological solution is physically viable. In the contracting model, one power-law solution attracts nearby trajectories, whereas another repels them. The strength of these effects depends on how the cosmological state is parametrized. Their evolution through the subsequent bounce is not considered here.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 51 pages, 3 figures. Changes in v2: additional sentences and references have been added to the Introduction; new material has been added to Secs. 4.1, 4.2, 4.3; the Acknowledgments have been revised. The conclusions remain unchanged. To be submitted to Physical Review D

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Krylov dynamics of deformed oscillator chains: localization, ballistic spreading, and indeterminacy
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Krylov and spread complexity map quantum dynamics onto a quantum walk on a half-line whose hopping amplitudes are the Lanczos coefficients, so that Krylov dynamics is the theory of orthogonal polynomials and Jacobi operators. We use this correspondence to study Krylov chains generated by the two-parameter $(p,q)$-deformed oscillator, which interpolates between the Heisenberg--Weyl chain, the $q$-oscillator chain of double-scaled SYK, and chains with exponentially growing Lanczos coefficients. For the deformed displacement chain the spread complexity is the mean excitation number, its rate is the deformed momentum quadrature, and its acceleration is $\ddot C_K=2ω^2\langle[a,a^\dagger]\rangle$, so the deformed commutator acts as a force along the Krylov chain and the mean deformation controls early-time growth. The deformation parameters separate four regimes. For $\max(p,q)<1$ the complexity stays bounded, a localization produced by the algebra alone. For $p=1$, $q<1$ it grows ballistically, with an exact asymptotic velocity given by a theta-type series. At $p=q=1$ it grows as $t^2$. For $\max(p,q)>1$ the Jacobi operator is not essentially self-adjoint, the moment problem is indeterminate, and the Lanczos coefficients no longer determine the dynamics. Even and odd truncations converge to two different evolutions, the two reflection-symmetric N-extremal solutions of the moment problem, the odd one carrying a zero-energy atom of closed-form weight; the self-adjoint extensions yield a family of complexity curves that coincide at early times and separate once the Krylov wavefront reaches infinity. Krylov complexity in this regime is thus defined only once a boundary condition at infinite Krylov index is specified. The orthogonal-polynomial procedure and its checks on exactly solvable chains are given in the appendices.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Wilson-loop formulation of Yang-Mills at finite mode truncation: a Level-Two structural bypass of the Gribov ambiguity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The unfixed real-time Henstock-Kurzweil functional integral for truncated Yang-Mills removes the choice of a gauge surface, but gauge orbits remain objects of the formulation: that is a Level-One bypass of the Gribov ambiguity. This paper carries out a Level-Two bypass at finite mode truncation: the Wilson loops W(C) are taken as the fundamental variables, so that the configuration space is a space of loop data and no gauge field, gauge orbit, gauge-fixing condition or Faddeev-Popov determinant occurs anywhere in the formulation. Nine statements are proved and machine checked in Lean 4 without sorry, without admit and without new axioms: the loop algebra is commutative, conjugation-closed and gauge invariant, with bounded generators and the SU(2) Mandelstam identity; the truncated Yang-Mills action is an affine polynomial in the plaquette Wilson variables; loop-expressible observables are cylindrical; the oscillatory integrand is Henstock-Kurzweil integrable on every bounded loop-space box for every calibration, with the Lebesgue value; the integral is independent of gauge-fixing data and gauge copies are the same point of the loop formulation; for loop observables the Level-Two integral with respect to the push-forward measure coincides with the Level-One unfixed integral; the one-plaquette SU(2) check is proved in full, including the closed form 2J_1(beta)/beta; the SU(N) Mandelstam relations are derived in covariant trace form; and the finite-M integrals are projectively compatible, their limit existing as a linear functional, not a measure. No continuum limit, mass gap, confinement or Makeenko-Migdal equation is claimed; the Giles reconstruction theorem is cited only. The honest report records exactly where each proof stops.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A Systematic Construction of High-Corank Kac--Moody Algebras
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We form a hexagonal prism from two six-cycles and iterate a doubling construction with a fixed positive integer edge multiplicity, producing a family of indefinite Kac--Moody algebras. The prism's spectrum determines the exact corank of every algebra in the family. Along each nonvanishing parity class, the corank grows exponentially, while its ratio to the matrix size tends to zero. For the twelve-node algebra we identify the two central directions, describe the first two graded levels, and characterize the integral central charges of its unitary highest-weight modules.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Proceedings of the 36th International Colloquium on Group Theoretical Methods in Physics, Valladolid, 13 pages, 2 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Teichmüller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We study Teichmüller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $θ= 2πβ$. For all $β>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $ω_β$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $β$, the form $ω_β$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^β(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit.
  For positive integers $β=n$, $ω_β$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $θ=2πn$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichmüller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holographic Mutual Information in an Anisotropic Field Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate holographic mutual information in an anisotropic strongly coupled plasma within the framework of gauge/gravity duality. Considering both parallel and perpendicular strip configurations, we analyze the effects of temperature, anisotropy, strip lengths, and separation distance on the correlation structure between subsystems. For strips with equal lengths, we show that increasing temperature suppresses mutual information and reduces the size of the correlated region in the phase diagram. We find that the parallel configuration exhibits a monotonic behavior. However, the perpendicular configuration displays a more complex behavior resulting from the competition between the effects of energy density and pressure. Similar qualitative features are observed for strips with unequal lengths. Our results suggest that the directional dependence of the energy density and pressure plays an important role in the behavior of mutual information and may explain the nontrivial directional effects observed in the phase structure.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Inflation at strong mixing as a connection problem: effective field theory, Stokes phenomenon and the cosmological collider
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study a massive field strongly mixed with the curvature perturbation during inflation, in the regime where the latter is described at low energies by a single-field effective field theory (EFT) with a quadratic dispersion relation. What this EFT captures, and what lies beyond it, are encoded in a connection problem, which relates the solutions that define the vacuum at early times to those that describe observables at late times. We solve it with a general method that does not rely on an exact solution. An expansion in the inverse mixing, keeping both fields, yields the EFT as its leading order, with corrections under systematic control. It selects the vacuum of the EFT, fixes a phase that the EFT cannot determine on its own, and describes the heavy mode at all times. Particle production lies beyond all orders of this asymptotic expansion. We show that it arises from a Stokes phenomenon at the complex branch points of the dispersion relation and that, in a rotating basis of the two fields, it reduces to the familiar production of particles with half the heavy mass. A reflection symmetry of the equations of motion, combined with the canonical commutation relations, then determines all exponentially small effects exactly, and with them the solution of the connection problem, which combines particle production with a conversion between light and heavy quanta. Together with the expansion, these exact results give a compact analytical formula for the cosmological collider signal, whose exponential suppression, half of the usual Boltzmann one, directly reflects the halved mass of the produced particles. The expansion only requires a separation of scales and the adiabaticity of the heavy mode, while the reflection symmetry holds for many systems in de Sitter space. We therefore expect this approach to bring physical understanding and simple formulas well beyond the present case.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: What makes spacetime spin in string theory?
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Type II string theory in the absence of orientifolds requires the target spacetime $X$ to admit a spin structure. We show that this familiar requirement arises directly from the consistency of the worldsheet GSO projection. The obstruction is a mixed global anomaly between $(-1)^{\text{F}_L}$ and the target space background data, detected by the spin bordism group $Ω_3^{\mathrm{spin}}(B\mathbb{Z}_2\times X)$. We compute the relevant mixed bordism group and identify the bordism class of the GSO-projected worldsheet theory. For smooth target spaces, vanishing of the anomaly reduces to the condition that $X$ is spin, while for general orbifolds $[\hat{X}/G]$, $\hat{X}$ has to carry a $G$-equivariant spin structure. We also classify all possible theta angles in the worldsheet theory and show that they correspond to all possible continuous and discrete background fields of the target space theory visible in string perturbation theory.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 27 pages + references v2: 2 references added v3: references and clarifications added + example corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cutting corners: exciting and magical bounds from the cusp bootstrap
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: An illuminating probe of the dynamics of a line defect is the global geometry of its worldline. For a conformal line defect in a conformal field theory, sharp corners in the worldline, i.e. cusps, host dynamical degrees of freedom characterized in part by a spectrum of scaling dimensions, called cusp anomalous dimensions. We present various general bounds on cusp anomalous dimensions following from unitarity and cutting-and-gluing consistency of different defect geometries. We first establish, for cusps involving conjugate defects, that level crossings upon varying the cusp angle are forbidden between the lightest singlet cusp and any non-singlet cusp, proving that singlet cusps are the lightest. Then, we study line defects arranged in a rectangular geometry, which are subject to bootstrap constraints reminiscent of the spinless modular bootstrap. We find an analytic ``magic" functional that produces an optimal and universal lower bound on the dimension of a right angle bare cusp in terms of the universal defect Casimir energy between the corresponding defect and its conjugate in flat space.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v2 References added, typos fixed; 13 pages, 5 figures

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum integrable matrix models of spinor Bose gases in one spatial dimension
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Degenerate spinor Bose gases with repulsive density-density interaction and anti-ferromagnetic spin-spin coupling in one spatial dimension are shown to be described by a quantum integrable matrix extension of the nonlinear Schrödinger model, whose fundamental fields are described by an $m\,\times\,n$ matrix of bosonic field operators. The eigenstates of this model are constructed for arbitrarily sized matrix field operators by means of algebraic Bethe-ansatz techniques, and the corresponding Bethe equations governing the spectra of conserved quantities are derived. The approach thus generalizes previously chosen techniques to account for arbitrary spin multiplets and their spin-spin interaction. Focusing on the specific case of the $2\times2$ model, which is shown to correspond to a spin-$1$ Bose gas, a set of integral equations is derived, which describe its equilibrium thermodynamic properties. From these, the ground state phase diagram is computed both, numerically and analytically in the parameter plane spanned by the chemical potential and an external magnetic field. Furthermore, we establish a sufficient condition for interacting bosons in one dimension to obey the Pauli exclusion principle. In particular, we show that in the presence of paired bound states, no two quasiparticle rapidities can coincide, provided that the Lieb parameter satisfies $γ>4/3$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 36 pages, 3 figures. v3: matches published version; v2: Added references, expanded explanations throughout and added a new numerical analysis (App. G)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Differential Equations for Feynman Integrals from Higher Residue Pairings
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a method for constructing differential equations for Feynman integrals directly from multivariate intersection numbers, without fibration. The large-$\varepsilon$ expansion of the intersection pairing, with $\varepsilon$ the dimensional regulator, is given by Saito's higher residue pairings, which localise at the critical points of a potential and admit closed multivariate formulae. In the Lee-Pomeransky representation, applying these formulae to Feynman integrals requires analytic regulators $δ$ on the coordinate hyperplanes, and the physical limit $δ\to 0$ is not manifest. Assuming that the regulated critical points are analytic in $δ$, we show that, as $δ\to 0$, they organise into sectors labelled by sets of pinched propagators. We derive closed formulae for the leading and first subleading higher residue pairings in this limit, written entirely in terms of unregulated sector data. These suffice to reconstruct differential systems at most linear in $\varepsilon$, including canonical ones, bypassing integration-by-parts identities. We apply the method to the massless planar four-point ladder families up to four loops and obtain their canonical differential equations, which are new at four loops.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Cyclic source pairings for Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor spaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We determine the stable source information carried by the gluing-groupoid algebra of the Penrose--Sparling non-Hausdorff twistor double. Relative normal residues define supported analytic $K$-classes with specified normal orientations. For a smooth double along a closed submanifold, we compute the full geometric periodic cyclic homology as the parity sum of the compactly supported cohomologies of the ambient manifold and the doubled locus. In the physical model, $K_0\cong\Z^4$ and $HP_0\cong\C^4$, with both odd groups zero. Four explicit cocycles give integral $K$-coordinates and exhaust continuous periodic cyclic cohomology; every periodic cyclic pairing on supported source classes is therefore a linear combination of rank and degree. Finite moments recover $K$-valued normal profiles modulo integral common line twists. A first-jet criterion tests mixed-line triviality and identifies the residue with the torsion cokernel of a generically invertible second fundamental form for pullback quotients. The degree-one Euler modification and the diagonal Coulomb embedding have identical filtered $K$-profiles in every algebraic $SL_2$ representation, while their rank-two Ward connections are respectively indecomposable and split. We give the Euler connection and its transition between both root charts. An elementary holonomy realization shows that the inherited ambient and divisor transverse classes annihilate supported source classes. The relative degree pairing uses an additional choice of opposite defect orientations.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 43 pages. v2 substantially revised and extended. Source classes now use relative normal residues and supported Thom induction; the quadratic common-twist claim is corrected. Adds analytic K-theory and periodic cyclic computations (supported pairings reduce to rank and degree), filtered profiles, mixed-line criteria, an explicit Euler ASD connection and a foliation realization

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. Our approach is complementary to the conformal bootstrap.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 7 pages, 2 figures. This Letter is aimed at physicists and mathematicians who are primarily interested in the global picture. Full mathematical details will be presented in a forthcoming paper

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Horizon dynamical entropies and phase space topology
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study phase space topologies induced by infinite-dimensional norms as a means to solve the problem of 'integrability' of Hamiltonian generators corresponding to diffeomorphisms of a null hypersurface, with the specific goal in mind to compare different prescriptions for the dynamical entropy of black holes, which replaces the area in non-stationary regimes. We first show that for a scalar field, there exists a family of norms that would provide integrability for different polarizations. We then show that a single member of this family applies to the gravitational field, and it is given by the Sobolev norm already considered in the literature. The obstruction to the other candidates lies in the semi-positivity of the metric.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 34 pages, for the proceedings "Geometry of Classical and Quantum Space-Times" of Jerzy Lewandowski Memorial Conference

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entanglement island and Page curve for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the information paradox for one-sided asymptotically flat rotating Kerr black holes formed through gravitational collapse using the island prescription. Near the horizon, the dynamics of a scalar field can be described by an effective two-dimensional theory, which provides the framework for our analysis. We study how rotation affects the location of the island boundary $\partial I$, the Page time, and the scrambling time, treating non-extremal and extremal Kerr black holes separately. For non-extremal black holes, the emergence of an island prevents the unbounded growth of Hawking radiation entropy at late times and restores the unitary Page curve. We further find that the island boundary depends on the location of the cutoff surface, in contrast to the behaviour found for eternal Kerr black holes. In the extremal case, the late-time entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation approaches the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of the extremal black hole. Our results demonstrate the important role of black hole geometry in determining the behaviour of entanglement entropy and suggest that the island prescription provides a semiclassical resolution of the information paradox for one-sided rotating Kerr black holes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Romans Mass from a $\mathrm{GL}(1,\mathbb{R})$ Topological Field Theory with Boundary
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct an eleven-dimensional topological field theory with boundary whose edge modes are the dilaton and form fields of type IIA supergravity, including the Romans mass. The bulk action is the Chern--Simons functional of the superalgebra of the doubled formalism, completed by two brackets that are invisible in ten dimensions; it is unique up to normalization, contains no potentials, and the metric enters only through a boundary term. The Romans mass is the boundary value of a zero-form, like the other field strengths: it is varied, and its equation of motion is an eleven-form Gauss law with no ten-dimensional counterpart. The boundary term breaks the $GL(1,\mathbb{R})$ gauge symmetry to $O(1)$: the dilaton is the edge mode on $GL(1,\mathbb{R})/O(1)$, and $(-1)^{F_L}$, which reverses the Romans mass, becomes a gauge symmetry. The holonomies of the flat connection are monodromies of the dilaton and of $(-1)^{F_L}$, fixed classically by the D8-brane charges when the mass is nonzero, and the hypersurface dual to the $O(1)$ holonomy can end on reflection seven-branes. Since no field is self-dual, the reduction gives Romans' action off shell, while other boundary conditions of the same bulk give massless type IIA and dual formulations.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holographic Spread Complexity of a Probe Particle with General Initial Data
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the holographic spread complexity of a massive particle probing global AdS$_3$ with general initial data. By constructing an adapted Hamiltonian, we map each bulk geodesic to a boundary Krylov dynamical pair, whose dynamics are governed solely by the conserved chiral charges. We find that, for generic initial data, the original identification $\dot{C}\sim p_ρ$ fails; instead, both the complexity and its growth rate depend nonlinearly on the bulk Noether charges. We systematically analyze this nonlinear encoding via several perturbative expansions. We further investigate two refined variants: the symmetry-resolved spread complexity, which restores the bulk radial $π$-periodicity, and the chiral spread complexity, which admits an exact closed form approaching the standard complexity at small angular momentum. Finally, by directly quantizing an effective AdS$_2$ theory, we obtain a new holographic interpretation of spread complexity in terms of the lapse function.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Spin chains for ADE quiver theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The spectral problem of four-dimensional superconformal quiver gauge theories can be mapped to one-dimensional spin chains with restricted Hilbert spaces, where the composition of neighbouring spins follows the path algebra of the quiver. To better understand such spin chains, we compute the one-loop planar dilatation operator for the 4d N=2 ADE quiver gauge theories obtained by orbifolding the N=4 Super-Yang-Mills theory and marginally deforming by independently varying the gauge couplings. This extends previous work which was mainly focused on the Z2 quiver. We characterise the general features of the resulting ADE spin-chain models and construct the 2-magnon Bethe ansatz for holomorphic states. We also evaluate, at large N, the N=2 superconformal index of these gauge theories and use it to study their protected spectrum in specific sectors.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 92 pages + appendices. Based on an MSc dissertation to be submitted by the first author to the University of Pretoria. v2: Published version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Single-valued flat connections in several variables on arbitrary Riemann surfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Polylogarithms on Riemann surfaces may be constructed systematically in terms of flat connections that can enjoy various algebraic and analytic properties. In this paper, we present a single-valued and modular invariant connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ on the configuration space $\text{Cf}_n(Σ)$ of an arbitrary number $n$ of points on an arbitrary compact Riemann surface $Σ$ with or without punctures. The connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ generalizes an earlier construction for a single variable and is built out of the same integration kernels. We show that ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ is flat on $\text{Cf}_n(Σ)$. For the case without punctures, we relate it to the meromorphic multiple-valued Enriquez connection ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ in $n$ variables on the universal cover $\tilde Σ$ of $Σ$ by the composition of a gauge transformation and an automorphism of the Lie algebra in which ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ and ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ take values. In a companion paper, we shall establish the equivalence between the flatness of these connections and the corresponding interchange and Fay identities, for arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Comments on holographic spread complexity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We revisit the holographic proposal relating the growth rate of spread complexity to the radial momentum of a bulk probe, aiming to identify its underlying assumptions and clarify how classical probe dynamics emerges from quantum dynamics. By quantizing AdS probes directly and using the extrapolation dictionary, we provide a more general derivation of the proposal within the probe approximation for the specified class of states. In particular, we discuss a probe analogue of the classical complexity observables appearing in the ``complexity=anything'' (CAny) framework and examine how such an observable can be quantized. Since probe dynamics is not intrinsically tied to the AdS/CFT correspondence, we also examine the proposal in flat and de Sitter spacetimes. In flat spacetime, the physical Hamiltonian does not preserve the coherent-state structure, and spread complexity measures the dispersive broadening of the wave packet rather than classical momentum. In de Sitter space, generic semiclassical wave packets in the static-patch energy representation show the same dispersive behavior. By contrast, coherent states adapted to the principal-series representation can exhibit exponential growth of spread complexity, with a growth rate that has the same time dependence as the classical radial momentum. These examples indicate that a semiclassical limit alone is not sufficient for a momentum--complexity relation.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v2: minor revisions; references added, wording improved, and typos corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum fields in a cold atomic simulator: relaxation and phase locking in tunnel-coupled 1D bosonic quasi-condensates
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider a prime example of simulating interacting relativistic QFT with cold atoms: the realisation of the sine-Gordon model by tunnel-coupled quasi-1D Bose gases. While experiments have shown that it can realise the sine-Gordon model in equilibrium, studies of non-equilibrium dynamics have revealed phase-locking behaviour that contrasts with predictions from sine-Gordon field theory. Here, we examine a one-dimensional field-theoretic model of the system and find that the phase-locking behaviour can be understood in terms of the longitudinal harmonic trap, and that the additional degrees of freedom observed in the experiment do not appear to play a significant role. Therefore, the experimental setup provides a good simulator of the sine-Gordon quantum field theory, even out of equilibrium, if the inhomogeneous background induced by the trap is taken into account. Furthermore, our results support the idea that modifying the longitudinal trap to a box shape should result in agreement with standard sine-Gordon dynamics. The main remaining open issues are accounting for 3D corrections and modelling the effect of the boundaries.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 17 pages, 9 figures. v2: added new discussion to clarify some points. Added references. v4: added author contributions

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Worldvolume Hybrid Monte Carlo algorithm for group manifolds
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Worldvolume Hybrid Monte Carlo (WV-HMC) method [arXiv:2012.08468] is a reliable and versatile algorithm for addressing the numerical sign problem. It resolves the ergodicity issues commonly encountered in Lefschetz thimble-based approaches without requiring explicit evaluation of the Jacobian during configuration generation. In this paper, as a general framework for applying WV-HMC to lattice gauge theories, we extend the algorithm to systems defined on connected compact group manifolds. The key is to introduce a symplectic structure on the tangent bundle of the worldvolume and formulate molecular dynamics on it. The validity of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated using one-site $SU(2)$ and $SU(3)$ models for purely imaginary couplings.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 93 pages, 15 figures; v2: typos corrected, figures updated; v3: typos corrected, proof of symplecticity elaborated; v4: references added, typos corrected; v5: references added, introductory section added (Sect. 2)

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The DBI critical electric field in stationary non-diagonal geometries
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the critical electric field for the holographic Schwinger effect in general stationary non-diagonal geometries. We show that, in such backgrounds, the DBI reality condition must be formulated in terms of the electric field measured in a local orthonormal frame, since the coordinate components of the field strength need not represent a purely electric field in that frame. The critical field measured in the orthonormal frame takes the universal value \(E_{\mathrm{proper},c}=T_F\), while its coordinate expression depends on the background geometry. The resulting critical field is independently confirmed by the holographic potential analysis, through the disappearance of the potential barrier. We further illustrate the general prescription using the planar limit and the global rotating Myers--Perry--AdS geometry, which exhibit different types of metric mixing.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Investigating tidal heating in neutron stars via gravitational Raman scattering
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We present a scattering amplitude formalism to study the tidal heating effects of nonspinning neutron stars incorporating both worldline effective field theory and relativistic stellar perturbation theory. In neutron stars, tidal heating arises from fluid viscosity due to various scattering processes in the interior. It also serves as a channel for the exchange of energy and angular momentum between the neutron star and its environment. In the interior of the neutron star, we first derive two master perturbation equations that capture fluid perturbations accurate to linear order in frequency. Remarkably, these equations receive no contribution from bulk viscosity due to a peculiar adiabatic incompressibility which arises in stellar fluid for non-barotropic perturbations. In the exterior, the metric perturbations reduce to the Regge-Wheeler (RW) equation which we solve using the analytical Mano-Suzuki-Takasugi (MST) method. We compute the amplitude for gravitational waves scattering off a neutron star, also known as gravitational Raman scattering. From the amplitude, we obtain expressions for the electric quadrupolar static Love number and the leading dissipation number to all orders in compactness. We then compute the leading dissipation number for various realistic equation-of-state(s) and estimate the change in the number of gravitational wave cycles due to tidal heating during inspiral in the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) band. We find that the shear-viscous contribution is small. Even for cold ($T\sim 10^5$K) and weakly compact stars it changes the number of cycles by less than $10^{-2}$, about an order of magnitude below the other conservative 4PN contributions, and it decreases as $T^{-2}$ for hotter stars.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 29 pages, 2 tables. v4 corrects a unit conversion error in the shear viscosity that overestimated the dissipation numbers and phase shifts in Tables I and II by a factor of 1000. Formalism, analytic results and Love numbers are unchanged. Corrected values agree with the independent calculation of arXiv 2611.30466. Discussion of shear-viscous tidal heating updated accordingly

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: D0-brane bound states in Matrix theory: nonperturbative bounds on matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
In Matrix theory, a single eleven-dimensional supergraviton is associated with a BPS bound state of D0-branes. Assuming the existence of a normalized physical BPS state, we derive nonperturbative bounds on its matrix extent, noncommutativity and spatial shape from supersymmetry in the BFSS model.
  The probability of matrix configurations smaller than a fixed fraction of an explicit extent scale is exponentially suppressed in the square of the number $N$ of D0-branes. In Yang-Mills variables, this scale for the trace-normalized extent is of order the cube root of the 't Hooft coupling. Relative noncommutativity, measured by a dimensionless commutator ratio, has an expectation bounded by a quantity of order the inverse of $N$, and its probability of exceeding a sufficiently large fixed multiple of the inverse of $N$ vanishes at large $N$.
  Concentration of the matrix extent along a fixed number of principal directions fewer than nine at large $N$ requires the total extent relative to a corresponding reference scale to diverge in probability. It also requires relative noncommutativity to be suppressed more strongly than the inverse of $N$, in every fixed finite moment of order at least one.
  These bounds apply to the full quantum wave function, including off-diagonal matrix degrees of freedom, and constrain the quantum structure of D0-brane bound states and the possible large-$N$ matrix geometries in Matrix theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A JT/KPZ correspondence
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We point out a correspondence between the Jackiw--Teitelboim (JT) gravity and the stationary measure of the Kardar--Parisi--Zhang (KPZ) equation on an interval. By relating the Schwarzian limit of the double-scaled SYK to the weakly asymmetric limit of the open ASEP, we establish that the path-integral measure defining the Euclidean evolution between two end-of-the-world branes in JT gravity can be interpreted as the stationary measure of the KPZ equation on an interval with Neumann boundary conditions. We also establish the match between correlation functions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Spiral Density Waves and Torque Balance in the Kerr Geometry
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) in relativistic accretion discs are a key science target for the upcoming LISA mission. Existing models of disc-EMRI interactions typically rely on crude dynamical friction or Newtonian planetary migration prescriptions, which fail to capture the relativistic fluid response induced by the binary potential. In this work we address this gap by providing the relativistic calculation. We apply standard methods from self-force theory, black hole perturbation theory, and relativistic stellar perturbation theory to compute the relativistic analogue of the spiral density wave and torque-balance results underlying planetary migration. Specifically, we calculate the response of a perfect fluid disc to the perturbing potential of an EMRI, consistently incorporating pressure effects. Using a master enthalpy-like variable and linearised fluid theory, we present a set of proof-of-principle calculations that reconstruct the fluid perturbations and relativistic spiral arm structure for a range of spin values in the Kerr geometry. We derive a relativistic torque-balance equation that enables us to compute and compare local torques with the angular momentum advected through the disc, finding striking agreement when applied to our relativistic disc-EMRI solutions. This opens a promising route towards establishing torque-balance relations between integrated disc torques arising from fluid perturbations and the forces acting on EMRIs embedded in matter.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 25 pages, 11 figures. v2: the source term now uses the height-averaged metric perturbation, resulting in the calculation no longer depending on an effective softening-length scale. All fluid solutions, torques and fluxes have been recomputed and the figures updated, along with a new appendix containing additional convergence plots

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Higher Spin Lagrangians for Black Holes in Arbitrary Dimension
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, we investigate the classical gravitational multipolar structure of rotating objects studying higher-spin Lagrangians coupled to gravity in arbitrary dimensions $D=d+1$. We first consider fields described by totally symmetric tensors with $s$ indices. At finite spin, the minimal coupling depends on both the spin and spacetime dimension. We show that, in the high-spin limit $s\gg 1$, the minimal multipolar expansion becomes dimension independent and it corresponds to the one which reproduces the Kerr solution in four dimensions. Furthermore, we identify a dimension independent relation among the non-minimal coupling coefficients that allows us to reproduce the Myers-Perry multipolar structure in arbitrary dimensions. We then extend our analysis to Lagrangians involving fields with different Young representations, which are allowed in higher dimensions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holographic Entanglement Entropy of Network CFT
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Miao et al. \cite{Guo:2025sbm, Guo:2026prm} proposed the AdS/NCFT correspondence, which explores the gravity dual of conformal field theories defined on networks. While previous studies investigated this model within Einstein and Gauss-Bonnet gravity (first- and second-order Lovelock gravity), in this paper, we generalize the framework to higher-order Lovelock gravity and more complex network structures. We derive the extremal and junction conditions for generalized Ryu-Takayanagi (RT) surfaces in third-order Lovelock gravity, which can be naturally extended to arbitrary higher-order Lovelock theories. Focusing on a network model comprising one node and three branches, we numerically investigate the relationship between the network holographic entanglement entropy (HEE) and gravitational coupling coefficients. Furthermore, by analyzing the HEE across various network configurations, we find that the primary structural feature affecting the network HEE is the presence of internal nodes within line-shaped networks. Our results indicate that the network HEE decreases as the number or depth of internal branches increases.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Para-fusion Category and Topological Defect Lines in $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermionic CFTs
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study topological defect lines (TDLs) in two-dimensional $\mathbb Z_N$-parafermoinic CFTs. Different from the bosonic case, in the 2d parafermionic CFTs, there exist parafermionic defect operators that can live on the TDLs and satisfy interesting fractional statistics. We propose a categorical description for these TDLs, dubbed as ``para-fusion category", which contains various novel features, including $\mathbb Z_M$ $q$-type objects for $M\vert N$, and parafermoinic defect operators as a type of specialized 1-morphisms of the TDLs. The para-fusion category in parafermionic CFTs can be regarded as a natural generalization of the super-fusion category for the description of TDLs in 2d fermionic CFTs. We investigate these distinguishing features in para-fusion category from both a 2d pure CFT perspective, and also a 3d anyon condensation viewpoint. In the latter approach, we introduce a generalized parafermionic anyon condensation, and use it to establish a functor from the parent fusion category for TDLs in bosonic CFTs to the para-fusion category for TDLs in the parafermionized ones. At last, we provide many examples to illustrate the properties of the proposed para-fusion category, and also give a full classification for a universal para-fusion category obtained from parafermionic condensation of Tambara-Yamagami $\mathbb Z_N$ fusion category.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Local Quantum Metrology: Precision Limits for Observers in QFT
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: How precisely can an observer estimate a parameter related to a quantum field? This question is answered for quantum-mechanical systems using the SLD--Bures--Fisher metric and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound. However, local algebras in relativistic quantum field theory are of type III: they carry no trace, so that states are not described by density matrices in the algebra, and they have no pure normal states, such that the SLD quantum Fisher information and the quantum Cramér--Rao bound cannot be defined in the usual way. We define the SLD (Bures) quantum Fisher information on arbitrary von Neumann algebras through Uhlmann's transition probability and prove a quantum Cramér--Rao bound for collective measurements. We also show that the bound is sharp, and equals the largest classical Fisher information obtainable by measurements in the region.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Sourced stationary Dirac bound states around Kerr black holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Ultralight bosonic fields can form macroscopic clouds around rotating black holes, whereas the existence of analogous stationary fermionic configurations is constrained by their intrinsic spin. Here we study stationary bound states of massive Dirac fields supported by an external source on Kerr backgrounds, in the test-field approximation, with a kinematic extension to Kerr--Newman, they are not fermionic condensates in the many-body sense. By mapping the Kerr--Dirac system to a globally integrated sourced radial problem, we isolate the boundary constraints dictated by horizon causality. The angular sector shows that for $|m|=1/2$ the regular boundary branches prevent the field density from vanishing on the rotation axis, whereas modes with $|m|\ge3/2$ vanish there, the reconstructed Kerr density is only mildly oblate. Precisely at the kinematic synchronization locus, the Frobenius matrix of the Dirac operator is non-defective and devoid of logarithmic divergences. Regularity on the future horizon nevertheless selects the ingoing solution, and an exact radial flux identity shows that this solution carries a positive flux, which excludes source-free normalizable states at all frequencies. The exclusion of source-free synchronized states demonstrates that a black hole's capacity to support macroscopic stationary fields is governed not merely by superradiant kinematics, but by the interplay between horizon regularity and the positivity of the Dirac flux.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Resolvent reconstruction of minimal strings beyond KdV II: D series models
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Three-state Potts gravity and tetracritical Ising gravity have the same central charge and the same conformal spectral curve. What distinguishes their amplitudes once a handle or a boundary is added? We answer this question by extending Johnson's differential-equation approach, in the reconstruction form developed in Part I for the reduced KP hierarchies, to D-series minimal strings. Their spatial operator is a pseudo-differential pencil with a nonlocal Pfaffian term, and the classical energy acquires a second pole at zero momentum. Regularity at both poles fixes the quantum corrections uniquely, ordinary string equations supply them, and the ordinary D flows add boundaries in a way that matches the tau function. At genus one the closed free energy follows from the pencil as a sum of logarithms of critical-value velocities. The two theories differ through the origin of the curve, which the D theory counts as two canonical directions, and through the pairing of every point with its reflection. We follow the origin contribution through the free energies to genus three, the one-holed torus and the torus one-point amplitudes, and in the primary range the latter reproduce the formulas conjectured from worldsheet numerics for both series.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Black Hole Entropy and Holographic Entanglement Entropy in DGP Brane Gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We investigate the relation between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity with gravitational dynamics localized on the brane. We first consider the DGP brane model, in which an Einstein-Hilbert term is included in the brane action, and demonstrate that the gravitational entropy of a braneworld black hole agrees with the holographic entanglement entropy for general stationary spacetimes.
  We then generalize the brane-localized Einstein-Hilbert term to higher-curvature gravitational theories. For Lovelock gravity and $f(R)$ gravity on the brane, we derive the corresponding expressions for gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy and show that the two entropies also coincide for general stationary spacetimes.
  These results establish the equivalence between gravitational entropy and holographic entanglement entropy in braneworld gravity for a broad class of gravitational theories and contribute to a deeper understanding of holography in braneworld settings.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum channel capacity of traversable wormholes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We formulate the Gao-Jafferis-Wall traversable wormhole protocol as a quantum channel and compute its quantum channel capacity. We show that this capacity is governed by the time derivative of an out-of-time-ordered correlator, hence by operator size growth in the holographic dual, and that its growth is bounded above by the Einstein gravity limit. The channel capacity therefore provides a natural benchmark for quantum simulations of traversable wormholes.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 12 pages, 8 figures. Updated to match the published version in Physical Review D

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entanglement structure in conformal Y-junctions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study how entanglement constrains energy transmission in conformal Y-junctions using holographic and free-field models. We define pairwise effective central charges from mutual information as a natural extension of the interface entanglement coefficient. For holographic junctions, we formulate a branched RT prescription and show that the resulting entropies satisfy monogamy of mutual information. We find that the pairwise effective central charge does not always bound the corresponding energy transmission, but a correction involving finite tripartite information restores the bound, with a sharp coefficient determined by limiting saturation. Free-boson and Dirac-fermion junctions also violate the pairwise bound, but the tripartite correction fails because the tripartite information is positive or vanishing, respectively. Analytic limits and numerical results instead support a candidate square-root correction based on L-entropy, which vanishes in the holographic complete-leg prescription considered here. We discuss the possibility of a common multipartite information bound in general conformal junctions.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Magnetic Catalysis and Fermion Mass Generation in de Sitter Spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider the dynamics of a charged fermion in de Sitter space in the presence of a uniform background magnetic field, and discuss magnetic catalysis of chiral symmetry breaking using the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model. We evaluate the mode functions of the charged fermion field in this background by imposing the Bunch--Davies vacuum condition. The gap equation is solved in the mean-field approximation. We derive analytic expressions for the gap in several limiting regimes, such as the large-magnetic-field and large-curvature limits. We find that the curvature effect restores chiral symmetry, whereas the magnetic field enhances chiral symmetry breaking through the conventional mechanism of magnetic catalysis. The phase structure associated with chiral symmetry breaking is revealed by numerical calculations.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Conformal line defects from matter-coupled 5D N=4 gauged supergravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study a number of holographic solutions describing conformal line defects within $N=2$ SCFTs from matter-coupled $N=4$ gauged supergravity in five dimensions. For $SO(2)_D\times SO(3)$ gauge group, the gauged supergravity admits two supersymmetric $AdS_5$ vacua with $N=4$ and $N=2$ unbroken supersymmetries. It turns out that only solutions that are asymptotic to the $N=4$ vacuum are possible leading to line defects within the dual $N=2$ SCFT. In gauged supergravity with $SO(2)\times ISO(3)$ gauge group, we find similar solutions with the $N=2$ SCFT appearing in the IR while the UV field theories correspond to six-dimensional $N=(0,2)$ field theories arising from M5-branes wrapped on a hyperbolic space $H^2$. The solution with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry is also uplifted to eleven dimensions via a consistent truncation on $H^2\times S^4$. Finally, for gauged supergravity with $SO(2)\times SO(3)\times SO(3)$ gauge group that admits two $N=4$ supersymmetric $AdS_5$ vacua, we find a solution describing a line defect that interpolates between these two vacua as well as a solution with only one asymptotic $AdS_5$ geometry.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: M5-branes wrapped on topological disks from maximal 7D gauged supergravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study new supersymmetric $AdS_5 \times Σ$ solutions for $Σ$ being a topological disk from the maximal gauged supergravity in seven dimensions with $CSO(p,q,5-p-q)$ gauge groups. These gauged supergravities can be obtained from consistent truncations of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $H^{p,q} \circ T^{5-p-q}$. We find a number of solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ and $SO(3,2)$ gauge groups as well as $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetric solutions from $SO(5)$ and $SO(4,1)$ gauge groups. Solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(3)$ symmetry preserve $16$ supercharges while the other solutions preserve only $8$ supercharges. Although some of the solutions give a holographic description of the dual $N=1$ SCFTs in four dimensions with finite central charges, most of the solutions describe codimension-2 defects within $N=(2,0)$ theories in six dimensions. For solutions with $SO(2)\times SO(2)$ and $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetries from $SO(5)$ gauge group for which a complete truncation ansatz of eleven-dimensional supergravity on $S^4$ is known, we also uplift the solutions to eleven dimensions and compute the holographic central charge of the dual four-dimensional $N=1$ SCFT with $SO(2)_{\textrm{diag}}$ symmetry.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: NS5-branes and the black hole/string transition
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Near to the onset of BTZ black hole formation in string theory is a large ensemble of 6d BPS supergravity solutions sourced by slightly separated fundamental strings and Neveu-Schwarz fivebranes. We extend the construction of these geometries to include gauge excitations of the fivebranes, and then study the energetics of D-string solitons in relation to the deconfinement transition of little strings, which are the natural non-abelian degrees of freedom that deconfine in the transition to the black hole phase.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Time irreversibility and entropy production in non-Hermitian Model A field theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a systematic framework to quantify irreversibility in scalar Model A field theories with a generic non-Hermitian term driving the dynamics. Using the stochastic path-integral formalism, we perform a controlled small-noise expansion, allowing the computation of the entropy production rate (EPR) and violations of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT). We show that the local EPR is entirely determined by the anti-Hermitian part of the linearised Langevin equation. Around steady states, the non-Hermitian component produces linear corrections to FDT violations and contributes quadratically to the EPR. As an illustration of the applicability of our approach, we analyse a minimal non-Hermitian extension of the Ginzburg-Landau $ψ^4$ theory describing a non-reciprocal Ising model at coarse-grained scales, for which we obtain explicit expressions of the local EPR, showing that it localises at interfaces in non-uniform states. Our results provide a general characterisation of TRS breaking in non-Hermitian scalar field theories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: What crossing symmetry forbids just above $c=1$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: What does a unitary two-dimensional conformal field theory look like just above $c=1$? Using the numerical conformal bootstrap, we study the four-point function of a scalar Virasoro primary $φ$ such that no primary lighter than $φ$ appears in its operator product expansion with itself. Slightly above $c=1$, crossing symmetry excludes the interval $0.17\lesssimΔ_φ\lesssim1$, although the compact boson realizes every such $Δ_φ$ at $c=1$. Combining this exclusion with results from the modular bootstrap, we show that the lightest primary of a compact unitary conformal field theory at $c=1.0005$ or $1.001$ has dimension $Δ_{\rm gap}<0.17$. Further from $c=1$, the largest excluded central charge at fixed $Δ_φ$ has two sharp minima near $Δ_φ=1/2$ and $4/7$. At these values it lies within $2\times10^{-7}$ of $c=8/7$, where the $\mathbb{Z}_5$ parafermion and its charge-conjugation orbifold have scalars of exactly these dimensions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 14 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables, v2: minor update

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A colored look at anyons and parastatistics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Color Lie (super)algebras were introduced in 1978 by Rittenberg and Wyler as generalizations of ordinary Lie (super)algebras. These color structures, graded by abelian groups, are defined by brackets which satisfy generalized Jacobi identities. Only recently the relevance of color Lie (super)algebras to physical applications has been pointed out and proved. The color framework not only describes, but also provides physical signatures for two broad types of parastatistics (particles beyond ordinary bosons/fermions): i) paraparticles which are exchanged via the permutation group and can exist in any space dimension D and ii) anyons (exchanged via the braid group), which exist up to D=2 space dimensions. This paper presents an update of the recent advancements which motivate a brand new "colored look" at questions involving parastatistics and braid statistics.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 20 pages; based on the plenary talk at the XLIII Workshop on Geometric Methods in Physics, Białystok, Poland, July 2026

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Modular flow and the area operator
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, the Jafferis-Lewkowycz-Maldacena-Suh (JLMS) formula relates the boundary modular Hamiltonian to the HRT area operator and the corresponding bulk modular Hamiltonian. In standard discussions of a holographic code built from perturbative excitations on a fixed classical background, the $A/4G$ term dominates over the bulk modular Hamiltonian in the limit $G \to 0$. However, this setup is insufficient to describe the action of boundary modular flows that change the classical background. In contrast, our recent discussion of `large' codes provides a useful framework to obtain a JLMS formula that relates bulk and boundary modular flows acting on appropriate states in the code. Here, one sees that the bulk modular Hamiltonian is not in fact subdominant when the modular flow defined by one state acts on another state peaked around a sufficiently different classical background. Instead, the bulk modular Hamiltonian can be of order $1/G$ and can dominate over the $A/4G$ term. Nevertheless, we show that if the two states have the same classical background except for data conjugate to the HRT area then, under mild assumptions and over a large range of flow parameters, the modular-flowed state is described by a classical background given by the HRT-area flow alone.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 28 pages, 4 figures, minor edits in v2

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Beyond the Thermodynamic-Volume Limit in Holographic Complexity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In the large black hole regime, holographic complexity obeys a thermodynamic-volume scaling law, while the finite-size approach to this limit remains unresolved. In this Letter, we develop an analytic description of finite-size corrections to this scaling for complexity of formation in the complexity=volume (CV) proposal of odd-dimensional equal-spinning Myers-Perry-AdS black holes. We find that the leading finite-size correction retains state dependence that is absent from the limiting thermodynamic-volume law. This correction changes sign at a distinguished Critical Horizon Ratio (CHR), where the generic leading finite-size contribution vanishes and convergence to the thermodynamic-volume law is correspondingly accelerated. We further determine the dimension dependence of the CHR analytically, showing that it approaches a finite nonextremal value at large dimension with a calculable leading finite-dimensional correction. These results show that the finite-size approach can provide a new probe of holographic structure, motivating its exploration across different realizations of holographic complexity and its eventual characterization in the dual field theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A cubic theory of gravity with quasitopological-like properties for compactified cosmologies
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We identify a cubic combination of curvature invariants in dimension $D=7$ that when added to the Einstein-Hilbert action, yields a healthy cosmological evolution in four dimensions after compactification on a constant-curvature internal space of dimension three. For generic backgrounds it leads to fourth-order field equations, nevertheless, on a warped product of a spatially flat, homogeneous and isotropic four-dimensional universe with a constant-curvature space of radius $b(t)$, the constraint is of first order in the scale factor $a(t)$ and in $b(t)$, while the remaining equations are of second order. Requiring this property uniquely singles out the cubic theory. We study the solutions describing a four-dimensional de Sitter Universe in direct product with an internal space of stabilized radius and evaluate its linear stability under time-dependent perturbations, showing that for a given sign of the curvature of the internal space, stability of the static solution fixes the sign of the higher curvature coupling. We also argue that linearized scalar perturbations depending on the spatial coordinates obey equations with at most two time derivatives. Finally, we numerically evolve the homogeneous and isotropic system non-linearly and present evidence that for a positive bare cosmological term $Λ_0$ and a hyperbolic compact space, the singularity formation present in GR in this ansatz is pushed into the future by increasing the higher-curvature coupling.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Hadron structure in $1+1$ dimensions from the infinite Hamiltonian lattice
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The internal structure of a hadron is encoded in matrix elements of operators between hadron states of definite momentum. In this paper, we develop a framework for computing such matrix elements in $(1+1)$-dimensional gauge theories by working on an infinite spatial lattice. We apply the method to the massive Schwinger model. We benchmark our method against discretized lightcone quantization (DLCQ) at $θ= 0$, and then use the lattice to study hadrons at $θ\neq 0$, where DLCQ does not apply. We compute parton distribution functions and gravitational form factors, and both show signatures of hadrons becoming large, loosely-bound states when we set $m$ greater than the critical mass $m_c$ and approach $θ= π$ from below. Moreover, we see the gravitational form factor change from that of a free boson to that of a free Majorana fermion when we set $θ= π$ and approach the 2D Ising critical point at $m=m_c$ from below.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Parton Physics in the Schwinger Model from Matrix Product States
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Parton distribution functions (PDFs) and light-cone distribution amplitudes (LCDAs) encode the non-perturbative structure of hadrons in terms of their partonic constituents. They are defined through matrix elements containing parton operators that are connected by a Wilson line along a light-front direction, which makes them difficult to access in Euclidean lattice calculations. We demonstrate how parton functions can be directly obtained in Minkowski space using the Hamiltonian framework. We compute fermion and antifermion PDFs, LCDAs, and decay constants of the vector meson in the Schwinger model for several fermion masses. States in Hilbert space are efficiently represented by tensor networks, with an expressivity that is systematically controlled by a bond dimension. The light-front Wilson line is implemented as a stepwise evolution on the lattice that alternates spatial shifts of an external charge with Trotterized time-evolution steps acting on a matrix product state. All systematic uncertainties are quantified by varying and extrapolating in the lattice spacing, volume, bond dimension, gauge-field truncation, and Trotter step width. The slow growth of the entanglement entropy makes moderate bond dimensions sufficient, which supports the feasibility of using tensor networks for computing light-front matrix elements in more general settings. We confirm that the computed distributions fulfill the expected normalizations, momentum sum rules, and symmetry properties.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Superstars, quantum wormholes and von Neumann algebras
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We entangle heavy 1/2-BPS states in two copies of $\mathcal{N}=4$ SU($N$) Super-Yang-Mills (SYM) theory. Each copy is separately dual to an extremal, supersymmetric, singular black hole geometry, in which the horizon coincides with a singularity. General ideas in the AdS/CFT correspondence suggest that the entanglement between the two copies should lead to some form of connectivity between the two geometries---a kind of wormhole. We use von Neumann algebra methods in the SYM theory to diagnose the possible existence of such wormholes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Revealing the conformal symmetry of the discrete series scalars in dS${}_2$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: On two-dimensional manifolds with nonzero constant Ricci curvature, there exists an infinite sequence of scalar fields with nonzero mass parameter that admit a pair of (anti-)holomorphic currents. After suitably defining the theory in de Sitter space ($\mathrm{dS}_2$), correlation functions of these currents obey global conformal Ward identities. We address the question of how this global conformal symmetry manifests as an action on the scalar field. An essential step is in leveraging an equivalent description of the scalar field in terms of a conformal Killing tensor. Through this, we find a conformal symmetry transformation that acts locally on the conformal Killing tensor, but non-locally on the scalar field. We show that the equation of motion transforms covariantly with respect to these conformal transformations, and further find a traceless stress tensor in both $\mathrm{dS}_2$ and $\mathrm{AdS}_2$, locally defined in terms of the conformal Killing tensor, which generates the global conformal isometry transformations.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: v1: 13 pages + appendices, v2: published version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Atom as an Agent: Emergent Order by Collective Predictive Coding
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: What is the intrinsic reason of emergence of macroscopic order parameter out of microscopic systems? In this article, we apply to physics the collective predictive coding (CPC), the theory of language/symbol emergence. As our language emerges out of our human communications, physical macroscopic order parameter emerges out of communications among atoms --- each atom is regarded as an agent who predicts each other's behavior through inference. We present three examples of classical spin systems: two-dimensional ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, a two-dimensional spin model with competing stripe orders, and the fully connected Sherrington--Kirkpatrick spin-glass model. In all of these examples, proper macroscopic order parameters including the replica overlap emerge automatically through communication informatics of CPC, only from observed spin configurations. We call the learned macroscopic coordinate the collective predictive order. Furthermore, for the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Ising models, the equilibrium distribution of the collective predictive order yields an emergent potential with the symmetry and thermal evolution characteristic of a Landau potential. Notably, the emergence of the collective predictive order does not refer to any structure of microscopic Hamiltonians/Lagrangians. Thus our ``Atom-as-an-Agent" (AaaA) principle offers a completely data-driven method for the emergence of macroscopic order, that is, machine learning physics.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 33 pages, 10 figures; v2: references and descriptions added, 34 pages

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: BPS baryonic tubes in chiral perturbation theory minimally coupled with electrodynamics and a novel crossover
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive a novel first-order BPS system (whose solutions are automatically solutions of the second-order field equations) in chiral perturbation theory (CPT) in $(3+1)$ dimensions. These BPS configurations describe baryonic tubes carrying a chiral current along the tubes themselves. Such baryonic tubes can be either homogeneous or modulated along the $z$-axis. We analyze the leading term in CPT, which is the $SU(2)$ non-linear sigma model minimally coupled to electrodynamics. These exact solutions are qualitatively different from the available analytic description of baryonic tubes since, due to their BPS nature, the positions of the energy-density peaks can be arbitrary. In contrast (in the case of the known solutions in the literature), the energy-density peaks' positions are fixed. We compare these two types of baryonic configurations; the relevant parameter that determines which one is energetically favored is the baryonic charge density: for low densities, the old solutions are favorable, while for high densities these novel BPS tubes are energetically favored. The inclusion of the electromagnetic field (together with the corresponding back-reaction on the baryonic tubes) can also be treated analytically. We discuss the differences in the electromagnetic field distribution between the two regions (low and high baryonic density). The analysis of potential terms for the chiral field is detailed in Appendix B.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Gravitational Effective Theories with Maximal Supersymmetry and a Peculiar Parity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the space of four-dimensional ultraviolet completions for $\mathcal{N}=8$ supergravity that are described at low energies by weakly-coupled effective field theories (EFTs) with maximal supersymmetry and $\mathrm{SU}(4)\times\mathrm{SU}(4)$ R-symmetry. We show that tree-level factorization of the 4-, 5-, and 6-point EFT scattering amplitudes, together with a certain ``peculiar parity'' condition, leads to nonlinear constraints on the 4-point Wilson coefficients. This peculiar parity is a property that can only be imposed on a subset of scalar amplitudes. Combining the nonlinear constraints with positivity, we find that the allowed region of 4-point Wilson coefficients is reduced to a non-convex domain with two sharp corners: one being the closed superstring Virasoro--Shapiro amplitude, the other an infinite spin tower amplitude exchanging states of every spin at the same mass. We show both numerically and analytically that requiring a finite number of states near the first mass level leaves only the Virasoro--Shapiro amplitude.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Probe branes from equivariant volumes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Classical Euclidean probe actions control non-perturbative weights and extended observables in holography. We present a geometric prescription for M2-branes in arbitrary BPS backgrounds and D3-branes in the five-form sector of type IIB. The framework accommodates compact and non-compact supersymmetric worldvolumes in both internal and spacetime directions, expressing their actions as relative equivariant pairings. Under stated extension and boundary assumptions, equivariant volumes evaluate these pairings without explicit background metrics and provide a regularization for non-compact probes. Examples in $\mathrm{AdS}_4\times SE_7$ backgrounds dual to ABJM, ADHM and flavored quiver theories reproduce and refine worldsheet-type instanton exponents and finite Wilson-loop actions. We also recover M2 giant-graviton and surface-defect actions in $\mathrm{AdS}_7\times S^4$. D3 probes in $SE_5$ compactifications dual to $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang--Mills and Klebanov--Witten theory provide tests involving giant gravitons, black hole probes and surface defects.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Weyl conformal geometry vs Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant (dressed) metric
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Weyl conformal geometry is the natural underlying geometry of gauge theories of Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincaré symmetry), such as Weyl quadratic gravity and its generalisation, Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). These are local, Weyl-anomaly free (quantum) gauge theories of gravity. We describe Weyl gauge symmetry from a more familiar Riemannian view of Weyl gauge invariant dressed fields by the Wilson line of dilatations. Weyl geometry can then be seen as Riemannian geometry of non-local dressed metric ($g_{μν}^*$), at the "cost" of (gauge-induced) non-commutativity in the UV, due to Wilson line. Then Weyl quadratic gravity and WDBI actions of Weyl geometry, which are Weyl gauge invariant in $d$ dimensions, have the same expression in Riemannian geometry defined by $g^*_{μν}$. This is a non-local map and dual description of the two geometries and actions in the symmetric phase. Unlike for the metric, the equation of motion of Weyl gauge field ($ω_μ$) does not commute with the dressing of the metric. Quantum non-locality, in particular entanglement, and non-commutativity are (gauge-invariant) physical artefacts of "translating" (local) Weyl geometry and Weyl gauge covariance into our real-world Riemannian geometry of Weyl gauge invariant observables, and they are evidence of Weyl gauge symmetry. At lower energies, $ω_μ$ becomes massive, can decouple and Einstein-Hilbert action and commutativity are recovered. The case of a light $ω_μ$ is also discussed.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: An Argument for the Weak Gravity Conjecture from Constrained Wormholes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The gravitational path integral (GPI) computes inner products between states of open and closed universes in any low-energy effective theory.
