We show that for Gaussian states the answer is exactly $2k-1$ when the neighbors use Gaussian measurements, with any number of measurement settings. The limit follows from a simple bound. To every neighbor we assign a share, computed from the covariance matrix, and we prove that the shares of all neighbors add up to at most $k$, irrespective of the amount of squeezing, amplification or noise the network contains. A neighbor steers the node by Gaussian measurements exactly when its share exceeds one half, and a network built from a harmonic tight frame reaches the limit. The same number governs remote Wigner negativity. A heralded non-Gaussian operation at the node can make at most $2k-1$ neighbors Wigner negative, and in our network a single heralded projection makes all of them negative in the same run. With $n$ settings of arbitrary measurements, at most $nk-1$ neighbors can steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it. More than $2k-1$ neighbors can therefore steer the node or violate a Bell inequality with it only if they use non-Gaussian measurements with at least three settings, whereas entanglement can reach any number of neighbors. These results determine exactly how many neighbors one multimode node can serve with steering and with remote Wigner negativity.

Quantum Physics.title: Bound magic in multi-qubit systems
Quantum Physics.summary: Magic captures nonstabilizerness, a resource required for quantum computational speedups. We prove the existence of multi-qubit nonstabilizer states from which no pure magic can be distilled, even with arbitrarily many copies and rounds of stabilizer operations. Such bound magic states have previously been only known to exist in odd Hilbert-space dimensions, where positivity of discrete Wigner functions can be used analogously to the positive partial transpose (PPT) criterion for bound entanglement. We introduce a PPT analogue for magic in multi-qubit systems that is closed under tensor products and stabilizer operations and reduces to the stabilizer polytope for one and two qubits. This enables the proof of multi-qubit bound magic and the explicit construction of bound magic states for $n \geq 3$ qubits.

Quantum Physics.title: Simultaneous computation of multiple excited states via double bracket flows
Quantum Physics.summary: Efficient computation of excited states is essential for studying strongly correlated many-body systems and molecular electronic structure. In this work, we propose a framework for simultaneously simulating multiple excited states based on dynamical flows. The main idea is to exploit a common double bracket flow that drives different pure initial states toward different target excited states without such prior information. We establish a necessary condition for convergence and a sufficient condition for exponential convergence. We further develop two scheduling strategies: Chebyshev scheduling, which achieves optimal convergence near a fixed point but requires prior spectral information, and adaptive scheduling, which achieves comparable performance in numerical simulations without spectral information. Our results enable new classical and quantum algorithms for excited-state computation without prior preparation of lower-energy eigenstates.

Quantum Physics.title: State convertibility in quantum-state texture from a general form of free operations
Quantum Physics.summary: State convertibility specifies which transformations between states a quantum resource theory allows. In quantum-state texture, deterministic conversion criteria are known for qubits and pure sources in arbitrary dimension, but a general criterion for mixed states in higher dimensions is missing. We derive this exact criterion from a complete characterization of free operations in arbitrary finite dimension. Because the unique free state is pure, every free operation splits into a quantum filter and a residual completely positive map. Using this decomposition, we show that every allowed conversion admits a two-outcome measurement that retains the filtered state after one outcome and prepares a fixed state after the other. Conversion thus reduces to finding such a filter whose unnormalized output leaves a positive semidefinite remainder when subtracted from the target, a search we show to be solvable by semidefinite programming. Beyond deterministic conversion, the characterization of free operations can be used to study probabilistic and assisted manipulation of quantum-state texture. More broadly, since the construction relies on a pure fixed state, it also applies to other resource theories defined by free operations fixing such a state.

Quantum Physics.title: Monotonic probes of asymmetry and robustness of the quantum Mpemba effect
Quantum Physics.summary: Entanglement asymmetry has emerged as a powerful probe of symmetry restoration and the quantum Mpemba effect. However, its conventional Rényi generalizations, defined as differences of Rényi entropies, are not monotones in the resource-theoretic sense. Here, we investigate an alternative family of asymmetry quantifiers based on sandwiched Rényi divergences, which satisfy monotonicity under symmetry-preserving quantum channels. Developing a two-parameter replica approach, we show how these quantities can be computed from charged moments and establish a remarkable correspondence with conventional Rényi asymmetries under the inversion of the Rényi index, $α\leftrightarrow 1/α$. This relation, exact for pure states, holds at leading order in the relevant scaling limits for homogeneous quantum quenches, including interacting integrable systems, and for Haar-random states. Applying these results to quenches from tilted ferromagnetic states, we demonstrate that the quantum Mpemba effect is remarkably robust, occurring throughout the entire family of sandwiched Rényi asymmetry monotones. We identify dynamical regimes in quenches from spatially inhomogeneous initial states where conventional Rényi asymmetries and genuine monotones exhibit qualitatively different behaviours. We also investigate a solvable toy model illustrating the possible dependence of Mpemba crossings on the Rényi index. Our findings establish a connection between conventional Rényi asymmetries and quantum resource theory, explaining their effectiveness in broad classes of nonequilibrium protocols while highlighting the additional information provided by genuine asymmetry monotones.

Quantum Physics.title: Interaction-Free Polarimetry
Quantum Physics.summary: The combination of interaction-free measurement and the quantum Zeno effect has been shown to both increase the signal-to-noise ratio of imaging, and reduce the energy absorbed by the imaged object. So far, however, it has not been used for quantitative polarimetry, the reconstruction of a sample's Mueller matrix. In this paper, we extend this to the polarimetry of diattenuating samples. For polarisation components that the sample strongly absorbs, the protocol identifies the sample with far less absorbed energy than a single-pass measurement, a benefit for delicate samples probed with high-frequency radiation. For weakly absorbing components the repeated passes through the sample absorb more, so the benefit is confined to strongly diattenuating features. A Fisher-information analysis shows that, for a sample with a lossless transmitting axis, the protocol locates the absorbing axis with far fewer absorbed photons than single-pass polarimetry, while it measures partial transmittances no more efficiently per absorbed photon, and that the same sorting of lossy components to one output port responds to retardance and depolarisation.
Quantum Physics.comment: 14+14 pages, 12+4 figures. Extended from just witnessing diattenuation to witnessing all polarising effects

Quantum Physics.title: $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ via Sublinear-Degree Pauli Approximation
Quantum Physics.summary:
We prove $\mathsf{AC}^0 \not\subseteq \mathsf{BQAC}^0/\mathsf{qpoly}$ in the single-copy, single-output model via an explicit $\mathsf{P}$-uniform family of linear-size monotone depth-2 CNFs. Every $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuit with arbitrary quantum advice achieves only an inverse-polynomial worst-case advantage over random guessing on this family. To prove this, we approximate the acceptance operator of any such circuit in operator norm by an advice-independent Hermitian operator of sublinear Pauli degree on a designated register alone, with degree exponent independent of width. Product-projection localization and Pauli twirling produce an auxiliary-register spectral cutoff that folds into contractions during backward peeling.
  The same approximation yields two stretched-exponential bounds against $\mathsf{QAC}^0$ circuits on $m$-qubit states. First, given polynomially many copies and input-independent quantum advice, single-output circuits distinguish exact or exponentially approximate state $2$-designs from Haar-random states with advantage at most $e^{-m^α}$. Second, any state prepared from fewer than $k$ arbitrary input qubits and remaining $|0\rangle$ inputs has spectral weight at most $2e^{-m^α}$ in a constant-energy-density band of an Anshu--Breuckmann--Nirkhe NLTS Hamiltonian encoding $k$ logical qubits. Both bounds hold for every fixed $α\in(0,1)$.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantitative Quantum Soundness for Bipartite Compiled Bell Games via the Sequential NPA Hierarchy
Quantum Physics.summary: Compiling Bell games under cryptographic assumptions replaces the need for physical separation, allowing nonlocality to be probed with a single untrusted device. While Kalai et al. (STOC'23) showed that this compilation preserves quantum advantages, its quantitative quantum soundness has remained an open problem. We address this gap with two primary contributions. First, we establish the first quantitative quantum soundness bounds for all bipartite compiled Bell games via a newly formalized convergent sequential Navascués-Pironio-Acín (NPA) hierarchy: any polynomial-time prover's score is controlled by a finite-level hierarchy value, and finite-level convergence gives a negligible gap to the commuting quantum value, or to the tensor-product quantum value under flat optimality. Second, we develop the sequential NPA hierarchy as a computational tool of independent interest, establishing its convergence and a stopping criterion based on flatness, and identifying its conic dual as a sparse SOS hierarchy.
Quantum Physics.comment: 43 pages, 1 figure. Accepted for publication in Quantum. See Section 4 of v2 for a discussion of whether the NPA convergence rate is necessary. For independent parallel work, see Cui, Falor, Natarajan and Zhang (arXiv:2507.17581)

Quantum Physics.title: Monotone Crossing Lattices for Exact Binary Optimization Encodings on Rydberg Arrays
Quantum Physics.summary: Programmable Rydberg-atom arrays realize maximum-weight independent set encoding on unit-disk graphs under the ideal blockade model, but embedding nonlocal interactions requires auxiliary atoms and limits the size of tractable instances. We introduce a four-state unit-disk crossing cell that couples directly to adjacent cells, with interfaces enforcing one-sided propagation: along occupied paths directed away from the diagonal, copy bits are nondecreasing. For the maximum-weight independent set problem, uniform cell weights guarantee that every ground state of the encoded instance decodes to an optimal solution of the original problem, even when local copies disagree. For binary quadratic objectives subject to pairwise Boolean constraints, every feasible optimum yields consistent active copies and a target weight given by an explicit constant offset minus the source objective. A rectangular variant of the architecture further encodes minimum set cover problem. Prior to constraint-induced site deletions, the full layout requires $2n^2 - n$ sites, halving the leading-order site count of a fixed complete-grid reference, while activity pruning yields an exact site count set by the propagation span. Across 18 paired benchmarks with independent ordering from a shared candidate pool, the layout reduces site counts by 12.1%-54.0%.

Quantum Physics.title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
Quantum Physics.summary: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.

Quantum Physics.title: Rugosity as a measurement-induced relative entropy
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum-state rugosity quantifies the departure of a quantum state from the flat superposition associated with a prescribed basis. We show that rugosity equals the classical relative entropy generated by the binary flat-state measurement. This identity gives two hypothesis-testing interpretations. Rugosity is the asymptotic discrimination exponent under repeated flat-state measurements and the exact finite-copy exponent under unrestricted quantum testing with zero type-I error. For smoothly parametrized states, we relate its local variation to the Fisher information accessible through the prescribed measurement. Using the local expansion of quantum relative entropy, we derive a bound on rugosity sensitivity in terms of the entropy-production susceptibility of a subsequent thermal reset. This susceptibility is given by the Bogoliubov-Kubo-Mori Fisher information. Finally, we formulate a measurement-dependent quantum speed limit whose endpoint distinguishability is determined by rugosity. These results connect quantum-state rugosity with statistical discrimination, thermal reset, and the geometry of experimentally accessible probability distributions.

Quantum Physics.title: The integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition for nonlinear dynamics: Efficient Hamiltonian simulation of the Stepanoff flow
Quantum Physics.summary: We propose an efficient unitary numerical time integration strategy for nonlinear dynamical systems: the integrable Lie-Trotter-Suzuki decomposition (I-LTS). First, express the generator as a sum of integrable parts. Second, approximate the full evolution operator using a Lie-Trotter-Suzuki (LTS) decomposition of the desired approximation order in time step. The I-LTS construction ensures that the full evolution operator can be represented as a product of terms that each have an efficient explicit tensor product factorization that can be handled efficiently with tensor network and/or quantum block-encoding methods. Next, we apply this method to an important non-integrable point example of a dynamical system: the Stepanoff flow on the torus. First, we derive an efficient unitary quantum algorithm for simulating the Stepanoff flow that can be thought of as a unitary classical version of a quantum map. Then, we provide a detailed description of the encoding of the two-dimensional system into an efficient quantum circuit, including an efficient block-encoding for all required operators. An efficient Hamiltonian simulation algorithm is constructed using a sequence of alternating quantum Fourier transforms (QFT) and Quantum Signal Processing (QSP) circuits. Finally, the circuit is simulated using a numerical emulator of fault-tolerant quantum computers, and the results are found to be consistent with several alternative classical computational methods. While efficient, the need for Trotterization introduces fundamental complexity in requiring small enough time step for an accurate approximation and solving for the transfer operator requires one to confront the linear scaling of the advection operator with grid size.

Quantum Physics.title: Fewer Parameters, Longer Runtimes: The Wall-Clock Cost of Hybrid Quantum Physics-Informed Neural Networks
Quantum Physics.summary: While hybrid quantum-classical physics-informed neural networks (QCPINNs) are often described as efficient because they have fewer trainable parameters than classical PINNs, parameter count does not measure wall-clock cost. To examine this gap on a one-dimensional seawater temperature diffusion benchmark, with the quantum circuits simulated on a CPU, we time the four cumulative stages a PINN needs (the forward pass, the first- and second-order input gradients, and the PDE-loss parameter gradient) for a classical PINN, four hybrid configurations that differ in qubit count and circuit depth, and size-matched classical controls that share the hybrids' classical layers. We find that the hybrids are 14-56x slower than the classical PINN for the forward pass and 10-97x slower for the PDE-loss parameter gradient, and even against the size-matched controls, they remain 9-85x slower. Further, over the tested ranges, runtime increased approximately exponentially with qubit count, approximately linearly with circuit depth, and sub-linearly with batch size, while for the circuit-only forward pass, a second simulator backend was 10-165x slower under the same calling pattern. Although the hybrids have 38-44% fewer parameters than the classical PINN, this reduction comes from their smaller classical layers, as the quantum circuit accounts for at most 2.5% of each hybrid's parameters. Yet parameter count failed to predict runtime even among the classical networks, since the size-matched controls, despite having fewer parameters than the classical PINN, run slower than it. Our conclusion is that fewer parameters did not mean lower cost: every hybrid took at least ten times longer than the classical PINN at every stage, and the gap grew quickly with the number of qubits.

Quantum Physics.title: Sharp Transitions of Copy Complexity in Local Certification of Typical Pure States
Quantum Physics.summary: We determine the asymptotic copy complexity of $n$-qudit state certification with tensor-product measurements. For given acceptance and rejection fidelities $a$ and $b$ ($b<a$), the optimal copy complexity is $Θ(n^r)$. For each qudit dimension $d$, $r$ is a piecewise constant function of $g=(a-b)/(1-b)$. This scaling holds for a family of sets of pure target states whose Haar measures tend to one as $n\to\infty$. We characterize the range of $g$ corresponding to each optimal exponent and provide an algorithm for computing its endpoints exactly. The optimal exponent grows logarithmically with $1/g$ as $g$ tends to zero. The upper bound is achieved by a nonadaptive protocol using only single-qudit projective measurements and classical postprocessing. The matching lower bound is established by constructing pairs of states that are difficult to distinguish under arbitrary tensor-product measurements. Our result can thus guide the design of certification tests when the number of available copies is limited.

Quantum Physics.title: Dynamical Complexity of Projected Ensembles: A Geometric Quantum State Approach
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the emergence of complexity in finite-size quantum systems as their dynamics transition from closed and coherent evolution to interacting and effectively open behavior. Using a state-based geometric framework, we represent mixed quantum states as probability measures on complex projective Hilbert space. Obtained by conditioning on the environment in a fixed basis, these geometric quantum states coincide with the projected ensembles that underlie deep thermalization and emergent quantum state designs. This representation allows us to track how interactions reshape the underlying pure-state geometry. We introduce two complementary diagnostics, a distinguishability measure based on the Wasserstein distance between nearby projected ensembles, which quantifies sensitivity to initial states, and a state-space coverage index, which measures long-time exploration of the subsystem state space. Applied to the quantum kicked top, both diagnostics generally increase with interaction strength. Their dependence on environment size is structured by parity symmetry, with integer-spin systems often exhibiting greater sensitivity and state-space coverage than half-integer-spin systems. These results highlight finite-size quantum effects and provide a geometric approach to quantifying dynamical complexity deep in the quantum regime.

Quantum Physics.title: Unitary Synthesis with a Unary Tracker
Quantum Physics.summary: This manuscript studies general unitary synthesis using unary-encoded ancillary register. Our first construction focuses on the $T$-cost of unitary synthesis. We maintain a unary register that coherently tracks the computational-basis label of the data. This allows Boolean lookups to use only CNOTs and shares the precision-dependent synthesis cost across the branches of each cosine-sine decomposition (CSD) factor. For a classically specified $n$-qubit unitary with $K$ mixing branches in its CSD, we obtain $T$-count $O(K+NL)$ using $N+O(L)$ clean ancillas, where $N=2^n$ and $L=n+\log(1/ε)$. We also give a related construction that directly applies the unitary onto a unary register to implement disjoint branches in parallel. Combining this with the quantum Shannon decomposition gives space-depth volume $O(N^2)$ using arbitrary single-qubit gates and CNOTs, which matches the asymptotically optimal bound.

Quantum Physics.title: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
Quantum Physics.summary: We compute vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer Rényi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex Rényi multi-entropy.

Quantum Physics.title: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors
Quantum Physics.summary: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry

Quantum Physics.title: Experimental Quantum Hardware Benchmarks of Flat Non-Clifford Hypergraph States, Antipodal Obstructions, and Nonlocal Games on IBM Heron r2
Quantum Physics.summary: Real-hardware demonstrations of quantum contextuality have reached high precision on superconducting processors, exemplified by Google Quantum AI's Mermin-Peres magic square and stabilizer games on Willow (Science, 2026). Extending such benchmarks beyond the Clifford regime requires non-Clifford hypergraph states |ψ_f> = 2^{-n/2} \sum_x (-1)^{f(x)} |x> governed by discrete algebraic invariants. Building on our Lean 4-verified framework of Modular Walsh Rigidity and Antipodal Obstructions, we present an experimental study on two 156-qubit IBM Heron r2 processors (ibm_fez, ibm_kingston) across 3 to 50 qubits and 11 auditable jobs (2.13 RUs total). First, we verify antipodal obstructions and mod-17 Walsh rigidity for degree-3/4 states (n=6,8,10), observing 5.4x-11.6x X-basis flatness separation between bent states, obstructed controls, and a degree-4 mod-3 fooler (W = +-1 mod 3), plus n=7 nonlinearity extraction (54.83 vs. 56.00). Second, barrier-protected Loschmidt echoes confirm non-Clifford coherence up to genuinely entangled 16-qubit degree-4 states (1,488x above random on ibm_fez; 17,296x on ibm_kingston for 2x8q, a 2.87x cross-chip gain) and locate a Heavy-Hex depth-513 coherence cliff. Third, calibration-aware layout raises the raw Mermin-Peres win rate on ibm_fez to 96.85 +- 0.09% raw (+87.4 sigma above 88.89% classical; 1.45 pp below Willow's 98.30% raw), while a tensored SPAM diagnostic reaches 98.35%. Uniformly random even-weight GHZ parity games beat the classical bound up to n=30 (89.44% [+79.4 sigma] at 6q to 59.46 +- 0.54% [+17.4 sigma] at 30q). Finally, 3-qubit CCZ rotated Mermin-3 (83.95 +- 0.29%, +31.2 sigma) and Hardy/Guhne-Cabello (77.15 +- 0.33%, +6.5 sigma) games strictly violate the exhaustive 75.00% LHV ceiling, and degree-3/4 antipodal parity witnesses achieve up to +45.87 pp (n=12) and +35.79 pp joint advantage on connected 16-qubit degree-4 states.
Quantum Physics.comment: 5 figures, 6 tables; 11 auditable IBM Quantum Heron r2 hardware jobs (ibm_fez and ibm_kingston)

Quantum Physics.title: Slow mixing of Gibbs sampling for the quantum Curie-Weiss model
Quantum Physics.summary: Hamiltonian evolution can spread local operators across a dense quantum magnet. We show that this global support does not remove the bottleneck to thermalization in the quantum Curie-Weiss model: at fixed low temperature and weak transverse field, the Chen-Kastoryano-Gilyen Gibbs sampler [arXiv: 2311.09207] has an exponentially large mixing-time lower bound. A dynamical quantum bottleneck theory that generalizes the classical notion of conductance has been proposed alongside existing frameworks that rely on spatial locality. We also give a complementary interpretation of slow mixing using an effective Fokker-Planck equation.

Quantum Physics.title: Magic Moments: An Operational Approach of Certifying Nonstabilizerness from Few Copies
Quantum Physics.summary: Magic is the key resource enabling universal fault-tolerant quantum computation beyond classically simulable stabilizer circuits. Certifying it, however, usually requires either full state tomography or an optimization over the set of stabilizer states, both of which rapidly become prohibitive as the system grows. Here, we introduce a moment-based criterion that certifies magic from a few moments of the discrete Wigner function, without fully reconstructing the distribution itself. For pure states of any number of qudits the criterion is necessary and sufficient, while for mixed states we construct a hierarchy of higher moments conditions that reaches the exact negativity threshold. We also derive lower bounds on sum negativity and mana from low-order moments, and use them to bound the negativity factor in quasiprobability simulation. Each moment can be evaluated as the expectation value of a two-outcome observable on a few copies of the state, measurable with a constant-depth Clifford circuit and a number of rounds independent of qudit number, providing efficient, experimentally accessible tools for certifying and quantifying nonstabilizer resources.

Quantum Physics.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
Quantum Physics.summary:
We prove path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of every fixed order $k \geq 3$: every spectral point is connected by a path to every "one leg versus the rest" flattening rank. In particular, the asymptotic spectrum evaluated at any fixed tensor is a closed interval, answering a question of Strassen. This was previously known only on specific families of tensors (Strassen, FOCS 1986, Crelle 1987-1991; Wigderson and Zuiddam, Bull. AMS 2026) or for specific families of spectral points (Christandl, Vrana and Zuiddam, STOC 2018; Sakabe, Doğan and Walter, FOCS 2026; Alman, Li and Pratt, FOCS 2026).
  To obtain our path-connectedness theorem we develop a general method for "interpolating" between spectral points, which applies to Strassen semirings that are appropriately decomposable (in the sense of an information-theoretic "method of types" on the semiring) and whose spectral points satisfy a cover property (inspired by slice rank). This covers tensors and asymptotic rank (with "types" given by decomposition into symmetric group irreps), as well as other objects and asymptotic problems, like graphs and Shannon capacity, where it matches the interpolation of Vrana (2019).
  Using our interpolation methods we furthermore obtain new results and simpler proofs of previous results regarding the asymptotic spectrum of rectangular matrix multiplication, polynomial multiplication and non-crossing (laminar) quantum functionals.

Quantum Physics.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin defect emission and quantum sensing
Quantum Physics.summary: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy (VB-) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of VB- by up to 45x at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A type-I band alignment at the PbI2-hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives VB- excitation. This process is consistent with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

Quantum Physics.title: Data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo with Rydberg-atom measurements
Quantum Physics.summary: We introduce a data-enhanced self-learning projective quantum Monte Carlo (PQMC) method that incorporates projective measurements from programmable quantum simulators into the guiding wavefunction of a ground-state projection. We demonstrate the approach for a two-dimensional Rydberg-atom array using restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM) and recurrent neural network (RNN) guiding wavefunctions. Experimental pretraining reduces finite-population effects and accelerates self-learning convergence, allowing unbiased estimation of ground-state properties to be obtained with fewer walkers and fewer self-learning iterations. The improvement is particularly pronounced for the RBM, while the more accurate RNN guiding wavefunction exhibits a smaller, though still observable, benefit from pretraining. Simulations across different system sizes suggest that the relative advantage of experimental pretraining may increase with system size. Improvements are also observed for the checkerboard order parameter, despite deviations of the experimental measurements from the equilibrium numerical results. Finally, finite-size scaling with self-learning PQMC without experimental pretraining yields the critical point and critical exponents of the disordered-to-checkerboard transition in agreement with previous numerical studies. Our results show that limited and imperfect experimental measurements can provide an effective initialization for self-learning PQMC, while imaginary-time projection combined with subsequent unsupervised learning progressively refines the guiding wavefunction toward the ground state.

Quantum Physics.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
Quantum Physics.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a prominent approach to quantum architecture search (QAS), the automated design of quantum circuits. However, transferring what an agent has learned from one number of qubits to another is still weakly explored: the state, the action space and the neural network of a state-of-the-art RL-QAS agent all grow with the number of qubits, which makes transfer learning across qubit counts prohibitive. We make this transfer possible by introducing LatentRL-QAS, a latent space transfer and refresh framework for RL-based QAS. At its core, a circuit variational autoencoder encodes a circuit as one token per gate and maps circuits on any number of qubits into the same latent space. An RL agent navigates this space instead of adding gates, so its state, actions and network have the same size at every qubit count. The latent space is periodically refreshed with the agent's new discoveries and, for a larger system, grown from the solutions of the smaller one, so what is transferred is the representation of circuits, not network weights or past experience. To show transfer, we consider absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states, a resource for quantum error correction. LatentRL-QAS discovers the five- and six-qubit AME states without being shown them and prepares them in 89-99% of evaluation episodes, whereas the baseline RL-QAS fails to find them with the same budget, even with a network 10 to 17 times larger. LatentRL-QAS remains robust under depolarizing noise with single-qubit gate errors amplified 10x and two-qubit gate errors 5x compared with IBM quantum hardware. By decoupling the RL agent from the number of qubits, LatentRL-QAS lets quantum architecture search reuse circuit representations learned on smaller problems, providing a foundation for the transferable design of circuits across quantum optimization problems.
Quantum Physics.comment: 26 pages main text + references and appendices (41 pages total), 6 figures, 10 tables

Quantum Physics.title: Sudden death of entanglement, rebirth of magic
Quantum Physics.summary: Local Markovian noise cannot bring entanglement back, but it can bring magic back. Local dissipation can push a state out of the stabilizer polytope as well as in. Under independent amplitude damping, the $n$-qubit state $α|0^n\rangle+β|1^n\rangle$ with $0<α<β$ loses its magic for a finite interval. The coherence between its ground and fully excited configurations keeps falling throughout. Magic returns when the fully excited population falls below that coherence. The damping probabilities for entanglement death and magic rebirth obey $γ_e+γ_+=1$ for every $n\ge2$. Magic returns to the register just as its reservoirs become entangled. For a sufficiently small ground-state amplitude the register is already fully separable at rebirth. Every proper marginal is a stabilizer mixture throughout, yet a joint parity measurement followed by Clifford decoding can concentrate the reborn magic onto one qubit. With thermal relaxation and dephasing, we find a range in which magic loss is permanent for every isolated qubit, yet two qubits exposed to the same noise can regain it.
Quantum Physics.comment: v3: New results on the minimum register size for magic rebirth, late-time magic, and limits on local extraction

Quantum Physics.title: Genuine multientropy, dihedral invariants and Lifshitz theory
Quantum Physics.summary: Multi-invariants are local-unitary invariants of state replicas introduced as potential probes of multipartite entanglement and correlations in quantum many-body systems. In this paper, we investigate two multi-invariants for tripartite pure states, namely multientropy and dihedral invariant. We compute the (genuine) multientropy for Lifshitz groundstates, and obtain its analytical continuation to noninteger values of Rényi index. We show that the genuine multientropy can be expressed in terms of mutual information and logarithmic negativity, a relation that also holds for stabilizer states. For general tripartite pure states, we demonstrate that dihedral invariants are related to Rényi reflected entropies. In particular, we show that the dihedral permutations of replicas are equivalent to the reflected construction, or alternatively to the realignment of density matrices.
Quantum Physics.comment: 6+14 pages, 2+7 figures ; v2: minor modifications, refs added ; v3: matches published version; v4: minor typos corrected

Quantum Physics.title: Sufficient quantum provenance: retained fields and certified recording precision
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum executions that share a provenance record can still produce different output distributions. We determine which execution details a record must retain, and at what precision, to guarantee agreement within a declared Hellinger tolerance. Under a specified channel model, a certificate combining independent stochastic mechanisms and coherent rotation differences fixes the recording precision without output simulation or explicit dependence on register dimension. For four-qubit quantum approximate optimization at depth one, a 13-bit comparison record suffices at tolerance 0.05 over a declared continuous noise range, uniformly in programmed angles for each fixed task, against 19 bits for a gate-by-gate sum over the same bin family. Pairwise separation constraints characterize sufficient field sets on finite context classes and expose omissions that pass individually but fail jointly. Separately, six-qubit measurements on an IBM Heron processor show, over six tested contexts, that raw outputs need a two-label record, supplied by qubit layout, whereas outputs after a fixed application decoder need no additional context bits, at tolerance 0.15 with 97% simultaneous confidence under stationary, independent shots. Execution records can thereby be designed to carry checkable agreement guarantees.
Quantum Physics.comment: v4: Clarified hardware interpretation; added an IQM Garnet scout pointer and citation. Revised abstract and presentation. Scientific results unchanged

Quantum Physics.title: Tripartite entanglement dynamics following a quantum quench
Quantum Physics.summary: We investigate the dynamics of multipartite entanglement after quenches from initial states which generate multiplets of quasiparticle excitations beyond the usual pair structure. We focus on the dynamics of tripartite entanglement through the lens of the Markov gap -- a computable quantity that signals irreducible tripartite entanglement when positive. In the tight-binding chain, we show that the Markov gap is positive at intermediate times, implying the presence of tripartite entanglement. After a time delay, the Markov gap increases and then decays at longer times, thus exhibiting an entanglement barrier. We argue that those qualitative features are consistent with an interpretation of the spreading of tripartite entanglement by triplets of tripartite-entangled quasiparticles.
Quantum Physics.comment: 3+3 pages, 3+2 figures; v2: minor typos corrected

Quantum Physics.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
Quantum Physics.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof [arXiv:1105.3445] assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state-operator duality. The asymptotic horizon charge is the momentum of a quantum clock; its conjugate gives the reading. The modular crossed product admits density operators whose entropy with respect to its trace reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time measurement of surprisal, the negative logarithm of the density operator, gives an FT for the complete exterior channel. It identifies the correction for a nonunital channel and gives a GSL bound for unital evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that preserves every dressed-charge sector and the full faithful dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The bounds establish the GSL in the slow-clock limit when the errors vanish and quantify what is needed at finite clock width.
Quantum Physics.comment: 34 pages and 5 figures; v2. Polish the logic chains and wording; add references

Quantum Physics.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
Quantum Physics.summary: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we expand the field in vector modes, quantize it, and introduce the quantity measured by a photodetector. We then show that the word ``phase'' refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, fixed by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state that excites the mode. Only the first determines the fringes. All calculations are given in full, and problems with solutions are included.
Quantum Physics.comment: 60 pages, 9 figures. Submission to SciPost Physics Lecture Notes

Quantum Physics.title: Robust Quantum Key Distribution Arbitrarily Close to Local Correlations
Quantum Physics.summary: Recently, Wooltorton et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210802 (2024)] and Farkas [Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 210803 (2024)] have exhibited the mismatch between Bell inequality violations and their cryptographic application in device-independent quantum key distribution, by showing that arbitrarily close to the set of local behaviours there exist quantum correlations guaranteeing a constant rate of secret key. While these results require correlations attaining the maximum quantum value of a suitable Bell observable (aka the Tsirelson bound) and rely on a kind of ideal self-testing of a maximally entangled state and associated Bell measurement, here we show that the effect is robust: for every one of the Bell inequalities considered by Wooltorton \emph{et al.}, a constant rate of secret key ensues if the observed Bell violation is sufficiently close to the respective Tsirelson bound. For these and also the Bell inequalities of Farkas, we furthermore present numerical results based on semidefinite relaxations of the minimum min-entropy consistent with a certain Bell violation, which demonstrate that small but nonzero key rates can be guaranteed (in principle) by practical and efficient means.
Quantum Physics.comment: added a robust self-test of the ideal strategy in arbitrary dimension (Theorem 2); author contribution statement; corrected errors in the proofs. 34 pages, 3 figures

Quantum Physics.title: Dynamics of a Charged Particle on a Conformal Helicoidal Surface
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the classical and quantum motion of a charged particle on a conformal helicoidal surface embedded in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A uniform ambient magnetic field pulls back to a nonuniform surface field. The cyclic longitudinal coordinate permits an exact transverse reduction. The ordinary helicoid in the same axial field shares the effective potential and the turning points, while the conformal metric increases the physical period at matched energy and longitudinal momentum. We classify the single- and double-well regimes and obtain the exact transverse periods in the two double-well sectors. The periods diverge logarithmically at the separatrix, with twice the leading coefficient above the barrier as below it. The zero-field limit allows transverse escape, and the weak-twist limit is locally free but nonuniform across the surface. Intrinsic quantization gives an exact weighted transverse eigenvalue problem. Fixed-momentum eigenvalues test the harmonic approximation in a central well and resolve the tunneling splittings in a double well.

Quantum Physics.title: Secure Quantum Handshakes: Quantum Network Verification Via Simon's Algorithm
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum networking represents the future of secure communication, enabling fundamentally new capabilities through quantum information exchange. However, these networks require secure, high-fidelity quantum communication channels. Currently, there is no reliable method to verify whether clients entering a quantum network truly possess quantum state communication capability over robust channels. In this work, we introduce a client-validation protocol that functions as a proof-of-quantum-communication handshake. Our protocol secures a quantum network against classical spoofers, faulty quantum computers, and genuine quantum devices connecting to the network over noisy or insecure channels. We validate the efficacy of this protocol through numerical simulations under erasure, dephasing, and depolarizing noise models.

Quantum Physics.title: PEPSKit.jl: A Julia package for projected entangled-pair state simulations
Quantum Physics.summary: We present PEPSKit$.$jl, a Julia package for simulating two-dimensional quantum many-body systems with infinite projected entangled-pair states (iPEPS). PEPSKit$.$jl builds on the TensorKit$.$jl package for tensor computations and provides high-level algorithms for iPEPS simulations that support both Abelian and non-Abelian symmetries, as well as fermionic systems. This work gives an overview of the main package features, which include support for ground-state, time-evolution, and finite-temperature simulations in systems with different physical symmetries and lattice geometries. These capabilities are illustrated through various examples and technical benchmarks.

Quantum Physics.title: Optimal GHZ extraction from MABK violations
Quantum Physics.summary: For $n\geq3$ parties, we prove that the least Greenberger--Horne--Zeilinger (GHZ) extractability compatible with a Mermin--Ardehali--Belinskii--Klyshko (MABK) score between the biseparable bound and the quantum maximum equals $(1+t)/2$, where $t$ rises linearly with the score from $t=0$ to $t=1$ across this range. The minimum is over all states and binary measurements in arbitrary local dimensions, and the extractability of a state is the supremum over local channels of the overlap with the GHZ state. With a qubit at every party, the minimum is strictly larger for $0<t<1$; we determine it exactly. We construct a mixture on one qutrit and $n-1$ qubits that attains $(1+t)/2$ with measurements independent of $t$. We prove that, for $0<t<1$, its product of local ranks (ranks of its single-party reduced states), $3\cdot2^{n-1}$, is the smallest among attaining states and, for $n\geq4$, it is the only attaining state with this product, up to local isometries and party permutations. On one qutrit and $n-1$ qubits with arbitrary binary measurements, for $n\geq4$ and $t$ bounded away from zero, we prove that an extractability within a small $\varepsilon$ of $(1+t)/2$ forces trace-norm distance $O(\sqrt{\varepsilon})$ from the mixture at the same $t$, up to local unitaries, uniformly in $n$ and with optimal exponent. Since the Bell statistics do not determine the extractability, we also bound this distance for $n\geq3$ and $t>0$ by the MABK score and the expectations of five calibrated binary measurements on the qutrit, assuming known local dimensions and a known two-dimensional qutrit subspace invariant under both Bell observables of that party; the bound vanishes when these expectations equal their values in the mixture.
Quantum Physics.comment: 48 pages, 1 figure. Reorganized the results and proofs, clarified the local-rank and stability statements, and added attribution for the two scalar MABK positivity cases

Quantum Physics.title: Resource theory of pi-ordered imaginarity and its resource quantifiers
Quantum Physics.summary: Conventional resource theory of quantum imaginarity takes real density matrices as free states without ordering constraints on their diagonal populations. Motivated by the role of population ordering in the incoherent ergotropy of quantum batteries and the recently proposed framework of $π$-ordered coherence, we develop the resource theory of $π$-ordered imaginarity. In this refined framework, free states are required to be real in the reference basis and to obey a prescribed permutation order $π$ for their diagonal populations. This theory thereby identifies two independent quantum resources: complex phases and population misordering, where the latter is inaccessible within the standard imaginarity resource theory. We characterize the structure of free states using majorization and the Schur-Horn theorem, define admissible $π$-ordered real operations, and examine their intersection with $π$-ordered incoherent operations. We further construct resource quantifiers for the $π$-ordered imaginarity based on relative entropy, fidelity and robustness, and derive inequalities relating the robustness of $π$-ordered imaginarity and that of $π$-ordered coherence. The present framework generalizes the standard resource theory of imaginarity to incorporate population ordering and is naturally suited for thermodynamic settings such as quantum batteries.

Quantum Physics.title: High-Throughput GPU Decoding of Quantum Bivariate Bicycle Codes under Circuit-Level Noise
Quantum Physics.summary: Bivariate bicycle (BB) codes reduce the physical-qubit overhead of quantum error correction compared to other codes such as Surface codes, but circuit-level faults create dependencies across measurement rounds that limit decoding throughput. We present a parallel-window GPU decoder that combines reusable fault patterns, compact shared-memory state, and persistent GPU workers using min-sum with Relay-BP recovery. On an RTX 5090, the proposed decoder keeps pace with one syndrome round every 1 $μ$s across all four evaluated codes, up to [[144,12,12]] with 63-144 $μ$s median commit delays. This rate has not been demonstrated in prior circuit-level GPU decoding studies and it provides $120\times$ higher decoding throughput than sequential sliding-window decoding. Checking neighboring detector rounds before accepting a decoding result reduces failure rates by up to 65%. For [[144,12,12]] at $p=0.002$, our proposed decoder achieves $7.58\times 10^{-6}$ failures per round, 36% lower than the published belief propagation (BP) with syndrome flipping (BP-SF) result.

Quantum Physics.title: Conditional multiparameter thermometry with neutrino oscillations: MSW energy diversity and a plasma-noise benchmark
Quantum Physics.summary: We address temperature-parameter inference in a restricted two-flavor neutrino dephasing model with fixed mean electron densities. When two zone temperatures enter the propagated state via a single accumulated dephasing exponent, the single-energy quantum Fisher information matrix has rank at most 1. Independent, energy-resolved samples restore regular local identifiability when their thermal-sensitivity vectors are noncollinear. Matter-dependent mixing provides distinct weights in an illustrative two-zone model. A separate two-probe benchmark shows how complementary Bell sectors can distinguish temperature from spatial noise correlations. An electron-only Debye-cell estimate gives a conditional longitudinal quantum signal-to-noise ratio of approximately $3.1\times10^{-13}$ at 10 MeV for a uniform central-density medium over one solar radius. This estimate is not a microscopic upper bound or a detector sensitivity forecast. Complete phase averaging removes temperature information carried solely by longitudinal coherence damping; to retain solar sensitivity, a separate calculation of population, refractive, or production effects is required. The results distinguish conditional state identifiability from operational temperature inference.

Quantum Physics.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
Quantum Physics.summary: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $λ_X,λ_Y,λ_Z$, the advantage is governed by $λ_X^2+λ_Y^2+λ_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a Rényi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model predicts. A three-qubit repetition code turns a shrinking advantage into a growing one with all processor and readout errors included, and under dephasing its memory performs better than Bell sampling in any memory frame on a perfect processor.

Quantum Physics.title: Exponential Analysis for Trace-Distance Errors in Quantum Information Theory
Quantum Physics.summary: We study the trace-distance error in classical-quantum soft covering, privacy amplification against quantum side information, convex splitting, and decoupling by a Haar-random unitary followed by partial trace. In the independent and identically distributed setting, we determine exact reliability functions and strong converse exponents for soft covering with independent codewords, uniform convex splitting, and Haar partial-trace decoupling. For privacy amplification, we determine the exact reliability function for independent random binning and the exact strong converse exponent for every two-universal hash ensemble. The reliability and strong converse formulas involve sandwiched and Petz-Rényi information, respectively. The proofs connect trace-distance errors to quantum hypothesis testing, using Rosenthal inequalities for sums of random matrices in the reliability analysis and conditional second-moment bounds for the strong converses.

Quantum Physics.title: Full-chip constrained quantum annealing via self-calibrating spin-susceptibility control
Quantum Physics.summary: Discrete optimization in finance, power grids, and logistics requires minimizing Ising Hamiltonians under coupled linear constraints. However, quadratic-penalty formulations superimpose dense cliques that exhaust the minor-embedding capacity of sparse superconducting processors at 128-176 spins, and first-order dual subgradient schemes diverge or stall under constraint coupling. Accordingly, this study proposes a hardware-native quantum-classical closed-loop primal-dual workflow, designated as Self-Calibrating Quantum Susceptibility Quasi-Newton (SelfCal-QSQN), in which linear constraints are encoded in longitudinal fields with zero auxiliary quadratic penalty couplings and dual curvature is reconstructed from single-shot spin-fluctuation covariances. This workflow requires no slack qubits or perturbation queries. Evaluated over 891 runs on D-Wave Advantage (5,612 qubits) and Advantage2 (4,560 qubits), SelfCal-QSQN drives the pre-polish trajectory-minimum raw QPU sample violation to $0.108 \pm 0.017$ at 4,560 qubits (83.3% exact feasibility after a deterministic 1-bit polish with best-incumbent tracking, reaching 47.3% of the continuous linear-programming relaxation bound), reduces high-constraint error by 6.1- to 20.1-fold over K-scaled first-order updates, attains 5.35-fold deeper feasible energies than linear programming with the identical 1-bit polish within a 4.10-s compute-only budget at 256 spins, and achieves 95.0%-96.7% feasibility on non-native and inequality benchmarks. Moreover, the workflow is robust toward shot noise and freeze-out drift.
Quantum Physics.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 3 tables. v2: expanded classical baseline comparisons, runtime breakdowns, and full-chip LP lower-bound verification

Quantum Physics.title: Direct-Coupled Architectures for Magic-State Factories
Quantum Physics.summary: In surface-code magic-state factories, the interface that passes level-1 T states to level 2, i.e., the transport channels, waiting spots, and $|0\rangle$ correction patches, occupies a large part of the factory area. We remove this interface by applying adaptive measurement, a principle known from gate teleportation, to the consumption of T states: in adaptive X/Y consumption, the T-state patch used for a $π/8$ rotation is read out in the X or Y basis depending on the merge outcome. The basis choice itself performs the $π/4$ correction, so no correction patch is needed and a T state can be consumed wherever it already sits. Building on this property, we present direct-coupled architectures in which level-1 suppliers are attached directly to the level-2 core. D1 consumes each T state in its supplier output slot and removes the interface entirely; D2 adds one small buffer per supplier so that the supplier continues distilling without pause. Because the method changes only how a supplied T state is consumed, it applies to the many factories that perform $π/8$ rotations by multi-patch Pauli measurements. As an example, we apply it to a CCZ factory and compare it with Litinski's factory under the same logical-error model and the same area accounting. For a maximum output period of 120 cycles, D1 and D2 reduce the area by 24% and 29% without increasing the space-time volume, and the smallest D1 factory is 37% smaller than the smallest Litinski design. The same approach also reduces the area of two-level T factories.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum dynamics of a charged particle on rotating curved surfaces and space curves in electromagnetic fields
Quantum Physics.summary: We develop a gauge-consistent framework for a charged particle confined to a rotating curved manifold in an electromagnetic field, starting from the covariant Klein--Gordon equation. The non-relativistic reduction casts the rotational effects as effective gauge potentials while preserving the $U(1)$ symmetry, so that rotation and the external field enter alike, the geometry entering separately as the da Costa potential. The obstruction to dimensional reduction is gauge--geometry entanglement: transverse magnetic fields on a two-dimensional (2D) surface and structural torsion on a one-dimensional (1D) curve couple the tangential dynamics to the transverse degrees of freedom. We remove this entanglement by three mechanisms---a generalized transverse Poincaré gauge, the rotation-minimizing Bishop frame, and the parity of the transverse ground state, the last of which annihilates the residual first-order magnetic coupling for a single inversion-symmetric well. On a torus, an axial field generates a joint Sagnac--Aharonov--Bohm residual of tunable sign without spoiling the poloidal--azimuthal separability, whereas an in-plane field couples only through the out-of-plane extent of the structure: it breaks the axial symmetry there but leaves a planar curve unaffected to first order. The same torus shows the axial field tuning the curvature-induced localization, and a corrugated quantum ring converts periodic geometric and flux modulations into an artificial superlattice whose in-plane-field immunity follows from planarity and parity, not from the smallness of the field. Non-inertial quantum dynamics on surfaces and curves of arbitrary shape is thus reduced, within the thin-layer regime, to two ingredients: an effective gauge potential and a geometric potential.

Quantum Physics.title: Experimental characterisation of compilation-dependent Grover--Rudolph probability distribution loading on a three-qubit NMR processor
Quantum Physics.summary:
Exact state-preparation circuits are normally judged by how closely the measured output distribution reproduces the target. Using the ancilla-free Grover-Rudolph construction compiled into {Ry, X, CNOT}, we ask instead how much the accuracy of a probability-distribution loading depends on which of several logically equivalent compilations is executed.
  Two Gray-code realisations of the level-2 uniformly controlled rotation, A and B, differ only in the order of their CNOT controls: same unitary, same angles. On a three-qubit liquid-state NMR processor they do not perform identically. Across 700 runs over seven targets the A/B contrast is significant for 3 of them under Holm, with no fixed sign.
  Two further campaigns isolate the effect within one unit. Removing the circuit's identity-equivalent gates, which changes the executed schedule but not the unitary, affects the two realisations differently: a ladder x intervention interaction of +0.0625 (95% CI [+0.0306, +0.0944], paired p = 4.8e-4), reversing the sign of the A/B advantage. Across five acquisitions of this one logical circuit the contrast runs from +0.0395 to -0.0229. Not every compilation choice matters: commanding the two level-1 inverse rotations as 720 deg - theta rather than -theta, with the gate list unchanged, moves the mean fidelity by -0.0006 ([-0.0157, +0.0146]) on one target in one session. We offer the order and timing of the executed pulses as the hypothesis these observations favour, without identifying a mechanism.
  The metric does not certify coherences, and the measured correlators are inconsistent with any global depolarising description: on the uniform target, at a classical fidelity of 0.962, a two-body correlation of +0.217 appears where the target has none. Run-level data and code are deposited for every campaign run on our own unit; the pulse-level campaign is reported from summary tables.

Quantum Physics.title: Native higher-order optimization with entropy quantum computing
Quantum Physics.summary: Higher-order interactions are common in applied optimization: parity checks, radar-code sidelobes, portfolio skewness and kurtosis, and marketing-channel synergies all yield cubic or quartic objectives. Quantum annealers and most Ising machines accept only quadratic objectives, and gate-based quantum processors build every higher-order term from two-qubit gates. Entropy quantum computing, realized in the hybrid photonic-electronic Dirac-3S system, accepts polynomials of degree up to five with all-to-all coupling over binary, integer or simplex-constrained continuous variables. No user-supplied quadratization or circuit compilation is needed. We formulate four industrial use cases as six cubic and quartic instances, run them on Dirac-3S with 30 samples each, and score every sample against a certified optimum or a classical best-known value. We also estimate their cost on quantum annealers, superconducting grids and trapped-ion registers under standard mappings. For the two densest instances, a portfolio with about 80,000 terms and a budget allocation with 360,000 terms, the quadratized problems need embeddings far beyond current annealers, over $10^5$ physical qubits for the portfolio alone, and one phase-separation layer costs over $10^6$ two-qubit gates before optimization. Dirac-3S ran all six natively and returned feasible, distinct solutions. All samples of the binary instances are single-flip local minima. The best portfolio sample lies within 0.32% of the best-known value and the best budget sample 15% above it, but no sample reached its reference. Classical solvers reach the references within minutes at these sizes, and random starts followed by a local polish reach comparable or better values, so the advantage established here is one of expressibility and mapping cost, not of solution quality. Whether it extends to time to solution at larger sizes remains open.

Quantum Physics.title: Construction of three-qubit positive-partial-transpose entangled states of rank four
Quantum Physics.summary: Multiqubit positive-partial-transpose (PPT) entangled states provide canonical examples of bound entanglement and stringent test cases for multipartite separability criteria. We study PPT entangled states of the minimum possible rank in the three-qubit system, namely rank four. In the established terminology, states with a nonzero Lorentz invariant are called type I, whereas those with a zero Lorentz invariant are called type II. Every such state constructed from an unextendible product basis (UPB) has a nonzero Lorentz invariant and hence is of type I. We give a necessary and sufficient criterion for determining whether a type-I state is SLOCC-equivalent to a PPT entangled state constructed from a UPB. For type-II states, we obtain a Bell-basis normal form and prove that it exhausts all such states up to SLOCC equivalence. We further give a necessary and sufficient condition for two states in this normal form to be SLOCC-equivalent. We also determine the range of the Lorentz invariant for multiqubit states.

Quantum Physics.title: Blockade-induced exchange primitives for scalable neutral-atom QPU
Quantum Physics.summary: Many quantum hardware platforms natively support either phase or exchange operations, yet converting between these two forms of control typically incurs substantial overhead. Rydberg-blockade neutral-atom arrays are highly developed for phase control. Here, controlled exchange is introduced as a native, blockade-programmed phenomenon in a collective excited manifold. Target operations are engineered such that two competing exchange pathways between |01> and |10> destructively interfere, while a single collective four-photon channel mediated by a symmetric Rydberg excitation remains resonant and drives a direct SWAP, with all other qubit configurations undergoing an identity action. Exchange conditionality follows from blockade, where exciting a control atom to a Rydberg state shifts and blocks the target collective resonance, suppressing exchange, whereas leaving the control in the ground manifold enables exchange in a single step. This approach yields a family of controlled-exchange gates with coherent average gate fidelities above 99.99% at selected operating points, while reducing circuit depth and Rydberg-state exposure time by an order of magnitude relative to decomposed implementations. Joint parameter optimization reduces sensitivity to laser-intensity fluctuations, Doppler shifts, and interatomic-distance uncertainty, with several SWAP-family gates retaining fidelities above 99.6% under realistic experimental fluctuations and Rydberg decay. Finally, the anisotropic interaction generalizes the same principle to multiplexed controlled-exchange operations, providing compact hardware-level primitives for conditional information routing in extended neutral-atom arrays.

Quantum Physics.title: Quantum theory of electrically levitated nanoparticle-ion systems: Motional dynamics and sympathetic cooling
Quantum Physics.summary: We develop the theory describing the quantum coupled dynamics of the center-of-mass motion of a nanoparticle and an ensemble of ions co-trapped in a dual-frequency linear Paul trap. We first derive analytical expressions for the motional frequencies and classical trajectories of both nanoparticle and ions. We then derive a quantum master equation for the ion-nanoparticle system and quantify the sympathetic cooling of the nanoparticle motion enabled by its Coulomb coupling to a continuously Doppler-cooled ion. We predict that motional cooling down to sub-kelvin temperatures is achievable in state-of-the-art experiments even in the absence of motional feedback and in the presence of micromotion. We then extend our analysis to an ensemble of $N$ ions, predicting a linear increase of the cooling rate as a function of N and motional cooling of the nanoparticle down to tenths of millikelvin in current experimental platforms. Our work establishes the theoretical toolbox needed to explore the ion-assisted preparation of non-Gaussian motional states of levitated nanoparticles.

Quantum Physics.title: Fisher-information limits of Compton polarimetry for entanglement-based positronium imaging with pixelated CZT detectors
Quantum Physics.summary: The polarisation correlation of the two annihilation photons, measured by Compton polarimetry, has been proposed as a PET biomarker of tissue microstructure. We quantify how many events this measurement needs, what limits that number and whether a small-animal CZT system reaches tissue-level contrasts. We parameterise the measurement by the correlation coefficient $κ$ ($κ=1$ maximally entangled, $1/2$ separable), derive the classical Fisher information of double-Compton events and compare it with the quantum Fisher information, relate $κ$ to the annihilation channels of positronium in tissue, and simulate pixelated CdZnTe (CZT) rings. The model is validated against three published measurements and an independent GATE/Geant4 simulation. A double-Compton event carries at most 0.12-0.14 units of Fisher information about $κ$ and 0.015 on average, 0.1-0.6% of the quantum limit. Event-wise maximum likelihood reaches the Cramer-Rao bound, whereas the conventional ratio R needs 1.2-2.3 times as many events. The observed coefficient is $κ_{obs}=1-α(1-κ_{pick})$ with a pick-off share $α$ of 0.13-0.29; it is sensitive to lipid fraction but not to oxygen, and published porous-polymer data give $κ_{pick}$ = 0.34-0.58. In a 15-mm CZT module, ordering ambiguity, position errors and electron transport halve the information per event, and sequence reconstruction recovers it. With $^{18}$F and an eight-module ring, $κ$ is measured to $\pm0.01$ in a 10-mm tumour with half of its decays, whereas separating tissues by $κ$ alone requires 6-74 times more decays than available.

Quantum Physics.title: Planckian bounds on thermalization times of strongly coupled open quantum systems
Quantum Physics.summary: We consider whether the thermalization of strongly coupled open quantum systems, whose equilibrium state is the mean-force Gibbs (MFG) state, is constrained by a fundamental Planckian time scale, $\hbar/k_B T$. By requiring that the same process thermalizes a family of nearby system Hamiltonians, we obtain a lower bound on the thermalization time, irrespective of the specific system-bath dynamics. The bound depends only on the distinguishability of the corresponding MFG states, and can therefore be computed from equilibrium properties alone. In its simplest form, it requires only a static susceptibility and an equilibrium variance of a system observable. We characterize this bound from weak to strong coupling in exactly solvable fermionic models, in the spin-boson model, and in a spin coupled to a two-dimensional Heisenberg antiferromagnet. These models show that strong coupling can lift the Planckian constraint when the MFG state retains little information about the system Hamiltonian, while preserving it when that information is carried by system observables with substantial equilibrium fluctuations at frequencies below $k_B T/\hbar$. The bound is complementary to open-system speed limits, since it constrains the acquisition of information rather than the preparation of the target, and can remain informative at strong coupling even when the latter become trivial.

Quantum Physics.title: Robust quantum metrology using disordered probes
Quantum Physics.summary: Disorder is ubiquitous in quantum devices including quantum probes designed and fabricated for quantum parameter estimation and sensing. We investigate the robustness of a quantum probe against the presence of glassy disorder. We define a disorder marker quantifying the effect of the disorder by expanding the quantum Fisher information in terms of different orders of the standardized central moments of the disorder-distributions. We classify the quantum probes in terms of the possible values of the disorder marker, and analytically show, for a disorder-sensitive probe with identical and weak disorder on all or a subset of the parameters of the probe-Hamiltonian, that the absolute value of the disorder marker exhibits a quadratic dependence on the disorder strength. We derive a robustness scale intrinsic to the probe that competes with the disorder, and provide a prescription for estimating the maximum disorder strength that the probe can withstand from the disorder-free probe-Hamiltonian for a given initial state of the probe, which can be computed without the disorder averaging. We also extend the prescription to classical Fisher information, and provide an operational perspective to the proposed marker in experiments. We demonstrate our results in the case of a single-qubit probe under disordered magnetic field, and a multi-qubit probe described by a disordered one-dimensional Kitaev model with nearest-neighbor interactions.

Quantum Physics.title: Intrinsically nonlinear nanomechanical resonator toward the single-phonon Kerr regime
Quantum Physics.summary: Manipulating a physical system at the single-quantum level typically requires an anharmonic energy spectrum. Nanomechanical resonators, however, are commonly admitted to be linear objects in the single-phonon regime, thus motivating most efforts to employ external sources of nonlinearity at the cost of added relaxation and decoherence channels. Here, we take a radically different approach by directly exploiting strong intrinsic mechanical nonlinearities. We quantify this nonlinearity using a novel method based on the coupling between bending modes. Using this technique, we establish an upper bound of 34.0 +/- 9.7 phonons for the onset of intrinsically mechanical bistability. In addition, we highlight a new tuning mechanism based on a mechanical polarization angle of an upward-buckled nanotube resonator allowing us to reach an optimal working point. Extrapolating this level of intrinsic nonlinearity to realistically shorter resonators shows that the single-phonon Kerr regime is within reach, allowing for the realization of purely mechanical Schrödinger-cat states and highly coherent mechanical qubits.

Quantum Physics.title: Squeezing-preserving coherent control in Fourier-shaped optical lattices
Quantum Physics.summary: Motional squeezed states of atoms in optical lattices are affected by the anharmonicity of the trapping potential. Unequal vibrational energy spacings cause dephasing among the occupied motional-state coherences, leading to distortion of the wavepacket and a reduction in squeezing. We show numerically that adding a weak second or third spatial harmonic to a one-dimensional lattice slows the initial decay of the squeezing. Squeezed states are prepared by one or two sudden changes of the lattice depth. For each harmonic and each preparation scheme, we choose the harmonic amplitude that keeps the evolved state closest, on average over 1 ms, to its evolution in a harmonic trap. We then compare the squeezing with that in a sinusoidal lattice with the same initial squeezing and trap frequency. In all four cases studied, the successive squeezing maxima initially decay more slowly in the shaped lattice. The improvement arises because the optimal harmonic nearly equalizes the two dominant vibrational level spacings over the region occupied by the squeezed wave packet, which canceling the quartic term of the potential alone does not achieve. Because the amplitude of the added harmonic is static and can be produced with existing Fourier-synthesis techniques, lattice shaping offers a simple way to preserve motional squeezing without additional time-dependent control.

Quantum Physics.title: On the performance of nanoscale detection methods in NV-center spectroscopy
Quantum Physics.summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) in subfemtoliter volumes operates in a regime where statistical fluctuations of the nuclear magnetization can exceed its thermal mean. Solid-state quantum sensors such as nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamond are sensitive enough to detect NMR signals from such small volumes, which has motivated several detection protocols, based either on correlating the statistical polarization or on coherently detecting hyperpolarized samples. Here we bring Qdyne, CS, MCS, and CASR into a single framework for nanoscale samples. Specifically, we derive a unified analytical expression for the SNR and spin-number sensitivity applicable to all four protocols under consistent experimental conditions. Numerical simulations of the full measurement sequences confirm this expression over the whole range of parameters explored. This formulation enables a quantitative comparison of their performance while accounting for the distinct measurement sequences, acquisition times, and other related parameters. Using the SNR and the spin-number sensitivity as figures of merit, we identify which protocol performs best in each experimental regime, thereby providing a practical guide for choosing and tuning the most suitable method for a given experiment.

Quantum Physics.title: Cross-chip transfer in quantum photonic neural networks
