We turn measurement-free quantum error correction---syndrome-free coherent feedback---into a probe: bit-flip and phase-flip codes polarize a few-qubit coherent error into single-logical-qubit channels, and seven identify an eleven-parameter three-qubit generator. Three references are read with the spectators in $|0\ldots0\rangle$, two with the spectators in $|+\ldots+\rangle$, and two are the code channels; each one single-qubit tomography, so the fingerprint is $112$ components at $84$ settings. An exact rational-arithmetic rank certificate proves local injectivity on a dense open subset, with the smallest singular value between $1.75$ and $1.83$ over $500$ sampled points, so conditioning is uniform, not merely finite. The $|0\ldots0\rangle$ references alone are not globally injective: a compensating rotation combined with the site exchange gives exact collisions; we classify them completely: the reflection is the only nontrivial permutation symmetry of the $n$-qubit generator. The $|+\ldots+\rangle$ references remove that ambiguity by construction and separate every nontrivial mirror pair. Because they dephase in proportion to the spectator magnetization, they also make visible the out-of-family Pauli directions---including the common $Z_{1}Z_{3}$ crosstalk---that a $|0\ldots0\rangle$ reference absorbs at first order. A Cramér--Rao analysis reaches $0.01$ rad per parameter with $1.5\times10^{3}$ shots per component, $1.3\times10^{5}$ events at twelve settings per channel, and a per-gate calibration allowance of $1.6\times10^{-2}$, so the probe is shot-noise limited. In a distance-three surface code the generator gives a $14.8$-fold encoding gain per site and a further $1.24$-fold ($1.21$-fold from an estimate) from the recovered correlations.

Quantum Physics.title: The Bilateral Efficiency of Ethernet: Recalibrating Metcalfe and Boggs After Fifty Years
Quantum Physics.summary: In July 1976, Metcalfe and Boggs published their foundational paper on Ethernet in Communications of the ACM. Their efficiency model -- E = (P/C)/(P/C + W*T) -- measures the fraction of Ether time carrying good forward packets under contention. For fifty years this model has framed how the community thinks about Ethernet performance. We argue it is silent on the question that matters for modern intra-rack interconnect: bilateral transaction efficiency -- the fraction of link time that produces committed agreements between sender and receiver. Metcalfe and Boggs themselves planted the seed in their EFTP "end-dally" protocol (Section 7.2.2), and the deeper anchor is older still: Abramson's Alohanet carried positive acknowledgments at the link layer -- a bilateral mechanism Metcalfe consciously removed in 1973 to obtain Ethernet's simple, ACK-free packet format. The result is a fifty-year bilateral zigzag: Aloha (bilateral) to Ethernet (unilateral) to the EFTP end-dally (bilateral) to TCP (unilateral-with-bilateral-above). We formalize bilateral efficiency, connect it to the back-to-back Shannon channel with Perfect Information Feedback, and -- scoping the claim explicitly to intra-rack distances of one meter or less -- describe how the Open Aethernet link recovers mutual knowledge at the link layer. The correction to Table 1 is not a different set of numbers. It is a different question. A new appendix places the 2025-2026 return of link-level retry (UEC, OCP ESUN, UALink) in this history and shows that it restores half of the end-dally: the sender learns of delivery, the receiver never learns that the sender knows. It opens from Ron Crane's observation that produced Fast Ethernet: carried to 100 Gb/s, the same arithmetic makes the minimum frame about one meter long.
Quantum Physics.comment: 23 pages, with appendices on the Open Aethernet fault model and the return of link-level retry. 50th anniversary of Metcalfe and Boggs (1976). v4: bilateral efficiency counts committed and complete transactions; Appendix B carries Ron Crane's Fast Ethernet arithmetic to 100 Gb/s and reads the 2025-2026 link-level retry of UEC, ESUN, UALink and IEEE 802 contributions against the end-dally

Quantum Physics.title: High-Dimensional Single-Photon Frequency Conversion for Orbital Angular Momentum Comb State
Quantum Physics.summary: The orbital angular momentum (OAM) degree of freedom provides an important resource for constructing high-dimensional optical quantum information systems. However, the generation of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state and its high-fidelity frequency conversion remain challenging due to limited spatial modulation resolution, imperfect mode matching, and finite nonlinear conversion efficiency. Here, we proposed and experimentally demonstrated a scalable scheme for the generation and frequency conversion of high-dimensional single-photon OAM comb state. We prepared a single-photon OAM comb state with a dimension of up to 128, achieving a fidelity of 0.787 between the reconstructed and target states and an effective dimension of 100. Furthermore, using the sum-frequency generation, we demonstrated the frequency upconversion of single-photon high-dimensional OAM comb state from the communication band to a visible wavelength of 520 nm, while verifying the preservation of both the OAM mode distribution and phase information through density matrix reconstruction. Our work established a versatile platform for the generation, manipulation, and characterization of high-dimensional OAM comb states, with potential applications in cross-band quantum information transfer, high-capacity quantum communication, and high-dimensional quantum networks.

Quantum Physics.title: Adaptive identification of low-degree polynomials in quantum singular value transformation: application to nonlinear quantum properties estimation
Quantum Physics.summary: Estimating properties of unknown quantum states via quantum singular value transformation (QSVT) often requires high-degree polynomials to handle small eigenvalues of density matrices. Specifically, the existing approaches determine the polynomial degree by relying on overly conservative worst-case bounds based on the minimum non-zero eigenvalue or the rank of the density matrices. In this work, we propose a spectral cutoff method that truncates the negligible eigenvalue tail depending on the task, the target accuracy, and the state, which enables the use of significantly lower-degree polynomials. To implement this, we develop a two-stage algorithm to estimate nonlinear properties, particularly von Neumann entropy and R{é}nyi entropy. In the first stage, we execute a search algorithm to identify the spectral cutoff directly from the unknown quantum state. In the second stage, we estimate the nonlinear properties utilizing QSVT with the degree of the polynomial adaptively determined by the cutoff. This two-stage algorithm enables adaptive property estimation without prior knowledge of the minimum eigenvalue or the rank, using low-degree polynomials beyond conventional worst-case choices.
Quantum Physics.comment: Final version; almost same as publication

Quantum Physics.title: Recovery gates as a resource in repetition-code process tomography: exhaustive gate-optimal designs for three, five and seven qubits
Quantum Physics.summary: Repetition-code tomography compares a code's logical channel with a reference through a decoder, almost always standard minimum-weight. We ask how many single-qubit Pauli gates it needs with the measurement basis fixed---the constraint that makes the count a resource. Exhaustive enumeration at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$, ranks decided in exact arithmetic, gives minima of $0$, $1$ and $5$ gates, against $6$, $10$ and $14$ for first-order and $6$, $50$ and $308$ for full decoding. The count depends only on how many sites are corrected, not which, so it splits into a budget and a placement that decides identifiability; more sites is not monotonically better: at $n=7$ full decoding has rank $24$ of $27$, and the $n=3$ precision curve is U-shaped under a calibration floor. The three-gate design is $9.0$ times more precise than the standard six-gate decoder at the median of $40$ working points and better at every one, by $1.8$ to $88$-fold; fixing the placement in advance gives $6.9$, or $3.1$ for a pre-commitment never worse. Two certified placements lose no direction either sees and reach $10$\,mrad within twice the shots wherever identifiable. Measuring the reference everywhere gives a $16(n+2)$-component map, full rank at $n=3$, $5$ and $7$ with no gate and $44$ to $93\%$ fewer settings, though at $n=5$ and $7$ its floor stays one and three orders above target. The optima are not covariant under chain reversal.
Quantum Physics.comment: 21 pages, 2 figures, 6 tables. Ancillary files: gate_count_analysis.zip (code and result records, with a SHA-256 manifest). Experimental supplement: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23993246. Supplementary note for Sec. 5: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24241028. Companion to arXiv:2610.19779

Quantum Physics.title: Matter-wave Interferometers as Open-system Dark Matter Detectors
Quantum Physics.summary: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) offer a uniquely quantum route to dark matter (DM) detection: DM can reveal itself through phase and decoherence between spatially separated wavepackets, even when energy deposition is negligible and no resolvable recoil displacement occurs. We formulate these effects in an open effective field theory for MWIs using the Schwinger--Keldysh formalism, which highlights a structural asymmetry between the two detection channels. For elastic spin-independent DM scattering, decoherence inherits novel Bose enhancement or Pauli blocking factors, while the phase is at most linear in the DM occupation number. By retaining the DM's coherence time, this framework spans Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics across a wide range of DM masses, and systematically organizes corrections beyond the heavy-probe limit.
Quantum Physics.comment: 6 pages + supplemental material, 1 figure. v2: Fixed typos, harmonized notation and conventions with arXiv:2610.36044, and expanded the Supplemental Material

Quantum Physics.title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
Quantum Physics.summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) requires a large number of physical qubits to encode logical qubits with sufficiently low error rates. Silicon spin qubits are a promising platform because of their small footprint, compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing technologies, and demonstrated high-fidelity operations. However, realizing a scalable architecture that supports quantum error correction, qubit transport, wiring, and logical gate operations remains a major challenge. Here, we propose a scalable dense silicon spin qubit architecture designed to support large-scale FTQC. The architecture consists of qubit memories, data qubit lanes, and cross junctions. Qubit memories store logical qubits encoded using the rotated surface code and support logical single-qubit operations. Data qubit lanes enable high-speed one-dimensional spin shuttling for connectivity between logical qubits, while cross junctions provide routing functionality and implement transversal logical CNOT gates. Using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin qubit parameters, we evaluate logical error rates as a function of code distance and estimate that a code distance of at least 21 is required to achieve logical error rates below $10^{-10}$ per syndrome cycle. We further analyze wiring constraints based on CMOS-compatible multiplexed control schemes and show that, with optimized wiring efficiency, more than 120,000 logical qubits could be integrated on a 100 mm $\times$ 100 mm chip. These results provide a practical roadmap toward large-scale FTQC based on silicon spin qubit technology.

Quantum Physics.title: RubriQ: Rubric-Guided Group Relative Policy Optimization for Constraint-Aware Quantum Circuit Synthesis
Quantum Physics.summary: Quantum circuits are crucial for understanding quantum algorithms and must be correct and efficient on quantum processing units (QPUs). Reinforcement learning (RL) with verifiers can train large language models (LLMs) to synthesize circuits; however, the reward system is unclear. In this study, we present RubriQ, a quantum rubric, where a verifier ensures correctness and scores assess cost. We demonstrate that, leveraging group relative policy optimization, the verifier controls correctness, while scores rank correct circuits. Our evaluation includes unitary, statevector, stabilizer-tableau, and randomized verifiers consisting of quantum Fourier transform (QFT), phase-estimation (QPE), and Trotter unitaries, along with Clifford, entanglement, unitary, arithmetic, and adder quantum circuits, up to 192 qubits. Our results show that training increases correct outputs from 7% to 91%, whereas the binary reward closes less than 10%. Notably, among verified circuits, the rubric reduces average cost by 91%. We believe our framework provides valuable insights into practical quantum computing.

Quantum Physics.title: Locally Acting Grover Mixers for Constraint-Preserving QAOA
Quantum Physics.summary: The Grover mixer quantum alternating operator ansatz (GM-QAOA) employs the Grover mixer to confine the quantum evolution to the feasible subspace defined by the problem. Its mixing unitary, however, requires a global multi-controlled phase-shift gate acting on all qubits, resulting in substantial circuit overhead on near-term quantum devices. In this work, we propose locally acting Grover mixers with independent variational parameters, tailored to initial states that admit a product structure over disjoint qubit subsystems, which may be obtained by encoding only a subset of problem constraints into the initial state preparation. The proposed method preserves the search space defined by the initial state while reducing the mixing-circuit gate count and depth relative to the global Grover mixer, as the global multi-controlled phase-shift gate is replaced with local operations on disjoint subsystems. Numerical simulations on the exact-cover problem and the traveling salesman problem (TSP) demonstrate that the proposed method achieves solution probabilities comparable to those of the original GM-QAOA, while using shallower circuits with fewer gates. Comparisons with shared-angle local Grover and partitioned XY-ring mixers characterize the trade-offs between solution quality, circuit complexity, and optimization overhead. We further compare two constraint encoding strategies for the TSP, encoding only a subset of constraints versus all constraints into the initial state preparation, and show that the former combined with the proposed mixer can yield markedly more compact circuits at the point where comparable solution quality is achieved.

Quantum Physics.title: Robust Certification of Non-projective Qubit Measurements without Inputs
Quantum Physics.summary: Positive-operator-valued measures (POVMs) beyond projective simulation (aka non-projective measurements) offer advantages over projective measurements, motivating their certification directly from observed statistics. Here, we show that this certification can be achieved robustly without input randomness, using only the joint outcome distribution of two measurement devices. We consider two spatially separated observers whose only shared resource is an uncharacterised two-qubit state. Each observer performs a local measurement. In the projective-simulable case, the measurement device privately randomises over qubit projective measurements and applies arbitrary classical post-processing to their outcomes. In the noiseless regime, we identify three- and four-outcome anti-correlations that certify that both local measurements lie beyond projective simulation. To establish noise robustness, we develop a non-linear covariance witness that combines the geometry of projective measurements with a contraction bound valid for every two-qubit state. For the correlations generated by identical qubit trine measurements or identical qubit SIC-POVM on noisy qubit singlet, we obtain exact critical white-noise fractions of (1/4) and (1/3), respectively. Below these thresholds, no pair of projective-simulable measurements on any two-qubit state can reproduce these correlations. We present explicit projective simulations that attain the thresholds and cover the remaining noise range. Finally, the same method yields a strictly positive noise tolerance for certification whenever both observers apply the same extremal qubit POVM with three or four non-zero effects to a depolarised qubit singlet. These results establish a general analytic framework for certifying non-projective qubit measurement resources without input randomness.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: KEBBABS: Kilometric Enhanced Balloon-Baseline for Axion Birefringence Search
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We propose a broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter through the rotation of laser polarization induced by the axion--photon coupling. Two stratospheric balloons flying at altitudes of 30--40 km form a free-space optical link. One balloon sends a linearly polarized beam to the other, which reflects it back to a polarimeter on the first balloon. The long physical baseline provides an alternative to the repeated reflections used in resonant optical cavities. We target axion masses in the range $4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_a\lesssim10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. The lower edge corresponds to a frequency of about $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, below which gondola roll about the line of sight can mimic a polarization signal. At $m_a=10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$, a low-cost Pathfinder using flight-demonstrated technology could probe couplings as small as $g_{aγ}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, about a factor of two below the CAST bound. At the same mass, the Feasible today configuration could probe couplings just below the astrophysical bounds considered here, while the Futuristic configuration could reach $g_{aγ}\simeq6.4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, roughly two orders of magnitude below those bounds.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite $G_N$. We promote its canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. Equipped with this, we use Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation, for which this algebra generates a type I factor. By composing amplitudes between states prepared on null cones, we then obtain a Lorentzian path integral in which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. As a check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in $G_N$ and find a finite closed form expression, even though expanding first in $G_N$ yields a logarithmic divergence. We next use diffeomorphism invariance of the path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given maximum size has a finite dimensional Hilbert space. From the Lorentzian trace we obtain the Bekenstein Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large Schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient Sen obtained through Euclidean methods. We end by deriving the semiclassical Einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Vacuum correlation measures as CFT partition functions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show that in any $d$-dimensional CFT, the vacuum sandwiched Rényi mutual information (SRMI) of integer order $n$ between two disjoint balls maps to a CFT partition function on a manifold of topology $\#^{n-1}(S^1 \times S^{d-1})$, with moduli fixed by the ball configuration and single-ball modular flow. At $n=2$, it is given by the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, upper-bounding the von Neumann mutual information. For $n>2$, SRMI diverges at finite separation due to a hot-spot limit of the partition function. Explicit CFT evaluations agree well with density matrix computations.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Separation of variables for non-diagonalisable models: XXX with twisted boundary conditions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the Heisenberg XXX spin chain with twisted periodic boundary conditions with a defective twist matrix. Using quantum separation of variables, we show that the generalised eigenvectors of this system can be characterised in terms of a modified TQ equation that we have named "Jordanian TQ equation". We also show that the wavefunction in the separated basis is only separable for true eigenvectors, while the wavefunction for generalised eigenvectors of higher rank is given instead by a sum over weak compositions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 24 pages. v2, Typos corrected, references updated. v3, Typos corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Time-weighted energy correlators are infrared unsafe in gauge theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Energy correlators are infrared safe because each detector weights a parton by its energy, but a weight in the arrival time makes them infrared unsafe in gauge theories. For the state created by a scalar operator that makes two partons at lowest order in a weakly coupled conformal gauge theory, we show that the correlator of two time-weighted energy detectors (the light-ray operators $\int\!du\,u\,T_{uu}$) at separated directions diverges at two loops like the logarithm of the time window. The logarithm does not come from a single soft gluon, but from a soft parton pair with comparable energies, one parton in each detector; its coefficient is a closed-form function of the angle for any matter content. In $N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, we recover this coefficient from the two-gluon Regge term of the known four-point function and derive a simple relation to the logarithm in the charge correlator. In the planar theory the leading logarithms resum to a power of the window, set by the BFKL intercept.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 8 pages. v2: Fixed orientation consistency issues and typos

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Character expansion of the Itzykson-Zuber pair correlator
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We revisit a long-standing problem of correlation functions with the Harish-Chandra-Itzykson-Zuber measure. The immediate goal is to reproduce the long-known answer for pair correlator in the form of character expansion - a sum over Schur polynomials with carefully adjusted coefficients. The infinite sum can be folded up into exponentials with the help of the Cauchy identity. What matters are the coefficients, which we express in terms of projectors, made from Cherednik operators. Development of character expansion methods for unitary integrals, which are much more difficult than the Hermitian ones, gives a hope for further generalizations - up to arbitrary correlators with non-trivial measures.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. In the extremal case, the spectral data comprises the zeros of the boundary source function, i.e. the QNMs, as well as its phase discontinuity across the branch cut on the negative imaginary axis of the complex frequency plane. This formula neatly factorizes into an infinite product over the QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity. We derive this pole-cut formula as the zero-temperature limit of the QNM product formula for holographic thermal correlators, with the branch-cut contribution arising from the coalescence of the QNMs on the negative imaginary axis. We also clarify the role of the near-horizon $AdS_2$ region in this context. Consistency with the OPE of the boundary correlator provides extremal sum-rules involving both the QNMs as well as the phase discontinuity function. We also find that this holographic consistency forces the asymptotic form of the QNMs to be related to the asymptotics of the phase discontinuity function. We verify our formula and these OPE constraints numerically. We also demonstrate that, in the time domain, the pole and cut factors each produce complex-time singularities, whose location is determined by the optical distance between the boundary and the black-brane singularity. We expect the pole-cut factorization structure of spectral functions to hold for more general fluctuations of extremal black branes.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $ν_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, plus End Matter and Supplemental Material

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schrödinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless Pöschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Minor changes, typos corrected and references added

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Logarithmic scalar soft factorization from matching conditions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Logarithmic soft theorems in QED and gravity can be understood as conservation laws associated with asymptotic symmetries. In contrast, for a massless scalar, no gauge symmetry is available to organize this relation. Despite that, we show that the logarithmic soft factorization for a massless scalar coupled to massive fermions through a Yukawa interaction follows from the asymptotic field equations and matching conditions at spatial infinity. From the first subleading logarithmic fall-off, we construct a conserved surface integral whose boundary values satisfy the antipodal map between past and future null infinity. At future null infinity, the field equations relate this quantity to the $1/u$ tail of the scalar radiation, while at past null infinity, for scattering states without incoming scalar radiation, it is carried by a non-radiative logarithm of the incoming particles. We derive the classical tail from the particle trajectories and obtain the hard charge from the asymptotic Dirac current. The particular solution of the leading scalar field gives the classical contribution, while its homogeneous component gives the quantum contribution. The resulting Ward identity reproduces the logarithmic soft coefficient of the one-loop scalar emission (up to a zero mode on the sphere), including its classical and quantum parts.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Realizing Braided Fusion 2-Categories as (3+1)D Mixed-State Topological Orders
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct large families of mixed-state topological orders in (3+1)D, including intrinsically mixed-state topological orders. We realize these theories by relating the data parameterizing braided fusion 2-categories to the strong higher-form symmetries and their anomalies that characterize mixed-state topological order. We focus here on bosonic theories, which include theories which admit an emergent fermion in the spectrum of line operators. Our general framework is exemplified on the lattice, where we present concrete models and identify how the data of braided fusion 2-categories are physically encoded. We then formalize this data and show that every braided fusion 2-category arises from a general construction (decoherence followed by strong and weak gauging) as the category of topological operators of a (3+1)D mixed state, with intrinsically mixed-state topological orders distinguished by the presence of strong higher-form symmetries whose anomalies cannot be realized in any (3+1)D gapped ground state. Notably, we show that (3+1)D admits a new mechanism with no (2+1)D counterpart: intrinsically mixed-state order whose topological operators braid non-degenerately, but which carries a gravitational anomaly.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Tensionless M5-brane in light-cone gauge. The spinor moving frame method is wanted
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We perform the complete light--cone gauge fixing for the tensionless limit of the M-theory 5-brane the action for which was recently obtained in [1]. The problem of gauge fixing of local fermionic $κ$--symmetry becomes quite nontrivial because the projector of that is constructed from the gauge field strength which is required to be nonvanishing and nontrivial in this limit for its consistency. To resolve this problem the spinor moving frame method has been adapted. The corresponding moving frame is constructed on a vector quadratic in the gauge field strength, which is required to be nonvanishing and nondegenerate in the tensionless limit, and the derivative of the PST (Pasti-Sorokin-Tonin) scalar. The symmetries of the gauge fixed action and equations of motion are briefly discussed. To make a comparison with the case of usual tensionless p-branes (null-p-branes), those which do not carry worldvolume gauge fields, we also elaborate their spinor moving frame formulation.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 26 pages. V2: A few misprints corrected. RevTex style, 19 pages

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Rényi multi-entropy from Riemann surfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute vacuum tripartite Rényi multi-entropy in a two-dimensional compact-boson conformal field theory (CFT). For every integer Rényi index $n\geq2$, we evaluate the partition function on the replica Riemann surface for disjoint intervals, obtaining the twist four-point function in terms of a ratio of theta functions. An independent calculation of the partition function on a Fermat curve yields the adjacent three-point coefficient. In the fusion limit, the Riemann surface for disjoint intervals degenerates into two Fermat curves, and the residue of the four-point function reproduces the squared three-point coefficient, as required by the operator product expansion. The genuine multi-entropy therefore approaches twice its strictly adjacent value. The CFT predictions agree with lattice calculations for the critical XXZ and Ising spin chains and a harmonic chain. We also exhibit a unitary CFT in which the canonical replica construction yields complex Rényi multi-entropy.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrtΘ$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $Θ$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order $\sqrtΘ$ at fixed areal radius. Holding the proper distance fixed, it cancels this term and recovers the common Rindler response close to the horizon. For a freely falling atom, emission and absorption obey detailed balance at the Hawking temperature in the leading horizon approximation. Random atomic injection drives the selected mode from the vacuum to a thermal state with an exact relaxation law and nonnegative entropy production. Near equilibrium, we obtain $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/4$ when the radiated energy is drawn from horizon heat, where $\dot A_p$ is the positive radiative area loss. When the radiation is assigned to ADM mass loss at fixed smearing length $\ell=4\sqrt{Θ/π}$, the result is $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/[4(1-\ell/r_+)]$. The mass dependence of the exterior source thus enters the entropy per unit area lost at order $\sqrtΘ$.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Interfaces in Long Range CFT$_1$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We consider interfaces in the theory of a single free scalar in AdS$_2$ defined by adding relevant operators along portions of the boundary. We begin with Neumann/Dirichlet interfaces, computing the associated scaling dimension and $g$-factor ratio; we also explain how arbitrary interface correlators can be computed numerically efficiently. Then we move on to interfaces between generalized free field and long-range interacting theories such as long range Ising, determining many quantities in perturbation theory. Finally we setup a bootstrap problem for four-point interface correlator. We use this to find tight bounds on the $g$-factor ratio as a function of the interface scaling dimension.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Comments on entanglement entropy in the $c=1$ string theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study entanglement entropy in the low-energy effective field theory of two-dimensional string theory as well as in the singlet sector of the dual $c=1$ matrix quantum mechanics. From the target space perspective, we argue that a generic bulk subregion is expected to have an associated generalized entanglement entropy combining a dilaton-dependent gravitational term and a matter contribution coming from the tachyon, extending the construction from black hole horizons to arbitrary subregions. Motivated by the absence of the gravitational area-like term in previous analyses of entanglement entropy in the $c=1$ model, we compute the effect on the entanglement entropy of the nonlocal transformation induced by the leg-pole factor that relates the target space tachyon and the matrix model collective excitations, finding that it cannot account for the area-like term. We offer preliminary comments on the possible origin of the area term in the non-singlet sectors of the theory.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 26 pages + appendices, 3 figures. Updated to match the published version, including a change of title

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Hadrons in group expansion
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We develop a general framework for describing symmetry-breaking responses in physical systems with approximate symmetries. Hadronic systems provide a particularly rich setting for investigating such symmetries. For example, the flavor $SU(4)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, $s$, and $c$ quarks is severely broken, the flavor $SU(3)$ symmetry involving the $u$, $d$, and $s$ quarks is moderately broken, and the isospin $SU(2)$ symmetry involving the $u$ and $d$ quarks is only slightly broken. An important question is how a physical system responds to further symmetry breaking when its symmetry has already been partially broken. Motivated by the observed mass nonadditivity of vector mesons, we formulate this framework in terms of the group expansion, in which higher-order responses may modify the coefficients within the inherited response space or unlock additional independent response directions outside this space. We refer to these two effects as coefficient evolution and response unlocking, respectively, and develop a differential description connecting the interaction flow, mass flow, and state flow. We apply this framework to $J^P=1^-$ vector mesons and $J^P=3/2^+$ and $1/2^+$ baryons within flavor $SU(4)$ and $SU(5)$ reference spaces. These analyses illustrate how the internal structure and dynamics of a physical system, together with additional symmetries, can shape and constrain its symmetry-breaking responses. The group expansion thus provides a unified framework for organizing the evolution, correlations, and constraints of symmetry-breaking responses, with potential applications beyond hadronic systems.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 55 pages, 5 figures, 14 tables; major revision with an expanded theoretical framework and new applications to baryons

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
For every finite subgroup $Γ\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincaré pairing on $S^3/Γ$.
  In particular, $Γ$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Zero Mode Constraint in the Dirac-Bergmann Analysis of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Type Equations
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive the Hamiltonian formulation of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) equation from a singular Lagrangian by means of the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm. The Lagrangian contains an auxiliary field, which leads to an irregular secondary constraint. On the branch that reproduces the KP equation, all constraints are second class, and the Dirac brackets give the known Hamiltonian and Poisson operator. We confirm these results by the Faddeev-Jackiw method. Then, we consider fields periodic in the first spatial coordinate. In this case, the zero modes of the derivative operator lead to an additional secondary constraint on the mean of the potential. This constraint replaces the inverse derivative by its zero mean counterpart, and the resulting Hamiltonian is in accordance with the one of Reiman and Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii, up to normalization conventions. For decaying fields, the same condition is necessary for rapidly decreasing potentials to remain rapidly decreasing. We show that this constraint appears for a general class of KP-type equations. In addition, we classify the smooth solutions of the auxiliary-field action. We also relate our results to an existing quantization of the KP equation, for which the potential Lagrangian provides an action.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Genuine multientropy, dihedral invariants and Lifshitz theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Multi-invariants are local-unitary invariants of state replicas introduced as potential probes of multipartite entanglement and correlations in quantum many-body systems. In this paper, we investigate two multi-invariants for tripartite pure states, namely multientropy and dihedral invariant. We compute the (genuine) multientropy for Lifshitz groundstates, and obtain its analytical continuation to noninteger values of Rényi index. We show that the genuine multientropy can be expressed in terms of mutual information and logarithmic negativity, a relation that also holds for stabilizer states. For general tripartite pure states, we demonstrate that dihedral invariants are related to Rényi reflected entropies. In particular, we show that the dihedral permutations of replicas are equivalent to the reflected construction, or alternatively to the realignment of density matrices.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 6+14 pages, 2+7 figures ; v2: minor modifications, refs added ; v3: matches published version; v4: minor typos corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: A perturbative approach to the non-relativistic string spectrum
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this letter we use a perturbative approach to find the spectrum of non-relativistic strings in the String Newton-Cartan (SNC) AdS$_5\times$S$^5$ spacetime. We perturb the bosonic sector of the action around a BMN-like folded string solution in light-cone gauge. We find strong evidence that the theory is described by a combination of massive and massless free fields in an anti-de Sitter background by showing that interaction terms up to six scalars vanish after field redefinitions.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 11 pages. v2: match published version. v3: typos corrected. v4: more typos corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The all-loop spectrum of GGK strings
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the non-perturbative spectrum of the non-relativistic limit of string theory in AdS$_5\times$S$^5$, also known as GGK theory. In light-cone gauge, we show that the bosonic spectrum on a number of vacua is described at all-loops by free massive and massless scalar fields in AdS$_2$, confirming a conjecture by de Leeuw, Fontanella and Nieto-García, arXiv:2403.09563. In static gauge, we obtain the same result for any classical string vacuum, and including fermions. We compute the quantum correction to the classical energy, and show that it vanishes once we adopt the regularised Hurwitz series. We conclude that the quantum energy spectrum built upon any GGK string consists solely of its classical vacuum energy.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Reflected entropy and Markov gap in Lifshitz theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the reflected entropy in $(1+1)$--dimensional Lifshitz field theory whose groundstate is described by a quantum mechanical model. Starting from tripartite Lifshitz groundstates, both critical and gapped, we derive explicit formulas for the Rényi reflected entropies reduced to two adjacent or disjoint intervals, directly in the continuum. We show that the reflected entropy in Lifshitz theory does not satisfy monotonicity, in contrast to what is observed for free relativistic fields. We analytically compute the full reflected entanglement spectrum for two disjoint intervals, finding a discrete set of eigenvalues which is that of a thermal density matrix. Furthermore, we investigate the Markov gap, defined as the difference between reflected entropy and mutual information, and find it to be universal and nonvanishing, signaling irreducible tripartite entanglement in Lifshitz groundstates. We also obtain analytical results for the reflected entropies and the Markov gap in $2 + 1$ dimensions. Finally, as a byproduct of our results on reflected entropy, we provide exact formulas for two other entanglement-related quantities, namely the computable cross-norm negativity and the operator entanglement entropy.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 34 pages, 12 figures; v2: minor corrections, matches published version; v3: minor typos corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Tripartite entanglement dynamics following a quantum quench
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the dynamics of multipartite entanglement after quenches from initial states which generate multiplets of quasiparticle excitations beyond the usual pair structure. We focus on the dynamics of tripartite entanglement through the lens of the Markov gap -- a computable quantity that signals irreducible tripartite entanglement when positive. In the tight-binding chain, we show that the Markov gap is positive at intermediate times, implying the presence of tripartite entanglement. After a time delay, the Markov gap increases and then decays at longer times, thus exhibiting an entanglement barrier. We argue that those qualitative features are consistent with an interpretation of the spreading of tripartite entanglement by triplets of tripartite-entangled quasiparticles.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 3+3 pages, 3+2 figures; v2: minor typos corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Power-law tunneling in the Razavy hyperbolic double well: Heun connection formulas and their resonances
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study nonperturbative level splitting in the symmetric Razavy hyperbolic double well, relating its double-confluent Heun connection problem to exact WKB and quasi-exact solvability. In the weak-coupling limit the wells separate logarithmically and approach two Morse systems. Reflection factorizes the two-ended spectral condition into separate even and odd quantization conditions. For each normalizable Morse level with noninteger decay exponent, the irregular-block connection formula yields the leading splitting with its full gamma-function coefficient, two analytic fluctuation corrections, and the leading logarithmic three-traversal contribution. The noninteger power of the coupling follows from the logarithmic growth of the barrier action. We express the classical periods in terms of complete elliptic integrals and derive the first quantum-period correction. At integer exponent, a convergent reduction onto the two resonant Floquet modes resolves the singular fixed-order expansion into two local spectral branches and reproduces the known finite-spin tunneling gap.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof [arXiv:1105.3445] assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state-operator duality. The asymptotic horizon charge is the momentum of a quantum clock; its conjugate gives the reading. The modular crossed product admits density operators whose entropy with respect to its trace reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time measurement of surprisal, the negative logarithm of the density operator, gives an FT for the complete exterior channel. It identifies the correction for a nonunital channel and gives a GSL bound for unital evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that preserves every dressed-charge sector and the full faithful dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The bounds establish the GSL in the slow-clock limit when the errors vanish and quantify what is needed at finite clock width.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 34 pages and 5 figures; v2. Polish the logic chains and wording; add references

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Smooth binary evolution from wide resonances in boson clouds
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Ultralight scalars can form superradiant clouds around rotating black holes. These may alter the dynamics of compact binaries and the ensuing waveform through orbital resonances and cloud ionization. We re-examine resonances involving states with nonzero decay width, deriving an effective treatment for resonances that are wider than the binary's frequency chirp. We demonstrate the utility of this approach by calculating an upper bound for the cloud's mass surviving up to the latest stages of the inspiral. Next, we study the accumulation of resonances with high-energy bound states. When these infinitely many, increasingly weak resonances are properly taken into account, they smooth out the "sharp features" in the binary's evolution that had been attributed to the ionization of the cloud. We compare our Newtonian results with recent relativistic calculations, highlighting common features as well as discrepancies. Our conclusions emphasize the need to carefully incorporate resonances in boson cloud waveform modeling.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. Very minor update: regenerated figures with higher numerical precision

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Superconformal Index Identities for Dual Gauge Theories
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study superconformal index identities for three classes of dual four-dimensional gauge theories. For $\mathcal N=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory with gauge groups $SO(2n+1)$ and $USp(2n)$, we prove at every rank the equality of flavored Schur indices predicted by $S$-duality, using Rains's diagonal trace transformation. For Kutasov--Schwimmer duality with adjoint superpotential $\textrm{Tr} X^{k+1}$, we prove the index identity between $SU(k+1)$ and $SU(k-1)$ with two flavors at independent elliptic nomes $p,q$, in the ultraviolet assignment $R(Q)=0$. On the locus $p=q^k$, we reduce the identity to that of ordinary supersymmetric QCD whenever the specialized expressions are generically regular. Finally, we test the dualities conjectured by Cho and Song between quiver and single-group descriptions of four families of Argyres--Douglas theories. For the rank-one $H_1$ theory we prove equality of the two full flavored indices, and for each family at arbitrary rank we evaluate the generalized Coulomb index in both descriptions, obtaining the product formula conjectured by Buican and Jiang.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_φ/n_{φ,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quark-Loop Corrections and Auxiliary Field-Strength Mixing in First-Order QCD
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In the first-order formulation of Yang-Mills theory the gluon field strength is an independent auxiliary field $F$, and the only gluon self-interaction is a momentum-independent cubic vertex. We determine how quarks, which couple only to the gauge field, act on this structure. Their divergences are multiples of $f(A)\cdot f(A)$, a term absent from the first-order Lagrangian that no rescaling can produce. Working with the background-field method in a general covariant gauge, we find that the quark sector is renormalized entirely by the mixing of the auxiliary field with the field strength known from pure Yang-Mills theory, $F_0=F+z\,f(A)$, with quark coefficient $z=-α_sT_FN_f/(6π\barε)$, together with a rescaling of the gluon field and no rescaling of $F$, so that the renormalized auxiliary field runs into the gluon field strength. When a heavy quark of mass $M$ is integrated out, the same mixing survives as a finite threshold coefficient $c=(α_sT_F/6π)\ln(M^2/μ^2)$, whose scale dependence is exactly the heavy-quark share of the running, and the invariant combination of the couplings reproduces the decoupling of $α_s$. Below the threshold, when the leading power correction is kept as a gauge-sector operator, the auxiliary field is no longer the field strength: $F=f(A)+(gα_sT_F/15πM^2)(D_αJ_β-D_βJ_α)$, with $J$ the light-quark colour current. We verify this identity against the full theory and show that it separates the long-distance gluon exchange, carried by $F$, from the short-distance heavy-quark effect, carried by a four-quark contact term.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Hawking-Page phase transitions of black holes in the Hamiltonian formalism
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We employ the Hamiltonian formalism proposed by P. M. Dirac to investigate the Hawking-Page phase transition of the non-rotating Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ), Reissner-Nordström (RN) and Kerr-Newman (KN) black holes in both on-shell and off-shell configurations. For the BTZ black hole, the on-shell Hamiltonian agrees with the corresponding Helmholtz free energy obtained from the Euclidean action, reproducing the established Hawking-Page phase structure, while the off-shell analysis is consistent with the corresponding continuous phase transition obtained from the Euclidean approach. The same agreement is found for the on-shell RN and KN black holes. We further investigate the previously unexplored off-shell configurations of the RN and KN black holes. We find that electric charge restricts the mass range of the thermal soliton state, while rotation in the KN case removes the upper mass bound and eliminates the distinction arising from arbitrary surface contributions between the thermal soliton and black hole states. These findings uncover new aspects of the off-shell thermodynamics of charged and rotating black holes and suggest a possible connection between their phase structure and the quantum nature of gravity.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 42 pages, 6 figures, published in Physica Scripta

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Robin--Hadamard states for unstable field in half-Minkowski spacetime
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the quantization of a real massless scalar field in four-dimensional half-Minkowski spacetime subject to an attractive Robin boundary condition. We show that the unstable modes, required for classical spectral completeness, are also essential to recover the canonical commutation relations (CCR) of the complete quantum field. By specifying the Cauchy covariances of the unstable sector, we construct a family of positive quasifree states compatible with the conservation of total energy. Within this family, positivity is incompatible with stationarity, so that the resulting states necessarily break the time-translation symmetry of the background. We also obtain a closed position-space representation of the two-point function for the chosen stable vacuum sector, including the contribution fixed by the CCR in the unstable sector. The resulting expression exhibits the direct and reflected singularities, including Robin-dependent logarithmic terms. Since the remaining unstable contribution is smooth, all states in the constructed family share the same singularity structure, consistent with the Robin--Hadamard framework.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: 5D Runge-Lenz Vector from Symplectic Reduction of 8D Harmonic Oscillator
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem in the SU(8) dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator acting on its phase space. Using a complete basis of real $8\times 8$ matrices constructed from five-dimensional gamma matrices and the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ generators associated with the symplectic reduction, we decompose the conserved quantities of the harmonic oscillator into representations of $\mathrm{SO}(5) \times \mathrm{SU}(2)$ and identify the SU(2)-singlet sector. We show that the corresponding conserved quantities generate an SO(6) subgroup of the SU(8) dynamical symmetry. We then perform the Hurwitz transformation and symplectic reduction with respect to SU(2), obtaining the five-dimensional Kepler Hamiltonian. We explicitly show that the SO(6) moment map reduces to the angular momentum and the suitably normalized Runge-Lenz vector of the five-dimensional Kepler problem on a fixed negative-energy surface. This establishes the origin of the Runge-Lenz vector in the dynamical symmetry of the eight-dimensional harmonic oscillator.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: improvements to discussions, references added, author affiliation corrected

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact Stress Tensor Flows in Causal Electrodynamics: Auxiliary Field Formalism
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Causal self-dual nonlinear electrodynamics can be described in terms of a single auxiliary field, with the theory specified by its potential $W(\varphi)$. We use this formulation to study exact, nonperturbative $T\bar T$-like deformations. The irrelevant deformation rescales the auxiliary potential, whereas the marginal ModMax deformation shifts its argument. The resulting flow equations are obtained directly from the auxiliary-field action. On any domain where $r(ψ)$ is regular and invertible, the irrelevant flow admits an autonomous representation, $\partial_λ\mathcal{L} = X F(r)$, with $r = -T^μ_μ/\sqrt{4X-Y}$ and $X, Y$ denoting the quadratic stress-tensor invariants. We derive the flow function $F(r)$ and show how the auxiliary potential can be reconstructed from it. On an increasing, invertible branch, causality requires $D(r)>1/(1-r)$. A globally single-valued flow function further requires the auxiliary-field ratio $r(ψ)$ to remain one-to-one throughout the physical branch. We also study the relation between the $\varphi$-parity of the auxiliary potential, the evenness of $F(r)$, and the analyticity of the Lagrangian, distinguishing the Maxwell and ModMax vacua. The construction extends to the Hamiltonian formulation, whose coupling flow has the opposite sign. We further express Legendre self-duality, the characteristic cones, and the energy conditions in terms of the flow function, and identify $r=(\varepsilon-p_\perp)/(\varepsilon+p_\perp)$. The framework is illustrated by exact results for generalized Born--Infeld, logarithmic, $q$-deformed, and no-$τ$-maximum electrodynamics.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 27 pages; Revised with added details and references

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Mathematical inverse problem for the world data inference of the parton distribution functions of the proton
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We show that the inference problem of constraining the parton distribution functions of the proton from deeply inelastic scattering data can be formulated as a linear tensor reconstruction inverse problem. This means that instead of fitting model parameters to the world data, a reconstructive approach to solve a system of coupled linear functional integral equations can be formulated. We leverage the mathematical structures of the integral equations defined by perturbative QCD and global analysis to pose the problem of global analysis as a coupled system of linear integral equations, and construct a proof-of-principle methodology to solve it. To formulate this approach concretely, we review all next-to-leading order accuracy results for inclusive virtual photon, neutral current, charged current, heavy flavor production, and neutrino deep-inelastic lepton--proton scattering. This mathematical methodology of inference opens a path towards a parametrization-bias-free extraction of the proton PDFs from the world data of deeply inelastic scattering in the spirit of indirect measurement employed in mathematical inverse problems, including robust estimation of uncertainties with reduced bias from model parametrization, while closely adhering to the established paradigm of perturbative QCD and global analysis.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 124 pages, 1 figure; v2 matches the published version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Deformations of Locally Conformal Parallel Spin(7) Instantons
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the infinitesimal deformation theory of $Spin(7)$-instantons on compact locally conformal parallel (LCP) $Spin(7)$ manifolds, that is, $Spin(7)$ manifolds whose fundamental 4-form satisfies $dΦ=θ\wedgeΦ$ with a closed, non-exact Lee form $θ$. We show that the gauge-fixed linearized instanton equations are equivalent to a kernel problem for a twisted Levi-Civita Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}^-_A-\mathcal{A}_θ\colonΓ(\mathcal{S}^-\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)\toΓ(\mathcal{S}^+\otimes\mathfrak{g}_P)$, compute the zeroth-order term $\mathcal{A}_θ$ explicitly, and show that its pointwise squared operator norm equals $\frac{49}{64}|θ|^2$. Combined with the Lichnerowicz--Weitzenböck formula and Ivanov's scalar curvature identity, this yields a sufficient condition for rigidity, which we show can never be satisfied by flat connections. Indeed, the trivial connection is never rigid: its deformation space contains $H^1(M;\mathbb{R})\otimes\mathfrak{g}$. Our main result concerns the product LCP manifolds $N\times S^1$, where $N$ is a compact nearly parallel $G_2$ manifold: for the pull-back of a $G_2$-instanton $B$ on $N$ we prove $\mathcal{H}^1_{Spin(7)}(\mathrm{pr}^*B)\cong\mathcal{H}^0_{G_2}(B)\oplus\mathcal{H}^1_{G_2}(B)$. This reduces the deformation theory of such instantons to the nearly parallel $G_2$ case, shows that this containment is an equality for the trivial connection, and produces non-flat examples on the Hopf manifold $S^7\times S^1$ and on other products with homogeneous nearly parallel $G_2$ manifolds.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 14 pages. v2: substantially revised; incorrect rigidity statement and the Sp(2)/T^2 example removed; new main result (Theorem 6.3) on product manifolds N x S^1

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Unitarity with respect to the Clock of a Dynamical Local Observer and the Einstein Equivalence Principle
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution with respect to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity. In the former case, we find that evolution relative to the internal clock is generally nonunitary, implying a violation of the Einstein equivalence principle at the quantum level. In contrast, in the latter case, diffeomorphism invariance allows us to adopt observer-centric coordinates. On the resulting partially reduced phase space, one of the diffeomorphism generators becomes linear in the clock Hamiltonian, generating a relational evolution that is consistent with the remaining diffeomorphism constraints. Assuming the existence of an effective quantum theory that consistently preserves diffeomorphism invariance, these features imply unitary evolution relative to the internal clock, thereby preserving the equivalence principle even in the quantum regime. Our results highlight the fundamental role of diffeomorphism invariance in shaping relational unitary evolution from the perspective of a local observer.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 34 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Title changed; conclusions unchanged

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, whose amplitudes are given by the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions whose shifts have power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, in which the slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed locally by matter and geometry without an external clock. This class includes the comoving and uniform-density gauges, whose spectra grow without bound at late times in radiation domination. Over this range of $w$, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, justifying its standard use in computing the gravitational-wave energy spectrum. In matter domination, by contrast, the out-state isolates the free wave from the static tidal response that asymptotically dominates the Newtonian-gauge tensor perturbation.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Twisted Cohomology of D-Brane Disk Integrals
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Disk-level scattering amplitudes involving one Ramond--Ramond and two NSNS states on a D-brane obey nontrivial identities among scalar world-sheet integrals imposed by gauge and T-duality Ward identities. We investigate the cohomological organization of these relations using twisted de Rham cohomology and show that the Ward identities admit twisted-exact representatives. In the $I/J$ sector, the unique generic linear dependence among the Ward identities is realized one degree lower in the same twisted de Rham complex, revealing a common cohomological origin for the identities and their syzygy. We also identify independent pointwise algebraic relations among the integrands. An independent cohomological rank computation then establishes that the physically selected $I/J$ family spans a five-dimensional subspace of the top twisted cohomology at generic complexified kinematics. Extending the construction to the $K$-family, including the exceptional double-pole representative $K_3$, introduces no additional cohomology direction. For a D1-brane amplitude, we exhibit a physical polarization component in which six scalar periods reduce to one at special kinematics.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: Substantially revised and expanded version, with additional derivations, appendices, and references; 30 pages

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local Lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the Lovelock class of theories of gravity. The horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. Naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full Lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. We show that on the horizon, the Hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local Lorentz boost is the Wald entropy.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The EEC-Hedron: Positivity Bounds on Energy Correlators
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the constraints placed by energy positivity on general unitary quantum field theories. We show that the coefficients in the partial wave expansion of energy-energy correlators all must lie within a bounded region of parameter space, which we call the "EEC-hedron". For the particular case of conformal field theories, these positivity constraints on energy correlators lead to bounds on the allowed values of coefficients in the operator product expansion. We demonstrate this approach in the 3d Ising and $O(2)$ CFTs, deriving new bounds on OPE coefficients in both theories.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Reconstructing massive quivers on a defect circle
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the kink and particle spectra for the massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformations of minimal models $\mathcal M_{k+1,k+2}$ via truncated conformal space approach (TCSA) on a defect circle. The massive $φ_{2,1}$-deformation preserves a set of non-invertible symmetries, furnishing a fusion category $\mathcal C_k\simeq {\rm SO}(3)_k$. These non-invertible symmetries are spontaneously broken, and thus label the vacua and organize the kinks and particles into their multiplets in terms of quiver diagrams. We employ a finite-volume truncated Hamiltonian approach on defect Hilbert spaces, $\mathcal H_{X_i}$ for $X_i\in\mathcal C_k$, to study these quivers in the IR theories. The symmetry defect can then close an individual kink on a circle. We first establish the relation between states of definite fractional momentum on the defect circle and physical kink and particle states labelled by their vacuum pairs. Using form factors of local fields, we independently measure the squared amplitudes between the states of the two bases in defect TCSA. Combining these measurements with defect TCSA spectra, we reconstruct the quiver diagrams for $k=3,4,5$ without assuming them in advance. In particular, for $k=4$ we reconstruct the distinct quivers of the ordered and disordered phases. For $k=5$, we identify the quivers of both the light and heavy multiplets.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 40 pages+4 appendices, 14 figures, 13 tables, ancillary code included

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gröbner elimination and graph combinatorics
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gröbner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators.
  An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Higher derivatives and ghosts through three centuries
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary:
We outline the history of the research of dynamic systems including higher derivatives in the Lagrangian, The story starts in 1744 when Euler published a book where the Euler--Lagrange differential equations for a HD system were first written. The next important landmarks were the papers of Ostrogradsky (1850) and of Pais and Uhlenbeck (1950). Many articles written in the second half of the last century were influenced by a misconception that was widespread at the time --- it was believed that higher derivatives necessarily bring about a violation of unitarity.
  We understand today that this is not the case and there are many systems with benign ghosts where HD are present but unitarity is not violated. In this review, we present and discuss several examples of such (quantum) mechanical systems and 2D field theories. Then we will briefly discuss higher-derivative gravity theories in 4 dimensions. In that case, the question whether the ghosts there are benign or not has a special status due to the absence of a nonperturbative Hamiltonian and does not have a definite answer yet. However, if one restricts oneself to classical theory, one can argue that the ghosts {\it are} benign (benign classical ghostly system is a system that needs an infinite time to reach a singularity, and it seems to the case both in ordinary and in HD gravity: the cosmic censorship conjecture implies that the singularities are always surrounded by horizons, and it takes an infinite time on the clocks of a distant observer to reach a horizon).
  Finally, I discuss supersymmetric HD theories: conformal supergravity, where the ghosts are also probably benign, and then an interesting supersymmetric HD gauge theory in 6 dimensions. It involves a dimensionless coupling constant, is renormalizable and rather beautiful. Unfortunately, it is not unitary --- ghosts are not benign there.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Defect Correlators from Supergravity: Finding the Missing Contact Terms
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We resolve a puzzle in the computation of holographic correlators using supergravity when defects are present. Previous direct supergravity calculations of defect two-point functions were found to differ from bootstrap results by a set of contact contributions.
