We show that the discrepancy arises from two effects: nonlinear Kaluza-Klein field redefinitions in the bulk, which induce additional quadratic couplings when applied consistently to localized sources, and off-shell terms in mixed bulk--defect vertices, which can collapse internal defect propagators. We demonstrate how these two mechanisms resolve the puzzle in two concrete examples in 4d $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM, where we consider two-point correlators in the presence of a $\frac{1}{2}$-BPS Wilson line and on $\mathbb{RP}^4$.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Carroll limits of bosonic and supersymmetric D-branes in the Polyakov formulation
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We derive the magnetic and electric Carroll limits of bosonic and supersymmetric D-branes in the Polyakov formulation at fixed positive rescaled tension. Eliminating the nonsymmetric auxiliary tensor recovers the full Dirac--Born--Infeld action. On the regular domain with a positive-definite induced spatial metric and a positive lapse bounded away from zero, the auxiliary constraints remain second class in both limits. Eliminating them before or after contraction gives the same local reduced phase space. The magnetic Hamiltonian retains the full spatial determinant and the electric Hamiltonian retains the electric displacement squared. We compare their dynamics on flat D2 solutions and on curves in a common warped Carroll background. Both limits retain sixteen independent $κ$-symmetry parameters for flat Type II D2--D7 branes. The electric limit also retains a Neveu--Schwarz flux term in the fermionic constraint and supercharge matrices. Spatial T-duality commutes with both contractions on fixed-radius circle zero modes when the dual transverse canonical pair is rescaled in the electric case. The prescribed local Carroll--Weyl transformation fails to preserve the constraints, and both actions admit exact global dilations.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. We also determine multiplicity entropies and correlations between dipole-size sectors. Applying a fixed negative-binomial dipole-to-charged-particle response reproduces the rising trend of the H1 charged-particle multiplicity entropy toward smaller $x$, but does not fully describe the measured multiplicity distributions. These results demonstrate an explicit coherent encoding of finite-state dipole branching and clarify its relation to continuous-cascade fluctuations and DIS phenomenology.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We obtain an explicit separation of the coupled gravitational and electromagnetic radiative equations on nonextremal Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter black holes with nonzero charge and rotation. By directly matching the Fourier coefficients, we construct a separating matrix with constant determinant that is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both spin sectors. We establish that this transformation is smooth and invertible throughout the open AdS exterior and between the event and cosmological horizons in dS. The resulting radial and angular systems are valid at arbitrary complex frequencies. We also translate the regularity of the radiative Newman--Penrose variables at the rotation axes and future horizons into boundary conditions for the separated solutions. In the asymptotically flat limit, the transformation is related to Hintz's matrix integrating factor by the allowed frame freedom. These results provide a basis for studying quasinormal modes and black hole stability in Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter spacetimes, as well as exploring holographic applications to strongly coupled systems.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Norms, overlaps and Yangian descendants for the Haldane-Shastry spin chain
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The Haldane-Shastry spin chain is a prototypical integrable model with long-range interactions, notable for hosting quasiparticles with fractional statistics and serving as a discrete analogue of a conformal field theory. Its remarkable simplicity is closely tied to a full Yangian spin symmetry. While the highest-weight states for this symmetry are known explicitly, a systematic treatment of the descendant states, needed for the computation of various physical quantities, has remained incomplete. In this work, we provide a detailed construction of these descendants in terms of the algebraic Bethe ansatz following recent work of Ferrando et al. In the limit of extreme twist, it includes the Gelfand-Tsetlin basis. As an application, we derive product and determinant formulae for norms and overlaps of these states.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $κ_τ\Barψσ_{μν}F_{μν}ψ$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi (WT) identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$. Consequently, at any fixed point with a vanishing gauge coupling, the eigenvalue in the direction of the gauge coupling is exactly~$-γ_A^*$, and the gauge coupling is relevant if and only if the vacuum polarization makes~$γ_A^*$ negative. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields such a fixed point, with~$γ_A^*=-1$ and three relevant directions. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line eliminate it unless $N_f$ is at least several tens. For~$N_f=1$, a search over the whole plane of the Pauli coupling and the mass parameter in the subspace~$e_τ=0$, where our flow equation is exactly of one-loop order, finds a single fixed point, at strong Pauli coupling and a finite mass parameter. Like one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell, it has a finite mass parameter and two relevant directions. At their fixed point, the gauge coupling is relevant. At ours, in contrast, $γ_A^*>0$, so that the gauge coupling is irrelevant, and the fixed point cannot provide a UV completion of QED with a nonzero charge. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$ on the critical surface connected to the Gaussian fixed point, $κ_τ$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value proportional to~$e_τ^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_τ^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Light-by-light scattering: asymptotic expansions, Coulomb resummation and NLO corrections
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Light-by-light (LbL) scattering is one of the earliest predictions of quantum electrodynamics (QED). Interest in this process has been renewed following its experimental observation at the LHC and the prospects of future measurements at free-electron laser facilities. In this paper, we refine theoretical predictions for LbL scattering by improving the full fermion-mass-dependent two-loop QCD and QED helicity amplitudes using high- and low-energy asymptotic expansions, and by performing Coulomb resummation in the threshold region. The $W$-boson contribution, relevant when the di-photon invariant mass exceeds twice the $W$-boson mass, is included at one-loop accuracy. We present state-of-the-art predictions for LbL cross sections in the Standard Model and provide a new event generator, LbLatNLO, for Monte Carlo simulations of LbL scattering.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 71 pages, 12 figures, 6 tables. The LbLatNLO code is available at https://github.com/huashengshao/LbLatNLO. Ancillary files for amplitudes and integrals. v2: journal version

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Anomalies and the Berry Phase: From $π^0\toγγ$ to the geometry of the fermion vacuum
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We review the chiral anomaly from a historical perspective, from the $π^0\toγγ$ puzzle and the work of Adler, Bell and Jackiw, to the Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) term. We then describe how the WZW term was motivated from quantum chromodynamics in 1983-85. Integrating out the non-Abelian gauge fields, that have a gapped spectrum, gives a Nambu-Jona-Lasinio type theory of quarks, and integrating out the quarks, which are gapped by chiral symmetry breaking, gives the WZW model. The fermion determinant splits into a regulator-dependent modulus, which gives the dynamics of mesons, and a universal phase, which is fixed by the anomaly and is the WZW term. Restricted to the collective coordinates of the baryon soliton, the WZW term imposes a U(1) constraint that makes the baryon wave functions monopole harmonics and fixes their spin, statistics and flavour multiplets. We then explain that this phase is a Berry phase: the Schwinger terms of current algebra are the curvature of a U(1) connection on the space of chiral field configurations, and the WZW term is its holonomy, which we call a Berry-Wilson loop. In 1+1 dimensions we write the connection explicitly in terms of Euler angles, exhibiting a Dirac monopole whose quantised charge is the level of the current algebra.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Controlling truncation errors in loop tensor network renormalization
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: At finite bond dimension $χ$, tensor network renormalization (TNR) of a critical model eventually becomes gapped. For LoopTNR with $O(2)$ symmetry on the $c=1$ critical line of the six-vertex model, parametrized by the Luttinger parameter $K$, we show that the correlation length $ξ$ of the gapped phase is set by the seed of the dimerization injected by the truncation, and depends on $χ$ only through it. Read from a weak-coupling window early in the same run, the seed predicts $ξ=10^3$-$10^{16}$ via the sine-Gordon mass-coupling relation with no free parameter, to within a few percent for $K\le1.5$ and about 10% at $K=1.75$; since the seed fluctuates strongly with $χ$, $ξ$ is not monotonic in $χ$. An alternation of the vertex weights shifts the seed; with its sign read from a $π$ twist, one short calibration predicts a counterterm that delays the breakdown in 16 of the 17 compensated groups of a campaign fixed in advance. A correction of the coarse-grained tensors, repeated during the flow, keeps the runs at $K=1$ and $1.5$ critical up to step 160, the last step computed, and exposes the marginal truncation error that remains. Our findings illustrate a systematic procedure for controlling the relevant truncation error, and thereby extending the critical window, in tensor network renormalization at finite bond dimension.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Moore--Read construction and explicit monodromies of Laughlin states on Riemann surfaces
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We revisit the Moore--Read construction of the $ν=1/k$ Laughlin states on compact Riemann surfaces, deriving their conformal blocks from $U(1)_k$ Chern--Simons theory through the CS/WZW correspondence. We compute their explicit monodromies under quasi-hole transport and Aharonov--Bohm flux insertion, and prove that the monodromies associated with flux insertion asymptotically coincide with the corresponding physical adiabatic holonomies. In particular, we prove that the physical $L^2$ metric on the vector bundle of Laughlin states over the Jacobian is asymptotically projectively flat. We also relate our construction to the recently developed algebro-geometric approach to higher genus Laughlin states.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 30 pages; added Section 4.3 and rewrote the introduction

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Quantum Riemannian Hamiltonian Descent
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We propose Quantum Riemannian Hamiltonian Descent (QRHD), a quantum algorithm for continuous optimization on Riemannian manifolds that extends Quantum Hamiltonian Descent (QHD) by incorporating geometric structure of the parameter space via a position-dependent metric in the kinetic term. We formulate QRHD in both operator and path integral formalisms and derive the corresponding quantum equations of motion, showing that quantum corrections appear in the action integral but they are suppressed at late times by the time-dependent dissipation factor. This implies that convergence near optimal points is controlled by the classical potential while quantum effects influence early-time dynamics. By analyzing the semiclassical equation, we estimate a lower bound on the convergence time and numerically demonstrate whether QRHD works as a quantum optimization algorithm in some examples. A quantum circuit implementation based on time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation is also discussed and the query complexity is estimated.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Late-time OTOCs in Toda conformal field theory
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study late-time out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) of semi-degenerate primary fields in two-dimensional $A_{N-1}$ Toda conformal field theory. In Liouville theory ($N=2$), we find that the OTOC decays as $t^{-3/2}$ when the continuum edge dominates, correcting a previously reported constant limit. For $N=3$, a transverse contour pinch reduces the spectral integral to one dimension. Assuming that the reduced expansion is complete, in the continuous phase the regulated edge behaves as a discrete state, and the OTOC approaches a pure braiding phase. As we check numerically, the edge block is a free-field correlator in a charge-neutral Weyl frame; this explains the pure phase and is consistent with crossing symmetry. For both $N=2$ and $N=3$, a dominant discrete residue gives a constant late-time limit. For $N\geq4$, the same one-dimensional reduction violates a crossing bound on the lowest intermediate weight of a positive diagonal expansion. Hence the $N=2,3$ phase diagram does not extend to higher rank without additional contributions below the reduced continuum edge or outside a positive diagonal expansion.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Three-Reggeon exchange in $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM to leading logarithmic accuracy
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study eight-point amplitudes in the planar $\mathcal{N}=4$ Super Yang-Mills theory in multi-Regge kinematics in the Mandelstam region that receives contributions from both two- and three-Reggeon exchange. We use an effective field theory approach to compute the leading contribution from three-Reggeon exchange, and we explicitly evaluate the relevant diagrams up to four loops. We also propose a compact Fourier-Mellin representation for the contribution from two-Reggeon exchange in this region which involves the same ingredients as in other Mandelstam regions and can in principle be evaluated to any desired order in perturbation theory. To validate our proposal, we show that we can reproduce the multi-Regge limit of the known results for octagons up to three loops. We then combine the contributions from two- and three-Reggeon exchange to obtain novel results for octagons in MRK up to next-to-leading-logarithmic accuracy at four loops for the maximally helicity violating (MHV) configuration, and up to three loops for non-MHV contributions. We also discuss how our result can be extended to more particles, and we present the contribution from three-Reggeon exchange for three-loop MHV amplitudes with an arbitrary number of legs. In the appendices, we provide details on how to perform the analytic continuation and take the multi-Regge limit of the three-loop octagon, and explain how our results are connected to previous results in the literature.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 36 pages, 4 figures, 2 ancillary files; v2: minor revisions, matches the version accepted by JHEP; ancillary files replaced with corrected expressions

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime. We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. The aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 28 pages, 1 figure; general treatment of the Dirac equation (in the absence of torsion) for cases in which $γ^{\hat 0}$ serves as the hermitizing matrix for the Dirac matrices

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Matter-wave Interferometers as Open-system Dark Matter Detectors
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: Matter-wave interferometers (MWIs) offer a uniquely quantum route to dark matter (DM) detection: DM can reveal itself through phase and decoherence between spatially separated wavepackets, even when energy deposition is negligible and no resolvable recoil displacement occurs. We formulate these effects in an open effective field theory for MWIs using the Schwinger--Keldysh formalism, which highlights a structural asymmetry between the two detection channels. For elastic spin-independent DM scattering, decoherence inherits novel Bose enhancement or Pauli blocking factors, while the phase is at most linear in the DM occupation number. By retaining the DM's coherence time, this framework spans Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics across a wide range of DM masses, and systematically organizes corrections beyond the heavy-probe limit.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 6 pages + supplemental material, 1 figure. v2: Fixed typos, harmonized notation and conventions with arXiv:2610.36044, and expanded the Supplemental Material

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: The Classification of 3+1d Symmetry Enriched Topological Order
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We use a 2-categorical version of (de-)equivariantization to classify (3+1)d topological orders with a finite $G$-symmetry. In particular, we argue that (3+1)d fermionic topological order with $G$-symmetry correspond to $\mathbf{2SVect}$-enriched $G$-crossed braided fusion 2-categories. We then show that the categorical data necessary to define these theories agrees with that arising from a fermionic generalization of the Wang-Wen-Witten construction of bosonic topological theories with $G$-symmetry saturating an anomaly. More generally, we also explain how 2-categorical (de-) equivariantization yields a classification of all braided fusion 2-categories.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 31 pages, v3 included a proof of the fiber sequence and added examples

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

High Energy Physics - Theory.title: Wrapping M5-branes on a non-spin manifold: Spin$^h$ structures and AdS$_7$ black holes
High Energy Physics - Theory.summary: We construct a solution of seven-dimensional maximal gauged supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_5$, where $M_5$ is the five-dimensional Wu manifold $SU(3)/SO(3)$. The solution is supersymmetric, despite the fact that the Wu manifold admits neither a spin structure nor a spin$^c$ structure. Rather, it admits a spin$^h$ structure, wherein the ill-definedness of ordinary spinors due to a minus sign in their holonomy is compensated by a further minus sign arising through the spinors carrying $SO(3)$ Yang-Mills charge, in a half-integer isospin representation of the $SU(2)$ double cover of the $SO(3)$. We show how the configuration can be lifted to a solution of $D=11$ supergravity of the form AdS$_2\times M_9$, where $M_9$ is the unit tangent bundle of the Wu manifold. We discuss the geometry and topology of $M_9$, and study the supersymmetry from the eleven-dimensional standpoint. We extend the seven-dimensional solution to a black hole, and discuss some aspects of its holographic interpretation and the UV to IR flow. We revisit a previously-known AdS$_2\times H^3\times H^2$ solution, and its UV to IR flow, showing that the flow equations in fact admit of an exact solution. Additionally, we give a detailed discussion of the lift of the AdS$_2\times S^5$ solution to $D=11$, exhibiting similarities and differences between the properties of its internal space $M_9$ (the unit tangent bundle of $S^5$) and the Wu manifold example of our main discussion. We also construct the non-compact dual of the Wu manifold solution, where $M_5$ is taken to be $SL(3,\mathbb R)/SO(3)$.
High Energy Physics - Theory.comment: 42 pages, 2 tables. v2: minor clarifying footnotes added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: An algebraic quantization of gravity from the null cone
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose a background independent quantization of vacuum general relativity on four dimensional Lorentzian spacetimes. Starting from first order gravity, we solve the gravitational constraints on intersecting null cones of a bulk subregion and obtain the reduced phase space at finite $G_N$. We promote its canonical Poisson brackets to commutation relations and use deformations of the reduced action to define an algebra of observables. Equipped with this, we use Gaussian wavefunctions of canonical pairs to construct a nonperturbative Hilbert space representation, for which this algebra generates a type I factor. By composing amplitudes between states prepared on null cones, we then obtain a Lorentzian path integral in which each sum over intermediate states converges absolutely. As a check, we compute the amplitude for graviton pair creation and annihilation on a null cone nonperturbatively in $G_N$ and find a finite closed form expression, even though expanding first in $G_N$ yields a logarithmic divergence. We next use diffeomorphism invariance of the path integral to show that a macroscopic causal diamond with a given maximum size has a finite dimensional Hilbert space. From the Lorentzian trace we obtain the Bekenstein Hawking entropy for marginally trapped surfaces and calculate its logarithmic correction for large Schwarzschild black holes, recovering at one loop the coefficient Sen obtained through Euclidean methods. We end by deriving the semiclassical Einstein equations to one loop as the low energy limit of this theory.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Massive Triangle in Cosmological Correlator beyond Conformal Coupling
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: A massive scalar coupled in pairs to the inflaton generates a one-loop primordial bispectrum whose mass corrections at generic momenta have lacked closed analytic expressions beyond conformal coupling. We obtain two leading mass corrections at arbitrary external momenta in terms of multiple polylogarithms of uniform weights three and four. Auxiliary-energy dressings preserve rational time integrals, revealing unexpected simplicity despite elliptic intermediate geometry. Independent full-loop evaluations, including blinded predictions, validate the closed forms. We also determine a subleading light-field singularity and recover the heavy-mass effective theory.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A catalogue of insights from the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Over the last decade, gravitational-wave science has developed from a detection being a Nobel-winning achievement to an (almost) everyday occurrence. The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) Collaboration's flagship scientific results are now their catalogues of detections. We review discoveries from the fourth observing run (O4) of the \ac{LVK}. The recent catalogues each include $\sim100$ new detections. Among these are remarkable single discoveries: the loudest signals detected, and sources unlike those seen before. However, significant advances also are coming from population-level analyses, leveraging the sample size to infer constraints on the astrophysical distribution of merging compact binaries, potential deviations from general relativity, and the expansion rate of the Universe. Analyses of the latest data have revealed evidence for multiple subpopulations of sources, providing a unique probe into the evolution of coalescing binaries. Our understanding of gravitational-wave signals and their sources will continue to deepen with more observations: the final catalogue from O4 will release in December 2026, and planned future observing runs with greater detector sensitivity will bring even larger catalogues and additional loud signals.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages (1 page title+abstract, 9 pages main text, 9 pages bibliography), 4 figures; updated to match published version, with additional citations beyond journal limit

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $χ= 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $τ= -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 8 pages. v2: Fixed orientation consistency issues and typos

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Pole-Cut Formula for Holographic Extremal Correlators
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We show that the holographic spectral function of a neutral massless scalar on the extremal Reissner-Nordstrom black brane in $AdS_5$ admits an elegant formula in terms of the quasi-normal modes (QNMs) and branch-cut data. In the extremal case, the spectral data comprises the zeros of the boundary source function, i.e. the QNMs, as well as its phase discontinuity across the branch cut on the negative imaginary axis of the complex frequency plane. This formula neatly factorizes into an infinite product over the QNM poles and a factor encoding the branch cut discontinuity. We derive this pole-cut formula as the zero-temperature limit of the QNM product formula for holographic thermal correlators, with the branch-cut contribution arising from the coalescence of the QNMs on the negative imaginary axis. We also clarify the role of the near-horizon $AdS_2$ region in this context. Consistency with the OPE of the boundary correlator provides extremal sum-rules involving both the QNMs as well as the phase discontinuity function. We also find that this holographic consistency forces the asymptotic form of the QNMs to be related to the asymptotics of the phase discontinuity function. We verify our formula and these OPE constraints numerically. We also demonstrate that, in the time domain, the pole and cut factors each produce complex-time singularities, whose location is determined by the optical distance between the boundary and the black-brane singularity. We expect the pole-cut factorization structure of spectral functions to hold for more general fluctuations of extremal black branes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Cosmological rigidity in $3$ spacetime dimensions
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We establish rigidity theorems for cosmological spacetimes in $3$ spacetime dimensions. In the setting of the Bartnik Splitting Conjecture, under the additional assumptions of null geodesic completeness and the dominant energy condition, we show that the spatial topology is either spherical or the spacetime splits as a product. Our methods rely on the theory of marginally outer trapped surfaces, known rigidity results in the presence of a timelike or null line, and more recent rigidity results in the context of Penrose's singularity theorem due to the first two authors, from which the existence of a foliation by totally geodesic null hypersurfaces can be concluded. Our second main result closes the argument by establishing a splitting theorem for cosmological and null geodesically complete $3$-dimensional spacetimes which satisfy the dominant energy condition and which admit a foliation of the aforementioned type. In its proof, we make use of the local Kundt structure of the metric and construct a global parallel generator for the null foliation.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schrödinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless Pöschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Minor changes, typos corrected and references added

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: phenjax: the IMRPhenomT waveform family in JAX for accelerated analyses on CPUs and GPUs
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We present phenjax, a JAX implementation of the precessing time-domain IMRPhenomT family of models for the gravitational wave signal emitted in compact binary coalescence. The code keeps the structure of its reference Python implementation, phenomxpy, and reproduces, on average, its polarizations to a few $\times 10^{-12}$ of the peak strain for all the models, aligned-spin and precessing. The waveform models now take advantage of the JAX construction: compiled once per array shape, vectorized over events (batching), differentiable and executed on CPUs or GPUs with the same source code. Different additional features address the cost of long signals and of heterogeneous populations in a batch. On one NVIDIA H100, for the precessing TPHM model on LISA-mass populations, phenjax is 3 to 6 times faster than phenomxpy when both codes evaluate one event at a time and 20 to 30 times faster when phenjax evaluates the events in batches of 8. We estimate that, for waveform generation, one GPU does the work of 1300 to 2700 cores of a current CPU node at 25 to 45 times less energy per waveform. As a backend of a global-fit LISA massive black hole pipeline, performed on the Sangria dataset, phenjax recovers the same posteriors as the other waveform backends at a lower computational cost. In a comparison with phentax, the wall time was 13 minutes instead of 21.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Is Gravitational-Wave Waveform Systematics a Bottleneck for Formation Channel Inferences using Effective-Spin and Mass-Ratio?
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational-wave measurements of the effective spin $χ_\text{eff}$ and mass ratio $q$ help distinguish binary black hole formation channels, motivating a search for structure in the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ plane. However, both these quantities are known to be strongly correlated in GW parameter estimation since both enter the leading-order spin-orbit term together, and thus, the detectors cannot easily tell them apart. In this work, we harness the susceptibility of such measurements to waveform systematics by using injection-recovery studies with NRSur7dq4 as the true signal and SEOBNRv5PHM and IMRPhenomTPHM for parameter inferences. Our study shows that, though there can be some parameter space in the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ plane, primarily in the unequal-mass regime, there can be some impacts from waveform systematics; overall, at a population level, the waveform systematics for the current detectors at their design sensitivity are not a bottleneck in recovering the underlying true population properties. We find that astrophysical properties such as $χ_\text{eff} - q$ correlations, which are signatures of different formation channels, are unlikely to be spuriously induced by waveform systematics, and inferences about formation channels based on such correlations are likely robust to waveform systematics at present, though some events that are in the parameter space of large impact can show some outlier behaviour. We find that some of the GW events such as GW190403$\_$051519 and GW240527$\_$230910 are in the vicinity of the $χ_\text{eff} - q$ parameter space, where large waveform systematics can arise, and these events are more susceptible to waveform systematics than others in GWTC-5. This study will play a vital role in precision astrophysical population inference from GW data in the future and in assessing the possibility of waveform systematics.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 10 pages, 5 figures. To be submitted to Phys. Rev. D

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Entanglement and HBAR entropy in a Lorentzian non-commutative black hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate how Lorentzian non-commutative smearing affects entanglement and horizon brightened acceleration radiation (HBAR) outside a black hole. For a massless scalar field, tracing over the interior partner gives the exterior quantum channel, its logarithmic negativity, mutual information, and Bell entanglement fidelity. At fixed mass and Killing frequency, increasing the smearing lowers the surface gravity, increases the accessible correlations, and suppresses the leading atomic emission probability. The horizon displacement begins at order $\sqrtΘ$, while the thermal correction at infinity begins at order $Θ$. At fixed local frequency, the redshift introduces a term of order $\sqrtΘ$ at fixed areal radius. Holding the proper distance fixed, it cancels this term and recovers the common Rindler response close to the horizon. For a freely falling atom, emission and absorption obey detailed balance at the Hawking temperature in the leading horizon approximation. Random atomic injection drives the selected mode from the vacuum to a thermal state with an exact relaxation law and nonnegative entropy production. Near equilibrium, we obtain $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/4$ when the radiated energy is drawn from horizon heat, where $\dot A_p$ is the positive radiative area loss. When the radiation is assigned to ADM mass loss at fixed smearing length $\ell=4\sqrt{Θ/π}$, the result is $\dot S_{\rm HBAR}\simeq\dot A_p/[4(1-\ell/r_+)]$. The mass dependence of the exterior source thus enters the entropy per unit area lost at order $\sqrtΘ$.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof [arXiv:1105.3445] assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state-operator duality. The asymptotic horizon charge is the momentum of a quantum clock; its conjugate gives the reading. The modular crossed product admits density operators whose entropy with respect to its trace reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time measurement of surprisal, the negative logarithm of the density operator, gives an FT for the complete exterior channel. It identifies the correction for a nonunital channel and gives a GSL bound for unital evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that preserves every dressed-charge sector and the full faithful dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The bounds establish the GSL in the slow-clock limit when the errors vanish and quantify what is needed at finite clock width.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 34 pages and 5 figures; v2. Polish the logic chains and wording; add references

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Reconstructed black hole solutions in the scalar-tensor theory with nonminimal coupling
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We consider the scalar-tensor theory witn non-minimal coupling in the Jordan frame. The action of the model contains a potential term $U(\varphi)$, a coupling function $f(\varphi)$. We explore a reconstruction procedure for a generic static spherically symmetric metric written in the Buchdahl parametrization: $ds^2 = \left(A(u)\right)^{-1}du^2 - A(u)dt^2 + C(u)dΩ^2$, with given $A(u) > 0$ and $C(u) > 0$. The procedure gives the relations for $U(\varphi(u))$, $f(\varphi(u))$ and $d\varphi/du$, which lead to exact solutions to equations of motion with a given metric. A key role in this approach is played by the solutions to a first order linear differential equation for the function $f(\varphi(u))$. The formalism is illustrated by two examples when: a) the Reissner-Nordström-(Anti-)de Sitter metric and b) the Bocharova-Bronnikov-Melnikov-Bekenstein-(Anti)de-Sitter metric are chosen as a starting point.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Smooth binary evolution from wide resonances in boson clouds
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Ultralight scalars can form superradiant clouds around rotating black holes. These may alter the dynamics of compact binaries and the ensuing waveform through orbital resonances and cloud ionization. We re-examine resonances involving states with nonzero decay width, deriving an effective treatment for resonances that are wider than the binary's frequency chirp. We demonstrate the utility of this approach by calculating an upper bound for the cloud's mass surviving up to the latest stages of the inspiral. Next, we study the accumulation of resonances with high-energy bound states. When these infinitely many, increasingly weak resonances are properly taken into account, they smooth out the "sharp features" in the binary's evolution that had been attributed to the ionization of the cloud. We compare our Newtonian results with recent relativistic calculations, highlighting common features as well as discrepancies. Our conclusions emphasize the need to carefully incorporate resonances in boson cloud waveform modeling.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 15 pages, 9 figures. Very minor update: regenerated figures with higher numerical precision

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $Λ> 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Genetic Algorithm Approach to Reconstructing Scalar-Tensor Lagrangians
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae observations, have been interpreted as evidence for dynamical dark energy whose equation of state crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Such a crossing cannot be realized smoothly by a minimally coupled scalar field $\varphi$, but can arise naturally in scalar-tensor theories. We present a data-driven framework that reconstructs the scalar-tensor Lagrangian directly from observations, using a genetic algorithm to evolve the symbolic expressions for the nonminimal coupling $F(\varphi)$ and the scalar potential $U(\varphi)$. Each candidate is evaluated through a forward model that self-consistently determines the expansion history, the effective gravitational coupling, and the growth of structure. Candidates are ranked by a joint likelihood of DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ supernovae calibrated with SH0ES Cepheids, compressed CMB distance priors, and redshift-space distortion measurements of $fσ_8$. We restrict to the unscreened branch of the theory and impose Solar System constraints on the post-Newtonian parameter $γ$ and on the time variation of the gravitational coupling, together with a Big Bang nucleosynthesis bound on its evolution. Across 64 independent runs, the best reconstruction improves the fit relative to $Λ$CDM by $Δχ^2=-16.6$, compared with $Δχ^2=-10.6$ for the CPL dark-energy parametrization. The preferred coupling is well described by $F(\varphi)=c_1\varphi^2+e^{\varphi}(1-c_2\varphi)$. The reconstructed theory shows phantom behavior at $z\gtrsim0.5$, but it remains close to $w=-1$ at low redshift.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: V1: 18 pages, 7 figures. The code and data that support the findings of V1 are openly available in the following GitHub repository: https://github.com/Rivillion/ScalarTensor_GA/tree/v1.0.0

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Accurate parameter inference for the Light-cone Epoch of Reionization 21-cm signal
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The light-cone (LC) effect breaks the statistical homogeneity along the line-of-sight (LoS) direction of the 21-cm signal. Consequently, the traditional power spectrum (PS) fundamentally fails to capture the full two-point statistical information. The evolving power spectrum (ePS) offers an alternative, explicitly accounting for the LoS evolution due to the LC effect while maintaining physical interpretability. We compare the statistical constraining power of three different summary statistics: the standard cylindrical PS $P(k_\perp,k_\parallel)$, slice-wise PS $P_s(k, z)$ (1D-PS computed over small bandwidth LC slices), and ePS $P_e(k, z)$. We first demonstrate that $P_e(k,z)$ successfully recovers the benchmark 1D-PS of coeval simulations across all scales and redshifts, whereas the slice-wise PS only recovers the 1D-PS at small scales. To efficiently perform parameter inference, we train artificial neural network (ANN) emulators on $500$ simulated LC 21-cm signals. Our forecasts incorporate cosmic variance, estimated using $50$ statistically independent realizations of the signal, alongside SKA-Low system noise for integration times of $1000$ and $104$ hours. We demonstrate that the ePS outperforms its peers, yielding credible intervals that are $\sim 3$ and $\sim 1.4$ times tighter than those obtained using $P(k_\perp,k_\parallel)$ and $P_s(k,z)$, respectively. These results establish the ePS as an optimal summary statistic for interpreting forthcoming large-bandwidth LC 21-cm observations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Ultralight Dark Matter Spectrum with Gravitational Focusing and Doppler Motion
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Ultralight dark matter can produce signals in experiments through its couplings with the Standard Model particles. The resulting signal spectrum is determined by the phase-space distribution of dark matter, which encodes information about its production mechanism and the history of the local universe. However, the local environmental effects can modify the observed spectrum and should be included in signal modeling to avoid biased parameter estimates. In this work, we investigate how the gravitational focusing by Sun and the Doppler effect due to the detector's motion modify the signal spectrum and affect inferring the underlying dark matter parameters. We analytically estimate the signal significance and perform Bayesian analysis on simulated data to demonstrate their impact.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Acoustic gravitational waves from primordial curvature perturbations
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Standard perturbative calculations of scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have neglected nonperturbative effects in the large-amplitude regime. We develop a hybrid numerical framework to signify nonperturbative effects on the stochastic gravitational wave (GW) background sourced by primordial curvature perturbations, focusing on the acoustic channel (fluid motions). Fully general-relativistic, spherically symmetric simulations are used to extract nonperturbative sound-shell profiles from isolated curvature peaks; these profiles are then embedded into three-dimensional lattice evolutions of relativistic hydrodynamics coupled to transverse-traceless metric perturbations to compute the acoustic GW spectra. The acoustic signal has a peak frequency determined by the comoving shell thickness, and its amplitude is extremely sensitive to the mean comoving separation of peaks, scaling approximately as $R_{*c}^{-7}$. We find a robust causal low-frequency tail $\propto k^{3}$, and the nonlinear hydrodynamic interactions can enhance the ultraviolet power. Comparing with SIGWs computed perturbatively from the same real-space configuration, we show that acoustic GWs can be amplified by an order of magnitude and display a peak shifted to a lower frequency in the large-amplitude regime. These results highlight the importance of nonperturbative effects for accurate predictions of stochastic GW signals induced from primordial curvature perturbations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 36 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables, major revision with more details and tests, the second companion paper (with direct numerical simulations for the acoustic gravitational waves) to the letter arXiv:2504.11275 and the long paper arXiv:2504.12243

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Black hole entropy from angular holonomies of Sine-Gordon soliton lattices in AdS$_3$
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We construct boundary conditions for AdS$_3$ gravity that realize Sine-Gordon dynamics. For a periodic soliton lattice at fixed winding, we relate the angular holonomy to the exact acoustic dispersion by continuing the Bloch momentum through the zero-frequency band edge associated with rigid translation of the lattice. For suitable embedding angles, the stable vacuum has a regular BTZ geometry. When only one chiral sector carries winding, we construct a family whose asymptotic region extends to a BTZ black hole. As the spectral parameter of the winding sector tends to the corresponding band edge, the black hole approaches extremality. The leading correction to the extremal entropy is linear in the Hawking temperature defined with respect to laboratory time, with a coefficient inversely proportional to the sound velocity of the lattice. The same inverse-velocity dependence appears in the low-temperature entropy of one-dimensional quantum fluids.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: A Geometric Derivation of the Einstein Equations from the Causal Action Principle
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The causal action principle for causal fermion systems is analyzed for a minimizing measure whose support is assumed to have the structure of a smooth manifold $\tilde{M}$. The concept of osculating vacua is introduced. It is shown that the Lagrangian induces on $\tilde{M}$ a Lorentzian metric. Moreover, the Euler-Lagrange equations of the causal action imply that the Ricci tensor must satisfy the Einstein equations of General Relativity for an energy-momentum tensor given in terms of a power expansion in the regularization length. The gravitational coupling constant is found to be the square of the regularization length. Our methods provide a systematic procedure for deriving corrections to the Einstein equations. The paper includes a self-contained introduction to causal variational principles and the causal action principle. Most geometric structures (connection, Riemannian metric and curvature) are introduced and analyzed in the general setting of causal variational principles for an arbitrary dimension of $\tilde{M}$. The Lorentzian setting works only for causal fermion systems and is worked out only in four spacetime dimensions.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 49 pages, LaTeX, 5 figures, minor changes (published version)

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Electroweak First-Order Phase Transition Triggered by Non-Gaussian Fluctuations of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-Symmetric Spectator Scalar
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose a novel mechanism to trigger a first-order cosmological electroweak phase transition using non-Gaussian primordial fluctuations of a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric spectator scalar field. We show that the large fluctuations of the spectator field can modify the Higgs thermal mass and enhance the thermal barrier, thereby enabling a strong first-order phase transition. Non-Gaussianities in the primordial fluctuation spectrum significantly increase the probability of large-amplitude fluctuations, allowing a substantial fraction of the Universe to undergo the transition. The spectator field also naturally serves as a cold dark matter candidate through its coherent oscillations, reproducing the observed relic abundance. The resulting stochastic gravitational-wave background peaks at $f\sim 10^{-3}-10^{-1}$ Hz, but its amplitude lies roughly ten orders of magnitude below the projected sensitivities of planned space-based and ground-based interferometers.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 64 pages, 6 figures, 1 table; accepted for publication in JHEP

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Hawking-Page phase transitions of black holes in the Hamiltonian formalism
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We employ the Hamiltonian formalism proposed by P. M. Dirac to investigate the Hawking-Page phase transition of the non-rotating Bañados-Teitelboim-Zanelli (BTZ), Reissner-Nordström (RN) and Kerr-Newman (KN) black holes in both on-shell and off-shell configurations. For the BTZ black hole, the on-shell Hamiltonian agrees with the corresponding Helmholtz free energy obtained from the Euclidean action, reproducing the established Hawking-Page phase structure, while the off-shell analysis is consistent with the corresponding continuous phase transition obtained from the Euclidean approach. The same agreement is found for the on-shell RN and KN black holes. We further investigate the previously unexplored off-shell configurations of the RN and KN black holes. We find that electric charge restricts the mass range of the thermal soliton state, while rotation in the KN case removes the upper mass bound and eliminates the distinction arising from arbitrary surface contributions between the thermal soliton and black hole states. These findings uncover new aspects of the off-shell thermodynamics of charged and rotating black holes and suggest a possible connection between their phase structure and the quantum nature of gravity.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 42 pages, 6 figures, published in Physica Scripta

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Semiclassical causal geodesics: Schwarzschild spacetime case
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We propose an extension of the integral quantization, applied previously to the semiclassical description of a test particle in the flat Minkowski spacetime, to the Schwarzschild spacetime. This extension yields a local integral quantization. We calculate the transition amplitudes between coherent states of a particle in a mass layer, which effectively leads to a Klein-Gordon-type dynamics. The calculated probability distributions reproduce locally the classical radial geodesic motion in the Schwarzschild spacetime. The local integral quantization presented here seems to be applicable to semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in other curved spacetimes.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Self-force calculations with numerical relativity methods
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: To model gravitational waveforms from extreme mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) for the upcoming LISA space mission, gravitational self-force calculations are needed to second order in perturbation theory. However, to date these calculations have only been attempted for the simplest case of circular orbits in Schwarzschild spacetime. In this work, we present a new computational method aimed at performing generic second-order self-force calculations in Kerr spacetime using methods from the adjacent field of numerical relativity. We perform an $m$-mode separation of variables, add null (``$vtu$'') slicing in horizon-penetrating coordinates, and solve the resulting elliptic partial differential equations using high-order discontinuous Galerkin discretization, adaptive mesh refinement, and an iterative Krylov-type linear solver with parallelizable multigrid-Schwarz preconditioning. We find that our method achieves exponential convergence for the self-force on a scalar point charge in Kerr spacetime up to spins of $|a|/M=0.998$ (Thorne limit) on circular equatorial orbits as close as the innermost stable circular orbit (prograde and retrograde), despite the nonsmooth solution on the grid. We solve for 20 $m$-modes in parallel in a few seconds and retain the flexibility to extend the method to gravitational self-force and more generic orbits in the future. The code to perform these calculations is publicly available in the open-source numerical relativity code SpECTRE.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures. Results are reproducible with the ancillary input files

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Unitarity with respect to the Clock of a Dynamical Local Observer and the Einstein Equivalence Principle
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution with respect to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity. In the former case, we find that evolution relative to the internal clock is generally nonunitary, implying a violation of the Einstein equivalence principle at the quantum level. In contrast, in the latter case, diffeomorphism invariance allows us to adopt observer-centric coordinates. On the resulting partially reduced phase space, one of the diffeomorphism generators becomes linear in the clock Hamiltonian, generating a relational evolution that is consistent with the remaining diffeomorphism constraints. Assuming the existence of an effective quantum theory that consistently preserves diffeomorphism invariance, these features imply unitary evolution relative to the internal clock, thereby preserving the equivalence principle even in the quantum regime. Our results highlight the fundamental role of diffeomorphism invariance in shaping relational unitary evolution from the perspective of a local observer.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 34 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Title changed; conclusions unchanged

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Curvature inequalities and rigidity for constant mean curvature and spacetime constant mean curvature surfaces
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary:
We establish curvature inequalities and rigidity results for constant mean curvature (CMC) surfaces in Riemannian manifolds and spacetime constant mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces in Lorentzian manifolds. In three-dimensional Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we show that the Christodoulou-Yau inequality $H^2\leq 16π/|Σ|$ ($H$ denoting mean curvature and $|Σ|$ area) for stable CMC spheres also holds for CMC surfaces of arbitrary topology under a new stability condition controlling only the constant mode of the second variation of area. Under an extrinsic curvature sign condition, equality forces the enclosed region to be Euclidean without additional intrinsic assumptions. We extend these results to higher dimensions and to the hyperbolic and spherical settings.
  In the Lorentzian setting, we develop a variational stability theory for STCMC surfaces based on the second variation of area in the mean curvature vector direction. We introduce two independent stability notions: variational stability, which recovers classical volume-preserving CMC stability for surfaces in totally geodesic spacelike hypersurfaces, and constant-mode stability. Under the dominant energy condition, either yields the sharp inequality $|\vec H|^2\leq 16π/|Σ|$. In the equality case, under suitable geometric assumptions, the maximal globally hyperbolic development of the enclosed spacelike region is a Minkowski causal diamond. These results imply nonnegativity and rigidity of the Hawking quasi-local energy for stable STCMC surfaces. Finally, we analyze known spacelike and null STCMC foliations, showing that asymptotic leaves are stable under positive mass conditions, whereas the local matter density and trace-free extrinsic curvature govern the instability of local foliations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 40 pages. Substantially revised version. The variational stability condition has been reformulated to recover classical volume-preserving CMC stability exactly in the time-symmetric setting for nonminimal surfaces. The two stability notions are now independent, the curvature inequalities hold under weaker variational stability assumptions

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, whose amplitudes are given by the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions whose shifts have power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, in which the slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed locally by matter and geometry without an external clock. This class includes the comoving and uniform-density gauges, whose spectra grow without bound at late times in radiation domination. Over this range of $w$, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, justifying its standard use in computing the gravitational-wave energy spectrum. In matter domination, by contrast, the out-state isolates the free wave from the static tidal response that asymptotically dominates the Newtonian-gauge tensor perturbation.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local Lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the Lovelock class of theories of gravity. The horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. Naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full Lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. We show that on the horizon, the Hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local Lorentz boost is the Wald entropy.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Carroll limits of bosonic and supersymmetric D-branes in the Polyakov formulation
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We derive the magnetic and electric Carroll limits of bosonic and supersymmetric D-branes in the Polyakov formulation at fixed positive rescaled tension. Eliminating the nonsymmetric auxiliary tensor recovers the full Dirac--Born--Infeld action. On the regular domain with a positive-definite induced spatial metric and a positive lapse bounded away from zero, the auxiliary constraints remain second class in both limits. Eliminating them before or after contraction gives the same local reduced phase space. The magnetic Hamiltonian retains the full spatial determinant and the electric Hamiltonian retains the electric displacement squared. We compare their dynamics on flat D2 solutions and on curves in a common warped Carroll background. Both limits retain sixteen independent $κ$-symmetry parameters for flat Type II D2--D7 branes. The electric limit also retains a Neveu--Schwarz flux term in the fermionic constraint and supercharge matrices. Spatial T-duality commutes with both contractions on fixed-radius circle zero modes when the dual transverse canonical pair is rescaled in the electric case. The prescribed local Carroll--Weyl transformation fails to preserve the constraints, and both actions admit exact global dilations.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. Together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We obtain an explicit separation of the coupled gravitational and electromagnetic radiative equations on nonextremal Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter black holes with nonzero charge and rotation. By directly matching the Fourier coefficients, we construct a separating matrix with constant determinant that is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both spin sectors. We establish that this transformation is smooth and invertible throughout the open AdS exterior and between the event and cosmological horizons in dS. The resulting radial and angular systems are valid at arbitrary complex frequencies. We also translate the regularity of the radiative Newman--Penrose variables at the rotation axes and future horizons into boundary conditions for the separated solutions. In the asymptotically flat limit, the transformation is related to Hintz's matrix integrating factor by the allowed frame freedom. These results provide a basis for studying quasinormal modes and black hole stability in Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter spacetimes, as well as exploring holographic applications to strongly coupled systems.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: PINN-Slicer: Exploiting Rotational Symmetry to Solve the Photon Orbit Equation Around a Black Hole
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) typically struggle with long-horizon domains, often requiring the network to be retrained as the domain grows. We present PINN-Slicer, a method for second-order autonomous ordinary differential equations, $\ddot{u} = G(u, \dot{u})$, which exploits the invariance of this class of equations under translations of the independent variable. A single PINN, embedded within a solution ansatz that enforces the initial conditions explicitly, is trained on a thin slice of the independent variable using Sobol-sampled initial conditions. The PINN is then deployed recursively, slice-by-slice, across the full domain. We demonstrate PINN-Slicer on the nonlinear equation that describes photon orbits around a black hole, and reach a point-by-point root-mean-square error (RMSE) below $10^{-3}$ in $u = r_s/r$ (the inverse radial coordinate in units of the Schwarzschild radius) relative to a finite-difference reference solution. A key advantage of PINN-Slicer is that a single trained network generalizes to any orbital initial condition within the training range, without retraining. In addition, PINN-Slicer can cope with solution domains that may not be known a priori.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 11 pages, 14 figures, 2 tables. Accepted at the 9th Workshop on Machine Learning and the Physical Sciences (ML4PS 2026). Code: https://github.com/soot-bit/pinnslicer

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Cosmographic Analysis of Gravitational Baryogenesis in Running-$G$ Cosmology
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: Gravitational baryogenesis produces a baryon asymmetry through the coupling of the baryon current to the derivative of the Ricci scalar, so its yield is set by the expansion history around decoupling. We study this mechanism in cosmology with a running Newton coupling of the asymptotic-safety type. Writing the Ricci scalar and its derivative through the Hubble rate, the deceleration parameter $q$ and the jerk $j$, we show that the yield is proportional to the kernel $K=2+q-j$, which vanishes for radiation in general relativity, and to a power of an enhancement factor measuring how strongly the running coupling accelerates the expansion at decoupling. We treat hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing and little-rip scale factors and determine where the observed asymmetry is reproduced for the $J^μ\partial_μR$ and $J^μ\partial_μR^2$ couplings; a table compares the six cases.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Stability and quasi-normal ringing in analogue black-white holes in SNAIL-based traveling-wave parametric amplifiers
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The circuit dynamics constructed by traveling-wave parametric amplifiers (TWPA), using superconducting nonlinear asymmetric inductive elements (SNAILs), are known to be approximately described by the Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) or modified KdV equations in the continuum limit and admit soliton solutions. The soliton spatially modulates the effective propagation velocity of the weak probe field, which leads to the effective realization of the causal structure of the analogue event horizons in the SNAIL-TWPA circuit system. In this paper, we derive the master equation for the weak probe field where the background soliton acts as an effective potential. We show, in the effective theory where the nonlinear dispersion is neglected, the absence of normalizable negative modes in the SNAIL-TWPA circuit system by using the language of supersymmetric quantum mechanics. We also present the first study of quasi-normal modes (QNM) of the SNAIL-TWPA analogue black-white hole system in the dispersionless effective theory by numerical and semi-analytic methods. Based on the resultant QNM frequency, we clarify the timescale at which nonlinear dispersion becomes effective in the SNAIL-TWPA circuit system and suggest the possibility of observing ringdown.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: The Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems and curved spacetimes - An orthonormal frames approach
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: In this pedagogical article we discuss the Dirac equation in arbitrary coordinate systems. We explain the need for connections when dealing with spinor fields and present the practical steps needed to compute the Dirac operator in a general setting, allowing for arbitrary coordinate systems and position-dependent orthonormal gamma matrices, both of which can simplify computations in certain scenarios. The extension to include minimally coupled gravity is straightforward. Examples are provided, including constructing the Dirac equation in spherical and cylindrical symmetry (with or without gravity) and the Kerr spacetime.
