We also briefly comment on the advantages and disadvantages of various tetrads and orthonormal gamma matrices. This manuscript should be accessible to readers who have studied the Dirac equation at an introductory level (e.g., in Cartesian coordinates in flat spacetime with constant gamma matrices). The emphasis is on the use of orthonormal frames, since these correspond to the coordinate systems most familiar to readers when dealing with most field theories, and represent the physical frames where measurements are performed. The aim is to get the reader quickly to the point of being able to do calculations, so the presentation favors a concise, pragmatic approach over extended derivations.
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.comment: 28 pages, 1 figure; general treatment of the Dirac equation (in the absence of torsion) for cases in which $γ^{\hat 0}$ serves as the hermitizing matrix for the Dirac matrices

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: Holographic probes and Krylov complexity on asymptotically Lifshitz rotating black branes
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: We study two types of holographic probes on a five-dimensional, asymptotically Lifshitz, rotating black hole. This geometry solves the field equations of Einstein gravity coupled to a dilaton, two axionic scalars, and a Maxwell doublet, supplemented by two vector doublets that enter the action through a parity-odd, Chern-Simons-like combination, as recently found in \cite{Bravo-Gaete:2026bdq}. This spacetime provides a concrete bottom-up arena to explore the imprints of rotation on probes in non-relativistic holography. First, we compute the holographic static quark-antiquark potential following the standard prescription that relates this boundary observable to the on shell-action of a string configuration whose endpoints are anchored at the boundary. We find that the screening length decreases both when the angular momentum is increased at fixed temperature and when the temperature is increased at fixed angular momentum. The former reflects centrifugal effects on the $q\bar{q}$ pair, whereas the latter stems from enhanced thermal fluctuations, which weaken correlations at a given separation. Second, we compute the growth rate of the Krylov complexity, using the holographic prescription that relates this observable to the momentum of a massive particle probe falling into the IR. In particular, we find that, at a given instant, the complexity grows faster as the dynamical exponent $z$ is increased.

General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.title: All known supersymmetric $\mathrm{AdS}_4 \times S^7$ uplifts from maximal supergravity
General Relativity and Quantum Cosmology.summary: The solutions of $D=4$ $\mathcal N=8$ SO(8)-gauged supergravity uplift consistently to eleven dimensions. All known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua of this theory lie in an $\mathcal N=1$ truncation containing seven chiral multiplets. In this paper, we work out the uplift of this seven-chiral sector, providing a unified eleven-dimensional geometric description of all known supersymmetric AdS$_4$ solutions in this class. We then specialise to the $\mathcal N=1$ vacua with U(1)$^2$ and SO(3) symmetry, obtain their new $D=11$ uplifts and bring out their internal geometries. Both of them admit a Kaluza--Klein-type description. For the U(1)$^2$ solution, this uses the global Hopf fibration of $S^7$ over $\mathbb{CP}^3$. One U(1) acts on the fibre, while the other generates the only continuous isometry of the deformed $\mathbb{CP}^3$ base. For the SO(3) solution, the geometry takes a local non-abelian Kaluza--Klein form, with SO(3) acting on the fibres and no residual continuous symmetry on the four-dimensional base.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Lattice gauge theory computation of $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections to the quarkonium potential
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We compute the static quark-antiquark potential and its $1/m_Q$ and $1/m_Q^2$ corrections, i.e.\ the $1/m_Q$ potential and all $1/m_Q^2$ potentials, which can be expressed in terms of correlators of two field strength insertions, in SU(3) lattice gauge theory and provide parameterizations for quark-antiquark separations $0.2 \, \text{fm} \lesssim r \lesssim 0.7 \, \text{fm}$. The field strength insertions in generalized Wilson loops are renormalized using gradient flow, which also leads to small statistical uncertainties. All potentials are extrapolated to zero flow time and, in contrast to previous lattice studies, to the continuum, using three lattice spacings and four flow times. The spin dependent potentials are matched to the $\overline{\text{MS}}$ scheme at NLO and provided at $μ= 3 \, \text{GeV}$. They can easily be converted to specific heavy quark masses, e.g.\ for Born-Oppenheimer effective field theory studies of quarkonium.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Unfreezing topology using out-of-equilibrium replica exchanges
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: Parallel Tempering on Boundary Conditions (PTBC) mitigates topological freezing by exchanging configurations between replicas that interpolate between periodic and open boundaries on a small defect. We generalize PTBC by replacing the instantaneous swap with a short out-of-equilibrium protocol, in which the defect couplings of two replicas are exchanged gradually while the fields around the defect are updated. We show that the swap rate depends only on the average work spent along the out-of-equilibrium trajectory by virtue of Crooks' and Jarzynski's fluctuation relations. From the theoretical derivation of the scaling of the work as a function of the number of replicas, protocol length, and defect size, we predict the swap rate and the optimal protocol length. These predictions are tested in the $2d$ $\mathrm{CP}^{N-1}$ model with $N=21$. The optimal setup agrees with the measured one, the total computational cost at fixed statistical precision decreases by $\gtrsim40\%$ with respect to standard PTBC for all explored lattice spacings, and the required number of replicas at fixed acceptance is halved.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Compositeness and decay properties of the flavor partner of $D^{*}_{s0}(2317)$
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: In view of the recent experimental finding of the heavy quark flavor partner of the $D_{s0}(2317)$ in the bottom sector, the $B_{s0}(5700)$, we perform a single and coupled-channel $B^{(*)}\bar{K}^{(*)}$ calculation in the hidden-gauge formalism within the on-shell and off-shell schemes, respectively. By fixing the $B\bar{K}$ bound state mass to the observed state with $J^P=0^+$, we also predict five new states with $J^P=\lbrace 0,1,2\rbrace^+$ in this sector, three of them with $J^P=1^+$. Additionally, in the coupled-channel calculation, two states with masses and decay widths similar to the $B_{sJ}(6114)$ and $B_{sJ}(6063)$ ones, with spins $J=0^+$ and $2^+$, respectivley, and decaying into $B\bar{K}$, are dynamically generated. Moreover, we evaluate the decay widths of the $B_{s0}$ and $B_{s1}$ states generated from $B^{(*)}\bar{K}$ through the isospin breaking decay mode $B_s^0π^0$ and $B_s^{*0}π^0$, respectively. We find that, because these states have large binding energies, the coupling to the bare component can reduce this decay width by more than half of the decay width, from $50$~keV in the purely molecular model to $10-20$~keV, when the $B_{s0}$ is coupled to the bare component. We also observe that, after considering heavy-quark-spin symmetry violating contributions, the decay width for the $B_{s1}$ becomes smaller than for the $B_{s0}$.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Gradient-flow scale setting from octet baryon masses in N$^3$LO covariant chiral perturbation theory
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We determine the gradient-flow scale $t_0$ by analyzing the lowest-lying octet-baryon masses on the Coordinated Lattice Simulations (CLS) $N_f=2+1$ ensembles in covariant baryon chiral perturbation theory up to next-to-next-to-next-to leading order (N$^3$LO). By including the finite-volume corrections self-consistently and the discretization effects from Symanzik effective field theory, we obtain a good description of the RQCD data and determine the gradient-flow scale to be $\sqrt{8t_{0,\mathrm{ph}}}=0.4120(14)_\mathrm{stat.}(16)_\mathrm{sys.}$ fm with sub-percent precision. The predicted octet baryon masses agree well with the experimental values in the isospin limit. Using the Feynman-Hellmann theorem, we also estimate the nucleon sigma terms, which are consistent with direct determinations from three-point correlation functions on the same CLS ensembles.

High Energy Physics - Lattice.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in QED with the Pauli term
High Energy Physics - Lattice.summary: We study the renormalization group (RG) flow of quantum electrodynamics (QED) with a Pauli term, $κ_τ\Barψσ_{μν}F_{μν}ψ$, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group (GFERG). In the GFERG, the gauge Ward--Takahashi (WT) identity takes the conventional form and is exactly preserved, and the gauge coupling flows only through the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$. Consequently, at any fixed point with a vanishing gauge coupling, the eigenvalue in the direction of the gauge coupling is exactly~$-γ_A^*$, and the gauge coupling is relevant if and only if the vacuum polarization makes~$γ_A^*$ negative. In the leading large-$N_f$ approximation, the vacuum polarization induced by the Pauli coupling yields such a fixed point, with~$γ_A^*=-1$ and three relevant directions. At finite~$N_f$, however, the $N_f$-independent one-loop effects on the fermion line eliminate it unless $N_f$ is at least several tens. For~$N_f=1$, a search over the whole plane of the Pauli coupling and the mass parameter in the subspace~$e_τ=0$, where our flow equation is exactly of one-loop order, finds a single fixed point, at strong Pauli coupling and a finite mass parameter. Like one of the fixed points of the asymptotically safe QED proposed by Gies and Ziebell, it has a finite mass parameter and two relevant directions. At their fixed point, the gauge coupling is relevant. At ours, in contrast, $γ_A^*>0$, so that the gauge coupling is irrelevant, and the fixed point cannot provide a UV completion of QED with a nonzero charge. Along the full flow for~$N_f=1$ on the critical surface connected to the Gaussian fixed point, $κ_τ$ is irrelevant and is attracted to an induced value proportional to~$e_τ^3$ at weak coupling, while $e_τ^2$ is marginally irrelevant as in QED without the Pauli term.
